A fairly mediocre "shoot 'n loot" experience with a lack of loot. The exploration is fun a for a while.
If you're like me then you'll get bored of the combat fairly quickly. There aren't really any interesting characters and I can't see anyone caring for the "story" all that much. It's basically me going on a wild goose chase after some baby that I don't care about. An hour in and you can have two sets of power armor and 3 mini nuke launchers a few miniguns and an invincible combat companion. Death Claws are a complete non threat. I could go on about how boring the combat is but I won't... It's just boring.
I had a good amount of fun exploring abandoned buildings and bunkers and the like. There are some cool bits of story hidden in terminals, on walls, in notes, etc. The primary story in the game is often ignored by many players in favor of just going out and exploring. I was really suprised by the amount of detail that was put into some things that most players will just walk right past and never return to.
Although, there is a complete and total lack of any kind of persuasion/charisma/karma system. You absolutely can NOT choose to play as an evil character. You are required to be a kind, caring parent figure (aside from some sarcasm dialog options). There are no speech options that matter; the only thing charisma is used for outside of combat is getting people to give you more  currency. The Brotherhood is totally uninteresting and boils down to a bunch of fetch quests (i.e. get this item, kill these things). There is a lack of unique armor, most of the armor you will wear comes from Raiders (really, the only enemy in the game) and is given a different name. The entire settlement system is pointless because nothing ever happens with it. Nothing. Sure you can build walls and turrets and windmills and what not... but, why?
Blah blah blah. I don't recommend, unless it goes on sale. Even if it does, you should look into Fallout 3 or New Vegas because they are lightyears better than this.

6. Ton of content within a deceptively small looking overworld map
The Bad:
1. World Textures
2. Load order for the textures

5. Companion AI - They will do their best to walk in front of you and stop moving so you have to jump around them or over them, and Dogmeat loves to block your escape when a mininuke is flying at you.
As stated before, overall I feel their is enough content and gameplay within it to warrant the price and like all Bethesda games it will eventually fall onto the fans to make the unoffical patches and mods which further advance the game.
So give it a shot.

The reasons I would recommend this game are for many of the reasons the negative reviewers argue against it.
1 The leveling system is far better in its new form.  Bethesda replaced the skill system were you increased skills to reach a hidden threshold value that would increase ability in a given area.  Instead you now chose a rank in the available abilities, achieving the same goal in a much more transparent way. Mix this with the fact that all of the special stats are useful and you receive fewer points at the beginning of the game, character builds are more important in fo4 than ever. Now can the system be broken? Yes but the old system could be broken just as easily if not more so by min maxing the useful stats.
2 The useless karma system is gone. I've seen so many complaints that the system is gone but it never really did anything but limit what companions would follow you.  It has been replaced by a relationship system with your companions who will react to your actions, building a relationship and letting you in on their back story, taking you on quests and eventually providing unique perks.
3 The Wasteland is as fantastic as ever.  Bethesda has a knack for environmental story telling and it shines in fo4.  Where other games rely on side quests to relay extra story bits Bethesda uses strategically placed terminals and sets to tell stories from before the war and after. It is up to the player to explore, find all the details and then tell the story of what happened.
4. It's different from fo3 and nv.  Many of the complaints I've read are that a player can not be evil. Meaning what? That I can't nuke megaton and join the slavers again. I like that their are 4 factions each having legitimate reasons for their actions and its up to the player to choose their faction and "role play" why they chose said faction and their intentions for amassing so much power.
5 though I agree in some regards the dialog system is not as deep as nv, it is deeper than fo3 imo. I do think the voice acting itself is great and the voiced protagonist is well executed and helped me to role play a woman character which I have avoided in the past.  I liked it and felt that it served its purpose with the style that Bethesda intended it to.
6 The combat in this game is fun and fun and smooth. In fo3 and nv combat was a chore. In fo4 wether using vats or not the combat just works. Partner the improved combat with a focused character build and the new system is incredibly fun and rewarding.
I have been a big fallout fan since the mid 90s and I have truly enjoyed this latest entry to the series.

I wish there was a neutral option or at least a leveled rating system rather than the yes/no option.   There are aspects of this game that I like and there are aspects that I don't like.
I confess to being Fallout OG.   I've played and replayed every single one of them with the exception of that BOS thing on the Playstation.   I loved what Bethesda did with Fallout 3 and especially enjoyed New Vegas.  So I was very much looking forward to Fallout 4.
And then... Well... what the hell just happened?
There are enough coherant reviews prior to mine to illustrate all the pro's and cons that I am feeling about this game.   Suffice it to say that Fallout 4 is different enough to put many of us old schoolers off our game.

As of now (the time I'm writing the review), I have 193 hours. While still not as high as some other people, I can say I have put in enough time to make a very critical review and have some credence in what I am about to say. Fallout 4 was overhyped. It lacked in many areas and I feel as though Bethesda wasted to much money allocating resources into areas they should not have put them. For instance, voiced protagonist. Having a voiced protagonist was an abosolute waste of money in my opinion. It was a waste of resources that could have gone into making quests or optimizing the game. Instead it was wasted on a series changer, maybe even a studio changer. It was like being forced to play Hawke in Dragon Age 2. Also, from what I've seen, there are no repeated voice actors. (If you played Skyrim, there were a lot of NPCs that had the same voice, which is what I mean by repeated voice actors). Having no repeated voice actors is not a bad thing, I enjoyed it actually; It helped immersion. This however, still really shouldn't have been a main focus for the studio. I'm rambling and I know this, but what I'm trying to say is this; Bethesda wasted money and overall, made a pretty average shooter. Notice how I said shooter? I hope you did, because I don't consider this an rpg.
-Great voice actors
-Amazing gunplay
-Good story
-More fleshed out companions (seems they took cues from Fallout: New Vegas)
-Huge environment and landscape
-Lots of places to explore
-Good writing (which kind of falls into story I guess)
-Customization system
-Sarcasm
-Settlement system (while it could have been modded in it's still nice)
-Open world
-Mods
-No karma system (this bugged me a lot)

I've spent nearly 200 hours on this game as of writing this review. So expect me to know what I'm talking about better than these sycophants that worship these rotten companies instead of calling them on their BS.
The game is good, but is a terrible Fallout game and an even worse RPG.
This game is pretty much a Far Cry game that has had the Far Cry formula improved. It lacks the replayability of Fallout games because the roleplay elements have been gutted from the game.
The main character has voice acting (which is really bad for male, not sure about female yet), and that voice limits the RP immensely.
There is now a dialogue wheel, and that wheel is only affected by charisma, so no more using Intellect or Science or any other stats to affect the dialogue choices. And the dialogue is not deep as it has been in past games with the dialogue trees. It's a lot like Mass Effect's dialogue trees, but ME dialogue was also deeper than this games.
Some times the NPC's you're talking to have responses to what you just said that don't even make sense in the context, like the dialogue tree got mixed up and used some default reply.
The perks are now all based off your main stats and you can choose them all if you really want making your characters in no way unique characters with each play though. It is really awful, because perks are just the character traits to your characters in each play, and you could only get a few and that made your character a unique individual, so by gutting that perk system and adding this terrible new MMO-like system kills replayability. To make what I'm trying to say here clearer: Everyone in real life has character traits that makes them who they are. So everyone is different. Fallout had that with the old perk system, but now it is gone.
I beat the game and tried making a new character to play through as evil, but the character talks the same way when using evil choices so I gave up. It's cringe worthy and annoying.
The voice acting also ruins playing as characters made to look like real people or characters from other entertainment. I tried playing as Negan from TWD and I just couldn't with that awful voice acting.
The shooting combat is good, but it doesn't matter if everything else about the game is bad, so that really doesn't matter. The Fallout series has always been an RPG, not a shooter.
The settlement system is actually a great new addition to Fallout, but it is not deep at all and has a horrible management system that everyone including Bethesda expects the modders to fix, and it is not RP friendly. You can use the settlements to gain stuff to sell, and stores to sell stuff at and give you money. And it gave purpose to scrap other than just selling. I always ignored it in the other games.
And finally, the main excuse people have been making about this game being so bad and lacking is that modders will fix everything wrong with the game, but Bethesda has mentioned that they will be bringing the paid mod system back in the future for Fallout 4 and Skyrim, so if you want the game fixed, you'll likely have to pay money to fix it. So these people are living in denial.
Will update and edit this review over time as I think of what to say. I want this to be one of the few honest reviews on this site because I'm not some company worshiping mindless tool or a "hater" so I have valid criticisms and stuff I am impressed by, and I want people to have at least one review that can be relied on for the truth.
If I had to give this game a number ranking I rank it 5/10.
+5 for the things they've improved, and -5 for gutting the soul of Fallout from the game.

OK so, here is my review in short, TL; DW ;)
Summary:
Some good, some bad, less FPSish RPG from FO3/NV, more RPGish FPS like Borderlands.
It's big change anyway. it's refreshing, it's still enjoyable.
But some design decisions are rather controversial and may NOT fit Fallout.
If i really want to play a good RPG, I will take FNV+FO3+Tales of Two Wastelands anyday
Fallout 4 is a good game, not the best RPG game atm, but it's good.
Gunplay:
The gunplay is a huge improvement, Gun mods, Grenade hotkey, etc. Feels like incorporated Fallout: NV Project Neveda mod!
It changes from the FPSish RPG of Fallout 3/NV to this RPGish FPS, with looting system; feels more like Borderlands now but I can't say I expect this from Fallout...
Story + Mission:
Main quest is ok, on par with Fallout 3. Of course, it is as linear as Fallout 3, not the multiple ending as in NV. Well I mean, FNV was a jewel in the Fallout series. Can't compare, maybe DLC changes things later.
Side Quests:
Well, I keep getting Minutemen save this guy/clear some place; and Brotherhood clear this/loot this side missions,  seems a bit repetitive. Probably they are like the endless auto-generated side quests in Skyrim, JUST FOR LEVEL GRINDING.
I dont know, I admit that at this point I am still taking my time in FO4, and haven't found lots more different side missions; maybe there are more interesting ones I haven't come across with.
But so far it seems side quests are much more linear than before...you dont get to decide much, and choose your reward.
Good Guys/Bad Guys/Karma:
This is really a bit of a let down. Even though I usually play Messiah/Jesus in Wasteland kind of guy (because I'm a nice guy?); Sometimes I enjoy doing some dirty work just as a greedy merc, or stealing(borrow) some necessity I need like stimpaks.
Now? Seems like there is no evil companions anymore, like in FNV everyone is anti-Caesar. Whenever I steal something, even if I'm completely undetected the companion "dislikes" me doing that :( I mean, what the ♥♥♥♥?
SPECIAL, Skill:
They didn't change too much in SPECIAL, but they removed the skills; upside is that now you are more evenly distributed, and balanced
Back in F3/NV days, if you get Speech, Lockpick, Science up quickly, the game will be a walk in the park because you will be looting/talking your way through all over early on. And later on, as you level up and get more HP and AP, and better high damage guns, you just become Rambo of Death with 100 Guns+Sneak skill.
I would like to see a rework than just simplifies it.
Perks:
Back then, linked with skills. Now it's just locked under SPECIAL level. I dont like this.
First, there are fewer perks to play with now. Where the ♥♥♥♥ is my Living Anatomy?! I want it back!! Or my Nuclear Anomaly?! They should add content, not remove it.
Second, some good/fun perks you can't unlock early anymore...obviously. sadly.
Dialogues:
4 lines...seriously? I will give Bethesda a plus for all the voiced dialogues, but if that means cutting options down? I rather they save the resources for the options.
Bugs/Crashes:
Godray depixelize bug confirmed, other than that, only a handful crashes I came across with.
Played 15 hrs continuously without crash, so I'm pretty satisfied with this initial release.

I was so nervous when I first saw all of the negative reviews for this game, but it has exceeded my expectations.
When I first started it up, I was unimpressed. I'll admit that it did take me a while to get into it, and that's because the FO4 is different from it's predecessors (which is not necessarily a bad thing.)
PROS
-Battles/enemies are fun to fight. The combat system is way improved in my opinion, and the enemies are more difficult in a good way.
-Exploring is fun. The Commonwealth is a dangerous place at times, but it's really fun to explore.
-Somewhat immersive NPCs. Try sneaking around some raiders and listen to what they have to talk about.
-The player character is fully voiced which can be a pro or a con depending on personal preference. I like it a lot, personally.
CONS
-The new dialogue system is boring. I don't like not being able to see what my character is going to say, but you do get used to it.
-Settlement building has so much potential to be better than it is. It feels as though this was an after thought, which is unfortunate because it is one of the most interesting/unique parts.
-Bugs. It's a new release so bugs are to be expected (unfortunately). I haven't encountered any gamebreaking ones yet, but I have experienced some really annoying ones.
All in all, I don't regret purchasing this game. I also don't understand all of the hate it's getting. It's a really good game!

I really want to give this game a good review as I am a big Fallout/TES fan, As much as I enjoy this new addition to the series, I can't help but realise that this game does alot of stuff right (like the new power armor system, looting, getting rid of alot of loading screens) but at the same time does alot of stuff wrong.
RPG element:
Compare to the older fallout games I feel like you have wayyyyy lesser choice here, every conversation feels like it is going to have the same outcome in the end (I've had npc reacted and said the same thing regardless to what I've said too) and I feel like there are way lesser interesting characters, there are no real choices in this game except the main questline where you have to decide which faction you're going to stick with in the end.
Questing:
The introduction of unlimited level cap means you will need alot more stuff to do than previous games, I've already ran out of quest towards 70 hours into the game, To combat this, Bethesda decided to introduce randomly generated quest which are unlimited, but this isn't an MMO, things like that should never be in a single player game, there should've been wayyyyy more quest than what we've been given.
Building:
One of the selling point of the game, I feel like there is alot of things that are missing in this, often you will find it really really hard to build walls for your town because they've included a auto snap function without a disable auto snap function, so you are unable to build a wall that circles your settlement (there are workarounds for this, but I just feel like it was a feature that should've been in there all along) you cannot build on alot of things and often you will find yourself  tearing your hair out trying to figure out what to do.
Voiced character, and your name:
I know that some people appreciate a voiced main character but I feel like this lessen the RPG element by alot, voice overs for a main character is a hit or miss for alot of people, afterall, fallout is all about making your own choices, with this game, you're just a character with limited choice in what they say, and when you do, you feel like you're "generic american army guy number 1" or “generic family women number 1"
Onto the topic of your name:
I can't believe they made this an actual selling point in E3, yes, you will hear codsworth call out your name, however this will be the only 1 or 2 time you will ever hear your name, (150 hours into the game and I've heard the name Lily twice, from the same NPC) I understand that it'll be too hard to make more npcs call out thousands of different names. but making this a selling point is insulting enough for me to write a whole paragraph about it.
I feel like Bethesda know what they are doing, they've definately learnt alot from the modding community and listened to feedbacks from past games, this isn't something alot of developer does, there are way lesser bugs compared to previous titles such as Oblivion, Skyrim and Fallout 3. But they have taken a very very wrong turn when they decided some things for this game, like the dumbing down the dialogue and letting you get a power armor rather early (you get your first power armor like 30 mins into the game, what???)

OK so, here is my review in short, TL; DW ;)
Summary:
Some good, some bad, less FPSish RPG from FO3/NV, more RPGish FPS like Borderlands.
It's big change anyway. it's refreshing, it's still enjoyable.
But some design decisions are rather controversial and may NOT fit Fallout.
If i really want to play a good RPG, I will take FNV+FO3+Tales of Two Wastelands anyday
Fallout 4 is a good game, not the best RPG game atm, but it's good.
Gunplay:
The gunplay is a huge improvement, Gun mods, Grenade hotkey, etc. Feels like incorporated Fallout: NV Project Neveda mod!
It changes from the FPSish RPG of Fallout 3/NV to this RPGish FPS, with looting system; feels more like Borderlands now but I can't say I expect this from Fallout...
Story + Mission:
Main quest is ok, on par with Fallout 3. Of course, it is as linear as Fallout 3, not the multiple ending as in NV. Well I mean, FNV was a jewel in the Fallout series. Can't compare, maybe DLC changes things later.
Side Quests:
Well, I keep getting Minutemen save this guy/clear some place; and Brotherhood clear this/loot this side missions,  seems a bit repetitive. Probably they are like the endless auto-generated side quests in Skyrim, JUST FOR LEVEL GRINDING.
I dont know, I admit that at this point I am still taking my time in FO4, and haven't found lots more different side missions; maybe there are more interesting ones I haven't come across with.
But so far it seems side quests are much more linear than before...you dont get to decide much, and choose your reward.
Good Guys/Bad Guys/Karma:
This is really a bit of a let down. Even though I usually play Messiah/Jesus in Wasteland kind of guy (because I'm a nice guy?); Sometimes I enjoy doing some dirty work just as a greedy merc, or stealing(borrow) some necessity I need like stimpaks.
Now? Seems like there is no evil companions anymore, like in FNV everyone is anti-Caesar. Whenever I steal something, even if I'm completely undetected the companion "dislikes" me doing that :( I mean, what the ♥♥♥♥?
SPECIAL, Skill:
They didn't change too much in SPECIAL, but they removed the skills; upside is that now you are more evenly distributed, and balanced
Back in F3/NV days, if you get Speech, Lockpick, Science up quickly, the game will be a walk in the park because you will be looting/talking your way through all over early on. And later on, as you level up and get more HP and AP, and better high damage guns, you just become Rambo of Death with 100 Guns+Sneak skill.
I would like to see a rework than just simplifies it.
Perks:
Back then, linked with skills. Now it's just locked under SPECIAL level. I dont like this.
First, there are fewer perks to play with now. Where the ♥♥♥♥ is my Living Anatomy?! I want it back!! Or my Nuclear Anomaly?! They should add content, not remove it.
Second, some good/fun perks you can't unlock early anymore...obviously. sadly.
Dialogues:
4 lines...seriously? I will give Bethesda a plus for all the voiced dialogues, but if that means cutting options down? I rather they save the resources for the options.
Bugs/Crashes:
Godray depixelize bug confirmed, other than that, only a handful crashes I came across with.
Played 15 hrs continuously without crash, so I'm pretty satisfied with this initial release.

Update:
After a good amount of game play I've adjusted to the changes and am really enjoying the game.  I could now recommend this game.
Original:
Having been a fallout fan since the top-down original and a Bethesda fan since Elder Scrolls Arena, no amount of negative reviews were going to keep me from checking this game out for myself.  If your in this camp I recommend waiting until they cut this game's price by at least 50% or some very compelling DLC is released.  If you follow this advice you'll thank me later, if your determined to pay full price then ignore the nay sayers and just buy the damn game already.  Find out for yourself.
If you've never played a Fallout game, don't bother starting with this one.
----
I wrote off the negative reviews I read as "The game didn't meet my fantasy about what the game was going to be".  Creators deserve the chance to innovate and try new things, complaining because something is different is just a Luddite thing to do.   Bethesda's artists did an amazing job brining colour to the wasteland, the graphical attention to detail is noticeable and appreciated.  The new VATS and perk systems are just different, hopefully I'll get used to them.
Giving the character a voice and and giving players a story to follow were a noble pursuit.  The dialogue mechanics are fine compared to previous games, you rarely had more than 4 options anyway. The game does force you down the tried and true "rescue your kid" thing.  I have always struggled to be a negative karma character anyway, so forcing me to be good wasn't terrible. For me the deal breaker comes in the many ways the dialogue breaks immersion.  Why do people know about things I haven't told anyone? I never met this person how do I know their name?
Buying a Bethesda or Fallout game is usually like buying a plane ticket to another universe. I've come to expect that I'll be plunged into a strange and interesting world, where I'll be rewarded for spending countless hours exploring every nook and cranny of the world map, and reading various "lore" trying to understand why and how the world is the way it is.  I become so immersed in the world that I actually want to make a home there and decide how to decorate my bedroom, or arrange my hard won souvenirs. I'll play so many hours, that I live out many different lives.
In Fallout 4 I don't feel like a stranger in a strange land, my story is being narrated to me, I don't need to seek out my adventure it will be spoon fed to me. Fallout 4's critical failing isn't technical at all... Bethesda delivered on all the infrastructure I need to be part of this universe. They just failed to inspire me to do so...  I'm hoping that if I force myself to play a bit more I'll change my mind.

I really want to give this game a good review as I am a big Fallout/TES fan, As much as I enjoy this new addition to the series, I can't help but realise that this game does alot of stuff right (like the new power armor system, looting, getting rid of alot of loading screens) but at the same time does alot of stuff wrong.
RPG element:
Compare to the older fallout games I feel like you have wayyyyy lesser choice here, every conversation feels like it is going to have the same outcome in the end (I've had npc reacted and said the same thing regardless to what I've said too) and I feel like there are way lesser interesting characters, there are no real choices in this game except the main questline where you have to decide which faction you're going to stick with in the end.
Questing:
The introduction of unlimited level cap means you will need alot more stuff to do than previous games, I've already ran out of quest towards 70 hours into the game, To combat this, Bethesda decided to introduce randomly generated quest which are unlimited, but this isn't an MMO, things like that should never be in a single player game, there should've been wayyyyy more quest than what we've been given.
Building:
One of the selling point of the game, I feel like there is alot of things that are missing in this, often you will find it really really hard to build walls for your town because they've included a auto snap function without a disable auto snap function, so you are unable to build a wall that circles your settlement (there are workarounds for this, but I just feel like it was a feature that should've been in there all along) you cannot build on alot of things and often you will find yourself  tearing your hair out trying to figure out what to do.
Voiced character, and your name:
I know that some people appreciate a voiced main character but I feel like this lessen the RPG element by alot, voice overs for a main character is a hit or miss for alot of people, afterall, fallout is all about making your own choices, with this game, you're just a character with limited choice in what they say, and when you do, you feel like you're "generic american army guy number 1" or “generic family women number 1"
Onto the topic of your name:
I can't believe they made this an actual selling point in E3, yes, you will hear codsworth call out your name, however this will be the only 1 or 2 time you will ever hear your name, (150 hours into the game and I've heard the name Lily twice, from the same NPC) I understand that it'll be too hard to make more npcs call out thousands of different names. but making this a selling point is insulting enough for me to write a whole paragraph about it.
I feel like Bethesda know what they are doing, they've definately learnt alot from the modding community and listened to feedbacks from past games, this isn't something alot of developer does, there are way lesser bugs compared to previous titles such as Oblivion, Skyrim and Fallout 3. But they have taken a very very wrong turn when they decided some things for this game, like the dumbing down the dialogue and letting you get a power armor rather early (you get your first power armor like 30 mins into the game, what???)
As a fan of Fallout and TES, I cannot recommend this game to anyone. all the depth of the previous games are gone, but if it is for anyone who is new to the fallout franchise, fallout 4 isn't a bad game at all because it still does alot of things right, just not in a fallout-y way.

I know that with as many hours as I have sunk into this game not recommending it seems odd. Also its kind of pointless given how many people already own it but whatever.
Fallout 4 has a lot of good ideas and mechanisms, but they all kind of fall flat. They tried to tell a singular story really well and didn't do a very good job of it mostly beause it made very little sense given the game world and expectations put upon the player vs the expectations of what your character would actually be doing and feeling. It's a game with a story that would see you rush through it with a sense of urgency in a sandbox game world that is nothing but distraction after distraction.
There is a heavy focus on gunplay with this game. A heavy focus on being a FPS shooter. Very little focus on being an RPG of any sort. Dialog options are sparce and at many times insufficent, at several times I found myself needing to intereact with an NPC in a certain way but unable to do so because they had some other quest over-riding their dialog wheel leaving me unable to do what i needed until i took care of something else first.
The UI is abysmal. As terrible as Skyrims was, Fallout 4 is worse. Buttons will do one thing here, another thing there, and the settlement building tools are horrifically clunky.
Locations are... in a word boring. Loot is boring. The upgrade system is boring. The perk chart is neat looking but needlessly complicates finding the perk you wanted or seeing if it even existed in the first place. Locking perks by level also cripples character development and makes it impossible to create the character you wanted like you could in earlier games. Want to focus on being a stealthy hacker and lock picker? Sorry you can't master anything till your in your 40's. Same with focusing on crafting or.. anything really. Despite a perk point a level you can't really take what you want very quickly.
Karma and reputation pertty much don't exist. You can't really be a bad guy and get anywhere in this game. You can't progress without being funneled into a faction quest line and as for the ending? Remember how people hated Mass Effect 3 for its RGB ending? Yeah. Well Beth didn't learn anything from that.
Mod's cant really fix the issues with the main game, and its impossible to tell what DLC will bring. But for a game I was so excited about to start with i came out of it frustrated and with a foul taste in my mouth.

I have been a fan of the Fallout series since Fallout 3. In comparison to the previous installments, i can tell you that Fallout 4 is certainly a improvement on the series. Fallout 4 doesn't take much away from previous games, but instead improves some faulty concepts and adds quite a few new ones. Here goes the Review.
I picked up Fallout 4 the first week of it's release, and i couldn't be more pleased with spending 60$. Each and every bethesda game, can easily be valued at that price tag. I haven't beaten Fallout 4 yet, but i feel i have enough experience to review this game with an honest opinion.
The story of this game, without spoiling anything for viewers, is your generic fallout story. I'm not going to say the story is amazing because in my opinion, it's really not. It's good at best. Bethesda games have always revolved more around Open World Interaction and the option for free exploration. Fallout 4 does a fantastic job, in once again giving us a vast open world to explore when we want and at the pace that we want. You can tell that there has been an update to the graphical quality as well which is only a positive trait. The game has also introduced several new features in which i will go into brief detail about in the next paragraph.
New Features:
Settlements- Probably the most significant feature that bethesda has added for us to tinker with, is the option to rebuild the capital wasteland as we explore it and progress with the main story. We can now establish several settlements that will attract settlers to migrate there. This is a brilliantly executed system and well thought out idea. Not only can we create entire towns, but we can fully customize them as well. There are some things i wish they would improve on with this system, but i feel future mods will add just that.
Customizing Power Armor- You can now collect several sets of power armor and actually mix the parts together to create your own set from scratch. To add even more complexity to this system, you can even add different layers of paint and improve the defensive values of these power armors. This is done through scrapping resources and using Power Armor Stations.
New Factions- Several new factions have been added to the game with the return of the popular Brotherhood of Steel. The institue, Railroad, and Minutemen are all newly introducted factions for you to experiment with. Each faction, has different views that will conflict with eachother, causing war throughout the wasteland (Like the previous installments).
There are many other New features that i will not go into detail on for the sake of this review. The point is, Bethesda has added a large chunk of content for us with these new concepts. This game is beautiful to say the least. I look forward to the rest of my time with this game.

This game is a great game. I want to make that perfectly clear before I digress. This game is great, but it feels very different from previous Fallouts. In my opinion this game gives you an extremely personal feel through it's vibrant story telling and dull world, along with its characters.
Almost immediately you are thrown into a situation that makes Fallout: New Vegas's story look fairly light. You aren't some random guy who can do whatever anymore, you have to find your son, then make moral choices for all of humanity. The RPG elements from the game are heavily supressed now by limited dialogue, set character backgrounds, and a semi-linear story. Most of the factions are too... good. They all essentially are good but with different views on how life should be in the wastes. I personally don't like the fact that you can't be evil anymore, as I enjoyed playing "Cowboy Hotline Miami" back in New Vegas.
The map is significantly more post apocalyptic, but trades in nearly all of Fallout's old americana vibes for this. The largest city in the game is very small, and it truly feels like a refuge, but not in a good way in my opinion. It's design is effectively centered around it's few central buildings (all of which are practically glorified shacks) with all of the rest being useless. I never really felt this way about New Vegas, as it was filled with well made and large casinos, bars, and MEANINGFUL locations. The entire world really doesn't take advantage of Boston as much as it should, and where New Vegas had whole towns built around actual roadside attractions (see Buffalo Bills), Fo4 has locations that you will likely not care about or remember.
The settlement building is well done for what it is. It is simplistic and easy enough. It makes you feel pressed for resources sometimes when you know that you will be attacked without those last few defense points. On the flip side, it's pointless and you will never be attacked in any meaningful way.
The companion reputation system is nearly as well made as in previous games with the important exception that commanding your wasteland pal no longer freezes time. And you may have noticed VATS also traded in its signature time freeze for a slo-mo as well.
All in all this installation in the Fallout series is pretty meh, and more personal than ever (which is either good or bad depending on your preference).
I say 75/100, but never the less... war never changes.

I've never played any games in the Fallout franchise before this one, but with all the hype surrounding it I decided I had to check it out. After basically putting my life on hold for over a week to fully immerse myself in the game, I can honestly say I'm glad I did. That said, I will be reviewing this game as a newcomer to the series and not somebody who had any pre-existing notions of what the game "should" be like.
Fallout 4 is a unique game in some ways. It has a lot of flaws that would get other games ripped apart. However, the overall experience is so good that it somehow manages to get a pass on all that negative stuff. During my time playing, I experienced my share of bugs and glitches, but it didn't ruin the fun. The game ran well enough on my rig, but it could've been better. The graphics are also a bit underwhelming for a game released in 2015, but it didn't seem to matter when I was busy admiring the ambience of the vast wasteland.
Where the game shines is the feeling of immersion in the post apocalyptic playground that is its setting. It is massively fun to run around building settlements, trying out different weapons, shooting raiders and ghouls, and meeting all of the interesting characters and factions. I've played many open world games in my time and this ranks pretty high on the list of how the genre should be done. There is so much to see and do that I feel I could continue playing this game for a long time to come if I wanted.
I really enjoyed the story as well. It's not the best one I've ever experienced in a video game, but it managed to hold my interest to the very end. It starts out with the player witnessing the beginning of a nuclear war and finding safety in an underground vault where they are frozen for two hundred years along with their family. During this time, the player's newborn child is kidnapped and their spouse is killed. The player wakes up sometime later and ventures out of the vault determined to find their child. The world is then revealed to have become a post apocalyptic wasteland with many different groups and mutated creatures roaming its ruins.
The game is full of choices. From the very beginning, it is possible to customize the main character. There are different options for how to respond during a converstion and various companions that can come along with the player for their adventures. Settlements and dwellings can be customized with everything from furniture to defensive weapons. But the biggest choices have to do with the main story missions and will determine how the ending plays out. The protagonist will be forced to side with a certain group and this will have major implications on the other factions in the world. This gives the game a lot of replayablility and I'm curious to see what the missions would be like if I had sided with someone else.
Some people might complain that a "true RPG" wouldn't give the main character such an extensive backstory, but I feel it's perfectly fine considering other franchises that have done it, such as Final Fantasy, The Witcher, etc. That's just my opinion though.
I'm not a huge fan of the combat gameplay, but I've heard it's actually an improvement over previous games in the series. This game is an RPG and it defintiely feels like it when shooting bad guys. I actually love RPG's, but there were times when I was frustrated by how hard it was to take down certain enemies due to the fact my level wasn't high enough or my weapons were too weak. This is not the type of thing I would normally be bothered by, but it felt somewhat strange in a game that seemed like it was meant to be a shooter. The V.A.T.S. system can also get a bit old after a while, but I still liked using it.
In the end, I feel this game's shortcomings are vastly overshadowed by all of its positive aspects. I absoutely loved the time I spent playing it and it captured my imagination in a way few other games have done in a long time. I would highly recommend it to anyone and feel it is money well spent.

114 hours at the time of writing this review, I think it's time. Brace youreslf, because I'm going to type up quite the lengthy review.
Fallout 4 has been a game I have anticipated since the day I finished Fallout 3, 8 years ago. And it's failed to disappiont. There is so much "beef" to this game, that you just can't stay focused on one thing for more than a few minutes before you stumble across an empty vault, or some historic monument, lost to the nuclear fallout that was the Great War. That being said, Fallout 4 does have a  few things I'm not a huge fan of, so let's break this down to The Good, and The Bad.
THE GOOD:
This game has so much to offer in terms of things to do. It presents a challenge right from the get go, but not enough so, that it's frustrating or annoying. Many reviews you will read say that the game makes it "too easy" because they give you access to a full suit of power armor in the first 20 minutes of the game. Allow me to clear the air. It's junk. The suit you are given at the beginning of the game is nothing more than a fancy looking outfit thats made of cardboard. So, don't let that fool you. Wearing that power armor has it's benefits, but it's well balanced in the long run, but I digress. The story is compelling, but with as much content to explore in this game, I found myself 80 hours in, and I had barely scratched the surface of it. One of my favorite new features is the weapon and armor mod system. It not only allows you to create some killer modifications to your equipment, but it gives an alternate sense of "purpose" you can mark items to search for, and scavenge buildings in downtown Boston. "Oh look a globe, and I need screws" or "10 pack of Duct Tape?! Hell yea!" (Trust me, that will be your reaction) But it's more than thar. It makes the Wasteland fell more... useful. They made this system around the basis of "every bit of junk can be used for SOMETHING" and I think they did a phenominal job. Now you can make any "weak" weapon, something to be feared in the Commonwealth. Another new feature I enjoyed (that many people didn't, for some reason) was the voiced protagonist. This was a bold move for Bethesda, and although it COULD be better, it did add a sort of "depth" to your character that previous games did not have. Some of the voice acting is a little dry, but it's not enough to taint my enjoyment of the game.
THE BAD:
Not that I want to type anything here, but there are definitely things that could've been better. One for instance are "radiant quests". The point of these is to always have something to do in the game that will reward you in caps and XP. However, with a game as large as Fallout 4, your room to work with is slim, so I find myself doing many of the same quests, just with slight altercations like, whether or not I'm fighting ghouls, raiders, or super mutant, or location. When it boils down to it, its usually, go here, kill these people, and talk to so and so. Radiant quests would have been MUCH more entertaining, if there was more variety to the objectives. Also, the ending of the story (don't worrry, I promise not to spoil anything). The story was absolutely fantastic..... right up to the end. It just kind of stops, and it's a little disappointing. The cinematics that play at the end are all fairly similar too, no matter which (of the 3 or 4) routes you take. Which leads me to my next point, choices. In terms of story, you're fairly limited compared to say, Fallout New Vegas. You can side with one of about four factions to complete the story, but they make it fairly difficult to help two factions with say, similar beleifs, who may normally work together. Now, I compared it to New Vegas, ONLY because NV had a TON of options when it came to the ending of the game. That being said, I beleive New Vegas was a bit too amitious which led to many of the crashes, freezes, and extreme;y annoying bugs, that I and tons of other people encountered. But, of the two paths I've taken thus far, the individual stories (though they are fairly similar) are very well done, again, with the exception of the ending. There are a few "game-breaking" bugs in Fallout 4, but I've really not had trouble with them... yet. Lastly in this category, is the dialogue. I know I did include it in the previous section, but it has one downside... you only ever have 4 options. Yes, No, Sarcastic, and More information. Now, I do understand that with voiced protagonists it leads to having a less colorful pallet of dialogue options, but it just gets to be a drag, always selecting the same option. On top of that, it doesn't tell you word for word, what your character is going to say, it sums it up in 1-3 words (there is a mod out right now that fixes that issue). Also with the 4 option dialogue tree, it gets rid of the skill  or perk based chat options, making it difficult to flesh out your character and really make them one of a kind.
All in all I think that Bethesda did a great job with this game. 114.2 hours in and I've hardly discovered the thinsgs that are available to do, because I keep getting sidetracked by small side quests, or interesting places to explore. You will find no shortage of things to do in this game, and I strongly recommend picking up Fallout 4. Tons of fun for literally, hundreds of hours. I give it a 9.5/10. Great game. Thanks for reading, and I hope this helped you in your decision!

Fallout has never looked so beatiful and lush. I'm glad they don't call it the Wasteland in this game, it looks nothing like a wasteland. The Commonwealth is a much more suitale name because of the vegetation, the colorful enviroments, and memorable landmarks. Enemies lurk at every corner, and treasures in others. Weapons and armour are in a variety, the enemies are tough to battle, and you're constantly on edge. The combat mechanics have improved since New Vegas, so shooting guns have more fluidity and using melee weapons are fluid as well. The new scavengiung window keeps movement constant. Instead of activating a box, stopping the game, and opening a window displaying the contants inside, it instead keeps the game going, and opens up a smaller window on the right side of the screen, in which you use the mousewhell to navigate and highlight items, and the left mouse button to select and store your desired item. Both of these improvements keep the gameplay in constant motion, and prevent any loss of immersion, but if you prefer the classic scavenging setting, it is also available. The musical scores in this game certainly go a great job sewing this game together as well.
This game is certainly worth $59.99. Hours of content, replayability, plenty of things to do and experiement with, and you're constantly interested and engulfed in the game.
However, this game does have it's down falls. When you're new to the game, you'll have trouble learning some of the new mechanics due to a not so solid tutorials on certain subjects. Like build mode, crafting mode, modding mode, and the new layout of the "perk" screen. Some of these tutorials are taught through quests, which are optional to do, but because they are optional to do, they may slip past your nose until you're far into the game. For me, this tutorial problem is minor, but brought me frustration when I first bought the game. Thankfully, there's an informational directory in the pause menu.
Second, this game is buggy, and not just traditionally Bethesda buggy, but this is the buggiest Bethesda game I've ever played. Physics bugs are more often than in FO3 or FO:NV, the game will crash somewhat often, and loading screens won't load. Matter of fact, right before I wrote this review, I was playing Fallout 4 and had stopped playing because the loading screen would not go away. However, personally, these bugs do not deter me from enjoying the game. It may actually be a good thing the game crashes sometimes to remind me to get some fresh air for a bit. Just as long as my save data isn't ruined, right?

I have been a fan of the Fallout series since Fallout 3. In comparison to the previous installments, i can tell you that Fallout 4 is certainly a improvement on the series. Fallout 4 doesn't take much away from previous games, but instead improves some faulty concepts and adds quite a few new ones. Here goes the Review.
I picked up Fallout 4 the first week of it's release, and i couldn't be more pleased with spending 60$. Each and every bethesda game, can easily be valued at that price tag. I haven't beaten Fallout 4 yet, but i feel i have enough experience to review this game with an honest opinion.
The story of this game, without spoiling anything for viewers, is your generic fallout story. I'm not going to say the story is amazing because in my opinion, it's really not. It's good at best. Bethesda games have always revolved more around Open World Interaction and the option for free exploration. Fallout 4 does a fantastic job, in once again giving us a vast open world to explore when we want and at the pace that we want. You can tell that there has been an update to the graphical quality as well which is only a positive trait. The game has also introduced several new features in which i will go into brief detail about in the next paragraph.
New Features:
Settlements- Probably the most significant feature that bethesda has added for us to tinker with, is the option to rebuild the capital wasteland as we explore it and progress with the main story. We can now establish several settlements that will attract settlers to migrate there. This is a brilliantly executed system and well thought out idea. Not only can we create entire towns, but we can fully customize them as well. There are some things i wish they would improve on with this system, but i feel future mods will add just that.
Customizing Power Armor- You can now collect several sets of power armor and actually mix the parts together to create your own set from scratch. To add even more complexity to this system, you can even add different layers of paint and improve the defensive values of these power armors. This is done through scrapping resources and using Power Armor Stations.
New Factions- Several new factions have been added to the game with the return of the popular Brotherhood of Steel. The institue, Railroad, and Minutemen are all newly introducted factions for you to experiment with. Each faction, has different views that will conflict with eachother, causing war throughout the wasteland (Like the previous installments).
There are many other New features that i will not go into detail on for the sake of this review. The point is, Bethesda has added a large chunk of content for us with these new concepts. This game is beautiful to say the least. I look forward to the rest of my time with this game.

Lotta people seem to hate Fallout 4. I mean, not commercially, but on forums and other collectives of bad opinions on videogames. Here's the skinny. If you like open world games with explorable locations this is pretty much the only place you're going to find them. The action-RPG genre has been really lacking lately. The only game that comes close is the Witcher series and I have had enough Geralt for the rest of my life, I think.
Gameplay is why you're here and it's very satisfying. The shooty guns are very good, the locations are very nice and tell good visual stories, and the perk system is very much refined. The new crafting system gives you a reason to loot random crap in the wasteland but manages to do it in a way that's not burdensome - it's very easy to remember what you're looking for.
That being said, the story leaves something to be desired. Dialogue options usually boil down to 'sure', 'yes', 'maybe', and 'lol i guess'. The 'open world' part of the game doesn't extend to the characters. Everything is very much on rails here. The addition of the fully voiced protagonist was nice but leads to very 'boxed in' dialogue options that sometimes rip you out of your immersion. For instance, Victoria, savior-detective of the Commonwealth, has no interest in any of the three major factions in the game. For her the only option is to just straight up ignore all three. Ignoring content isn't really an option Bethesda; we learned that from all those Fable games where moral choices boiled down to 'do quest' or 'walk away and don't do quest'. Why can't I undermine more than one faction without obliterating them? Why can't I pick a fourth option that opposes all three? Why do I care so much about my baby?
Some of Bethesda's world famous bugs are here too. I haven't experienced any crashes, but disappearing (or appearing) NPCs, monsters stuck in their stock poses, stuff like that. One time I talked to an NPC that I clearly wasn't 'supposed' to be talking to; my dialogue options all included information my character definatley hadn't acquired. Because I hadn't looked up any spoilers I was super confused. That kind of thing happens kinda frequently if you poke your nose around a lot.
It's a good game - possibly even a great game - that is only held back by its writing and inattention to characters. Which is a shame because this could have been one of the best games ever made if they'd just payed a little more attention to the story. It wouldn't be a big deal if this was Morrowind or even FO3, but story gets a little thin on the ground once you leave out the main quest and the three main factions. Still, you should play it - this is one of those games everyone will have an opinion on.

Fallout has never looked so beatiful and lush. I'm glad they don't call it the Wasteland in this game, it looks nothing like a wasteland. The Commonwealth is a much more suitale name because of the vegetation, the colorful enviroments, and memorable landmarks. Enemies lurk at every corner, and treasures in others. Weapons and armour are in a variety, the enemies are tough to battle, and you're constantly on edge. The combat mechanics have improved since New Vegas, so shooting guns have more fluidity and using melee weapons are fluid as well. The new scavengiung window keeps movement constant. Instead of activating a box, stopping the game, and opening a window displaying the contants inside, it instead keeps the game going, and opens up a smaller window on the right side of the screen, in which you use the mousewhell to navigate and highlight items, and the left mouse button to select and store your desired item. Both of these improvements keep the gameplay in constant motion, and prevent any loss of immersion, but if you prefer the classic scavenging setting, it is also available. The musical scores in this game certainly go a great job sewing this game together as well.
This game is certainly worth $59.99. Hours of content, replayability, plenty of things to do and experiement with, and you're constantly interested and engulfed in the game.
However, this game does have it's down falls. When you're new to the game, you'll have trouble learning some of the new mechanics due to a not so solid tutorials on certain subjects. Like build mode, crafting mode, modding mode, and the new layout of the "perk" screen. Some of these tutorials are taught through quests, which are optional to do, but because they are optional to do, they may slip past your nose until you're far into the game. For me, this tutorial problem is minor, but brought me frustration when I first bought the game. Thankfully, there's an informational directory in the pause menu.
Second, this game is buggy, and not just traditionally Bethesda buggy, but this is the buggiest Bethesda game I've ever played. Physics bugs are more often than in FO3 or FO:NV, the game will crash somewhat often, and loading screens won't load. Matter of fact, right before I wrote this review, I was playing Fallout 4 and had stopped playing because the loading screen would not go away. However, personally, these bugs do not deter me from enjoying the game. It may actually be a good thing the game crashes sometimes to remind me to get some fresh air for a bit. Just as long as my save data isn't ruined, right?

Thanks for reading, and good luck in the Commonwealth.

I don't like to write reviews but I think I have to. If you step out - the game is good, but it's not Fallout - it's Farcry in future. At first it's fun to gather resources, explore new settlements, build in them and all that. But later you more and more think "What the hell!!!":
1. Settlers complain about raiders. You agree to help and see that raiders come from the other side of map. Raiders have 7 settlements nearby, but decide to raid one far away. Not to say there are raiders den nearby theat would raid themself and fight foreigners... In logic but not the fact. Well... Possible, but very strange.
2. You clear out raiders, report, travel a bit and bump! You have to clear the same location again. Because raiders (or mutants) respawned and raid again. What the hell you think and start to search the mod to decrease respawn time.
3. Settlers complain about hostage taken in location you've just cleared. Maybe you have to fight someone there again or just go there and release hostage while no one at all present.
4. By that time you are also tired of selling weapon/armour/aid to buy junk to be able to build some turrets or upgrade your weapon/armour. You have 20k caps but can't get enough junk to build.
5. You have several power armours and you don't know what for. You upgrade and use one. Power core is not a problem (with built traders and money earned). You are almost invincible in it even on survival difficulty... until bloatflies come in. You think - I'm in a 100500mm thick armour - how can they poison me? Even radiation can't come through! But they have super armour-penetrating stings and you die in a few shots.
6. You go over same locations again and again to protect, rescue, kill raiders and collect resources.
7. And yeah - you travel alone. Because companions are more a headacke than a help.
8. Leveling system is also strange. You can become master lockpick with 4 Per, but have to wait "levels". And you can't even try to pick lock of higher level than your mastery. Skyrim was much better in this.
9. Dialogs are... You can choose yes, no (any reason to choose no?) and sometimes "demand more money".
10. Building in you settlements is also "strange". You can build ladder-ladder-ladder-enourmous room with generator and lot's of sleepbags and your settlement will behave the same as if you pay attention to walls, doors and other decorations.
11. Story... Well it starts pretty interesting but after a full start it's rather dull. Withcher 3 has story for almost every side quest, while Fallout 4 has almost story for main quest.
12. So yes Fallout 4 is more like Farcry 3 (Or MMO without multiplayer)- you secure the same locations over and over, you collect resources to build unneccessary things and can rob everything with no need.
Be careful you will get addicted to this game.

在老滚5结束之后，大家都万分期待辐射4的日子里，B社突然搞出来个上古OL，我们很担心是否会影响辐射4的开发进度，但是知道了上古OL是另外一个团队来做的就放心了。

It's hard to nail down how exactly I feel about Fallout 4. On one hand, the combat and looting systems have been vastly improved and the crafting is pretty satisfying. However, I never felt truly immersed in the game world. When I look at it as a whole, it looks great. Multiple factions vying for control of the Commonwealth, kidnapped son yadda yadda, neat lore and notes spread about to take in at your leisure, setting up towns to bring back civilization, etc. But while I was playing the game, I didn't feel as if the world reacted to me or even took my actions into consideration. I felt like, for the most part, I was mearly putting my character through the motions of his pre-determined journey with fairly obvious splitting paths along the way. No one would react to anything I did besides shooting them. I don't know, this game was weird for me. I enjoy the improvements over previous iterations, but the story really wasn't as fulfilling as I expected it to be based on my past Bethesda experiences. I've experienced one ending and really don't feel the desire to touch the game ever again. If you enjoy Bethesda games, wait for a sale or don't - just know that there's no need to rush in and play this one at this point in time.

It's a fun game.  It just isn't a fallout game.  If you are interested in continuity and progression of the series, you'll likely be disappointed.  If you are just looking for a fun diversion, this is a fun diversion.
To expand on the former, there are just simply too many elements that made fallout what it was that were either nerfed beyond recognition, removed entirely, or ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ized from cannon to make this an actual fallout game.  For example, leveling up in this game feels EXTREMELY shallow.  It really just feels like a smokescreen to allow you access to better guns to level with the enemies.  While there are perks that do similar stuff to previous fallout games, the omission of skills is painfully obvious as the perks are supposed to supplement skills, not replace them.  Since they've been replaced, perks feel hollow and rote.
There are also pretty glaring continuity errors from the lore of the fallout world.  An example being Jet.  Jet was pretty well explained in fallout 2, and there's no question that it was developed post-apocalypse, however this game basically comes right out and says no it wasn't.  Which makes a big part of the plot of fallout 2 at best, discontinuous.
New mechanics with weapon mods and the power armour have interesting touches, but they do feel a bit unrealized.  Modding your power armor with custom paintjobs and perks is awesome, but the need to have fusion cores seems a bit silly.  I get that they didn't want the armor to make you too powerful too quickly, but there were probably better ways to accomplish this.
The gameplay itself is quite good.  Some people have complained about the container system being an overlay rather than a game-pausing event as it was previously.  Personally, I think the newer system is much cleaner and more immersive.  Trying to loot a corpse in the middle of a gunfight is now a bad idea (as it should be).    The enemy AI is also much better than it has been in previous fallout games making it much more fun tactically.
The settlements idea is an interesting add on.  Unfortunately, even though there are lots of "pieces" to play with, I dont' feel like my settlements are as I want them and the tools to actually build/assign are very lacking.  Even if everything was perfectly manageable in this regard, it would still feel like there's not much to do besides play dolly dress up with them and defend the occasional raid.  It would be nice to have more influence on the day to day operations or allow expansion etc.
Overall the game is fun.  It's a good, solid, entertaining diversion.  It's just fundamentally not what I think of when I think of a fallout game.

114 hours at the time of writing this review, I think it's time. Brace youreslf, because I'm going to type up quite the lengthy review.
Fallout 4 has been a game I have anticipated since the day I finished Fallout 3, 8 years ago. And it's failed to disappiont. There is so much "beef" to this game, that you just can't stay focused on one thing for more than a few minutes before you stumble across an empty vault, or some historic monument, lost to the nuclear fallout that was the Great War. That being said, Fallout 4 does have a  few things I'm not a huge fan of, so let's break this down to The Good, and The Bad.
THE GOOD:
This game has so much to offer in terms of things to do. It presents a challenge right from the get go, but not enough so, that it's frustrating or annoying. Many reviews you will read say that the game makes it "too easy" because they give you access to a full suit of power armor in the first 20 minutes of the game. Allow me to clear the air. It's junk. The suit you are given at the beginning of the game is nothing more than a fancy looking outfit thats made of cardboard. So, don't let that fool you. Wearing that power armor has it's benefits, but it's well balanced in the long run, but I digress. The story is compelling, but with as much content to explore in this game, I found myself 80 hours in, and I had barely scratched the surface of it. One of my favorite new features is the weapon and armor mod system. It not only allows you to create some killer modifications to your equipment, but it gives an alternate sense of "purpose" you can mark items to search for, and scavenge buildings in downtown Boston. "Oh look a globe, and I need screws" or "10 pack of Duct Tape?! Hell yea!" (Trust me, that will be your reaction) But it's more than thar. It makes the Wasteland fell more... useful. They made this system around the basis of "every bit of junk can be used for SOMETHING" and I think they did a phenominal job. Now you can make any "weak" weapon, something to be feared in the Commonwealth. Another new feature I enjoyed (that many people didn't, for some reason) was the voiced protagonist. This was a bold move for Bethesda, and although it COULD be better, it did add a sort of "depth" to your character that previous games did not have. Some of the voice acting is a little dry, but it's not enough to taint my enjoyment of the game.
THE BAD:
Not that I want to type anything here, but there are definitely things that could've been better. One for instance are "radiant quests". The point of these is to always have something to do in the game that will reward you in caps and XP. However, with a game as large as Fallout 4, your room to work with is slim, so I find myself doing many of the same quests, just with slight altercations like, whether or not I'm fighting ghouls, raiders, or super mutant, or location. When it boils down to it, its usually, go here, kill these people, and talk to so and so. Radiant quests would have been MUCH more entertaining, if there was more variety to the objectives. Also, the ending of the story (don't worrry, I promise not to spoil anything). The story was absolutely fantastic..... right up to the end. It just kind of stops, and it's a little disappointing. The cinematics that play at the end are all fairly similar too, no matter which (of the 3 or 4) routes you take. Which leads me to my next point, choices. In terms of story, you're fairly limited compared to say, Fallout New Vegas. You can side with one of about four factions to complete the story, but they make it fairly difficult to help two factions with say, similar beleifs, who may normally work together. Now, I compared it to New Vegas, ONLY because NV had a TON of options when it came to the ending of the game. That being said, I beleive New Vegas was a bit too amitious which led to many of the crashes, freezes, and extreme;y annoying bugs, that I and tons of other people encountered. But, of the two paths I've taken thus far, the individual stories (though they are fairly similar) are very well done, again, with the exception of the ending. There are a few "game-breaking" bugs in Fallout 4, but I've really not had trouble with them... yet. Lastly in this category, is the dialogue. I know I did include it in the previous section, but it has one downside... you only ever have 4 options. Yes, No, Sarcastic, and More information. Now, I do understand that with voiced protagonists it leads to having a less colorful pallet of dialogue options, but it just gets to be a drag, always selecting the same option. On top of that, it doesn't tell you word for word, what your character is going to say, it sums it up in 1-3 words (there is a mod out right now that fixes that issue). Also with the 4 option dialogue tree, it gets rid of the skill  or perk based chat options, making it difficult to flesh out your character and really make them one of a kind.
All in all I think that Bethesda did a great job with this game. 114.2 hours in and I've hardly discovered the thinsgs that are available to do, because I keep getting sidetracked by small side quests, or interesting places to explore. You will find no shortage of things to do in this game, and I strongly recommend picking up Fallout 4. Tons of fun for literally, hundreds of hours. I give it a 9.5/10. Great game. Thanks for reading, and I hope this helped you in your decision!

text:
I am a huge fan of the Fallout series, and unlike some who claim to be, i am able to love this game for what it is. Because what it is is worth loving.
First, let's get the bad out of the way. The new dialogue system. Don't get me wrong, I admire Bethesda trying new things with their games, but this doesn't work. Different skill checks and SPECIAL stats are brought down to just a colour-coded Charisma check. Not once does your Intelligence or your Luck matter in dialogue, neither does your Science! or Medic skill. You're forced to play a character rather than define one and while Bethesda and both male and female voice actors do a good job, the system just doesn't work and it isn't Fallout.
Also, the bugs, which I personally haven't encountered that many of. The most annoying one I encountered was the TAB button not working (and it's kind of important because, you know, pip-boy). However, in my 71 hours of play the game has only crashed once, which is incredible progress compared to, say, New Vegas.
And now for the good.
Combat is easily the most noticeable and welcome improvement to the Fallout series in this installment. New Vegas made subtle improvements over FO3 by including things like ADS and expanding weapon types and ammo systems, but at its core it was still the same clunky system. Fallout 4's combat is slick, smooth, and a real joy to play through. Everything about it is beautifully put together, from the cash register sound effect whenever you kill an enemy to the improved and (at least in my experience) cinematic VATS moments. Changes like the addition of sprinting and VATS slowing down time instead of just pausing it also improve the experience, and a character is easily buildable around different playstyles (melee + lots of chems is my personal favourite).
The world of Fallout looks better than it ever has before. The colour palette is much more vibrant, compared to FO3's monotonous grey and New Vegas' reliance on orange. The art style is also much more noticeably focused and stylised, and it works to the game's credit as it is a good art style that fits the tone of the game. And although the graphics sure aren't Star Wars Battlefront (2015) level, they do look good and there were a few moments where i found myself in awe, realising that what i was seeing was not only as beautiful as it was, but BEAUTIFUL IN A FALLOUT GAME.
The addition of the Settlement system is nice. Sure the tutorial could've been a lot better and the controls can be clunky, but once you get past that you're left with a really nice system that you can spend as long as you want on. There's no crutch forcing you to extremely deck out every settlement, and you only need to build objects for faction missions twice, and you're given resources to do this with on both occasions. My only complaint is that in the end, the system does feel kind of pointless. I feel like full-scale assaults on your settlements instead of just a group of 5 or so raiders or super mutants would have made it much better, but it's still a good addition as it stands. + Bobblehead Stand.
The crafting in this game is just incredible. The thing that always stopped me from getting into the crafting in 3 and NV was the UI, as well as the lack of any real introduction to it. While Fallout 4's crafting doesnt have much of an introduction, the UI is greatly improved over the previous games, as is the crafting as a whole. There's very rarely a better feeling than when you finally build that rare weapon mod you've been saving up your resources for, or when you turn a default boring gun into a badass upgraded powerhouse. Fallout 4's crafting is truly innovative and brilliant, "it just works".
The design of the world is also great. It's much larger than FO3 and NV and is filled with many more locations and secrets. This isn't really something I can describe much, as it's more of a thing you learn to appreciate when you experience it, but the world design is greatly improved over 3 (and especially NV, weakest aspect of that game) and will leave you obsessively wandering the Commonwealth for hours. "Just one more location" you'll most likely keep telling yourself.
A lot of people have a problem with the removal of the skill system, and at first I did too, but the new 'perk chart' eventually won me over. The interface itself for the system is great; the little animations for the Vault Boys, as well as their sound effects, are brilliant little tidbits. And most of the perks act as replacement for skills, but in a way, force you to be more selective due to you only getting 1 perk point per level, and there were a few situations where I genuinely spent 5+ minutes thinking about where I wanted my character to focus on.
The story, while not perfect, delivers what is in my op.inion Bethesda's best writing since Morrowind (i'm not saying it's AS GOOD as Morrowind's though). The factions are MUCH better than Fallout 3's, because it's much harder to chose between them and they are all coated in shades of grey - none of them are 'evil' but they all have their own ideals and methods, and each of them have their own positive and negative points. One thing i HATED about the story, however, is the endings, or rather lack there of. 3 of the 4 endings are basically exactly the same and unlike NV there is no ending narration about how the wasteland changes based on your choices, which is extremely disappointing. But other than that, the story is actually well presented, and all of the companions you can find in the game feel like real, interesting people and you feel like you really are forming relationships with them as your approval increases with all of them.
Okay...i think that's everything. In conclusion, or for those of you who just skimmed/skipped the rest of the review, I do love this game. Is it perfect? No. Bethesda try new things with this game, some of them work and some of them really, really don't. But the game is a huge improvement over Fallout 3 and even better than New Vegas in some aspects. This game is truly great, and I recommend you get it it and form your own opinion of it instead of being deterred by those who are♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥off by its changes (who are a minority).

Fallout 4 is defintely a Bethesda Fallout Game. I am throroughly enjoying my play time right now. I played New Vegas with DLC 3 times, each time at least 70 hours. I'm still playing my first play thru, already 60 hours in. FO4's qualties greatly outweighs its faults. I would recommend this game highly. Here are my gripes and likes.
Gripes:
-Not as many silly moments as New Vegas in regards to dialogue or quests but it still has it's moment.
-Disappointed that there wasn't a low intellienge dialogue branch.
-Lack of hardcore difficuty option, i.e. sleep, food, thirst mangement. Repairing isn't in the normal game but I feel it could have its place in a hardcore difficulty.
-Lack of karma, I wish there was a sophisticated karma system. FO3/NV karma wasn't all that special or sophisticated but it added a something to the role playing.
Likes:
-Streamlined perk/skill system, I feel there are no worthless perks. Getting 10-15 skills points every level or a perk every 2 levels in FO3/NV never felt as special as getting a single perk point in FO4. It never sat well with me that I could have 100 speech with 1 charisma or rockets doing no damage with 1 explosive skill. Intimidation in NV was fun for the few moments that you use it as a dialgoue option but it was otherwise useless in NV.
-Power Armour. FO3/NV it was just another set of endgame clothing. I love that in FO4, you feel like tank in your armour and using it, is completely optional.  I had no issues with getting the power armour early since you had modding options. Power armour although abundant actually feels special and different from your normal gear.
-Crafting and Junk. Junk isn't junk anymore, everything has a use. I like that they removed the repair system from the normal game, it got tedious in FO3/NV.
-Combat. Feels like the natural progession from FO3/NV. It's smooth and flow very well. Gun shooting feels like a FPS. Melee was rewarding when I dodge, block, and time my swings correctly to take a group of enemies. VATS transistion so smooth. Action points doesn't just affect VATS.
-Settlements. I didn't spend too much time building settlement since it's optional but I'm glad that I have that option for some creative outlet for later play thrus. Having high charisma is actually useful, allowing settlements to provide vendors and combat support.
-Locations. Every area and building, looks and feel unique. Boston doesn't look bland at all.
-UI. Having played NV so much, it was an easy transistion. Mostly I didn't find myself constantly reorganizing my inventory everytime I accidently press E one too many times and taking all the items from a container.
Fallout 4 feels like the natural successor to FO3/NV. Despite the bland dialogue, combat is fun, crafting junk is worth, and power armour is actually special. I see myself playing Fallout 4 for many hundreds of hours more.
