I don't like to write reviews but I think I have to. If you step out - the game is good, but it's not Fallout - it's Farcry in future. At first it's fun to gather resources, explore new settlements, build in them and all that. But later you more and more think "What the hell!!!":
1. Settlers complain about raiders. You agree to help and see that raiders come from the other side of map. Raiders have 7 settlements nearby, but decide to raid one far away. Not to say there are raiders den nearby theat would raid themself and fight foreigners... In logic but not the fact. Well... Possible, but very strange.
2. You clear out raiders, report, travel a bit and bump! You have to clear the same location again. Because raiders (or mutants) respawned and raid again. What the hell you think and start to search the mod to decrease respawn time.
3. Settlers complain about hostage taken in location you've just cleared. Maybe you have to fight someone there again or just go there and release hostage while no one at all present.
4. By that time you are also tired of selling weapon/armour/aid to buy junk to be able to build some turrets or upgrade your weapon/armour. You have 20k caps but can't get enough junk to build.
5. You have several power armours and you don't know what for. You upgrade and use one. Power core is not a problem (with built traders and money earned). You are almost invincible in it even on survival difficulty... until bloatflies come in. You think - I'm in a 100500mm thick armour - how can they poison me? Even radiation can't come through! But they have super armour-penetrating stings and you die in a few shots.
6. You go over same locations again and again to protect, rescue, kill raiders and collect resources.
7. And yeah - you travel alone. Because companions are more a headacke than a help.
8. Leveling system is also strange. You can become master lockpick with 4 Per, but have to wait "levels". And you can't even try to pick lock of higher level than your mastery. Skyrim was much better in this.
9. Dialogs are... You can choose yes, no (any reason to choose no?) and sometimes "demand more money".
10. Building in you settlements is also "strange". You can build ladder-ladder-ladder-enourmous room with generator and lot's of sleepbags and your settlement will behave the same as if you pay attention to walls, doors and other decorations.
11. Story... Well it starts pretty interesting but after a full start it's rather dull. Withcher 3 has story for almost every side quest, while Fallout 4 has almost story for main quest.
12. So yes Fallout 4 is more like Farcry 3 (Or MMO without multiplayer)- you secure the same locations over and over, you collect resources to build unneccessary things and can rob everything with no need.
Be careful you will get addicted to this game.

It's a fun game.  It just isn't a fallout game.  If you are interested in continuity and progression of the series, you'll likely be disappointed.  If you are just looking for a fun diversion, this is a fun diversion.
To expand on the former, there are just simply too many elements that made fallout what it was that were either nerfed beyond recognition, removed entirely, or ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ized from cannon to make this an actual fallout game.  For example, leveling up in this game feels EXTREMELY shallow.  It really just feels like a smokescreen to allow you access to better guns to level with the enemies.  While there are perks that do similar stuff to previous fallout games, the omission of skills is painfully obvious as the perks are supposed to supplement skills, not replace them.  Since they've been replaced, perks feel hollow and rote.
There are also pretty glaring continuity errors from the lore of the fallout world.  An example being Jet.  Jet was pretty well explained in fallout 2, and there's no question that it was developed post-apocalypse, however this game basically comes right out and says no it wasn't.  Which makes a big part of the plot of fallout 2 at best, discontinuous.
New mechanics with weapon mods and the power armour have interesting touches, but they do feel a bit unrealized.  Modding your power armor with custom paintjobs and perks is awesome, but the need to have fusion cores seems a bit silly.  I get that they didn't want the armor to make you too powerful too quickly, but there were probably better ways to accomplish this.
The gameplay itself is quite good.  Some people have complained about the container system being an overlay rather than a game-pausing event as it was previously.  Personally, I think the newer system is much cleaner and more immersive.  Trying to loot a corpse in the middle of a gunfight is now a bad idea (as it should be).    The enemy AI is also much better than it has been in previous fallout games making it much more fun tactically.
The settlements idea is an interesting add on.  Unfortunately, even though there are lots of "pieces" to play with, I dont' feel like my settlements are as I want them and the tools to actually build/assign are very lacking.  Even if everything was perfectly manageable in this regard, it would still feel like there's not much to do besides play dolly dress up with them and defend the occasional raid.  It would be nice to have more influence on the day to day operations or allow expansion etc.
Overall the game is fun.  It's a good, solid, entertaining diversion.  It's just fundamentally not what I think of when I think of a fallout game.

I'm not going to sugarcoat it. While Fallout 4 is a good open world FPS, it falls short for an RPG. Even now I am incapable of deciding what kind of RPG Fallout 4 wants to be. For now, I can't really recommend this until the issues are sorted out.
But before I'm going to dive into what's not so good about the game, I'd like to take a moment to appreciate what I thought was good of Fallout 4.
The combat is so much better. Everything feels more fluid than before. While there's still something left to be desired of the camera movement, the end result is a combat system that's vastly superior to its predecessors.
On top of that, the new perk system works really well for Fallout 4. In Fallout 3 and New Vegas I often found myself at odds with the leveling system where I deliberately tried not to complete quests or kill anything, just so I could try to get as many skill increasing books / bobbleheads as possible since leveling up meant being forced to spend points.
Then there's also the crafting system, which is amazing if you ask me. So many options to mod your guns in whatever style you desire. And the way they handled power armor in Fallout 4 is great. It actually feels like I'm using powerful gear. Not to mention the fact that you can mod your power armor to give you that edge in battle.
In a way, I also think the voiced protagonist added something to the game. This is more of a personal thing, but I felt it added a little bit of personality. I know many people will disagree with me on this one and that's okay. I just prefer a voiced protagonist over a silent protagonist who communicates with people through telepathy.
Surprisingly, the voice acting is actually good in Fallout 4. The only voice I have anything to say about is Preston Garvey's voice. He just sounds so bland and uninteresting. If they keep this quality up, I don't mind if they have voiced protagonists in the next Fallout. I'd prefer if it went hand in hand with more than one voice for both male and female, the option to change the pitch of their voice and more fleshed out dialogue options. Allows for a bit more roleplaying. Or have an option to ditch the voice altogether.
And unlike Fallout 3 and New Vegas, the world feels much more alive in Fallout 4. There's just more vibrancy in the world around you. It doesn't feel as gloomy as it does in its predecessors, which is certainly nice. And unlike Fallout 3, where it feels like humanity is barely progressing, the Commonwealth does feel like it's going forward. It doesn't feel hopeless. It feels like humanity is actually starting to rebuild.
The companions are actually interesting. While the way you get their approval can be questionable at times, they feel more alive than any other companions they made in previous games. While the companions could've benefitted from more character depth, they're pretty well done as it is.
All in all, if it weren't for those things (or most of those things), I don't think I could've played Fallout 4 for this long. Because for all the things it does right, it also does a bunch of things wrong.
Where the predecessors often allowed a ton of options when it came to dialogue, the answers in Fallout 4 boil down to the following: yes, yes, sarcasm and yes with the occasional investigate option thrown in the middle. The dialogue wheel is way too small, which in turn leads to a shortage of possible things you can say. And those can very well make or break your character, especially when you get questions related to your character's motivations that you just can't give a proper answer to because the answers don't fit at all. It's infuriating because depending on how you try to roleplay your character it can completely shatter your immersion.
It's impossible to say no in this game. When you select no, the game won't care at all about what you said and will still force you to do something. The most jarring example of dialogue not mattering at all is when you're made the leader of the Minutemen. No matter your choice, the game forces the title on you. Why allow us to say no then? You could argue that you can walk away from conversations or just shoot the person you're talking with, but that's hardly a solution. Especially the latter, considering most if not all of the named NPC's are immortal and can't die.
In short, the game just doesn't seem to allow your character to be what you want him or her to be except what falls within the boundaries of the game. Fallout 4 tries to be like Mass Effect and The Witcher by providing a focused and linear story, like a JRPG. That isn't a bad thing. However, at the same time they try to provide the freedom a WRPG offers, causing conflicts in roleplaying opportunities and the like. The end result is a game that puts you on a railroad that has little depth and just doesn't have the story or meaningful choices to back it up and go along with it.
The removal of the old skills system came at a cost: skill checks are pretty much non-existent from what I've seen, aside from the percentage based Charisma checks. Not to mention the removal of traits, which still could've kept their place in Fallout 4.
I also think there could've been more depth to the perk sheet. It could've benefitted from more perks  per tier and more non-combat perks.
Neither are the difficulty options great. Enemies soak up more bullets. That's it. No improved AI, no additional actions or other stuff. Just more health and more damage.
The AI isn't that great either. I came across plenty of issues with settlers and companions. But at least it wasn't too bad. Just frustrating.
And the build mode itself has some issues of its own. While it has potential, more often than not the snapping and collision detection infuriates me because I can't get things the way I want them to. Not to mention certain unremovable objects getting in the way of my builds. And we really need a better way to properly manage our settlers.
While the game does its best to present meaningful factions, it also falls short on others. Most notable are the Minutemen. While I get the idea of the Minutemen being your faction, it just doesn't feel that way. Why am I, the leader of the Minutemen, running around protecting settlements while the other Minutemen do nothing?
On the topic of factions, the removal of the karma system comes with its own set of issues. While the karma system was very easy to abuse, the absence of the karma system leaves a hole that could've easily been filled with a system akin to New Vegas' faction reputation system.
There also seems to be a distinct lack of unique quests in this game. Most, if not all, seem to follow one pattern: go here, kill X, get Y, report back. At least try to make it look interesting with a story or something.
There's also the fact that the game does not give me enough time to get attached to the character's spouse and their child. How can I care when they only have about five minutes screen time tops? And what if I want to roleplay a character who just doesn't care?
The ending also leaves something to be desired. As soon as you confront the leader of the Institute, the game simply does not allow you to ask any of the important questions that you might have, like why the Institute kidnaps people and stuff like that. Why would I buy the leader's speech when I can't even ask the hard questions? And the worst part is, even after all that, after you're done talking with him and you explore the Institute, you still don't get answers to these questions.
All in all, I think it's quite a shame really. Where Fallout 4 took a step forward with combat, it took several steps back in most other departments.
And yet I can't deny that, in the 150 hours that I've played, I enjoyed my time in the wasteland. Even though the RPG aspect of Fallout 4 confuses me in what it wants to be, I do enjoy the FPS aspect of Fallout 4.
Fallout 4 brings many aspects beloved from fallout 3, and makes this sequel one that will be talked about for a long while. Great job Bethesda on shaking things up a bit.

I liked Fallout 3 allot, but I loved Fallout: New Vegas. In New Vegas I could define my own character and my chosen skills and perks were not only fun, but they changed the narrative and game play experience completely. Many of the fan favorite Fallout RPG elements do not exist in Fallout 4 (or were dumb down severally) and those were the things I wanted most from this game. Here are more examples..
-I preferred to read exactly what my character was going to say in my dialogue choices (they try to do the Mass Effect wheel thing and it does not work).
-I liked that the wasteland was….as wasteland (I tried to wonder off constantly and kept running into something a minute later).

-the game is very item based, appealing to people who enjoy building and collecting (that’s fine, but they really milk it to make up for what doesn’t work).
-It did not matter that my character had 1-strength, he could still carry as much crap as he wanted and fire any gun, wear any armor.
-I believed that playing on "survival" (which I thought was the renamed "realism mode" difficulty meant I would be dependent on scavenging the wasteland so I did not starve or die or thirst. It just means that the enemies are extremely accurate and the amount of damage you can take is minimum.

This is still a fun open world game that appeals to a wider audience, but it has left behind so many of my favorite game play elements from the series.  I ended up getting a refund. I got Witcher 3 instead and I am very happy with it.

Fallout 4 is defintely a Bethesda Fallout Game. I am throroughly enjoying my play time right now. I played New Vegas with DLC 3 times, each time at least 70 hours. I'm still playing my first play thru, already 60 hours in. FO4's qualties greatly outweighs its faults. I would recommend this game highly. Here are my gripes and likes.
Gripes:
-Not as many silly moments as New Vegas in regards to dialogue or quests but it still has it's moment.
-Disappointed that there wasn't a low intellienge dialogue branch.
-Lack of hardcore difficuty option, i.e. sleep, food, thirst mangement. Repairing isn't in the normal game but I feel it could have its place in a hardcore difficulty.
-Lack of karma, I wish there was a sophisticated karma system. FO3/NV karma wasn't all that special or sophisticated but it added a something to the role playing.
Likes:
-Streamlined perk/skill system, I feel there are no worthless perks. Getting 10-15 skills points every level or a perk every 2 levels in FO3/NV never felt as special as getting a single perk point in FO4. It never sat well with me that I could have 100 speech with 1 charisma or rockets doing no damage with 1 explosive skill. Intimidation in NV was fun for the few moments that you use it as a dialgoue option but it was otherwise useless in NV.
-Power Armour. FO3/NV it was just another set of endgame clothing. I love that in FO4, you feel like tank in your armour and using it, is completely optional.  I had no issues with getting the power armour early since you had modding options. Power armour although abundant actually feels special and different from your normal gear.
-Crafting and Junk. Junk isn't junk anymore, everything has a use. I like that they removed the repair system from the normal game, it got tedious in FO3/NV.
-Combat. Feels like the natural progession from FO3/NV. It's smooth and flow very well. Gun shooting feels like a FPS. Melee was rewarding when I dodge, block, and time my swings correctly to take a group of enemies. VATS transistion so smooth. Action points doesn't just affect VATS.
-Settlements. I didn't spend too much time building settlement since it's optional but I'm glad that I have that option for some creative outlet for later play thrus. Having high charisma is actually useful, allowing settlements to provide vendors and combat support.
-Locations. Every area and building, looks and feel unique. Boston doesn't look bland at all.
-UI. Having played NV so much, it was an easy transistion. Mostly I didn't find myself constantly reorganizing my inventory everytime I accidently press E one too many times and taking all the items from a container.
Fallout 4 feels like the natural successor to FO3/NV. Despite the bland dialogue, combat is fun, crafting junk is worth, and power armour is actually special. I see myself playing Fallout 4 for many hundreds of hours more.

With Fallout 4 Bethesda has delivered another great addition to the series. We find ourselves back on the West Coast amid the ruins of Boston in the Commonwealth.This time our Vault dweller is a survivor of the bombs dropping  in 2077 , having been kept frozen in Vault 111 for 200 years. And in a reversal of Fallout 3s main story its now the parent looking for the child as your child is kidnapped just before your vault dweller awakes from being frozen.
Good points:
- the map in this game is brilliant with the Commonwealth covering a large area that is densely packed with locations to visit and explore. Its also a lot more colourful with the horrible green and orange filters from the previous games making a welcome departure.
- combat has been improved a lot and now aiming down the sights with your weapon is as viable approach to combat instead of being overly reliant on VATS to score hits (though VATS is still there to use). Grenades and explosives now have their own button for throwing which makes combat a lot more enjoyable.
- one of the big new features in this game is being able to construct your settlements and though the interface is a bit flawed its a lot of fun and can be addictive. Not to mention the random junk you find in the Comonwealth now has a use for construction parts.Its not mandatory and you can completely avoid it if you want but it makes for a fun distraction.
- another new feature is the ability to customize weapon and armour. Again junk is now useful for this too and you get a lot of customization weapons for each type of weapon and armor. Power armour is now a seperate suit that you climb into and is now really powerful with high damage and rad resistancewith the trade off being it requires depleteing fusion cells to power it for use.
Bad points:
- another big change for this game is the fact your character now speaks. The problem with this is the dialogue options are now more restricted as a result and conversations feel dumbed down. While i appreciate the attempt to try something new its sort of backfired in the sense that conversations feel like theyve taken a step backwards after the great dialogue options in New Vegas.
-and speaking of New Vegas is had hoped Bethesda might have learned something from Obsidian about making a great story with interesting quests that have many outcomes and resolutions. Instead for the most part its the standard Bethesda quests with not many outcome options and a story which is ok if not amazing.
tl:dr this is a fanatastic game and a great addition to the series. The Commonwealth is an amazing environment and the new settlement construction and weapon mods are fanastic additions. The game has it flaws mainly with the dialogue interations and quests with limited outcomes but i doesnt spoil what is a fun and entertaining experience.

Amazing game. There are a couple of things that feel simplified that I don't like, like the lack of weapon and armor repair besides power armor, but the things that they added completely outweigh the things I feel were left out. Weapon customization is awesome, even though it ends up being rather predictable after you get into it. Gameplay is in an entire new league compared to the other Fallouts, and character movement is much more fluid than before, but still not up to modern FPS standards. All in all, gameplay, story, and mechanics come together to make a very nice game, and the glitches have been pretty minor on launch.

The Good: Shooting is fun.
The Everything Else: Exploring new places would be pretty fun if it didn't feel like grinding because enemies and items respawn.
The dialogue system literally doesn't exist, at best you'll use your Charisma stat to ask for more money or have a rare option of persuading somebody. Even though you get several choices in dialogues all of them lead to the same conclusion. The only thing it seems to influence is your companions since some of them like it when you're mean, nice, sarcastic or try to shake down people for more caps.
The main story feels like it was written in an evening and all of it is held together with duct tape. The story railroads you pretty heavily into helping a certain faction to the point where you build a thing you help sabogate later.
The ending is awful without any redeeming qualities. Not only does it not change at all depending on the faction, you don't really feel like anything, well, ends. (Preorder Fallout 4 Season Pass for 29,99 EUR now!) There's plenty of unanswered questions that feel like they've been sweeped under the rug.
The settlement thing would have been interesting if the actual building wasn't incredibly clunky and required less resource management between settlements. But mods, right?
Do I recommend this game? Unfortunately steam doesn't allow for anything other than yes/no so i'll have to go with no. If you'd like to shoot things in a post-apocalyptic setting then sure go ahead, but it's barely a Fallout game or an RPG at this point.

Ghouls throw surprise parties for you from fridges, toilet stall doors throw surprise shotgun parties for your face, deathclaws throw surprise "you're totally ♥♥♥♥ed" parties when you least expect it.

Amazing game. There are a couple of things that feel simplified that I don't like, like the lack of weapon and armor repair besides power armor, but the things that they added completely outweigh the things I feel were left out. Weapon customization is awesome, even though it ends up being rather predictable after you get into it. Gameplay is in an entire new league compared to the other Fallouts, and character movement is much more fluid than before, but still not up to modern FPS standards. All in all, gameplay, story, and mechanics come together to make a very nice game, and the glitches have been pretty minor on launch.

The Good: Shooting is fun.
The Everything Else: Exploring new places would be pretty fun if it didn't feel like grinding because enemies and items respawn.
The dialogue system literally doesn't exist, at best you'll use your Charisma stat to ask for more money or have a rare option of persuading somebody. Even though you get several choices in dialogues all of them lead to the same conclusion. The only thing it seems to influence is your companions since some of them like it when you're mean, nice, sarcastic or try to shake down people for more caps.
The main story feels like it was written in an evening and all of it is held together with duct tape. The story railroads you pretty heavily into helping a certain faction to the point where you build a thing you help sabogate later.
The ending is awful without any redeeming qualities. Not only does it not change at all depending on the faction, you don't really feel like anything, well, ends. (Preorder Fallout 4 Season Pass for 29,99 EUR now!) There's plenty of unanswered questions that feel like they've been sweeped under the rug.
The settlement thing would have been interesting if the actual building wasn't incredibly clunky and required less resource management between settlements. But mods, right?
Do I recommend this game? Unfortunately steam doesn't allow for anything other than yes/no so i'll have to go with no. If you'd like to shoot things in a post-apocalyptic setting then sure go ahead, but it's barely a Fallout game or an RPG at this point.

I've spent many hours playing this game. From wandering the wasteland, to settlement building, to just scavenging for supplies. To say that this is a game you can get lost in, is truly one of the most true statements. Now, it has bugs, oh yes, many a time have I been forced to deal with some sort of bug. From getting stuck my a loose board to having my companion enter a seemingly permanent state of being downed (it wasn't), this game has many bugs. But this game has also been an amazing experience. In 144 hours of playing, I have only now gotten to the Institute. Now, is that because I took my time?
The answer is no, I went and explored the world. From small little details in terminals and holotapes, to quest lines that will make you laugh and wonder, this is truly a world where you'll be on your way, and find something that makes you completely forget you had a goal. The story, while some things are indeed predictable, others are, well, certainly nice surprises.
While I refuse to spoil the story for you, I will talk about some features.
Power Armor is truly powerful feeling. It doesn't make you invincible, but it makes you more of a one man army. Which, considering some of the fights you'll have, evens the playing field. The customization of each piece is possibly my favorite part, upgrades for many situations, and plenty of ways to switch around for what you want. I can't tell you what it was like to finally build a full suit of Enclave power Armor, scrounging up the armor piece by bloody piece, until I finally have a full set to call my own.
Mods are, while sometimes limited, othertimes, they make a dramatic difference. Turning a gun from something to run in with, to something to stay quiet and pick your shots with. Keep in mind, some guns are more customizable than others, and if you're heading a more melee route, be prepared to not quite have a huge selection.
I could go on and on, but, I think for now, I'll head off and see about finishing this game's story.

It has some flaws, but it's still a good game nonetheless.
Power armor is amazing and actually has a different use this time around. No longer is it just a slightly better set of armor. Now it's a full suit that you step into and become some sort of "man tank". It gives an insane amount of damage resistance, removes fall damage, increases carry weight, and more. It's really, really good. But that's where the first problem is. The only downside of power armor is that you need Fusion Cores to use it, and there are far too many scattered around. So you're left in the situation where you can use power armor 24/7 and still get more Fusion Cores. Even with a jetpack that supposedly drains cores faster, I've been outpacing my usage. (And I use it a lot.) Eventually I just got tired of it making the game too easy and left it behind.
Other stuff is also way too common. By the time I completed the main story, I had around 300 stimpacks in my inventory. I didn't buy a single one of them. That was only 20 hours into the game. If I theoretically got into a massive firefight and starting popping stimpacks like they're going out of style, it wouldn't even dent my supply. Again, it makes the game too easy at times. You're never faced with the decision of, "Can I take these guys?" because with enough stimpacks (or power armor), you can.
The companion system can also get a bit annoying. Each companion has their strengths and weaknesses, and once they like you enough, they'll get some sort of special perk. Problem is, companions are so whiny. The each have things they like and things they don't like. They are the most arbitrary things too. Strong dislikes power armor and lockpicking. Why? Hell if I know, but he just decided he doesn't want to person he's roaming with to stay safe. Preston Garvey things I'm a terrible person for asking for any money whatsoever, because how dare I spend that money on supplies for the base I'm building for him. The only reasonable companion is Dogmeat, becuase Dogmeat doesn't care. (And Dogmeat is arguably the best for a lot of reasons.)
Base building is nice, but it needs some improvements. There needs to be a way to disable snapping temporarily, because trying to set up a wall that isn't perfectly alligned is really annoying. It'll just try to snap and go straight if it's anywhere close. There's also a cap to how big a base can be (how many items you can put in it). It's okay, it's not too restricting, but I really wish I could just keep building it bigger. I wanted to make a massive town, and I was left with a pretty average shanty town. I get that the limits are in place for performance reasons, but if someone can handle more, why not let them?
Other than that, it's the same old game with some improvements. You can sprint now, so it feels like a game from this decade. There also aren't any arbitrary mountains right in the middle of the map to make it seem bigger. Basically, if you want to go somewhere, you can and it won't take half an hour. The map is dense and there's a lot to see. There are multiple endings if that's your thing. I'd recommend it to anyone looking for a game to sink loads of time into.

THIS IS A VANILLA REVIEW. I WILL CHANGE IT WHEN I PLAYED THE REST OF THE DLC.
I've logged a couple hundred hours in both Fallout 3 and Fallout: New Vegas. After putting in around 60 hours into Fallout 4, my opinion can be summed up as follows: good game, terrible TERRIBLE port, with a few misguided attempts at innovation. GREAT level design and once again, TERRIBLE PORT. I hate the menu system.
Pros:
+ Fantastic character customization. Even without more detailed controls, the system allows for truly unique looking characters.
+ Great characterization. I've frequently heard people claim characters are "bland" and "boring", but those that I've run in to so far have been anything but. I think that this opinion stems from the first few hours of the game, when you're first getting a feel for things. Preston Garvey is admittedly pretty bland, as well as the inhabitants of every tiny settlement until you reach the edge of Boston. Once you start getting into the nitty gritty of it, you'll find some charming characters. I don't want to spoil any characters that you might meet, but i found most to be intresting.
+ Good AI, improved companion AI. This is another point of contention. I've seen people complain that the AI is bad, but in my experience, it's above average when compared to most other AAA titles these days, and leaps ahead of where Bethesda was with Skyrim and the previous Fallout. Enemies make frequent use of cover, attempt to flank, etc. Companions position themselves to accurately fire down at people. I've had very few issues so far. Sometimes you will get stuck on your dog companion beacuse he stands in a doorway and refuses to move, that might the biggest issue i had so far.
+ Amazing gun/armor customization. Glad they added in layered armoring. Looks cool and is fun to do.
+ Music. Great song choice, cool radio station, funny announcer (though I do hope he'll actually tie into a quest at some point). Non-radio music is also great. Just wish they had some more tracks, hopefully they release a free DLC with a music pack or something.
+ Environment and Level Design. Very pleased with how it turned out. Plus, the increased amount of outer-cell and vertical-gameplay oriented areas makes me very happy. This is where they exceeded expectations for me, the level design is crazy good and it never feels copy&paste at all, just pick a direction and you will see cool stuff. This is easily the best level design that Bethesda has had in any of their games.
Contested:
= Dialogue. I don't like the four-button system, and I don't like the whole "color indicated difficulty" with speech checks. I liked the RPG aspect of the earlier games, where what stats you put point in could give you different options when talking to NPC's. This is pretty much gone. The four-button system usually just give you the options of "walk away" "say yes to whatever they say" "sarcasm" or "<charisma option>", there's no depth to it at all and this is one of the bigger things i don't like with this game. Some will like beacuse it's more fluid and "easier" but I personally wouldn't mind it being reworked completely.
= Bugs. This is probably the most bug-free Bethesda release I've ever seen, not counting the problems associated with Gamebryo (the games engine) or the game's status as a mediocre (awful) port. Still, the bugs are there, and they are occasionally jarring. Every major release should expect some bugs, and Fallout 4 seems about average for the games industry rather than for Bethesda's historically poor track record. Considering that the game is HUGE with millions of stuff that you can interact with and move around, i feel having bugs is OK. They are not totally gamebreaking, some are even funny and I'm sure that most of the bigger ones will be patched out. As of writing this only one minor patch has been done. I CTD three times, which sucked, but the game autosaved so it didn't mess anything up for me. Overall you won't notice bugs that much and comparing it to the old releases Fallout 4's release is pure bliss in comparison.
= Story. I can take it or leave it, which may be better to take as a bad sign. If this game were linear, this would be a major downer. I can't really talk about this without spoiling, but the writing has never been the best thing with the fallout games, even though i wish it was a liiiittle more intresting. It feels bland and not that well put together.
Cons:
- Controls. Jesus F**** christ, the control scheme is bad. UI is terrible. This was a case of people reassigning keys to be used on the PC rather than giving it the attention is deserves. This is probably the worst of it. With a decent UI, almost half the problems with the game would instantly disappear. It's horrible to navigate through the menus, but if you played Fallout 3+New Vegas you will be right at home. I thought that this was one of the bigger things that they would have been working on, since it sucked equally bad in the older games and I don't know a soul on this earth that thinks they are good. Fallout 4's menu system is the perfect example of why PC needs it's own UI.
- Voiced Protagonist.  Personally, I find the voice actors did great jobs doing this, but it still doesn't fit, and completely removes the ability for me to make a character of my own, Once again the RPG aspect have taken a back seat to having a voiced protagonist, I don't really feel like im playing "my character" and i'm playing someone else when they are talking. I don't see my character with that voice and that takes me out of the game. Another problem is I can't get wrapped up in this character's problems. I can't bring myself to care about his/her plight on the Earth. I think this is mostly a matter of poor execution. A voiced protagonist would work fine if they also managed to keep the character's motivations ambiguous, and not have it so heavily reliant on a preestablished backstory that I personally didn't care that much for anyway.
- Like mentioned before, They dumbed down the "RP" in "RPG". It's now an FPSrpG. I want my perk/skill based dialogue checks back. I want there to be moral chocies that shape how my character is seen. I want there to be a karma meter that shows how I'm perceived in the wasteland. At the moment i can do whatever and that is boring beacuse there is rarely any consequences to anything i do.
- Gamebyro and all of the issues associated with it. I hate the engine and wish that they get rid of it to Skyrim 2 or Fallout 5. The engine sucks and is old. It needs to be taken out back and shot.
- Terrible PC options. You'll have to go directly into the preferences & initialization files to change things like mouse acceleration and FOV. This is something that should be in the main menu of the game, not outside of the game. WTF.
Not Rated:
~ Performance. I have a very high end system, so I can't speak as to how nicely this runs on budget machines, but I've heard good things. I do get the occasional FPS drop but 97% of the time it runs flawlessly. I even opened the console, flew high up in the air and started spamming stuff, i kept going for a few minutes until it finally crashed. So it seems stable enough even when you try to break it on purpose.
Last words:
Is it better then Fallout 3 and New Vegas? Well it depends, did you just like the atmosphere of the old games or were you intrested in the story? DId you care about the RPG-elements? These are the questions you need to ask yourself. The game is buggy and definitly feels incomplete as of now, but DLC are planned and coming so who knows where the game will end up. Do i recommend this game? Yes, but not whole heartedly. It has issues, but it's a solid game and if you can pick it up as GOTY you will have made a good deal. I would NOT recommend buying it at full price, since i don't think its worth it at this time.
Hope this was helpful for you on the fence on buying the game or not.

[Dialogue System]
At any point in a converstion you will always have four options to choose. Unfortunately the choices do not matter most of the time. Basically you will have 3 ways of saying yes and one way to say no. In previous games of the series other attributes like intelligence gave you  additional options for the conversations. The way the power armor works in the game is one of the best features in this game. You can tinker and improve it and give it additional functions like a jetpack or a cloaking device. Power Armor loses durability when hit and also needs to be repaired. [Settlements]
Fallout 4 allows for the construction of settlements. Unfortunately the mechanic feels a bit unfinished. There are almost no tutorials and placing some objects can be frustrating. This makes a side mechanic very intrusive since it is required to develop the character differently than expected.
[Conclusion]
I enjoyed the game but everyone who played one of its predecessors needs to be aware that many things which made Fallout unique and intresting are missing in this game. The best feature of every Bethesda game in the Elder Scrolls or Fallout universe is the exploration of the worlds (ESO does not count). If thats not your thing you should think twice before buying this game.

The Fallout franchise has come a long way to reach this point. Played every single one and this one is by far my favourite in terms of game play. So here's my comprehensive review of a GOOD game;
Pros
First off...
POWER ARMOUR: this is the first game where power armour actually feels like a power armour... in previous titles it was just end game armour. In Fallout 4, you now need a Power Core to be able to effectively run around in Power Armour and not only that, they do not last very long either; that's a good thing. I'll admit getting introduced to Power Armour so early into the game was a let down and wished it was introduced at least mid-game. Thankfully they didn't bring back Power Armour training because then that would severely limit who you get that training from; Brotherhood of Steel mainly.
Combat: a MASSIVE improvement from Fallout 3. The FPS aspect actually feels like an FPS game and I love it. The movement also has drastically improved from previous titles. My only issue is the default POV, though this can be rectified using a mod that changes the .ini file.
Wasteland: it's not as large as I expected but it's still pretty big and scary nonetheless. I'm always constantly being side tracked, finding a deserted/abandoned house to a Satellite overrun with Super Mutants and either avoiding places entirely or trying my luck against the baddies. So much to see and do.
Settlements: this is the biggest hype I had for the game when it was announced at E3. At first it was confusing but once you've got the hang of it you'll be spending hours on end making the perfect settlement. It also doesn't just stop at Sanctuary, you've got countless other settlements at your disposal which you can fortify and call it a home for you and other settlers.
Voiced Protagonist: it's definitely different, and a very much welcomed change/addition to Fallout. Some people dislike it but I certainly love it.
Modding: weapons and armour have so many combinations of mods to be put on which makes that weapon unique to you. I've spent hours already just modding my guns, armour, power armour etc - just to get that perfect set up.
Graphics: a lot of people complain about this and I don't understand why... it's much better than Fallout 4, the details are amazing. Yeah, it isn't as great as current AAA titles out these days with a minimum recommendation of a GTX Titan X (sarcasm) but gameplay over graphics any day.
Cons
Dialouge: I'm really disappointed that dialouge this time around has been severly dumbed down... where Charisma is the ONLY determining factor of progressing with extra information. I miss when other attributes like Science could play a role in getting better information out of scienctists or Bartering would get you better prices at vendors... hopefully this will return in FO5 in 7-10 years ^^
Story: overall, I am happy with how the story ended depending whom you've gone with but I can see how the endings aren't that much different from each other depending who you sided with. I did rush mid-game to the ending so that may have played a role in it but I'm more disappointed that the faction system isn't as "prominant" in F04 as it did in NV... for example, anything that would directly hinder or sabatoge another factions mission or goal wouldn't cause any form of infamy towards you... instead, you can happily role with all 3 major factions (Railroad, Brotherhood and Institute) right up until the very end. I wish you had to choose a faction mid-game and stick with said faction for the rest... though tryinbg to figure out who to help and who not to help was great, didn't really feel like I belonged to any of them since I was essentially helping other factions as well, indirectly or not.
TL;DR ? Fallout 4 is great, definitely a game to buy. Don't think... buy it.

Please do not misunderstand me because this game is worth every penny put into it.
The gameplay and overall graphics have been improved, and the soundtrack isn't half bad. However, it is not as friendly to the hardcore roleplayer. Your character essientially comes with a set story that doesn't leave a lot of room for a custom backstory. Not to mention that the story doesn't change by much no matter what choices you make which reduces the replayability by a noticeable margin. There is also the seemingly Dragon Age 2/Mass Effect inspired dialogue system that creates the illusion of choice. Essientially, you can only answer with Yes, No, Sarcastic remark, or ask a Question which is redundant most of the time. The dialogue choices made often end up getting the same response from an NPC regardless of the chosen dialogue.
In the end, despite all of the flaws in this game it still manages to bring me back in with it's irresistable charm and gameplay. I have fun playing this game, and I cannot wait for the DLC to come out so I can enjoy more content!
Overall, here is how I feel about the game:
Pros:
-Soundtrack
-Combat (faster paced, immersive, and it makes more sense than the previous Fallout games)
-Armor & Weapon Mods (Fantastic! There are visible differences with each mod made, and it makes junk VALUABLE)
-Exploration (You could say it's..... Out of this world)
-Power Armor (It actually feels like POWER ARMOR. I was skeptical at first, but it is balanced very well)
-Companions (Great personalities, useful perks, great dialogue, and the romance option is a nice touch)
-It works (Not near as many bugs as a typical Bethesda game, and most bugs are resolved shortly)
-Wasteland (It is not boring like Fallout 3. Brighter colors, and more interesting sights)
-Construction (Once it is figured out it can be a lot of fun. Get your Minecraft: Fallout 4 Edition on)
Cons:
-Roleplaying is not as deep as it could be
-Dialogue System (Quite limited as to what you can say, and choices don't seem to carry much weight)
-Main Character Voice (I hate there is one PC voice. It works for Mass Effect, but not for an open world RP game)
-Not new player friendly (No solid tutorial for VATS and construction. New players will start with some difficulty)
-Perk Tree (It is not explained very well. I bet $5 many didn't know how to scroll at first. Otherwise, it's kinda okay)
-Construction (There is almost no tutorial, and it feels thrown together at the last minute. It's fun once figured out)
-Main Story (I feel it has a nice beginning and middle. However, the ending is lacking a lot and it's rather short)

Additionally, the S.P.E.C.I.A.L system seems to not matter much anymore other than being a baseline for you to put points into to obtain perks. Now for the S.P.E.C.I.A.L system you have a very casualized system where many of your 'skill points' go towards  perks  that have have no  benefit  like lead-belly and some that you will highly desire like local leader, but  just for say perks like local leader you will be forced to  deal with  the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t of  investing  in the S.P.E.C.I.A.L stat tied to that perk for an insane amount of levels; I think Angry Joe said for local leader you needed to put in 9 skill points into Charisma.

YES, NO, MAYBE OR SARCASM ARE YOUR ONLY ♥♥♥♥ING ANSWERS.  NPCs you will speak in the game will have very similar responses to the dialogue you select to speak to them; one such example is when you go to Diamond City  and  talk to the mayor about Piper's newspaper. Fallout 4 is EXACTLY what we were waiting for. Don't allow misleading reviews to steer you away from what is, or rather can be considered, the game of the year. So far I have clocked around 70+ hours on it, and have not found myself bored once. People are complaining about the graphics, and glitches, but comon this is Bethesda! The game itself is a stunning upgrade from the otherwise bland visuals from Fallout NV, and the glitches are few and inbetween (which is a rarity for a Bethesda game).
Overall I have found this to be extremely immersive, and find myself exploring every nook and cranny for my next piece of armor, loot, or ammo. The vats system was much improved in this new release, as well as the attention to detail that Bethesda has taken.
Examples of the detail that I myself have noticed:
-You move your pip boy and fiddle with the knobs when not active.
-When you use you light from the pip boy it shows an actually lit up device on your arm.
-When you get into and out of power armor, the game displays the detailed procedure it takes to get "integrated"
-Rain effects, Rad storm effects, ambient mother fracking weather!
-Legendary armors make you feel like you are actually getting somewhere with loot.
-A new loot stash system for us "hoarders".
-The building system for settlements as well as integrating skills from your tree into your leadership ability.
-ETC ETC ETC......
I plan to continue playing this game, so why don't you? It seems silly to base a Bethesda game solely on reviews, when you as a gamer are well aware of how much time and effort goes into the build. This isnt EA fracking you with a rusty spoon, but rather an excellent example of what has been so lost in the gaming industry with every COD rehash, and lackluster grinding MMO. Get the game, kill some Ghouls, and enjoy the apocolypse..

Please do not misunderstand me because this game is worth every penny put into it.
The gameplay and overall graphics have been improved, and the soundtrack isn't half bad. However, it is not as friendly to the hardcore roleplayer. Your character essientially comes with a set story that doesn't leave a lot of room for a custom backstory. Not to mention that the story doesn't change by much no matter what choices you make which reduces the replayability by a noticeable margin. There is also the seemingly Dragon Age 2/Mass Effect inspired dialogue system that creates the illusion of choice. Essientially, you can only answer with Yes, No, Sarcastic remark, or ask a Question which is redundant most of the time. The dialogue choices made often end up getting the same response from an NPC regardless of the chosen dialogue.
In the end, despite all of the flaws in this game it still manages to bring me back in with it's irresistable charm and gameplay. I have fun playing this game, and I cannot wait for the DLC to come out so I can enjoy more content!
Overall, here is how I feel about the game:
Pros:
-Soundtrack
-Combat (faster paced, immersive, and it makes more sense than the previous Fallout games)
-Armor & Weapon Mods (Fantastic! There are visible differences with each mod made, and it makes junk VALUABLE)
-Exploration (You could say it's..... Out of this world)
-Power Armor (It actually feels like POWER ARMOR. I was skeptical at first, but it is balanced very well)
-Companions (Great personalities, useful perks, great dialogue, and the romance option is a nice touch)
-It works (Not near as many bugs as a typical Bethesda game, and most bugs are resolved shortly)
-Wasteland (It is not boring like Fallout 3. Brighter colors, and more interesting sights)
-Construction (Once it is figured out it can be a lot of fun. Get your Minecraft: Fallout 4 Edition on)
Cons:
-Roleplaying is not as deep as it could be
-Dialogue System (Quite limited as to what you can say, and choices don't seem to carry much weight)
-Main Character Voice (I hate there is one PC voice. It works for Mass Effect, but not for an open world RP game)
-Not new player friendly (No solid tutorial for VATS and construction. New players will start with some difficulty)
-Perk Tree (It is not explained very well. I bet $5 many didn't know how to scroll at first. Otherwise, it's kinda okay)
-Construction (There is almost no tutorial, and it feels thrown together at the last minute. It's fun once figured out)
-Main Story (I feel it has a nice beginning and middle. However, the ending is lacking a lot and it's rather short)
-Side Quests (At first there seems to be an abundance, but it's a trick! They become rather scarce after the Main Story)
-Food (Cooking is fine, but food seems to almost have no purpose to the PC. Wish we had Hardcore mode like Vegas)
Many of my complaints are nitpicks, and the game makes up for it's flaws. Again, it is worth every penny invested.

I found this a hard one to review. I mean its a good game for sure, but when put to contrast against its predecessors Fallout 3 and new vegas, it falls short on some aspects.
What I like:
-Combat: The combat is super sweet and smooth as oiled butter. It's all well balanced, animations run smooth, VATS works great, love it. Grenades, guns, plasmas, lasers, mines, melee's, it all just works. This for me is definately the main selling point for this game. The combat is just really, really fun to do.
-Bugs: I have 60'ish hours so far and i haven't encountered any bugs 'till this point which is quite a feat. So definately A thumbs up.
-Perks & Levels: I really like the new system. I mean yeah the fact that you can rank up your SPECIAL means you can be whatever "class" you want to become and so that takes away from the replayability value, but overall I like that they tried something new and especially the perks being linked to your Special I think is pretty kewl.
What I don't like:
-City building: One question: WHY? Why should I waste my time perfecting every settlement, see to all their needs, make a fortress end stockpile it with defences? It has no use! All you need is one base from which you can do all your stuff. I mean yeah i guess you can build some artillery in settlements, i guess you can call minutemen to your aid. But is it worth the ours you have to put into micromanaging the settlements? The answer for me is a solid no.
-Controls: What the actual♥♥♥♥♥♥ I mean come on I know there are only a few countries with azerty but come on guys, the controls for azerty players are completely broken. You can adjust the bindings for regular playthrough but they all change back when you go into city building, making it ♥♥♥♥ing unplayable. Now every time I play fallout 4 I have to set my computer to querty just to be able to play the game. Aside from that, the controls are also heavily dumbed down to be compatible with consoles, which I truly think is a big shame. Rifle melee attack and grenade have the same binding? come on, my keyboard has nearly 100 keys.... you can do better Bethesda.
Mixed feelings:
-Story lines/quests: Its a huge world, like, really huge. you can wonder for hours on end and come across so many different locations, and yet to me the world feels kinda empty. What I really dislake are repetitive quests. Quests that have no consequence whatsoever. Go to that village, talk to the elder, he says someone or something is bugging them (which are always always mutants, fiends or raiders,) you go kill them, turn in quest, nothing changes. It takes away all sense of completion for me. Like, Fallout New vegas, you could really complete that game, do all the quests even though it would take ages. but in theory you could. Here in fallout 4 I miss that feeling sometimes. Be that as it may the stories behind the quests are still solid as has always been in Bethesda games. So hence the mixed feelings.

Sometimes I walk trough the abandoned wasteland and really think: "my ♥♥♥♥ing♥♥♥♥♥♥this is beautiful", but then sometimes when I converse with someone I can almost see the ♥♥♥♥ing pixels on their face. Following is my personal opinion. If you like it take it under consideration, if not ignore it. My opinion doesn't necessarily represent the objective point of view in this game. So;
I love FO games and I like to think that I like to support bethesda's projects so far.
FO4 is a great game. Great but not perfect.
PROS
✔ Fully voiced main character (finally!)
✔ Environment has quality and quantity. There's variety of environmental design and this is really amazing.
✔ NPCs can call you by your custom name. This is very original and sets a new ground for better RPG experiences.
✔ A ton of things to do. Just simply won't get bored. This is an original to the core Fallout Game.
✔ Many sweet side quests with some great story backgrounds out there.
✔ Mod support (can never do without them in such a game).
✔ A fun game mode that helps you build bases and settlements (so addictive that you might end up playing a SIMS simulation rather than the rest of the game)
CONS
✖ I'm writing this and it hasn't been but a few days since release so yeah, there's some ridiculous bugs out there.
✖ Ridiculously outdated graphics and physics. Bethesda better use that money earned to develop their next game on a new engine.
✖ The world map. I was kinda expecting it to be bigger.
✖ Controls. They should at least had added more key binding options in the settings. Dialogue controls at the moment looks like a bad console import.
MIXED:
☢ Took me some time to get used to how interactions with NPCs work. it's not bad. not good. it's different.
☢ Outdated graphics could be considered as a good thing for people with weak hardware.
FINAL:
I do not consider this as a final review cause I know i haven't done all that the game has to offer yet. So I guess you can consider it more as a hands on opinion.
For me personally; the game is great. For me personally it's not GOTY material, but it really is very great. i can foresee me spending more than a couple of hundreds of hours of game play in total by the time i'm done with it so that is enough criteria for me to say that it is worth the full price of the game.
Bethesda has proven to know how to make games that have a tone to offer and I have trust in them.

I was 60 hours into Fallout 4, and I had seen everything. Did I get all the collectibles? No. Did I beat every variant of the main quest? No. But other than that, I was done. This was the last thing I expected from this game. Being disappointed I expected (which I was in a lot of ways), but lack of content is not something I assosciate with Bethesda. Not to say that 60 hours is aything to laugh at. 60 hours is a long time, it's just not as long as I expected from Bethesda. I thought I would get bored with the game before I saw everything.
Anyways, Fallout 4 is good. The weapon crafting is one of the best things I have seen this year and has so much potential for future Fallout and TES games. The main quest is better than I expected it to be, with real moral decisions and interesting characters (at least for the BOS). The skill system is changed drastically, which is to say that it has been extremely simplified, but it works with the design philosophy of the game. The amount of detail everywhere is astounding, and it lends a great atmosphere to world. Companions are super interesting. The looting system is improved. The gunplay is much, much better than New Vegas or 3. But what is lacking is content, and I think I know why.
Moment to moment gameplay is great, but the bigger picture ends up being kind of dull. Fallout 4 is missing the forest for the trees, so to speak. The details are, appropriately enough, very detailed, but everything is small. The quests are short, the dungeons are short, the combat takes five minutes per encounter at best, and even how fast you level up is fairly quick. Don't get me wrong, all of it is fun, but there just isn't any value in your accomplishments. The best example of this is when I was asked to get a cat that a little girl had lost. In Skyrim, this would have started a half-hour long quest with a strange moment of world building at the end. In Fallout 4, I found the cat and sent it back to the girl. That's it. I didn't even have to kill anyone. Another time, a quest started with a mysterious name. I was led into an abandoned museum to find what killed some raiders (gunners I think they're called), and as I searched the building shook and dust feel from the ceiling. As I walked up the steps to the second floor, a loud roar rattled the wood around me. Then, I found a big deathclaw and killed it. That's it. Quest over. Yeah, you get some backstory and an amusing couple minutes, but nothing past that. The game is just obsessed with brevity.
Fallout 4 feels like a test game. Bethesda tried some new things like the settlements, the crafting, and, of course, the voiced main character. Some worked and some didn't, and I'm axious to see what they'll do with the ones that worked. Fallout 4 is worth playing, but it isn't the best in the series or the best open world exploration game. Skyrim, New Vegas, and the older Fallouts are better than Fallout 4 in their own unique ways, and I would recommend those more.

Not even an RPG, you don't make decisions that lead to new outcomes, you're a nobody. You do what you're ♥♥♥♥in' told (literally can't decline most quests). Read any of these other negative reviews and you've got my full review in a nutshell.

Your character may have a (bland)role in this world but it isn't "your" role. It's whatever you're told to do on this linear branch that has 3 twig endings - but these all feel like a forced end. There are, quite literally, nearly no choices in the game that will ever truly effect anything in this game. You literally can't even play as a bad guy for 95% of the game. You have no role. You have a rollercoaster. Exciting; but you don't decide jack when it comes to where to go story-wise.
There's been so much good added, there really has. You can't just go and throw away half of the spirit that brought the previous games alive in exchange, though. Power armour, the modification system, settlements, scoped shooting feels a little improved, etc.
However, it's become more of a loot-&-level empowered kind of progression. No free roleplay. Extremely dull companions. The list goes on.
The game is extremely fun, don't get me wrong - but not a true RPG. Worse than older FO games in some aspects, in my own opinion. Still got love for Bethesda, though.
Update: I have decided to switch the game to recommended. Although it lacks in certain aspects that define the rpg genre, the game will, in the end, provide players with many, many hours of fun. ========FALLOUT 4: Overview========
Look guys, the graphics are good, if a little bland because hey, NUCLEAR APOCALYPSE , ie lots of rubble and dead things. And not gonna lie, there's the odd bug or two but generally they resolve themselves (my major bug is that my V.A.T.S. systems stopped working about 3 hours into the game, but it's definitely not necessary for combat - you'd never even know it is there for you to use because the traditional combat handles itself so well and the power is well-balanced).
Dogmeat is great and he can never die so yay (try giving him a teddy bear, 10/10 will not regret). I like the companions that I've come across so far and that they have different preferences that match their character (still waiting to find one with greyer morals to approve of my non-combative approach but also won't throw a tantrum when I pickpocket the odd NPC). The Diamond City radio announcer is a nervous wreck and I love it and the selection of music on the station is great (and it's often extremely ironic, which the announcer tends to lampshade).
Also I like collecting comics.
But I've heard quite a few grievances about the story of Fallout 4 and at the time I couldn't put my finger on what it was that made me disagree.
========FALLOUT 4: Story, and the open-world========
To clarify, I'm well over 50 hours in (some of it was offline so my steam stats aren't 100% accurate) and I've only //just// started following the main storyline. Sure, throughout the main storyline (what little I've played of it so far) things generally end up at the same conclusion with pretty standard dialogue choices (yes, no, sarcastic, or "please clarify")
But I've realised that
Skeletons strewn behind sandbags across an abandoned chapel; their last stand against raiders. The many notes, holotapes and terminals you find, often with diary entries by people pre- and post-war. The fact that most raider sleeping bags will almost always have chems nearby - combine this with a couple of terminal entries you read and you realize that most raiders only join up so they can sustain their addictions (not because they are bloodthirsty, crazy or believe in some higher power).
In this way the richness and depth of the game is increased tenfold, though I expect that most players don't take the time to read through the various log entries or explore the basement of the paranoid pre-war technophobe which is a shame because they are missing out on the TRUE bulk of the story in Fallout 4.
========FALLOUT 4: Miscellaneous (me, my hoarding tendencies in video-games)========
And I'm still not bored, despite having hardly done any of the main questline and only the odd side quest, and I've only thoroughly explored about a third of the map. Though to be fair this is probably due to the fact that I completely empty an area of every last tin can before moving on to greener pastures.
Can I also say that this game is simultaneously a hoarder's dream and nightmare. On one hand there's SO. MUCH. STUFF!! On the other hand...there's so much stuff. I've never played a game so expansive and it's always great to be still be surprised by the occasional environmental easter egg - such as finding a teddy bear with glasses on sitting on the toilet reading a newspaper upside down in an obscure part of the map. Or finding a skeleton without its skull in a bathtub, surrounded by mannequins holding machetes and toilet plungers. (It's quite an unsettling scene)
========FALLOUT 4: Conclusion========

I found this a hard one to review. I mean its a good game for sure, but when put to contrast against its predecessors Fallout 3 and new vegas, it falls short on some aspects.
What I like:
-Combat: The combat is super sweet and smooth as oiled butter. It's all well balanced, animations run smooth, VATS works great, love it. Grenades, guns, plasmas, lasers, mines, melee's, it all just works. This for me is definately the main selling point for this game. The combat is just really, really fun to do.
-Bugs: I have 60'ish hours so far and i haven't encountered any bugs 'till this point which is quite a feat. So definately A thumbs up.
-Perks & Levels: I really like the new system. I mean yeah the fact that you can rank up your SPECIAL means you can be whatever "class" you want to become and so that takes away from the replayability value, but overall I like that they tried something new and especially the perks being linked to your Special I think is pretty kewl.
What I don't like:
-City building: One question: WHY? Why should I waste my time perfecting every settlement, see to all their needs, make a fortress end stockpile it with defences? It has no use! All you need is one base from which you can do all your stuff. I mean yeah i guess you can build some artillery in settlements, i guess you can call minutemen to your aid. But is it worth the ours you have to put into micromanaging the settlements? The answer for me is a solid no.
-Controls: What the actual♥♥♥♥♥♥ I mean come on I know there are only a few countries with azerty but come on guys, the controls for azerty players are completely broken. You can adjust the bindings for regular playthrough but they all change back when you go into city building, making it ♥♥♥♥ing unplayable. Now every time I play fallout 4 I have to set my computer to querty just to be able to play the game. Aside from that, the controls are also heavily dumbed down to be compatible with consoles, which I truly think is a big shame. Rifle melee attack and grenade have the same binding? come on, my keyboard has nearly 100 keys.... you can do better Bethesda.
Mixed feelings:
-Story lines/quests: Its a huge world, like, really huge. you can wonder for hours on end and come across so many different locations, and yet to me the world feels kinda empty. What I really dislake are repetitive quests. Quests that have no consequence whatsoever. Go to that village, talk to the elder, he says someone or something is bugging them (which are always always mutants, fiends or raiders,) you go kill them, turn in quest, nothing changes. It takes away all sense of completion for me. Like, Fallout New vegas, you could really complete that game, do all the quests even though it would take ages. but in theory you could. Here in fallout 4 I miss that feeling sometimes. Be that as it may the stories behind the quests are still solid as has always been in Bethesda games. So hence the mixed feelings.
-Graphics: Oh man, I just don't know. I have a high end pc, and have turned everything on ultra. Sometimes I walk trough the abandoned wasteland and really think: "my ♥♥♥♥ing♥♥♥♥♥♥this is beautiful", but then sometimes when I converse with someone I can almost see the ♥♥♥♥ing pixels on their face. So I figured it out. What they have done really well, and which is something they probably learned from skyrim mods, is the lighting. It also makes everything super smooth and beautiful. But when in dark places, like say for example Virgills Cave, The lighting doesn't matter, and the actual texture quality, which in my opinion is pretty♥♥♥♥♥♥for ultra setting, falls short. Seriously Talk to Virgil and just look at that monstrosity.
All in all I can recommend Fallout. Most of the complaints are overshadowed by the good stuff and I had a ton of fun playing. Overall, despite some flaws, its still a real good experience. 9/10

Fallout 4 is a great time, and a solid step forward for Bethesda, showing promising evolution, yet there are mistakes made beyond the bugs.
Pros:
+ Visuals
I mean it would be awkward if the graphics weren't improved over Skyrim.
Graphics aside, the animations and lighting in this game are a treat.
+ Combat
Shooting, melee, power armor, V.A.T.S, and everything else from Fallout 3 has been ramped up. Making every part of combat more exciting and more comfortable.
+ Crafting and Settlements
You'll have a blast with weapon upgrades, armor upgrades, cooking food, cooking drugs, and upgrading in the now fantastic power armor system that Bethesda had implemented in Fallout 4. You can also build settlements which are a massive upgrade from the likes of Hearthfire (the building focused dlc of Skyrim) that add even more hours to the game. Bethesda put a lot of detail in this department.
+ Future mod support
At the time of this review Bethesda has not released support for modding the game, but if we get the same amount of support that Skyrim had (if not more) then we're in for a treat. Skyrim is the king of all modded games when it comes to it's modding community, and I can't wait to see what modders will do with Fallout 4.
+ Voice diversity
Remember how everyone sounds the same in Skyrim? Yeah, the diversity of voice acting has improved.
+ Companions
The 13 companions in Fallout 4 area all unique and very detailed, however...
Cons:
- Stupid AI
...along with other NPCs, companions suffer from stupid AI, they run into walls, stand still while under fire, run straight into suicide bombers so much to the point that I use them as bait, and still block your path through doorways. Companions are especially stupid with melee weapons. Anyone who has Strong will know what I'm talking about.
- Watered down dialogue
Remember how we used to have over four dialogue choices at a time that were full sentences? Well Bethesda watered that down to a simple four choice system that doesn't tell you what you're actually going to say (similar to Bioware games) for no reason. Thankfully modding has already fixed this, and I would recommend anyone with this game to download Nexus and the "Full Dialogue Interface" mod.
- Watered down character upgrade system
There are no skills in Fallout 4, but instead the character upgrade system relies on the S.P.E.C.I.A.L system and perks. I don't think it really affects the balance of the game, but it hurts the game as an RPG and is less immersive.
- Armor diversity
The armor that you're going to be wearing (not counting power armor) is going to be either leather, metal, or combat armor, and that's it. You're characters are going to end up looking the same unless you make sacrifices for style. This is a smaller complaint, but one of the most frustrating for me.
Overall I would recommend this game to just about anyone, as it's a ton of fun. Thank you for reading my first review. I really think that user reviews are important feedback and hope to be making more in the future.

Fallout 4 is a great game. Yes, there are bugs and glitches. Yes, they've almost streamlined the RPG right out of what's supposed to be a futuristic open-world RPG/FPS hybrid. Yes, the writing is pretty much formulaic and feels like what someone that played Fallout 2 for 20 minutes tops might think Fallout is all about. And yes, they probably spent far too much time and effort on the settlement building aspect when the Wasteland Settler and Real Time Defense mods did it all so much better already.
But y'know what? Look past all that. Take a few minutes to explore the Commonwealth. Do a side-by-side comparison of the combat with Fallout 3. Enjoy the fact that we've been given such a large sandbox to play in. Savor the things that Bethesda really gets right. Immerse yourself in the post-Apocalypse. Quit trying to compare this game to one that came out almost 20 years ago. After all, without Bethesda wanting something to do between Elder Scrolls games, we wouldn't have any new Fallout at all. No, it's not quite the same as the old games, but it's something new, something different. But at the core, it's still Fallout. And it's still Bethesda.

Fallout 4 is a great time, and a solid step forward for Bethesda, showing promising evolution, yet there are mistakes made beyond the bugs.
Pros:
+ Visuals
I mean it would be awkward if the graphics weren't improved over Skyrim.
Graphics aside, the animations and lighting in this game are a treat.
+ Combat
Shooting, melee, power armor, V.A.T.S, and everything else from Fallout 3 has been ramped up. Making every part of combat more exciting and more comfortable.
+ Crafting and Settlements
You'll have a blast with weapon upgrades, armor upgrades, cooking food, cooking drugs, and upgrading in the now fantastic power armor system that Bethesda had implemented in Fallout 4. You can also build settlements which are a massive upgrade from the likes of Hearthfire (the building focused dlc of Skyrim) that add even more hours to the game. Bethesda put a lot of detail in this department.
+ Future mod support
At the time of this review Bethesda has not released support for modding the game, but if we get the same amount of support that Skyrim had (if not more) then we're in for a treat. Skyrim is the king of all modded games when it comes to it's modding community, and I can't wait to see what modders will do with Fallout 4.
+ Voice diversity
Remember how everyone sounds the same in Skyrim? Yeah, the diversity of voice acting has improved.
+ Companions
The 13 companions in Fallout 4 area all unique and very detailed, however...
Cons:
- Stupid AI
...along with other NPCs, companions suffer from stupid AI, they run into walls, stand still while under fire, run straight into suicide bombers so much to the point that I use them as bait, and still block your path through doorways. Companions are especially stupid with melee weapons. Anyone who has Strong will know what I'm talking about.
- Watered down dialogue
Remember how we used to have over four dialogue choices at a time that were full sentences? Well Bethesda watered that down to a simple four choice system that doesn't tell you what you're actually going to say (similar to Bioware games) for no reason. Thankfully modding has already fixed this, and I would recommend anyone with this game to download Nexus and the "Full Dialogue Interface" mod.
- Watered down character upgrade system
There are no skills in Fallout 4, but instead the character upgrade system relies on the S.P.E.C.I.A.L system and perks. I don't think it really affects the balance of the game, but it hurts the game as an RPG and is less immersive.
- Armor diversity
The armor that you're going to be wearing (not counting power armor) is going to be either leather, metal, or combat armor, and that's it. You're characters are going to end up looking the same unless you make sacrifices for style. This is a smaller complaint, but one of the most frustrating for me.
Overall I would recommend this game to just about anyone, as it's a ton of fun. Thank you for reading my first review. I really think that user reviews are important feedback and hope to be making more in the future.

Fallout has changed. Pretty much all of the episodes in this long-running series have sooner or later garnered some kind of a classic status, cult or otherwise. However, it seems like we've gone through at least one period of decay during the seven-year wait since the previous part.
Some things have improved. The combat system is the best it's ever been, the world has more colors than just grey and brown, character faces actually look decent and the glitches are at a record low. From a technical point of view, it is the best Fallout.
Some things have been added. You can craft modifications for your weapons and armor, and build your own bases in an elaborate construction mode. Most of the new systems didn't do much for me since I'm not a gear-oriented person; I only dabbled with armor modding and didn't build much anything unless the game forced my hand (which it unfortunately seems to do, if you wish to complete the main questline).
Most of it feels familiar. It's the same Fallout world with small warring factions, two-headed cows and bottlecaps. In many ways, firing up the game felt like coming home. A home that, while superficially looking the same as it ever was, ultimately proved to be strangely devoid of its earlier personality.
You see, for me, the essence of Fallout is the Wasteland. The environment is the true protagonist of the game. My character is just a vessel to explore and experience all the stories the Wasteland has to offer.
A lot of those stories have already been told -- I can recall multiple great little tales hidden far from the main storyline in the previous games. However, after finishing Fallout 4, no stories spring to mind. I was left with the feeling that while the Wasteland still looked authentic, it had started to wither from the inside.
I don't know. Maybe I did it wrong. My character steered clear from most of the recruit-starved organizations, stealthily tiptoeing in the shadows and finally choosing only one cause as her own. No companions journeyed with her. Equipped only with a merc attitude and a maxed Lone Wanderer perk, she eventually scoured 90% of the locations during a 60+ hour trek.
The Wasteland had lost some of its charm, or maybe gained too much of it. Most of the grittier elements seen previously in the series were nowhere to be found in Fallout 4. It was all too safe. Too politically correct. Downright jolly. I surprised even myself by choosing to reply "It's actually not that bad out there" during one late conversation.
Judged against previous Bethesda RPG's, I think Fallout 4 loses against both Skyrim and Fallout 3. Is it still a good time and money well spent? Yes. Will I be playing the DLC? Absolutely. But some of the radiance has been lost.
