Fallout 4 is a mockery of what the Fallout games used to be.
For Starters, the F4 (proceeded by Alt is what most Original Fallout fans should be pressing when seeing this crap online) game completely removed skills. Let's get this straight... A game that falls within the ROLE PLAYING GAME genre REMOVED skills. Yes, talk about dumbing the game down beyond belief. Aren't an "energy weapons" character but find a cool energy weapon? Who gives a♥♥♥♥♥♥ no skills here. Go ahead and do pretty much full damage with it regardless of the fact that your character hasn't used or specced into an energy weapon at all beforehand.
Dialogue is now broken down into "Yes, I'll do the quest", "Tell me more about the quest", "Snarky remark about the quest", and "No, I wont do the quest"... Not that saying no matters anyways, because this game is literally about the illusion of choice. In Fallout 2, you could actually join the Slavers and go on missions to enslave people. In F4, you can't even approach the "gunners" or "raiders" for dialogue because Bethesda determined that they are evil and you are not before the game was even launched.
How about Loot? Items gathered throughout the game that traditionally make an RPG feel more awesome as you go along by making your character increasingly more powerful? Well Bethesda introduced another giant F.U. to traditional Fallout fans by making the guns and armor in this game as homogenous as possible. One rifle, one Sniper Rifle, two shotguns (one of which clearly outclasses the other and basically invalidates it), etc etc. So what did they introduce instead? A crappy "mod" system that allows you to basically make your "Shotgun" a "Shotgun+", and then a "Shotgun++", and gave the game a random "legendary" system where you get crap that supposedly makes your game more unique by adding prefixes that they omitted from the crafting system to inflate the number of "guns" you can collect in each playthrough.
So what did F4 add to make the game so revolutionary? You can spend 50+ minutes crafting a character that you will see occasionally when the pre-canned dialogue pops up. You can play Sim City with your settlements that mean a total of jack crap outside of posting pictures on reddit of how cool you are for wasting 40+ hours of your life building something that no one other than you will ever appreciate.
Are the graphics better? Yes. Is the dialogue better voice acted? Yes. Is the gunplay better? Yes. There you go, 95% of the idiots that buy games now a days will be satisfied. Talk about pandering to the lowest common denominator. 20 million units sold no problemo.

Let me really mind ♥♥♥♥ you for a moment, you could fix up a car and use it to travel faster! This is a great addition to the reboot of the franchise. I have definately put my time in and am planning to put in much more.
Things I enjoy:
- I love the sandbox Fallout 4 lets me play in. I have already build a castle and have an army its pretty rad.
- If I take the time to run places and not fast travel the weather system + how landscapes are made = gorgeous vistas. So much so that I have several screen shots as desktop backgrounds.
- Base building? Did i mention this?
- The new perk system. It is a lot less of a "did I mess up my build" expereience since you can dump points each level into literally any stat. Beautiful
- The companions. They are very dynamic in this game. They all have different feels for the type of people that they are.
- The scale of the game and world. It's large, it takes a long time to move through the content
- Developer easter eggs. I have seen more teddy bears doing lewd and ridiculous things than I can count. Also skeletons dying in some pretty awkward poses and doing some very questionable things pre-war haha.
- Some of the bugs. For instance, Dogmeat came out of a swamp dog paddling and wouldn't stop until I entered a new area/ reloaded. I laughed very hard watching him try to crouch and dog paddle and look at me with a face like "dude what is happening!?". Moments like this can't be recreated just experienced.
The things I don't enjoy
- Lack of an excyclopedia/ reference material for the game. There are many features/ things that were added that haven't been discussed.
- Building alignment and the "snap" system of putting pieces together. While the base building is amazing trying to stack some things on top of other things is very difficult. It's like trying to stack 2 blocks on top of each other except you have not tools to smooth the edges to make things align just perfectly at the seams.
- Some of the bugs. The bug where my weapons vanish and I can't see my iron sights or melee weapons is a little agrivating albeit has a simple solution. Also the one I just experienced where I can only look left and right and lose the ability to look up and down in first person. Again this has a simple solution so I can ditch the whole "Wolfenstein 3d" feeling.
I am sure I missed some stuff and will update this as nessecary. Overall this is a great game to get immersed in if you are into post apocolypic do what it takes to survive type scenarios. Very excited to see what modders and DLC can bring to the table!

This is not an RPG, but it is probably the most fun I've ever had playing an FPS!
While I was certainly more than a little disappointed initially, after setting the game aside for a week or so and coming back to it with (as close as is possible) no expectations, I realized that Bethesda's apparent end game of creating a first person, interactive action movie is, if not currently finalized, an emotionally fulfilling experience in its own right.  Even the Minecraft like portion, which I usually find very annoying (seriously game developers, not everything has to be Minecraft, give it a rest), is engaging and fun!  Often times the only reason I'll stop building a town is because I have to go scav more material.  Crafting and modding weapons and armor feels more meaningful than it ever has before, quite possibly out of every game I've ever played.  The juxtapostition of the FPS combat system and VATS is certainly much more balanced than in the previous two Fallout titles, though it took me some time to fully appreciate this.
Things that are great about this game aside, I do get the odd pangs of RPG longing from time to time.  Charisma feels like a largely useless perk tree, although perhaps if maxxed out you might get to talk your way out of (or into) things.  I might be the only one buying Bethesda games anymore who feels this way, but I miss skill points.  Min/maxing is fun for me!  The dialogue wheel is terrible and though there is already a handy mod available through NMM that will help out, the four options lack depth.  This is somewhat understandable due to having voice actord record all the dialogue options (another blow to role-playing from my point of view), but I can't help but feel there could have been more thought put into this.  The stress of a looming deadline can kill creativity, though, that's for sure.
One last thing about the voice acting: the entertainment industry, movies and television as well as games, will always pick a generic target audience feel for voice/look/direction so that the target audience doesn't have to do too much work trying to empathize with the main character.  For AAA games, that means boring white guy.  While I'm sure Brian T Delaney is very talented, the direction he probably received was to be middle of the road.  If this is the sort of thing that is likely to bother you, play as a female.  Courtenay Taylor, while also very probably directed to be middle of the road, manages to emote in effective, small ways that has added so much to my playing experience.  Whether this was encouraged or merely tolerated by the director(s) I really couldn't say.
Anyway, that's my two cents.

First off, let me just state that buying this thing for disk is as pointless as buying Metal Gear Solid V on disk.
I tried to get past the 23 gigabytes of download and nope, it only installed 5 gigabytes of data than forced me to install the rest of the ♥♥♥♥ing game.
Any ways, onto the review. This game is the only thing I've been playing since I bought it. I sat on my♥♥♥♥♥for two days straight when I first got this game. I'm sad to say though, that it isn't as good as we all hyped it up to be. The game is bland, doesn't even live up to Bethesda's ruining of Fallout 3 inwhich they mess up the entire canon for Fallout.
Alright, gameplay is great at times. I love the shooting as it feels lively and active. Nothing feels too forced or clunky like Fallout 3 and New Vegas had problems with. I applaud Bethesda for keeping me interested through the entire game as not many RPGs from them or many others seem to do. The character creation is nice, but the game tricks you with the SPECIAL stats. You don't GET to DEVELOP your character, you get a crumby linear story idea that tricks you into thinking it's open world. With that being said, this game focus MUCH MUCH more on gameplay than story, which is incredibly unfortunate as I had hoped we were going to get more indepth with the lore. I'll get more into that in a bit.
The voice acting is, well it's wierd. They do an OK job at times, other times the main character's voice sounds like he's confused. Infact, the whole dialogue system? It's TERRIBLE. I had to get a mod to fix this and come to think of it, is Bethesda doing this on purpose for modders to fix their PURPOSEFUL mistakes? Who knows, wouldn't be surprising if it were true. Back to the topic at hand, it feels like your character is out of place from the entire world. He'll say something entirely irrelevant like he just had an angorism or something and the other characters will think it's ok and response normally. It just feels so badly organized and didn't have any effort put into it at times.
The music is probably the best bethesda's done. I love the soundtrack. But holy♥♥♥♥♥♥ they cheat ALOT for the radio. They reuse, and I counted, EIGHT SONGS FROM FALLOUT 3. EIGHT SONGS. If you haven't played Fallout 3, it'll be fine I guess. But come on, alot of fans are gonna get sick of it. And their is TOO few ones, or ones that just don't play enough. The host though, oh my god. At first I loved him. He was so much better than Three-Dog cause he wasn't howling into your ear constantly. Then you notice something really big. He repeats the news every frickin' second. Too few events happen and it made me turn off the radio, it sucks.
Finally, the story. You may not notice this, but this story is especially a vice versa version of Fallout 3. Seriously, if you havent played Fallout 3, it goes like this. !*SPOILER FREE*!
>In Vault
>Dad goes
>Go Find Dad
Now this is the first two acts of Fallout 4
>In Vault
>Son goes
>Go Find Son
That's it ladies and gentlemen. The story gets GOOD in Act 3 with Faction Tension. You have my favorite faction, The Minutemen. The FIXED Brotherhood of Steel, who hate the idea of charity and want to have full control of Technology. You have the Institute, these people who I won't go into that much but they make synths who are called boogeymen by the people of the Commonwealth due to how they kidnap people in the night. And finally, you have The Railroad, people who want to free synths as they believe they are sentient. The game begins to get more diplomatic and you really start to see each side to the factions and the bad they do.
AND OH YEAH, DID I MENTION IT USES THE CREATION ENGINE? AGAIN??? LOL! SAME ENGINE MEME.
Come the ♥♥♥♥ on Bethesda, make a new engine.
The game does a somewhat good job in keeping you in but I found myself bored after completing the game with nothing to do. The game has a♥♥♥♥♥♥performance when running on my GTX 960 which is ♥♥♥♥ing unbelievable. If you are a long time Fallout fan or enjoyed Vegas more than 3, this game is not gonna be for you. IT plays like a SHOOTER. Not the strategic diplomatic fallout we all know. When you get to act 3 it gets good but falls short as it's only 5 hours long in act 3. The game has SOME replayability but once you hit your 3rd playthrough, it's meh.
Again, Fallout fans will not be happy with the outcome of this one. Hopefully when the GECK comes around we'll see something interesting happen.

Gameplay - The games overall feel has changed from a crappy RPG feel to a modern FPS (it's still not perfect but it is much much much better)
AI - FAR FAR better, they actually take cover and makes the game far more challenging
Graphics - Up to personal opinion, but to me they look good, and you must remember that mods improve the visuals greatly, with minimal performance hit
Quests/Story - Quests are varied and interesting, and the main story line (if you havent had it spoiled for you) is brilliant, however the endings are not great. The main factions are very interesting and all the lines between good and evil are blured, as each faction is good and bad in certain repects, and i personally found choosing a faction a hard choice because of the moral questions each one poses
Settlements - Basically no tutorial, but once you know how it works it is very good and you can easily sink 10 hours into making your perfect settlement which will make certain resources for you and gain caps from traders + LOTS of vary different locations to make settlements
SPEECH - Both one of the best and worst features in the game, the new system makes conversations flow better and the voice acting makes all interactions feel more meaningful, making the main story line even better at many points. HOWEVER the options you are given are fairly limited and you will often wander what your character will say to people (NOTE: there is already a mod to fix this). It removes a fair amount of choice from the game, and you cannot really play pure evil like you could in new vegas for example
OVERALL - Amazing game, even better with mods, feels like a modern shooter with more an amazing story and so much content my 50+ hours of game time so far have only scratched it's surface

What Fallout 4 does right:
- Graphically speaking, I personally feel the game is more than adequate. I know that a lot of people are complaining that it isn't quite comparible to standards today, but I'm certainly not complaining. Hell, I run it at minimum settings and it still looks great.
-Combat: Nothing to complain or change with the combat system. I feel as though it lives up to standards and isn't lacking anywhere.
-environment: While I was always depressed by the environments of fallout, this one is no different, but I believe that is the point. The environment is obviously indicative of a post-apocalyptic world, one that was destroyed and has yet to truly rebuild. I've read some complaints that it should be a little cleaner, a little greener, and a little less destroyed, but let the lunacy of that sink in for a moment..
Now for what is "just there"
-New Settlement Build: While this is an obvious plus as far as I'm concerned, it's far too limited to be anything worth the trouble. You need to gather supplies from around the settlement or the world in order to build things. Fair enough, wouldn't question that. What I do question is the lack of "decent" things to build. Why are we only allowed horrifically damaged buildings, shacks, fences, etc, when there is plenty of wood around? While this may go against my previous point on the environment, let's not be confused with what I mean: the ability to add visually appealing things like log cabins would be a nice feature.
Not only that, but the way the invasions work is a little strange. From my experience, instead of charging at the settlement with a barrage of bullets and lazers, they simply "appear" in the middle of the settlement, completely bypassing fences, walls, turrets, etc. Something that kind of irritated me.
-Perk system: Don't get me wrong, I enjoy the way our perks earned. You level up and get to place one point into any perk to unlock the first stage of said perk. That being said, I don't like that you are not able to view the end results of perks that *may be of use* as opposed to perks you know you need. It's neither a hit nor a miss, but rather a refreshing change.
-radiation: Again, not quite a bad thing, but nothing I entirely enjoy either. The radiation system now directly effects how much max hp you have. Should you take a few nasty doses of rads, you now have that much less max health until you heal up. Personally, I prefer the old style of rads; take to many and your health isn't affected, but you'll gain negative buffs instead. I feel that they could have improved upon the old system, perhaps after so many rads, movement speed is reduced and visually wobbly, vision becomes blurred and you take increased damage. Maybe vomiting even, just for some added effect.
-Power Armor: Not really complaining about it, just not really used to the idea that power armor is no longer a true "armor" but now functions more or less as a highly mobile vehicle.
-Store: I never truly cared for any of the storylines of the fallout series, or even elderscrolls for that matter. It never captured my attention. I may be judging harshly however; a good storyline for me is one that compares to Chrono Trigger, a very difficult task to achieve.
And now for the negative..
-Bugs/glitches. This is the single worst part of the entire game. I've experienced more bugs and glitches than I can remember, ranging from the game freezing and suddenly teleporting me several minutes backwards and underground, to an annoying never ending gunfire noise. Let's not forget the most annoying ones of all: I don't have a lockpicking interface. That's right. I can't see what I'm doing when I pick a lock. There is nothing there, just a blank screen. I have to rely purely on sound to get the job done, which might actually be a positive note for realism, but an annoyance to say the least. I also have no power armor interface. I cannot see how much ammo I have left in powerarmor, or any general hud information at all to be honest. I was pretty disappointed when I learned that. Also noticed that everytime it storms, my screen turns white and everything has a strange delayed visual appearance. In other words, if I look at someone, it will take about 3 seconds for them to slowly appear into view, much the opposite of fading out of view. Several crashed, several bugs that required a savegame to be loaded, etc.
Final rating: on a scale, 7/10. While the game has it's horrific glitches and aggravating mishaps, it's still a fun and greatly enjoyable game. It lives up to the standard of other fallout games as far as I'm concerned. The story is a little bland and predictable, the game play is pretty solid, and the action is well rounded. There is always room for improvement, but I'm not sure if fallout 4 is the kind of game that will receive many contant patches. This is it, the open world action RPG I've been waiting for Bethesda to make, a clear evolutionary step forward in their developmental canon; from Bethsoft's clunky, dated-at-release origins with
and
to the lame disappointments that were
and
,
towers over them all; not even
's close-but-no-cigar execution can compare.
The writing is for once solid; not bad, not tolerable, but *solid*. I actually care about what's happening in this game world. The companions are lovely, present but without annoyance, always available for a quick chat or even a sarcastic quip along the way. Could the introduction be more open-ended? Sure, but it's a minor side complaint in comparison to the rest of the game.
Dialog roleplay? It's now an actual thing. Responses are less canned and without repetition and the player is given sufficient options to really make the PC their own person. Quests aren't railroaded anymore, either;  numerous ways to be completed or turned down.
Gameplay is leaps and bounds above any
game to-date, competent shooter action no matter which perspective you prefer; the gunplay feels 'right', I *adore* the gear upgrade system and paired with extremely clever, flank-heavy A.I. makes firefights and stealth a challenge, if not downright unapologetic. To top it all off, the combination of the classic S.P.E.C.I.A.L. stat system and modern perk choices works well, a beautifully blended merger of old and new.
Did I mention the game is gorgeous out of the box? Long gone is the brown and green smear or garrish, desaturated blue tint of past Bethsoft games, replaced with a vivid array of rusty and worn 1950s pastels, desolate woodlands, industrial relics and accurate east coast architecture. Even on a technical level it impresses; 2k textures, highly detailed and customizable character models, a plethora of well-tweaked DirectX 11 goodies, gorgeous lighting and color balance... this may very well be the first title Bethesda has released where I honestly will never touch the visuals in any way.
On the subject of music: both the original score and radio selections are wonderfully lush and atmospheric. Physical release, please!
That said,
isn't without issues. As usual, Creation Engine's early 00s Gamebryo origins creak at every step; the launch week stuttering returns again, textures have a habit of streaming in too slow and performance is relatively poor despite exceeding recommended requirements. Thankfully in-game bugs have been minimal and I've yet to encounter anything game-breaking, though others have not been as fortunate.
Settlement building is... a hassle to say the least, significantly limited by its underwhelming GUI; supply routes and resource management are the biggest tedium and more building/furniture options would have been a welcome addition. Better visual customization for the Pip-Boy (or even an option to straight up hide the almost endearingly clunky thing) is on the wishlist, as well, and the removal of visibly holstered weapons is baffling when so much time was spent on an in-depth customization system for gear.
These flaws, however, do not detract from the engrossing experience that
manages to be. If the past creations of Bethesda Softworks disappointed or angered, then I dare say check this one out; it's near-brilliant.

I, like many others who have posted a review here, am simply confounded by the negative reactions this game has got. Granted, there are disappointing elements if you are a die-hard RPG fan, as many of the more enticing aspects of the genre which were present in the past titles are not in this one -- I won't go into detail about them, others have done more than enough of that already. What I do want to mention, however, is how much Fallout 4 is bringing into the franchise with its crafting, MUCH better combat, more dense exploration, etc. The sound is top notch as are the visuals(the latter surely[and oddly]being a point of contention for many), and there is a plethora of small details too specific and numerous to mention that make all the difference when you notice the improvement they bring vis-a-vis its predecessor.
Indeed, Bethesda took some chances with Fallout 4, doing some things they'd never done before. Some of them aren't great and at times annoying, but they become trite when taking into account all the positive you get at the same time. Complaining about it is kind of like if someone gave you a top-notch 5-star meal in the best restaurant and you start belly-aching about the color of the tablecloth. Just suck it up and enjoy it! Heartily recommended.

Pros:
> Very large, and dense map with tons to explore. The detail in this game is amazing.
> Lots of quests. The main story is pretty interesting.
> Combat feels much more exciting comparative to other Bethesda games.
> Weapon, and armor customizations.
> Lots of perks that offer many different ways to play the game. Stealth, brawler, sniper, and anywhere inbetween.
> Enjoyable characters. Every companion has a story to tell, a perk to give, and some quests to complete.
> Graphics are amazing comparative to other Bethesda games but definitly no Forstbite quality.
> Very immersive. I've put in 150 hours since release, this game has no problem drawing you in.
> SETTLEMENTS. You can essentially create your own city just about anywhere. there are TONS of places to build.
> Every Junk item in the game now has a purpose, this can either be a Pro or a Con depending on how you look at it. You can pick them up, haul them back to your settlement and get anything from Steel and Wood to Cloth and Leather. All of these items are used to build and mod weapons and armor.
> Character creation is also pretty nice. You can make your character look like a super model or something out of your nightmares.
> Armor layering. You can layer different parts of armor if you are wearing clothes that are thin enough. You have Right arms, Left arms, Right legs, Left legs, Head armor, and Chest pieces. There are many different kinds so you can mix and match them as you please.
> Legendary are items with special abilities such as an armor piece that gives you +1Agility and +1Perception. Or a weapon that fires an extra projectile. These are dropped from Legendary enemies that are harder to kill than normal enemies.
> No level cap. You can just keep going, and going and never stop leveling. Of course gaining XP does get harder as you progress so at some point you may find that it's so slow that you may just want to make a new character. I'm currently level 70 and it took me 150 hours. Of course by that level I had already had all the perks to make my Stealth character effective so I just started picking random perks that sounded interesting.
Cons:
> They've downgraded from the old Fallout/Skyrim way where you have many different options from nice-evil to a dialogue wheel... You're choices are limited and vague so you have to pick 1 of 4 options that you have no idea what the character is going to say. You may pick something like "I dont know." and get "I don't f*****g know, go screw yourself". The dialogue wheel is incredibly restricting and it really makes it hard for the character to feel like your own when you are so limited.
> There isn't a way to play this game as a villian. You are pretty much forced into playing the good guy, you never get the option to just screw someone over.
> There are only rare cases where you can use your perk levels to get special dialogue. You never get the chance to use your level 10 intelligence for special dialogue so often times you may end up feeling like your character is a moron even they opperate on a completely different level from everyone else.
> As of the time of writing this review the game runs at a mediocre level. I'm playing on Ultra with a GTX 970, 16GB of ram, and an i5-4460 CPU and get down to 30 fps while I'm in the city. I've sort of fixed the game a little by spending hours researching and troubleshooting. I had to uncap the game from 60fps in the Falloutprefs.ini only to find out that for whatever reason the framerate is tied to the speed of the game so when I started getting 140 fps the game turned into Sonic Adventures. I then RE-capped the fps to 60 using a different program, I also had to change the game to Fullscreen, turn Godrays to Low, change Shadow Distance to medium, add some times to my Fallout.ini and Falloutprefs.ini. I mostly get 60 fps now but sometimes when I get onto a really high building and look around my frames drop down to about 40-45 range.
> During the story I felt like I really didn't have much control over the situation. There were times where I wish I could just tell certain people to screw off, or make someone change their mind, but the game really never lets you do this. As the person that is in the seat of power in all of the major factions you would think that you'd be able to tell someone "no, I don't really think we should screw these guys over" but the game says screw you, I don't care if you want to destroy these guys or not, you WILL DO IT if you want to complete the story. Essentially the game guides you on rails but you can pick between which set of rails you want to be on but most of them are pretty much the same thing. I wanted to be able to negotiate some sort of peace between all of the factions or something close to it but the game absolutely will not allow it.
> I miss the Hardcore mode from New Vegas where you've got to eat food, sleep, drink water, and you and your enemies die in only a bullet or two. The Survival mode in this game simply increases the damage of enemies and makes them more bullet spongy.
CONCLUSION:
I feel like this game is definitly worth $60. I've had a blast playing this game since release and I haven't even really gotten to far into the game, I've played through ONE of the endings in 150 hours. 150 hours on one ONE CHARACTER. There are still many more play styles I wish to try so I'll definitly be making more, unique, characters such as a Mike Tyson build where I only use unarmed weapons and beat the crap out of anyone who apposes me. Typically by this time in past Elder Scroll, and Fallout games I've already made 5 different characters but this game really draws you in; so much so, that you become so attached to your current character that you may not even want to make a new one. If you like Fallout or the Elder Scrolls, BUY THIS GAME. If you like Mass Effect, watch some gameplay first but I'm willing to bet you'll be interested in this game. And if there is something you don't like about the game you can bet that there WILL be a mod to fix it just like in the past games.

Here is my spoiler free review of Fallout 4. I want to only include 3D Fallout Games (3 and New Vegas) in any comparisons. Fallout 1, 2, and Tactics are very different.
* Story - This is where Fallout 4 falls short the most. The main story is disappointing from beginning to middle to end. The execution is very similar if not the same as New Vegas, but the plot is very dry lacking urgency. The characters are based on age old tropes making the Fallout 4 storytelling experience even more predictable than before. All antagonists (depending on how you play the game) are more of the same cookie cutter stock characters.
Fallout Ranking: NV > 4 > 3
* Dialog - Unfortunately, the dialog system in Fallout 4 is inspired by Mass Effect. This is a huge step back from the series. The player basically have four tones, each leading to the same result, but in different attitudes. No matter what dialog branch you pick, it will lead to the same outcome so dialog has no stake in gameplay. The dialog itself isn't very memorable. The sarcastic option lacks humor. The other options are well... are there... The void acting performance is okay. Only one performance in particular (you will know it when you hear it) is really worth noting.
Fallout Ranking: NV > 3 > 4
* Graphics – There are a lot of negative comments surrounded by the game's aesthetics. But before making any judgment, there are tradeoffs between making decent textures and having an intractable world. Fallout 4 manages to do just that. By comparing the graphics by it's predecessors, Fallout 4 does feel like a “Next Gen” game with weather effects, volumetric lighting, depth of field, and detailed shadows. However, I definitely recommend using a SweetFX mod to make textures more vivid without sacrificing performance.
Fallout Ranking: 4 > NV > 3
* Audio/Score – The score fits and sounds like other fallout games. It's not memorable as Skyrim or Dark Souls, but it's not nauseating.
Fallout Ranking: 3 = 4 = NV
* RPG Elements – I found Fallout 4 to be extremely balanced. In Fallout 3 and mostly New Vegas, there was a clear optimal path for completing missions. Fallout 4 is like almost every western RPG where you gain experience and level up through combat, exploration, and quest completion. You designate points to seven categories called S.P.E.C.I.A.L: Strength, Perception, Endurance, Charisma, Intelligence, Agility, and Luck. In previous fallout games, the route to go would be to buff intelligence for early XP bonuses and spend the rest on Perception and Endurance. Fallout 4 is much more balance. Each category are equally important. This is great because this allows the player to make builds more effectively. On top of that, there is a perk system where you get to choose from list of perks as you level up. The perk system was also a step up from the previous games because more than half of the perks are actually useful.
Fallout Ranking: 4 > NV > 3
* Exploration: This is where Fallout 4 really shines. Initially I was disappointed that there were only a small handful of cities to explore, but Fallout 4 focuses more on the wasteland aspect. The variety of places to go for loot and exploration is much higher than Fallout 3 and New Vegas. You'll encounter gas stations, restaurants, shopping areas, hospitals, schools, junk yards, boats, and much more. Each area keeps the post apocalyptic atmosphere, but with different flavors.
Fallout Ranking: 4 > NV > 3
* Armor and Weaponry – Fallout 4 adopts a weapon model very similar, but much much better than the Borderland series. Weapons are automatically generated based on a handful of components. For an example: you might pick up a 10 mm suppressed pistol in one area and a 10 mm glow in the dark scope pistol in another. Along with randomly generated weapons, there are legendary weapons with special perks. Armor is similar to weapons in that it has randomly generated loot. However there are fewer armor components, which means less variation. However, power armor makes up for this. Power armor is a different set of armor that allows taking heavy damage at the expense of a rare item called fusion cores. You can modify weapon and armor components with a nifty crafting system. Usually I ignore crafting systems in most games, but Fallout 4 is an exception. You'll encounter relatively tough enemies early and mid game that force most players to use the weapon and armor crafting system.
Fallout Ranking: 4 > NV > 3
* Combat – There are two ways to approach combat: VATS and plain old FPS. VATS allows for a more turned based approached to combat. Players will get to slow down movement and choose a specific target on the enemy. Players are assigned action points which dictates how many targets you choose at once. In early game, players will have a low AP cool down rate and fewer AP slots, which discourages the use VATS. The FPS combat is a huge improvement from the old and plays like any regular FPS at a much slower pace. The enemies are more or less the same as before: super mutants, raiders, and the occasional death claw. The only difference is an introduction of one new enemy type and legendary enemies. Killing a legendary enemy will have a high chance of dropping legendary loot. You can tag a companion along for the fights. My only complaint is the path finding for companions.
Fallout Ranking: 4 = NV > 3
* Interface – The biggest improvement on the UI side is that you don't have to open every container to find out what is in it. When you hover over a container it will automatically show what is inside and sorted by value. Cancel menus can be a bit of pain. The pip boy and terminal UI is strange as you can't use arrow keys or WASD to traverse through menu items or scroll the perk chart. It is something that requires getting use to.
Fallout Ranking: 4 = NV = 3
* Questing: This is Bethesda we're talking about. Most of the quests involves going somewhere, killing someone or getting something, and reporting back. Usually the motivation for completing quests is to advance the story. Although I am not big fan of Fallout 4 story, I will commend their approach towards the end of the quest as you can jump ship and betray your faction based on non-scripted actions. This adds to the much needed extra immersion to the game.
Fallout Ranking: NV > 4 > 3
* Technical Issues: Fallout 4 is riddled with bugs so save often. I recommend saving before every quest and letting autosave do the rest. The clipping issues, I can forgive, but the potentially game breaking bugs that can potentially mean hours of waste time. One of the more serious bugs I encounter is going up an elevator, clipping my character, and causing my character to immediately die. Luckily I learned from Fallout New Vegas to save often. Another more serious bug is that I wasn't able to turn in a particular side quest because I performed tasks in a different order. Apparently a lot of players had the same issue and were forced to use console commands.
Fallout Ranking: 3 > NV > 4
* Extras – I have mentioned before that Fallout had a base building system. This feature is more than welcomed and is lightly required in a few quests. The base building UI takes a lot of getting use to. There is a learning curve if you want to take advantage of all of the benefits that base building has to offer. For an example: you'll have to learn how to power a string of lights efficient using power generators.
Fallout Ranking: 4 > NV = 3
Final Consensus: Despite Fallout 4 lackluster story, occasional glitches, and terrible dialog options, it still manages to be a great game by heavily improving exploration, armor, and weaponry. The rewarding combat system and the beautiful Boston wasteland as well as the base building feature makes the game hard to ignore even with a sixty dollar price tag.
Fallout Ranking: NV > 4 > 3

Fallout 4 is very different from Fallout 3 and New Vegas. There are many changes that deviate from the previous formula, but at the same time it is refreshing to have this different style of gameplay. This review is based on the initial release from the first week of sale where many bugs and performance issues will likely be patched by the time this is posted.
Graphics
At the time of this review I didn’t have the best equipment, but I would say this game still ran very well. On my older machine with an i7-3770K @ 3.5 GHZ, 16GB RAM and a 4GB GTX 680 I was able to run it on very high at 1920x1080 with 55-60 FPS average. Textures and Lighting on Ultra with God rays on Medium, everything else on High.
Fallout 4 generally has a nicely mixed color pallet that shows a vibrant outdoor environment while maintaining a darker, gritty post-apocalyptic cityscape.
Gameplay
The S.P.E.C.I.A.L. systems was changed to a skill tree type system similar to Skyrim. Perks are now managed in a branching pattern based on points allocated to S.P.E.C.I.A.L. While this might diminish strategic character planning, it allows one to explore a wider variety of skills.
Rather than pause gameplay, V.A.T.S. just slows down time now. Action points can now also be used for sprinting which can be useful at putting some distance from melee attackers.
Power armor is now a tank-like exo-suit that you enter rather than “wear” as it was in past games. Although it is introduced early on in the story, the usage is limited by fusion cores that drain when the suit is in motion. All the individual components are now independently customizable and can be interchanged with other variants of the armor.
A big change is that weapons and armor no longer degrade with use. This was likely done in conjunction with the new crafting system that enables players to upgrade base weapons and armor as they progress through the game.
The new crafting system for weapons and armor is fairly well done. There should have been a more in depth tutorial but it’s not too difficult to figure out with a bit of tinkering. Once you have the right skills and materials it opens up a lot of customization options. Workbenches for this are widespread and easily accessible.
Crafting settlements is far trickier and I feel was poorly implemented. This can take a lot of trial and error to figure out but once the initial learning curve is past, it’s fairly straightforward. However this is a mechanic that easily suffers from rinse-and-repeat and after one or two major developments, it can become tediously repetitive.
The basic map (precluding any DLC) is not as large as in previous titles, but it is more densely packed with things. Settlement areas are more common and the ruins of Boston are teeming with various factions throughout.
To sum it up: I enjoyed my time with Fallout 4 so far and will definitely spend many more hours with my main character. There’s plenty to do story and quest-wise but one can also easily spend hours searching for specific materials to modify weapons and armors or just take a walk off the beaten path. Fallout 4 introduces some major changes to the series which I find overall are good and progressive. The only glitch I had encountered by the time of posting was two occasions of disappearing pip-boy and weapons textures, but a reload remedied the situation each time.

Now let's write something a bit more interesting ( spoilers ).
From the start, playing F4 was some kind of rollercoaster : one day it was good, the day after I did a main quest and saw the terrible writing and lack of choice, then I went exploring some nice building and it was good again, just to be giving a random fetch and kill quest in the same location a few hours after.
The beginning was nice, even if the graphics are not top notch, it's a Bethesda game so I didn't expected better ( it's still a huge improvement compared to F3/NV ). They improved the character creation since Skyrim at least, and I really like the voiced protagonist, the woman at least has a nice voice ( it's the same actress who voiced Jack in Mass Effect ). It's just too bad that they had to dumb down the dialogue and choices for that, because with a bit more effort they could have done better. If you install the mod to see what your character is going to say instead of having the dialogue "wheel", you'll notice that most of the time, they just recorded the same answer 4 times with slight changes... which is stupid and useless.
After the intro, once in the Vault I had to fight several hours to get the game running at 60FPS. I tweaked the ini and managed to get 60 FPS at 1080p in fullscreen with Vsync on.
And then I was finally able to start my journey... unfortunatelly, even if I got hooked after some hours ( I just love wandering in open worlds, I can't help it ), the cons quickly started to outweight the pros. I still had hope, and then I went to the institute, met Shaun, saw the poor and unoriginal plot twists ( and badly explained plot holes ), and what made me gave up was the total inability to ask important questions to NPCs, and the total lack of any reaction to my actions and knowledge of anything ( for example ( spoiler ahead ) I killed old Shaun and everybody in the Institute before building Liberty Prime, and nobody at the BoS gave a ♥♥♥♥ about it. Like, I killed the goddamn leader of the opposing faction and nobody noticed ).
PROS :
- better character creation than other Bethesda games
- plenty of weapons to have fun with
- crafting and customization
- exploration is still good, even if the setting of a post-apo world in a city makes a lot of areas kinda the same.
- FPS elements have been improved
- some nice NPCs with good voice acting ( Piper, Codsworth )
- a few nice quests with a funny tone, like the one with the robots and the flying ship
- aliens
CONS :
- bugs, glitches
- terrible AI and pathfinding ( NPC walking into walls everywhere, ennemies constantly strafing, companion always blocking the path, etc. )
- game and story breaking bugs
- ugly NPCs with extra low res textures ( the old woman at the beginning, Nick Valentine )
- annoying NPCs and companions who won't STFU for a second, commenting on everything
- stupid and useless dialogues limiting roleplay and choices
- did I mention bugs ? Even the ones preventing you from finishing the game after playing for 2 weeks ?
- no NPC seems to have any real motivations outside destroying everything that is not like them.
- too many stuff makes no sense and are poorly explained, or not explained at all.
- weak story and factions
- 99% of fetch and kill quests, even in the main story ( having to fetch a magnet for Liberty Prime when there are some available in the BoS stock room ? Really ? That's just an excuse to make the game longer ).
- hardlocked key mapping not made for azerty keyboards ( can't move in construction mode, game has not even been tested ).
- settlements are nice but ultimatelly useless
- no main character motivation. Why would I care about a 60 years old man acting as my son ? We didn't have time to love him when he was a kid, and when we meet him it's too late.
- ennemies have super senses and can hear you walk silently through 3 floors in buildings, and can spot you from 300m in the dark, no matter if you're level 1 or level 40 with all the skills, shadowed armor and muffled boots.
- legendary ennemies makes no sense in this world, and their loot makes no sense either ( a legendary radroach dropping a gun ? I killed it in one shot, how was that legendary ? ). Also, legendary Synths can mutate... What ? How ?
- UI is painful to use and badly designed
- no skill checks in dialogues
...
Damn, this list would take too much time so I'll just stop here. It's really too bad, because they could make a great game with that. But it feels like those guys watched Blade Runner and skipped the interesting parts just to keep the action, without trying to understand the story...
It's a waste, and I fear for the future games. Especially because so much people have so low standards that they would call this GOTY...

Overview:
Offline, I have played this game for ~12+ hours. The story isn't the greatest, but the gameplay and quests are really fun. I find Fallout 4 well made with only several annoying bugs.
Cons:
> Low performance computers will find a big struggle playing the game. I would recommend Intel i7 with 6gb ram or better.
> There are some bugs that might disable you from completing some quests. I haven't seen any main-quest breaking bugs.
> Deathclaws are now scary and deadly (might be a pro for some).
Pros:
> Graphics look really nice (if your computer can handle them).
> Gameplay and fighting has improved some since Fallout 3 and New Vegas.
> The game is decently long without completing any side quests.
> The game still has a console that can be used to manipulate the game (if you are about that life).
> The map is very big and DLC may increase its size in the future.
Conclusion:
Fallout 4 is like Skyrim but takes place in a post-apocalyptic wasteland. If you have enjoyed Fallout 3, or enjoy role playing games, then Fallout 4 isn't a waste of money.

Go have a read of the negative reviews. They are so, so hyperbolic they make no sense and completely ruin the credibility that any of the authors may have had. After reading 10 or so, the primary focus is "It lost it's RPG elements!" and for most people, that's perfectly fine. Most of the negative reviewers would have sad the same thing about Fallout 3 or Fallout New Vegas... Had they actually played those games!
They picked up FO4 with the mindset of "Oh, this should be a depressing, drab, atmospheric story-driven RPG game that forces me to make moral decisions like a Tell Tale game!" Well this isn't a Tell Tale cinematic experience. This is a video game designed to be replayable and fun with an enjoyable combat system and hefty amount of sidequests.
That being said, great game so far. I would recomend it to Fallout 3 and Fallout New Vegas fans. The atmosphere of "Damn, this place is ♥♥♥♥ing♥♥♥♥♥♥quot; really came back a little in this title from Fallout 3, which I loved immensely. Always great fun making your way to a quest beacon as there's 3-4 firefights and a mini-nuke detonating at any given time between some raiders and mutants, just like the old capital wasteland.

If you liked Fallout 3, you will like this game.
At 98 hours in, I have not even finished the story yet because of how many other interesting things there are to do in this game.  The attention to detail that the devs put into every area you visit is astounding.  I have yet to run into a new area where I felt like I had been there before because it's exactly like the last 100 caves with monsters.  All the little details and easter-eggs they put into each place make it fun to keep exploring.
It's somewhat true that a lot of the quests involve killing raiders (or mutants, or ghouls...), but there are quests and other events that can be resolved peacefully (or stealthily) with the right character builds.
The only disappointing part of the experience is the dialogue system which has been made into yet another console-friendly 4 choice system with little to no description of what you're character is actually going to say.  Even though some of the conversations have deceptively good dialogue options, it's hard to see them with that dumbed down system.
The complaints about the Perk Chart and how they got rid of the Skill system are largely unfounded.  Just like with the skill systems in Fallout 3 and NV, if you want to be good at something, you need to pick S.P.E.C.I.A.L. stats and perks that support that activity.  Even though there is no level cap, it would take an obscene amount of play time to be good at everything, so what you pick each level definitely matters.
Overall, I highly recommend this game.  It's fun, quirky and exciting to play.

After spending some time critically analysing the game I simply can't recommend it.
The Story is absolute garbage, and for a game and series that's supposed to be an RPG it is one of the worst possible "role play" simulators. Players have little to no room to create their own character's identity and who they want to be. You're either a mom who might be an ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ or a good guy looking for their son, or a dad in the same roles.
Meanwhile NV and Skyrim lets the player have complete leeway with what you want your character to be, you're essentially given a blank slate to do with as you please, the only things that bind you to your role are the fact that you're a courier, or that you're the Dragonborn. There's no real set role that you're forced to follow.
The mechanics in the game are god awful, factions and karma were just completely removed from the game when that's one of the major plot points of these games. You could go walking into a Legion camp in NCR gear and they'd immediately attack you on sight even if you have good karma or unless you're doing a specific quest.
Fallout 3 even had roughly the same thing, but more in the ways of the BOS and the Enclave having radically opposed views and siding with either side would test the others tolerance of you.
Fallout 4 gives you 3 or 4 different factions, 1 of which serves little to no purpose as you can never fully make it recover. The other 3, no matter what you do, will always have to be killed off for a faction's questline. Doing a number of missions will make you hated by both and etc., NV and Fallout 3 had a plethora of factions that you constantly had to make sure that you're either in good or bad standing in order to fulfill whatever role you wanted to fill.
For instance, everyone in Freeside will love you if you kill the thugs and attack the NCR. However, attacking the NCR would also make them less likely to cooperate with you, and if you're really unlucky, even send out hit teams to you. The closest Fallout 4 gets to that is with the Synths teleporting around, but they're not a coordinated group or faction trigger. If you side with one of the factions for too long you're just immediately attacked no matter what, nevermind that they attack you even if you plan to join the Institute.
The story (not the role playing elements) is complete and utter garbage. You're forced to kill Kellog, only to discover shortly afterward that he wasn't that bad of a guy, Bethesda just wants to guilt trip you despite only encountering this character once, and having no backstory until after you kill him. Fallout New Vegas and Fallout 3 at least allow you the option of talking major villians into surrendering or killing themselves after learning more about them. Colonel autumn in Fallout 3 can be talked out of the final battle at the water purification plant if you have high enough speech, and this is after you have the potential of learning more about him while you're in the Enclave base. In Fallout New Vegas you can learn more about Benny before potentially killing him, or even have him run away where he's captured by Caesar's Legion, and then you can help him fight Caesar and his body guards to get away and essentially forgive him for trying to kill you.
Unique items are almost completely gone, now all you have are these stupid "legendary" weapons and armor that give % increases to damage types or defense. The unique weapons are by far one of the coolest bits about the other 2 Fallout games, nevermind that New Vegas was able to both add unique weapons and weapon modding into the game, albeit to a lesser extent than fallout 4, but at the same time the mods were more useful and weren't locked behind ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t perk tiers. You could just go to the GunRunners, find a mod for a weapon you have, buy it, and install it immediately. Fallout 4 you have to grind for levels and perks (not to mention the stupidity of being able to level up SPECIAL perks) as well as items in order to craft a single mod for a weapon that may not even make the weapon all that much better.
last couple bits are grouped together, but 1. The UI is garbage, half the time I can't even see what the hell it's supposed to read out, combine that with the need for animations for everything and you've got a 2-3 second long animation for healing in the middle of a firefight. 2. The settlement system is ♥♥♥♥ing god awful without mods, building good looking buildings and towns is next to impossible. Recruiting people to said settlements is a pain in the♥♥♥♥♥ and there's close to no benefit to doing any of it unless you waste a lot of time and effort into building and maintaining as many as possible. 3. Power armor in Fallout 4 is garbage, Fallout 3 and NV had the right idea in making it able to wear only with proper training, allowing for it to be a power armor choice in the mid to late game, Fallout 4 you get a full suit (albeit half charged)  in the beginning of the ♥♥♥♥ing game, and with no training whatsoever. Fusion Cores are also incredibly easy to get once you know where to look, nevermind the fact that you can also buy them from literally just about every vendor in the ♥♥♥♥ing game.
Add on top of all of that Bethesda's attempted monopoly on mods for the game by trying to force you to use their ♥♥♥♥♥♥ service (which also stole mods from other people, most notably xbox users stealing well known pc creator's mods and passing them off as their own. This was also done multiple times to the same mod) the same service which would also block your ability to unlock achievements if your game was modded. Luckily as always the modding community got around this within a few days of this ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t, but regardless it's a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ thing to do and should devalue anything they promise in the future.
Despite all this It's got decent gun mechanics despite ever rifle being left handed for some weird ♥♥♥♥ing reason, and their third person camera was significantly improved considering it was absolutely abysmal in every other game both in fallout and elder scrolls.

The new mechanics bring the fallout experience to life, and allow almost infinite replayability, however the vagueness of the dialogue options make conversing with NPC’s frustrating, and role playing difficult. In conclusion I would definitely recommend the game, and additionally recommend that Bethesda fully display the lines, and tone of dialogue, in future games.

After 36 hours sunk in to the game, I THINK I finally have enough insight to write a review.
To preface: I'm going to be making comparisons to other fallouts, specifically the "Modern" Fallout games. Fallout 1, 2, and tactics aren't gonna be mentioned here. So if i say one has the best asthetic, or the best story of all the games, know it's just out of the newest three: 3, NV, and 4. Also, I will not be covering the story as to avoid all potential spoilers. All I'll say is that I prefer fallout 3 and NV's stories to it in the end, due to predictability.
Alright, let's start with the meat of the game. The gameplay. Fallout 4 probably has the best gunplay of all three games, without a doubt. Vats doesn't feel like a necessity: Hell, there were times I went hours without even opening it. Sure, the shooting is still kinda dodgy, but it's vastly superior to what we saw in the prior titles. Melee combat is stll barebones, the expected 'Left click to bash guy' stuff, though that doesn't mean it was ignored from the upgrade. Enemies will parry your attacks, you can parry theirs, some enemies pretty much block attacks if you hit them in a certain way (I'm looking at you, mirelurks), etc. Another feature they added was a dedicated grenade button. Unlike in 3 and vegas where you had to equip them like any other weapon to toss them out, you can equip a grenade, along with a weapon at once. Some people say that they've watered down fallout to a generic FPS by focusing on the gunplay by doing changes like this, but I can't seem to imagine why. As long as they don't pass over other aspects to make the gunplay better, it's all good to me... Don't worry, we'll touch on that subject further in.
Next on gameplay, but shifting more to the less action-y side of things, the new dialogue systems is admittedly a step down from the prior installments. The only stat that can really be shown naturally is charisma checks, which are sorted in difficulty from yellow, to orange, to red- red being the hardest. One nitpick here is that due to the real-time dialogue system, you can just save when you see a C.Check is available, and keep clicking it and reloading that save before you get it right. I'm guilty of this, I won't lie (I just wanted that Piper romance, a'ight?). Another nitpick, it just that the whole dialogue wheel feels out of place when you consider the series' roots. People make jokes about mass effect and hurhur haha SHEPARD WREX HUR, but at least mass effect's dialogue wheel had some sort of impact. I told one of the first NPCs to basically ♥♥♥♥ off and die, and the next time I saw him he was happy as can be to see me. Just... Did you forget what I said to you? Yeesh. It just makes a lot of your choices seem like they had no effect. Not to say that there AREN'T any dialogue choices that have effect, just that a majorty left me scratching my head.
And, on the note of dalogue... Voiced protagonist. This has to be one of those most debated tid-bits in this game. Some hate it, some love it, and others don't really care either way.  I, personally, like the voiced protagonists. They're great actors, and I love the way they deliver most of their lines. Of course, such a thing doesn't come in without bringing some limitatons. People fear that they will mis-represent their choicies due to their tones of voice. They're expecting a calm reaction, instead the character explodes- or vice versa. While I can see that being a HUGE problem, I PERSONALLY never experienced such a disconnect. Back on the note of the dialogue wheel, odds are, it was introduced sheerly due to this addition, bethesda probably knowing that recording the amount of dialogue that was in games like 3 or new vegas would take a LOT longer than if they only had 4 options for most situations. People also have speculated that due to the higher emphasis on gameplay, the dialogue wheel was introduced. If anything, this could POTENTIALLY be an alright trade off, depending on your beliefs/tastes.
Next up, the crafting. Dear GOD the crafting. Customizing weapons feels much more important than it was in new vegas where it was introduced. Next to no npc in the waste will have a 'Hunting rifle' or a 'Combat shotgun', it will likely be modified in some way. Shorter/longer stocks, scopes, bayonets, different receivers, muzzles, barrels- you name it. Having that one special weapon in your arsenal really DOES feel special in this game. You can even name your beloved Scum-Shooting 10mm pistol exactly that if you so desire. There are also melee weapon and armor mods to accompany this, so if you collect enough materals, you can deck yourself out in the best of the best armor in the commonwealth. This also adds on to the fact that every little item has a purpose now. Junk around the wasteland can be collected for various crafting materials, and there's even a function to tag items baring components you need with a small magnifying glass icon near their name, so you can pick em' up when you're bartering or exploring.
On the note of crafting, lets transition to the base-building aspect of the game. To quote our lord and savior, Todd Howard, "It just works." And he wasn't joking. Sure, it's not exactly the BEST building system out there, but it really does work. I'm especially having fun building my small city on an island, allowing my lovely people to fend off mirelurk attacks accompanied by an army of rocket-turrets. How it works, is after clearing some areas, you gain access to a workshop. From then on, holding (Default) V will bring up a build menu for you to work with. My main problem with this system is that you can still DIE while building. So, if you feel the need to make a giant tower in to the sky, dear god save often. Because if you fall off, your legs will shatter like fine china. A fun fact, if you really just want to have fun building without the worry of materials, pop in to the console and toggle god mode. This'll give you unlimited building materials while its on. I did this myself to see exactly what I could manage to build with that kind of power, and I have to say, it's pretty easy to lose track of time when your settlement starts taking shape.
In closing, I personally like fallout 4. Sure, it has dummed down a lot of things, but at the same time, it's refined and added a lot as well. From my perspective; this is just a phase where bethesda is figuring everything out. Fallout 4 is that awkward middle entry that's trying radical, out-stretching new things to try and find out if people like them- a mold-breaker, if you will. After seeing everyone's criticisms, I'm sure that one of several things may happen. One, they could improve upon all of this in fallout 5 or some other sequel, combining the good from 4 and it's predecessors in to a masterpiece. Two, they could tweak some of these problems with their upcoming updates and DLC. Or 3, they could just. You know. Not learn anything, and take the money and run. Let's pray for the prior. So yes, I recommend fallout 4, despite some of its flaws.  just left the whole experience with a smile on my face, so I can't really NOT recommend it. And there's a lot I skimmed over in this review, I just summed up MY views and beliefs. If you want more, I'm sure someone else in the reviews here has your answer.

I was quite confused when I saw all the negative reviews for this game, as so far for me it has proved to be nothing less than spectacular. I soon spotted a common theme that featured in all of these negative review; it seemed that what most people were losing their tampons over was the simplified dialogue system. Now I have never played a Fallout game before this, so I have no idea what it was like before, but for me this is the optimum way of communicating. I would say that the way that the game narrows down dialogue is perfect, it allows you to convey a wide range of opinions without having to tediously scroll through many speciffic phrases, most of which mean the same thing. And to address the issue of PC optimization... It really isn't that bad. It seems that people these days are far too willing to deem a game "not reccomended" because of these truly minor issues that only naturally accompany such an ambitious game.
You see, when I close my eyes and try to think of a perfect game...I picture an extensive and content-packed open world that is both challenging and rewarding to master. I see endless opportunities to tell an immersive story and flesh out a character that I can really call my own. I want to be able to know my place in this extreme world; know which creatures or clans that I can handle with ease, and the others that I'll learn to respect. I want to eventually work my way up this hierarchy, until my legendary name sparks fear into the hearts of all who dwell from Concord to the Glowing Sea. At the end of all this... What better to return to than a settlement that you built from scratch, the smiling faces of settlers that owe you their lives, and like everyone else in this unforgiving world...have come to respect you.
Fallout 4 manages to meet all of the requirements for this "ideal game". And I have no doubt that this masterpiece will rightfully claim from me many hours of gameplay to come.
As gamers of this generation you owe it to yourself to get this game.

A well welcomed edition to the Fallout franchise. Fallout 4 brings in many new additions to an already very polished and addictive game. I have spent over 100 hours in this game happily exploring areas and picking up everything as now everything has a value for your weapon, armor, and power armor modding needs along with the new settlement buildings.
Positives:
Changes to the crafting system has made it easier to track what junk items are needed to craft and mod stuff.
All junk has value beyond just selling to a vendor for caps.
Settlements provide a good change of pace for when you grow weary of exploring the wasteland and killing things.
Better risk vs reward system where playing on higher difficulties causes more legendary monsters to apear and drop unique weapons or armor gives special boons to the player, if you can kill them.
Neutrals:
The perk system is now rolled into SPECIAL points. you no longer place points into upping small guns, lock picking, etc. instead you are locked into placing points for only the perks you have access to, tied to how many points you have put into your SPECIAL stats. However you gain a point for each level and you may put that point into any of your SPECIAL stats and become stronger that way, allowing you more chances and ways to play without being limited by your starting SPECIAL stats you chose.
Negatives:
The dialogue system has been streamlined into only 4 choices. Yes, No, Sarcastic (yes), or information are the typical choices when you are given a choice.
Charisma also seems to have taken a back seat because of this and really only comes up if you are looking for better settlements, bartering, or chances to pacify animals in the wild. The times of having a unique dialogue option because of a high SPECIAL stat, high charisma, or other high skills are gone and makes talking to people much more straight forward and linear.

Where to begin, well Fallout 4 is massive in content, but it is a love and hate relatioship you will have if you have any notion of what the Fallout franchise comes from. If you don't the game will probably feel really big and nice - but the interface, the design decisions, the GUI, the inventory, the perk system, the VATS - it will most likely infuriate both new and old players.
They are user unfriendly - that's the quickest way and most accurate way to describe them.
Also, it is published as an RPG game, but of all Fallout games - this feels mostly like an action game with some parts FPS and some parts RPG-themed stuck onto it. Also, a new dialouge that is possibly the worst yet for any Bethesda games. Where Skyrim actually made some sense and worked pretty well, the concept there has been taken its toll on Fallout. The game have the same wonderful - "just another (insert whatever thing it is)" build up and addiction as Skyrim. That is the good part, only good really that is beyond most other games. But the system, the shooting, the ugly textures, the less then useful PIP-Boy, the bugs, the easier and easier system to please people that don't like RPG's (?) have been exchanged for micromangement of villages, crafting and upgrades that are difficult to handle and understand than most Gnogard terms out there.
In my opinion the game is one of the weaker Fallout titles, but if you consider it as only just another game - it works pretty fine. But there are more concerns. The world is crammed with absurdities and stupidities. The world can't function as you grow in power - you still go out to help farms with two parents and a kid - and they want to join your cause and settlement-frenchise-protection. Great - now you have to rebuild Fort Knox, because just around the corner lives an entire clan of blood-thirsty Super-Mutants ready to kill and eat everything. Makes sense that a family is out there neighbours to Super-Mutants - you sometimes hear them in teh background.... It is utterly stupid and the game is impossible to play seriously at some times. It is like they have gone out of their way to make simple task impossible. Third mission - go here - other side of the map - you will fight Deathclaws, get power armour, fight super mutants, meet Dog Meat, save towns, get drafted by the Brotherhood of Steel - all before you make it to the measly little farmer wanting help to kill three ghouls... Great.
This is a game best not played as it should be and simply played as a randomized FPS like generator. Oh, and after some time - all the places you cleared next door - they will be repopulated by bigger meaner versions of earlier - so better build an army of watchtowers...
Still, there are so many negative things because it is so huge. And that it self is a reason to play this game. Not for immersion but for just solving that other thing - but when you get tired of the game panning out and becomming just a hunt for aluminium and adhesive - you start getting bored. Still - I got a load of hours sank into it so it is still worth it. I would say 3+ - for a Bethesda game.

In some respects, you kind of have to imagine your way into a richer narrative than actually exists (this is par for the course with recent Bethesda games). But in when it comes to the sheer scale of the world-building on offer, Fallout 4 has no rival.
If an open-world adventure is what you want, look no further. This is an incredibly satisfying experience and should not be missed.

At first I didn't really like this game that much, but over time I've started to like it a lot more. It's grown on me.
When it first came out, there were a fair number of bugs issues and glitches, but for the most part they seem to be sorted out now.
Rather than approach this game as a fallout role-playing game, you should approach it as a first person shooter with rpg elements. Yes, it does seem silly considering it is titled Fallout 4, but it helps.
It's fun to play. The gameplay is good. You have this great loop of gameplay that doesn't really get too boring. You get a mission to do something somewhere, you go there, you do your task, and then you can loot the place. Then you go back home and craft a bunch of things and hand in your mission. On paper this might seem a bit dull and repetitive, but it practice it ends up being rather encapsulating.
The world design is good, there's lots of little hidden secrets that you can explore and find, a fair number of NPC interactions are amusing and there are some NPCs that will reference things in the world in neat ways that you might not notice.
Recently during a sale, I bought all of the DLC via the season pass, and have been playing through that. You have 2 small DLCs (Wasteland Workshop and Contraptions Workshop) which really only add some new cotent to the base building stuff in settlements, so they're not that great. (Though I suppose it makes settlement building a bit more creative and mixed up (outside of modding))
Then you have Automatron and Vault-Tec Workshop, which are basically a long quest that introduce a new feature (robot companions and a vault settlement), both of which are alright.
Then you have the big two DLCs, Far Harbour and Nuka-World, which are both quite good and definitely an improvement upon the base game.
So long as you get the season pass on sale, I'd say it's definitely worth it.
There are some obvious flaws with the game, like the overall story being a bit rubbish, a fair number of small quests not really going anywhere, and also all of the settlements can be a bit much to handle. I feel that these issues aren't bad enough that they detract from the good parts of the game.

Well, now that I'm done with all the achievements and the story, I suppose I could write a review.
It feels like they wanted to make a game with a more engaging combat system, whilst making a story that's analogous to the success of Fallout 3. So the obvious question, did they succeed?
Well for starters the combat feels much more dynamic and alive, which is really good because you're constantly shooting things. I'd sometimes wish for the chance to sidestep, or even have a perk that allowed you to sprint sideways, granted this would be an OP feature, but I'd imagine it could make an already dynamic combat system even more alive and adrenalin pushing.
Storywise I'm a little disappointed. The story itself starts out well, and they made the right decision in having it start during the prewar time. Even though it's short lived, I'm pretty sure everyone with a keen interest liked it. Events transpire, and plot twists occur, but I felt by the time the quest "institutionalized" was over, the story had grown somewhat stale. It felt like at that point everything was just turning into a: "Go here, talk to that person, get that item, shoot that moron, talk to more people, pick up more stuff." By the time I had to choose an alliance, I was pretty tired of the game.
If we look at the features they changed/added:
Base building is one of the most fun features they've added, oddly enough I enjoyed it more than the main storyline.
Power armor is modifiable and actually runs on an energy source. While I have seen complaints about the fusion cores, you don't really need power armor at all in this game, especially not in the beginning. Even then it doesn't matter because they are really easy to come by as is. Fallout 4 in a nutshell
The Good: Fallout 4 is a good game worthy of a full price purchase, but it is also overall a let down for me as a fan of Fallout 3 and New Vegas. The game's gunplay is the best it has been in the series and I would never go back. I never understood why so many rpgs had to have awkward clunky combat, Fallout 4 says no to that and mixes it with an improved VATS system for a very gratifying combat experience. Even though the visuals are not the best in the industry they are still a huge improvement over previous game and some of the remolded enemies such as ghouls actually look horrifying.  The voice acting cast has been expanded and improved upon. Finally the world of Boston is big unique and I loved every minute of it.
The Bad: Being a Bethesda game I expected a fair number of glitches and problems, that being said considering that my personal experience with Skyrim at launch was fine for the most part I had expected less bugs and glitches, I was sadly mistaken. In some respects this the worst offender. I encountered a glitch where I couldn't use the elevator to go to the top of a building I would get caught in an invisible wall. I had to console command cheat on a main story mission to access a crucial part of the game. Being forced to do that is just sad and I was hoping for better from Bethesda, despite their track record.
I did my best to get used to the MC Main character voice actor and new dialogue system but after almost 80 hours of gameplay I have to say it is worse than in previous games. While I am judging Fallout 4 as its own game to illustrate my point I will use New Vegas as my example.  In New Vegas your MC had very little background info and honestly that was a brilliant move on the writer's part. Being an RPG I could make up my own backstory almost anything and it would jive well with the rest of the game. Because the MC in New Vegas is a blank slate that allows the player to really make the character they want to and identify with them more. Fallout 4 does tell a decent and gripping story but it clashes with what the player wants their character to be. As for the dialogue system, I found it was limited at best and annoying the worst of times. In previous game I felt more immersed in the world because I could ask detailed questions about the world from NPC's. Due to having only 4 options at any given time three is you never use sarcastic, the result is a dialogue system the that tries too hard when the simple system from previous games just worked.
One final minor gripe I had was I had to dig really deep to find interesting quests. No quests like Those, Agatha's Song, or even the Misfits are present. Most of what I found was "Hey go here find this artifact", previous games also had this but it was the people you met and the places that made the quests interesting. Remember in fallout 3 when you found that group of raiders who were "Vampires". I could be wrong but based on my experience Fallout 4 does have some interesting quests but it mostly contains uninteresting filler side missions.
I have more good and more bad to say but If I kept going this would be a novel length. Would I say you should buy it? Yes I would say it's worth the purchase but it is a departure from previous games. Some changes are better than others but it is still a very fun game.

Great game. Terrible RPG.
The GOOD:
-Excellent gunplay
-The settlement building system is awesome
-Lots of stuff to do. You can barely wander out for about a minute or so without running into something else you can do. The wasteland is not empty.
-Really cool weapon upgrades/mods and a lot of the legendary weapons rock
-The companions all have some sort of actual backstory
-The story is pretty decent.
-It's Fallout
-Enemies do not scale.
-There are quite a few perks
-No level cap, you can literally play forever. Eventually you'll run out of perks to gain though, but hey that's what DLC is for, right? RIGHT??
The BAD:
-Skill points are gone. Completely. Entirely replaced by perks. It makes the game feel much less like a true RPG (like Fallout is supposed to be) and more like Borderlands or something.
-You get a total of four dialog options, and they're basically the same every time.
-The map size is a bit small
-Sometimes it's a bit difficult to place stuff in a settlement because of awkward positioning controls
-When you put your gun away in third person mode, it just disappears.
-Some quests (like the Minutemen quests and a few BoS quests) are highly repetitive and never end.
-The PIP-Boy UI is kind of a pain if you're using a keyboard & mouse.
-Fusion cores last for about 5 minutes, which I guess makes sense in game terms but doesn't make sense at all in terms of lore.
All in all, the game's absolutely fantastic. Yeah, they really, REALLY strayed from the RPG formula that Fallout is supposed to have, which is disconcerting but in the grand scheme of things doesn't really make the game less fun. It's kind of like Skyrim on crack.

In short Fallout 4 is a game about exploring a post apocalyptic world in the search for your son. You wander the world exploring, looting items, crafting, building houses and doing quests for many of the factions around.
