The game looks pretty good considering its running on a very old engine. The engine also comes with it´s problems that have always been around and u think Bethesda would have fixed them by now. Some examples are:
Fps lock to 60 and vsync ON (you need to change that in the config files or the graphicsdriver) But you actually don´t want it to run much higher then 60 because the games mechanics is tied to the framerate so it completely screws up the gameplay.
Mouseacceleration ON by default (also needs to be changed in configfiles)
No field of view slider (Config file fix)
You need to restart the game to change graphicssettings.
Bad optimisation in the cityareas, "shadowdistance" just hogs the framerate i get low 40:s in some areas with 980Ti and a 4790K@4,7ghz. I suggest turning it down to medium or entering a custom value in the configfiles.
Mods is a really big part of this game and it resolves alot of the technical issues thanks to some great modders. It also adds more fun and replayvalue to the game.
Despite some really annoying technical issues this is a must buy for anyone interested in these kinds of games.

I think Fallout certainly stands as a worthy expense of gaming cash. An excellent open world shooter with somewhat lacking RPG elements.
Mind you, I play DnD and occasionally weird stuff like Cyberpunk with pen and paper, so I know what a "real" RPG is. Fallout is an excellent open world shooting game but a sub par RPG. My god, the combat in FO4 surpasses every previous title hands down. The responsiveness of the guns is excellent, the AI is decent for Fallout, and the gun modding system is top notch. I'm also in the lower % of players who thinks the new Power Armor system is great.
RPG wise, Fallout is weak. The lack of persuasion attempts based on skills/perks, the usual Bethesda less than interesting Main Plot, the lack of any real choice other than who you finish the game with, and the lack of notable named side quests to make way for more Skyrim style radiant quests compared to previous titles really degrades the RPG quality of the game.
All that being said, I love this game. Just look at my playtime. I am so happy with my purchase, but as a longtime RPG fan (both video game and pencil/paper) I feel Bethesda failed to make this game everything it could have been. Still awesome, but still lacking.

I've played this game for a fair amount of hours now, and quite honestly, while it is entertaining (it kept me busy for a significant amount of hours), I wouldn't recommend this game to anyone YET.
Not that there's many "good" points, because it's "just another fallout game" with no real innovation and nothing that makes it stand out.
The good:
- Graphics have improved over the previous fallout games albeit still outdated.
- Probably enough content in here for roughly 100 hours of unique gameplay.
- The new power armor is amazing.
The bad:
- The main storyline is short, one could go through the main storyline in less than 5 hours (while not rushing).
- The game is too easy (even on survival mode).
- Dialogue options have been dumbed down significantly. Not only can you not see what your character is about to say, but all of the New Vegas abilities like speechchecks for every stat (Medicine 15/30 - I erm... know how to stab people with a syringe) are gone. A real shame that.
- Terrible controller-oriented UI with the PC version hacked in
- Performance is decent, but the game is too heavy for the actual graphical fidelity given.
- NO SLI support (my second gpu is just... sitting there...)
- Random crashes. Just going straight to desktop, no error messages or anything, and at seemingly random times.
- Corrupted saves, past the 10h mark I had to restart my savegame as it was all corrupt.
- Windowed fullscreen with G-Sync limits you to 15fps.
- Having a monitor with more than 60Hz native refresh WILL glitch out the games physics, causing you to get stuck at several occasions (I quicksave roughly every 30 seconds because of this)
All in all, this game radiates (heh, get it, radiates) laziness. It has all the same glitches and issues of all the previous Bethesda games. I lost count of the amount of times I got stuck because of either the physics engine, NPCs getting stuck, falling through the world / walking through the wall etc etc
tl;dr Don't buy this until it gets a serious amount of patches / discounts.

While my initial review was due to saltiness over not having the correct hardware for the game, I later saved up my pennies and built myself a decent gaming PC.
Performance
First, I'll review the performance of the game itself. The game runs, on all ultra settings, on my i5-6500, GTX 1060 3gb, and 8 gb of RAM, with a stable 60 fps. You may rarely see frames drop at random, but these are infrequent and don't impact gameplay when they do occur. Which brings up my next topic:
Gameplay/Mechanics
This is where the game severely lacks what its predecessors Fallout 3 and New Vegas gained; Bethesda decided to give the  protagonists voices. While this may have seemed fine earlier in development, it overall cut the game down to a fraction of its potential. Due to the voiced options(as well as the horrible dialogue option screen design), it not only reduced the dialogue options from unlimited in the previous fallout games to a mere 4 options, but it also took away exactly what you would be sayiing, which often is misconcepted by the player, and then your 'RPG' is totally off track and you need to reload your save to get back where you want it. However, there are positive gameplay mechanics that Fallout 4 improved upon; it reduced the usefullness of VATS by making it slow time instead of stopping it, making people actually use skill and strategy to overcome their enemies, as opposed to hiding in VATS and taking 12% potshots until you hit your target.
Conclusion/Synthesis
This game seems to pruposely fall in a gray area between FPS and RPG, though it does lean toward FPS, and Bethesda makes that apparent in the reduced dialogue options and voiced characters, both of which break the immersion that people get in a classic Fallout 3/New Vegas RPG. However, while I prefer Fallout for the RPG, I also don't mind playing FPS games as well. The common saying about Fallout 4 is right; its a good FPS game, but not a very good Fallout game. If you play Fallout mainly for the RPG and the immersion of the game, I would just mod the hell out of New Vegas or 3 and replay that instead of purchasing this. However, if you're like me and you don't mind the FPS-oriented game style, I recommend you purchase it, you'll have a great time :D

Fallout 4 is a great game but with many flaws, but it is so awesome that you will somehow just ignore the parts of the game that clearly suck. Fallout 4 is an improvement over Fallout 3 and New Vegas in most ways. The combat feels like a modern shooter, if I had to compare the shooting mechanics to any other shooter I would say that it most resembles borderlands. Bethesda has added a cover shooting mechanic which fits in nicely and makes shooting gallerys all the more enjoyable. Also a weapon bash and gernade button improve the overall enjoyment of the shooting elements of the game juxtaposed to having to switch to a dedicated melee weapon if a target is close enough or to gernades if you want to frag them. However on higer difficulties enemies can sometimes turn into bullet sponges (although not most of the time) which can make shooting feel less enjoyable. Exploring the wasteland is even more fun than before with the introduction of legendary enemies that drop legendary loot with special bonuses. Were the game falters is its dialouge system which seems like a copy of bioware rpgs as you allways have 4 speech options that give you a brief approximation of what your character will say. It feels as if nuisanced speech option have been reduced to a bare minimum because you essentially know how each reponse will go with most npcs.Overall I am disappointed with how they handled speech. They have completely removed skills from the game; now only your S.P.E.C.I.A.L. stats matter. If you want a perk you have to have a certian SPECIAL stat level to aquire it, and overall I like this system. The Karma system has been completely removed so doing bad things when nobody sees them wont matter. I have to disagree with design choice because I feel there is noting preventing me from being bad if you know you are going to get away with it.  Also I feel there is not enough evil quest choice like the megaton descion in Fallout 3. The only incentive you have for not doing bad things is that your comapions may judge you for it and may eventually leave you depending of which compainion was following you. Another design descion I diasagree with was the removal of equipment ware and tare (execpt for power armor) . It feels like there is little incentive to use a worse weapon in the same caliber to save the condition of a better weapon with the same ammo type. And with melee weapons that is even worse. However this is somewhat mitigated if you choose to mod your gear. You can scrap weapons and armor you dont need or modify them to serve a plethora of combat situations. The gear moding system in this game is excellent. Another minor gripe I have with this game is it occusionally has questionable art decsions. What I mean by this is that some weapons look ridiculous like the new super sledge which is basically a sledge hammmer with a rocket attatched. My final criticism of this game is its poor optimization and bugs. While most of us expect some bugs, broken quests just should not be acceptable. Beware there are more than a few broken quests. Across all platforms fallout 4 runs poorly. Be prepared to turn the graphics down to medium even though it says ultra is recommened. The games graphics while not bad are nothing too iimpressive for 2015. In summary Fallout 4 is a great game with major flaws. Most of its flaws can either be ironed out by Bethesda in patches or fixed by the modding community (although it should be perfect at launch). I Recommend this game however if you can't stand bugs wait a month or two before buying this game

Fallout 4 is by far the best game I've played this year, but it looms alot of problems. Next to bugs, glitches, graphical issues and not being optimized for the PC. Fallout 4s biggest issue stems from a lack of innovation or change to the Bethesda formula. The game is for the most part just Fallout 3 with elements of Fallout New Vegas added in. They did add alot of things to the game, that makes it alot more enjoyable, like not having to constantly find items to repair items. But they also didn't do alot of things to their fullest.
My biggest complaint of Fallout 4, is that you as the player, do not and have not ever truely felt like you leave that great of an impact in the world. You can join one of 4 factions or join all 4. I've waited years for this game, and it's surprising that it lived up to my expectations.
Fallout is my favorite franchise, for a plethora of reasons. In a word though, I think the games are "tasteful." They're dark, and retro, and there's lots of attention to detail in every aspect of the game.
It seems like an unwritten rule that after waiting for something for so long, it can't possibly be as good as you'd hoped. I'm very pleased to say that Fallout 4 takes the previous installments to new places.
Pros:
-Weapon variety is unmatched by most other games. For reference, it's not quite to a Borderlands standard, but it certainly is more than you'll find in the arsenal of most FPS games.
-The map is large, there's plenty to explore.
-The main story is well balanced among the factions. I was actually VERY impressed with Bethesda for this. Even the groups that are supposedly "bad guys," are viable to be a part of.
-The interface is far more convenient that in New Vegas or 3. You no longer have to open every container or corpse that you want to loot. The list of items within it are seamlessly presented without having to enter a menu.
-The controls are basic, and graspable.
-The crafting is SO captivating. I found myself grinning wildly as I constructed weapons, and armor alike.
-There is no level-cap this time around.
-Each of the SPECIAL stats are very "special" this time around, unlike in previous games where you could get away with not touching any of them. They're all necessary now.
-The soundtrack is once again very fitting, and the new host of Diamond City Radio is amazing. He stands toe to toe with Three Dog and Mr. New Vegas.
Cons:
-I found myself a bit demoralized at the number of loading screens. They're fast, and the game is worth it, but it's still a frustrating bottleneck in the action.
-It's annoying how many characters in the game are immortal. Any of the many companions you have to choose from can not be killed, so it's annoying if you would for some reason want to do so, and they don't die...
-This one's not too extreme, but I'd hate myself if I didn't warn you all... There is very limited variety to things that the raiders will say. The dialogue is otherwise vast, but the raiders in specific say like 4 things.
Mostly only good things to say though. Well worth the wait to have this game, especially because I've been so fortunate as to come across very few minor glitches so far. My experience has been smoother than some though, so be advised for that.

However on higer difficulties enemies can sometimes turn into bullet sponges (although not most of the time) which can make shooting feel less enjoyable. Exploring the wasteland is even more fun than before with the introduction of legendary enemies that drop legendary loot with special bonuses. Were the game falters is its dialouge system which seems like a copy of bioware rpgs as you allways have 4 speech options that give you a brief approximation of what your character will say. It feels as if nuisanced speech option have been reduced to a bare minimum because you essentially know how each reponse will go with most npcs.Overall I am disappointed with how they handled speech. They have completely removed skills from the game; now only your S.P.E.C.I.A.L. stats matter. If you want a perk you have to have a certian SPECIAL stat level to aquire it, and overall I like this system. The Karma system has been completely removed so doing bad things when nobody sees them wont matter. I have to disagree with design choice because I feel there is noting preventing me from being bad if you know you are going to get away with it.  Also I feel there is not enough evil quest choice like the megaton descion in Fallout 3. The only incentive you have for not doing bad things is that your comapions may judge you for it and may eventually leave you depending of which compainion was following you. Another design descion I diasagree with was the removal of equipment ware and tare (execpt for power armor) . It feels like there is little incentive to use a worse weapon in the same caliber to save the condition of a better weapon with the same ammo type. And with melee weapons that is even worse. However this is somewhat mitigated if you choose to mod your gear. You can scrap weapons and armor you dont need or modify them to serve a plethora of combat situations. The gear moding system in this game is excellent. Another minor gripe I have with this game is it occusionally has questionable art decsions. What I mean by this is that some weapons look ridiculous like the new super sledge which is basically a sledge hammmer with a rocket attatched. My final criticism of this game is its poor optimization and bugs. While most of us expect some bugs, broken quests just should not be acceptable. Beware there are more than a few broken quests. Across all platforms fallout 4 runs poorly. Be prepared to turn the graphics down to medium even though it says ultra is recommened. The games graphics while not bad are nothing too iimpressive for 2015. In summary Fallout 4 is a great game with major flaws. Most of its flaws can either be ironed out by Bethesda in patches or fixed by the modding community (although it should be perfect at launch). I Recommend this game however if you can't stand bugs wait a month or two before buying this game

Personally, I enjoyed Fallout 4 quite a bit. It has a lot of character to it, with an interesting setting and incredible level design; the combat is much more interesting now with elements of verticality and ambush points rather than the flat open expanses of the Mojave from New Vegas (I can't comment on 3, as I haven't played it much). Going into it, though, you have to expect that the game expects you to play a given character in a set story. It's very different from previous BethSoft games which promised the opportunity to be anyone you want to be in another world. This game hands you a back story, a motivation for exploring, and ultimately a rather satisfying conclusion to that story, although the ending doesn't really change much based on which faction you choose, basically it's just destroy the other two factions and that's it. It's a fun game, but it suffers in the replayability department because of the fact that it just asks you to play the same character each time. Thankfully there is plenty to do with that one character, as my playtime suggests.

A whole lot of fun, an excellent game. I'd probably enjoy it no less if Bethesda had included some actual RPG elements, but the game isn't necessarily worse for lack of them. Unlike some other developers who have been moving to engines that make modding difficult (e.g., Bioware), Bethesda seems appreciate, and thus enables the modding community, and in the future this will no doubt add potentially hundreds or thousands of extra hours of enjoyment to the game. Skyrim is still one of the most played games on Steam as a result of this. In my honest opinion, this adds a lot to the value of the game.

In an attempt to bring a more open-ended and sandbox-y feel to the franchise, Bethesda have added to Fallout 4 a base construction system and procedural missions. You can, using metal, wood, and all the other trash found in the wasteland, construct settlements, craft weapon and armor mods, and even build rudimentary computers, using settlement workshop items. If you should run out of missions, certain NPCs will be able to grant you new ones, repopulating formerly [CLEARED], or dispatching you to absolutely new, areas of the map.
PROS:
- Fallout has never looked better. It even appears that Bethesda have included the entire Nevada Skies - Weather Effects addon, down to the radstorm mechanic.
- Engrossing gameplay driven by multiple storylines.
- The Power Armor mechanic has completely changed: armor is based on a frame that requires (and depletes with use) a Fusion Core to operate. It engulfs the user like the Iron Man mk 1 and mk 47 armors had a baby (without the jet-propelled parts).
- Power Armor's introduction happens immediately after the start of the game. However, due to the scarcity of the Fusion Cores that power it, and the rate at which the player depletes them, there is effectively active discouragement to use the armor in the beginning, though later on, especially with certain perks, players may never leave their armor, and in fact, may use the optional jet pack virtually all the time.
- Several of the Power Armor variants have optional Jet Pack mods. Given the nature of the flight this allows (hold jump while in air to engage jets), and depending on the skill of the user, this can result in nearly gamebreaking travel.
- There seems to be no level cap, though eventually, the entire SPECIAL chart will be filled, on a long enough timeline.
- Companions can only be temporarily injured, not killed.
- Caravans, like in Fallout 3, have their own personalities, and are also immortal (essential flags). It's fun to watch Trashcan Carla take out an entire Super Mutant base.
- The new conversation system involves dynamic vignettes, which generate conversation scenes that may actively be exited (say, to pop a Grape Mentats to boost charisma for a speech check) or even savegamed through, while the NPC keeps talking.
- There's an endless vignette in the Institute that shows how Synths are manufactured that should earn some kind of award. A video game Emmy maybe.
- It feels like twice as many buildings are open for exploration as FO3.
FACTS:
- Skills are completely gone, as are almost all old perks, replaced with an à la carte leveling reward system; one point per level to be assigned to any SPECIAL attribute, or qualified perks. A player qualifies for certain perks at specific levels, and more perks open up depending on how many points are assigned to each SPECIAL attribute.
- There are no obvious major tutorials; many major optional parts of the game (electrical connectivity, supply routes, parts programming, building construction) are often glossed over with a cursory explanatory popup.
- Every item in the game now has at least some use. Expect to become a hoarder.
- While NS-WF was completely incorporated, Precision Ballistics was not. Most small arms are still now hitscan based, while others, like the plasma rifle, are projectile based.
- VATS no longer stops reality, but slows it down to about 10% speed. This is more realistic, but also somewhat mitigates the potential insane power a VATS-based character build will generate.
- For the first time in Fallout history, the fact that the bombs dropped only 8 days from Halloween is finally acknowledged, though to a somewhat limited (primarily a mention in the opening scene and decorations in a few game areas, no mention of costumes) and anachronistic (200-year-old plastic jack-o-lanterns filled with candy, more than a week out from Halloween) extent. Might have been better to just add canon concerning a ban on halloween after the moon wars.
- As fingers are articulated armatures mounted on Power Armor, crafting stations cannot be used while while wearing armor. Power Armor also cannot sit down, and thus a number of terminals must be used only while dismounted.
- Because AI pathing is so poor, and companions cannot use the Power Armor Jetpacks, active companions will teleport to near the player from time to time, if left behind. Contrast this with FO3's forever lost companions.
- Ghouls have been redesigned: they look less like skeletons, but also much less like people. They also may be alive if found lying down.
CONS:
- The AI is still very dumb.
- Grabbing is now accomplished, when using a gamepad at least, by holding interact. This also causes dismounting from power armor, so if a grip is failed while in power armor (too far away is the most common, not grippable is the next), the player will instead dismount.
- Melee builds are still largely pointless.
- The vanilla base construction parts CLEARLY indicate that DLCs will be required to gain parts that look halfway decent (anything with plaster, wallpaper, or rugs that aren't dark grey, for example).
- There's no option to tell Preston that you don't want to bother with recruiting new settlements, or defending random settlements from whatever randomly-generated thing may be causing them trouble. In fact, just listening to the Minuteman radio station will auto-accept new, randomly-generated missions regarding settlements.
- Settlements will come under attack from time to time, moreso when poorly defended, but the popup warnings the game gives concerning these attacks are quite easy to miss, though they do show up in the Misc quest list in the Data tab.
- Settlements are ugly and a pain-in-the♥♥♥♥♥to deal with. While you can scrap entire cars and razed buildings within your first home build area, you can do nothing about the leaf piles or dilapidated structures, even within your own home. You can destroy giant trees and piles of tires and even radioactive barrels, but weeds are an elusive and impossible meanace.
- The ability to call in a mortar strike from properly equipped settlements is diminished by the fact the grenade to call them in is thrown
- Some mechanics, such as the player cover system, the new command to grab items, and the fact that Dogmeat is also a pack animal of some significance, are never mentioned.
- The Pip Boy Map interface is an atrocity in late game, with no remedy.
- The construction interface is anti-clipping to a fault, while the game physics engine will happily clip your carefully placed items the moment you leave your house.
- Though the game gives you the ability to use a jet pack, it appears the programmers didn't prepare for how this mechanic would be exploited (the city has a substantial number of false walls in somewhat difficult-to-reach places).
- The Fat Man has barely any range at all. Unfortunate, for being a nuclear warhead launcher.
- Captioning is poorly transcribed in many cases.
- Dialogue writing is sometimes painful.
- Mole rats and radscorpions can travel faster underground than above ground. Mole rats will explode from the dirt (or cement or bedrock) directly under you in swarms.
- The game will often hit you with seemingly randomly-placed mines that no longer appear after a save revert. Perhaps a joke for saving too often by the devs?
- While there are many more open buildings in the game compared to previous Fallouts, many more buildings are still boarded-up, apparently from before the war, without any explanation beyond an economic depression in 2077.
- A Kill Everything run is NOT POSSIBLE without severe rule restrictions. All vital NPCs are not only unkillable, but more than that, attacking NPCs in many cases will not even elicit a reaction.
- While Boston is less of an innavigable mess than DC was, faction control (ghouls, Raiders, Gunners, Super Mutants, civilians) varies from block to block, with no clear safe route among certain major safe areas.

So I completed my first playthrough of Fallout 4 at about 60 hours in whereby I had explored some of the map, collected some of the collectables & built up some parts of my settlements.
I am now 147 hours in and have explored even further and yet there is even more there still taunting me with its incomplete status, this game is bloody jam-packed full of content and I'm just going to start off this review saying: BUY THIS GAME, IT IS GODDAMN WONDERFUL.
So to begin, the game is an absolutely fantastic first person shooter with a vast world to explore, many weapons, armours and modifications to collect to make anything you collect your own, whether that be renaming the weapon, customizing its components or its optics or adding compensators, suppressors, muzzle breaks; the list goes on, there is so much to be done here but holy♥♥♥♥♥♥ nothing in this game compares to power armour, the power armour customization in this game is superb, It's on a whole other level.
The power armour customization may not be Mad Max's Magnum Opus levels of customizable but it is absolutely vast, you can make any piece of power armour truly feel like it is your own, make your own unique exosuit to roam the wastes with. (once you have enough fusion cores; batteries for the armour)
The environments are gorgeous, the attention to detail is absolutely insane as quite literally every object in your vision at almost any time can be looked at up close in high resolution detail, even the goddamn computer buttons have had so much love and effort poured into their creation from the dirty appearance to the faded colouring, it's phenomenal.
Now we come to the thing this game does best, the shooting. This game has some of the best First Person Shooter gameplay I've seen since Wolfenstein: The New Order, every bullet fired feels satsifying, every impact feels, sounds and looks amazing as body parts implode from a withering barrage of munitions, Rocket Launchers leave little behind but gibs, miniguns tear holes through people and rip them to pieces and the Fat Man, oh sweet christ the Fat Man and the Mini Nukes it fires are goddamn wonderful, easily one of the best weapons in the Fallout series now.
And now we get to the part where I complain because this game is one of the worst RPGs I have ever seen, the story is an atrocious, tedious mess of a story, it seems like it'll pick up eventually and it'll get better but it never does, the story is absolutely laughable in how simplistic it is, how bland the characters are and just how linear it really is but this is a fault of almost all Bethesda games.
If you're looking for a fun first person shooter with some leveling mechanics for stat boosts, this is your game, if you're looking for a post-apocalyptic RPG, you won't find it here, the game is absolutely fantastic as an fps and as someone who loves this genre I don't mind at all but this game is definitely going to be another black mark on Bethesda's track record when it comes to storytelling, branching stories and characters.
tl;dr. Buy this game if you want an FPS, Buy Fallout 1 & 2 if you want a good RPG.

I've waited years for this game, and it's surprising that it lived up to my expectations.
Fallout is my favorite franchise, for a plethora of reasons. In a word though, I think the games are "tasteful." They're dark, and retro, and there's lots of attention to detail in every aspect of the game.
It seems like an unwritten rule that after waiting for something for so long, it can't possibly be as good as you'd hoped. I'm very pleased to say that Fallout 4 takes the previous installments to new places.
Pros:
-Weapon variety is unmatched by most other games. For reference, it's not quite to a Borderlands standard, but it certainly is more than you'll find in the arsenal of most FPS games.
-The map is large, there's plenty to explore.
-The main story is well balanced among the factions. I was actually VERY impressed with Bethesda for this. Even the groups that are supposedly "bad guys," are viable to be a part of.
-The interface is far more convenient that in New Vegas or 3. You no longer have to open every container or corpse that you want to loot. The list of items within it are seamlessly presented without having to enter a menu.
-The controls are basic, and graspable.
-The crafting is SO captivating. I found myself grinning wildly as I constructed weapons, and armor alike.
-There is no level-cap this time around.
-Each of the SPECIAL stats are very "special" this time around, unlike in previous games where you could get away with not touching any of them. They're all necessary now.
-The soundtrack is once again very fitting, and the new host of Diamond City Radio is amazing. He stands toe to toe with Three Dog and Mr. New Vegas.
Cons:
-I found myself a bit demoralized at the number of loading screens. They're fast, and the game is worth it, but it's still a frustrating bottleneck in the action.
-It's annoying how many characters in the game are immortal. Any of the many companions you have to choose from can not be killed, so it's annoying if you would for some reason want to do so, and they don't die...
-This one's not too extreme, but I'd hate myself if I didn't warn you all... There is very limited variety to things that the raiders will say. The dialogue is otherwise vast, but the raiders in specific say like 4 things.
Mostly only good things to say though. Well worth the wait to have this game, especially because I've been so fortunate as to come across very few minor glitches so far. My experience has been smoother than some though, so be advised for that.

Definitely a lot of fun, but I feel like Bethesda lost the content forest for the game mechanics trees. I really enjoy the combat, the settlement building, and the crafting, but the (main) story was definitely the weakest of any Fallout game. It was startlingly short, and some of the decisions the player has taken away from them make it feel a bit contrived (e.g. "I'm friends with {x other faction}, can't we find some way to compromise?" "No, you have to kill them all because I say so.").
The other major problem I have is that a lot of the wackiness that gives Fallout its flavor was missing. I haven't looked in every nook and cranny yet, but it didn't seem like there were any offbeat encounters like those granted by the Wild Wasteland perk in New Vegas, or the bridge guardian in Fallout 2.
Referring back to my first sentence, for all the customization the weapon modding system allows, it feels like there is less weapon variety than previous games. Sure, you've got the requisite rifles, lasers, plasma, etc, but the mods all do essentially the same thing. There's a mod for sniping, shotgunning, automatic fire, aaaaand... not much else. I liked the targeting computer on the missile launcher, but that's the only thing I can think of that dramatically changes a weapon's behavior, aside from the flamer mod for plasma weapons (which I found to be lame, as it didn't appear to have any sort of DOT, but was just a really short-range, ammo-inefficient beam weapon). Where's the Turbo Plasma Rifle from the mods for New Vegas (photon torpedo launcher, essentially)? Where's a quad-barrel shotgun, or a circular-saw blade launcher? Ricocheting bullets? Hell, I'm annoyed that there isn't even a .50 caliber heavy machine gun (imagine hauling a Browning M2 around in power armor) to give an alternate use for the .50 ammo. I would have at least expected that Bethesda would have the sense to include fun weapons that the community has introduced with mods over the years, as they've basically been handed out on a platter. Sigh...
All my kvetching aside, I still put 100 hours into my first character and enjoyed the crap out of it. I didn't even do much in the way of exploring the map beyond where faction quests took me, so I plan on making a second character with a completely different play style.

If you're interested in this, do yourself a favor and play literally any other Bethesda RPG on Steam instead.
When you judge Fallout 4 by objective merits, it stands above Fallout 3, Skyrim, Oblivion and whatever other release you care to refer to. It crashes a lot less, it looks a lot nicer,  it's a bit better balanced.
But we ask specific things of Bethesda. They make a type of game that nobody else does; the open-world RPG that lets you make and play your own character in your own way. And saying Fallout 4 fails at this would imply that they actually tried beyond token efforts.
The voiced protagonist and limited dialog ruins your own attempts to define your character. The plotline itself mandates you play a straight, married parent looking for their son whether you care or not (so screw you, gay people). Skill checks are now entirely the domain of the Charisma stat; if you enjoyed being able to put your tech, medical, or bartering knowledge into play to solve problems, sorry to say that's not happening, and it will hurt every time you see when it might. And as nice an idea as it might seem, the new character advancement system is clearly designed with a particular playstyle in mind; namely, the guy that wades straight in guns blazing. Sure, there's enough stealth bonuses that you can make a good sneaky character, but it's clearly not what the game wants you to do.
It is still a good game, and I'll still be playing it for a while. But the prevailing sensation I have is one of frustration and disappointment, at seeing a series I really like decide to deviate from all the reasons I liked it.

I've got too many hours in to admit and I love the game.  That said, I'll try to give a fair review.
The play style mimics other iterations of Fallout quite a lot, in a good way. In other words, it is very Fallout-esque.
The story is not particularly engrossing, but for my play style, I haven't been bothered by it much. New Vegas' story was more rich and compelling, but this doesn't fall entirely flat. There are several factions to engage with, with shorter story lines and those are pretty sweet.
You have the option of playing with an NPC companion. Dogmeat is the German shepherd and he's my favorite. There are several others and each offers different styles of companionship. Google has more on this and how they differ.
The crafting and building of settlements is pretty awesome, if you're into that kind of thing. Some people aren't. The one thing I found lacking here is variety of building materials.  As an example, there is only one wall with a door in wood construction.  One version.  No versions with windows.  I anticipate modders will fix that, so I can wait.  Also, collision is as bad as it was in Skyrim; you put a lamp carefully on a table, and the next time you log in it's under the table.  This really, really annoys me.  Weapon and armor crafting is also rewarding and engaging, but again, you have to be a person who likes crafting in a game.  You'll get nowhere if you don't upgrade weapons and armore regularly, but as far as I can tell, you can ignore building settlements.  I wouldn't, because it would take a lot out of the game - searching for mats, looting and bringing it "home", etc - these are pretty typical enjoyable elements of a Bethesda open-world game and this is no different.
The map is large and absolutely filled with locations. If you wander off story and just out into the wilderness, it doesn't take long to encounter a new settlement or raider camp to take down and loot. And there's loots everywhere. Also, the types of locations are extremely varied and interesting; a water processing plant you have to drain, a crashed airliner, a robotics plant, a bowling alley, a drive-in, various towns, and of course vaults. It is definitely not one shack after another after another.
Ranged combat is spot on and the need to use different weapons for different situations is real and fun. Magically the game keeps your ability to locate ammo and your need for ammo in a pretty good balance, as long as you don't become addicted to one variety in particular, and depending on how much time you spend out of story just looting the hell out of everything.  I did.  I have plenty of ammo.
Now the bad - which hasn't been bad enough to stop me from playing at all.
Close range combat suffers from bad communication between an RNG miss and the animations. In other words, if I'm melee distance from a ghoul with my shotgun, and I see the blast in his chest, I don't expect no knockback and zero damage. And it happens. And frankly, it's just too damned easy to score a miss at this range. Of course you can melee with the gun, but not well.  So, sometimes it's easier to just open PIP, change to an actual melee weapon, then beat the thing to death. Or, run far enough away to get a shot off - not an easy thing. These fckers are fast.
Also, quests "break." It's all over the web. But, after hours of play and running into this and friends also running into this, we've figured out the problem - for the most part. The quests are fine. What's going on is Bethesda's complete fail in telling the player "you can't do this yet." You'll get a quest that says "Talk to this NPC" as it's next step, and the NPC won't talk to you. And you throw things, and scream, and pull your hair out, btching out Bethesda the whole while. Then later, after you've advanced the main story usually, you go back and it works fine. The game doesn't ever tell you that though. The quest line just quits working.
Sadly, some quests actually do break though.  A word of caution: Don't interrupt any quest action taking place.  If you're following someone, don't talk to any other NPC.  If the quest involves your companion, let them do their thing without interrupting.  If it seems like an NPC is not following through, be patient.  Strangely enough, sometimes they have to think - or something - before they move.  All that said, I currently have no broken quests because I've been patient, and because I was able to use console commands to reset the follow quest I broke.  I agree that a player shouldn't need console commands, and I agree that this is a smudge against Bethesda, but I also expect patches and repairs and there's plenty else to do.  Look - this game is f'ing huge.  Some things are going to be less tidy than others.
Also bad are all the broken bits and pieces scattered throughout the game; a companion just disappears, a group of settlers just vanish, guns that don't run out of ammo, floating glasses, chairs that don't offer a wait timer.  None of these things ruin the game, but if you're the kind of nit-picky player that rage quits over this kind of thing, don't buy it.
So, that's my take.  I think it's worth the investment and I've already bought the Season Pass.  I think the community is going to mod the hell out of it and make some really great improvements, and I think Bethesda will eventually fix the bits and pieces.  The main story is not all that great, but I'm not that far into it so I'm really no judge.  The characters and their backstories are very well done, and that makes up for it, definitely.
Fallout 4 is another hit, and Fallout 4 will indeed be as legendary as the rest of the series has been.  Well done Bethesda.  88/100.

I love the settlements aspect of the game. While I'm disappointed that they have limited the size of the settlements (ie: # of objects) to make this a multi-platform game, the best is yet to come. Modders will make the settlements system even better. I wish Skyrim would have had the flexibility to provide the same.
Overall the new features and engine are spectacular additions. I can't fault the game for what some are calling shortfalls. While Bethesda's engine is aging, I still feel like this is a very good engine for this game. And the game is very stable considering that it has only been out for a few weeks. I honestly cannot wait to see what the modders create once the Creation Kit is released. Maybe some don't consider this an RPG per say, but that doesn't change the fact that it is a spectacular game in my opinion.

It's like Skyrim with guns... literally.
Here's a post-DLC support review:
Disclaimer: I am playing a devil's advocate for Bethesda. Like it or not, I played a lot of Fallout 4 and will continue playing it once I get a better computer because my Alienware is so outdated it can only just barely run this game. I believe that Fallout 4 wasn't a bad game. It's the current Black Sheep of the Fallout Games. If you feel "offended" deal with it. Bethesda ♥♥♥♥ed up, sure, but the community response, both before and after Fallout 4's release with the PS4 mods controversy are things I don't care about. Now onto the review.
I have played Fallout 4 the most out of the Fallout Games I own. Here's my personal gripe with people hating on the game: They literally went in to the Hype. For Bethesda, this was one of the hugest problems with Fallout 4, people expected so much. Too much. What they should've done considering the game was "mostly done" was either release it over the summer or released it when it actually had "Gone Gold" (translations done, game done, some bugs fixed, etc.) but the bugs have been 99% ironed out (I get as many Infinite Loading Screens as I did in New Vegas, which wasn't many, but I've played much more Fallout 4 than New Vegas, so results may vary).
Now the problems with Fallout 4:
-Immersion: Yeah, there wasn't much of it, that's a valuable tool for keeping fans intrested. When I played through New Vegas, I would fail a quest every quest I completed. "We want Mr. House's life preserving technology.", I want to beat him over the head with this golf club and I did, it was worth it. But the problems with some facotrs such as immersion is that too much overwhelms casual players and too little alienates the hardcore players, you'd need an equal amount of immersion to not overwhelm those casual players, and enough immersion to keep your hardcore fanbase happy, it's pretty hard to please both sides without hurting one side even a smidge.
-Dialogue: It could go one way most of the time. Even in some of the DLC's, there would be DLC that ended off with the same statement.
-Voiced Protagonist: Not a huge issue. In about 1-3 years from now, my guess is that people will replace Nate and Nora's dialogue with a text-to-speech program or their own voice. If you do that last one, do a good job. If you use something like Audacity, add a small delay so that if your mouse picks up your mouse clicks or anything keyboard taps, you can just edit the file and there goes that background noise. It's not a huge gripe, but it's one that had some effect on the Fallout Fans. In the future, don't have somebody spend 2 years voices your male and female, even if they're good. I didn't mind in Skyrim when I talked and didn't hear myself, or in Fallout 3, or New Vegas, so I don't think this was necessary, still cool.
-The Dialogue Wheel: Pretty self-explanatory, don't cross the ip's.
-The AI still sucks: Yeah, no comment there.
-The Engine: The Creation Engine is an upgraded Skyrim Engine. You had basically 4 years since Skyrim came out, surely a new engine would've been a good idea. Bethesda, it is with my opinion that before ESO 6 comes to see the light of day, that you should make a new engine, from scrach, or reworked, but upgrade it, by 2020, I'm expecting that games will look like Uncharted 4 at the least, or a little worse than Uncharted 4. After all, if your engine works as well as a car with no wheels, then why use it?
And now my nit picks:
-Named Enemies in Enemy Factions: This was my own gripe. The only person who is a Raider Boss that even bothered to talk to me, was Slag. Only. Slag. I think it would've been intresting to have a dialogue with Red Tourette or Tower Tom and then asking for Food or finding their sister, but then again, they're raiders. And what about the Gunners? Captin Wes would probably like to have Mr./Mrs. Main Character Power on his side.
-Codsworth: Out of the 1k names Codsworth says, he doesn't say a whole bunch that aren't some swear or pop-culture reference. And it's only Codsworth that knows your name. Not Preston, Nick, just Codsworth. Which is both understandable, but considering it sounds like you're giving your life story out, don't you think somebody would be like "Oh, hey, what's your name?"
-Weapon Design Changes: I get this is a new area, but the Flamer looks less like a combat weapon and more like a fancy blowtorch. Or the Gauss Rifle from Fallout 3? Not here either. Instead the Railroad has their own Gauss Rifle cobbled together. Or the Gatling Laser? Different Variant. Combat Rifle? Not even the R91 from 3. Assault Rifle? Different as well. And let's not forget the lack of a Chinese Assault Rifle from Fallout 3. It was in the files. And only until Nuka-World did you get an Ak-styled weapon.
Things I liked about Fallout 4:
-The Combat System: Better. Aiming down the sights isn't like leaing in your head a little closer to see your enemies, or up in your face so close that the recoil from the gun will give you a concussion. ADS was good, and leaning. And everything else, oh, except the AI could've been reworked.
-I could keep coming back to it, even if it was for an hour or two, I loved to come back and continue playing, heck, I am trying to get the rest of the achievements from the main quest specifically in a new playthrough!
-The areas: While Fallout 4 didn't give us 4-5 new areas with differences between them, whether it's how they look or how they were, I liked Far Harbor and Nuka World. Both had their own themes, new or not. Nuka Worlds was Raiders and Rollercoaster, but Far Harbor's theme was much more like Point Lookout.
-The colors: Fallout 4 has lots of color. I like to see that. Sure, it cuts down the grimy perspective that the Captial Wasteland's Wasteland City had, or New Vegas' Desert feeling, but I liked it. It felt like a 50's post apocalypse and not some washed out area where clouds were always in the sky.
And if I forgot to talk about any DLC's I'll put my reviews of them here:
Automatron: Felt very good, liked the armors, liked the robots, gets this if you've got Nuka World, you can put robot mods from that onto Automatron robots.
Wasteland Workshop: Settlement building stuff, was okay, liked concrete stuff, like neon lighting. Still could've been in the base game.
Far Harbor: Take Point Lookout, place it in Maine, throw in some references to older factions, boom. Did a good job with this concept, though.
Contraptions: Take a Rube Goldberg machine and make it in Fallout, could've been better.
Vault-Tec Workshop: Was pretty cool, but Vault Size felt small, I had to disable various debris in order to make it. So in the future, if you do make a vault, make it a huge, open space and allow us to build it as big as we want, no limits, especailly on PC. Also, a molment of silence to Clem, if you had him go back to the power cycle and he died, I'm sorry.
Nuka World: Was probably the best one out of all of them. It's a Disney Land with 2 old-school references thrown in, maybe more. I'm still playing through it, fixed Fallout 4's "You can only be a good guy" issue. You want to be raider, get this, and Automatron, since you know, Robot Parts.
Again, I love Fallout 4, that is my preference. You can say "I did not agree with your opinion." but don't take it as fact. I'm no robot. I'm human, just like you. Bethesda did ♥♥♥♥ up, but I sort-of know why it did ♥♥♥♥ up, and frankly, we're still at fault, as a community, we made so much hype, that it made this game dissappointing. So in the Future, for any game, don't join the Hype train, trust me, hype is what can make or break a game sometimes.

well 116 horus in and i finnally polished off the main story quest.  Not that they took me that long to complete , I just happened to poke around quite a bit, any way  a review is in order  , but where to start.
THE GREAT:
We are back in yet another open world RPG made by bethesda - and boy does it show.  huge land scapes  thousands of places to explore  the fun never stops.
The voice acting-  the VA in this one is superb. There are a lot of returning voice talent that you will recognize if you played any of bethesda's previous games  (such as  the guy that voices Valentine). But lo and behold Bethesda has also hired a lot of new talent that you may have heard in other games.  you'll recognize voices from actors that played parts in the  mass effect series (if you played that series) and the dragon age series . such as the main character's voice  (her name excapes me at the moment) , but she voiced Jack from ME 2 and ME 3. I also heard several characters that were voiced by Garrus' voice actor too.  That said there is a lot of good talent  and all the voice work is top notch.
The setting -  not only is the land scape big but in typical beth fashion the environments ooze character  and atmosphere. (love those radiation storms). also as a move away from previous fallout games  there are actual rain storms in FO 4 too.  I always felt it was stupid that there never was rain in FO games.  a nuclear war would not dry up earth's atmosphere especialy considering that the earth's surface is 70% covered in said water.  so the enviroments and the weather is a big plus in my book.
Weapon crafting -  This is just awesome. there are so many ways to customize a weapon  it's unbeleivable.  I love how the weapon's apperance actually changes to reflect the modifications too. really can't say enough about this aspect of the game.
THE GOOD:
The story -  It's top notch in this game as expected . Bethesda is good at telling a story. it will pull you into the game. not gonna say any thing else about it as i don't want to give any spoilers. however , a few things hold this bacvk from being great. for starters there seems to be less story pathing than say FO NV.  it does offer the same pathing ammount as FO 3 , but after NV I had hoped Bethesda would have upped their game for FO 4.  Suppose I shouldn't have expected that much. after all Skyrim also released after  NV and it's story has next to no actual story branching.
Settlement crafting -  This is awesome too, but you are probably wondering why I only marked this under "the Good"  section and not "the great" section.  while there are many things you can build and many options in the system it has some drawbacks.   first off there is a limit to how many objects you can place in a given settlement. if you try to go crazy detailed with every house, or try to build a large premeter fence (like i did at first), you will hit this limit fast.   Second you can't build every thing from the get go. You have to find those picket fences magazines to ad more stuff. that said the default  stuff you do get is quite extensive.  Overall it was a good addition to an already great game  and i suspect many gamers will just dive into settlement crafting and forget all about the main story.
THE BAD:
The graphics -  are they horrid ugly and festering?  NO.  are the dripping with uber next gen sauce? no there as well.  Do they get the job done and look pretty doing so.  Yeah, but for the experince  they use too many resources.  Don't get me wrong I really LOVE the graphics on this game. and they do have quite a few next gen features  such as tesselation, hair physics, and god rays. but being on the same engine as skyrim with just dx 11 updating  they don't impress as much as they could have. in places some textures are blurry, the hair styles are relatively short to shoulder length despiote having good hair physics in game (why cant they give us some really long hair styles?)  and in general ther are some really odd frame rate drops in odd places.  one minute I could be walking through a dense forest  fighting dogs and bugs at 46-60 fps,  then i would go into a city that had far less shadows casting, far less god rays and next to no enemies to fight in that spot,  but my frames would plummet to the 22-32 fps range. just weird. I did figure out if i turn shadow distance to medium , god rays to high and shadows to high I could keep the dips in the 27-35 fps range , more playable but still odd.
Lack of money and resources- this one was an odd one to me.  the game throws you all the ammo you ever need  constantly. by the end of my play i had 2000 something fusion rounds for laser rifles,  2000 something rounds of .45 weps and qutie a few plasma rounds as well.  what I barely ever had was caps , and building resources. it's an odd mis-balance i felt the devs could have did better with. they should have threw you a  good deal less ammo , and about double the caps they did give you and about 50% more resopurces and the game would have balanced much better.  as it stands , i am never hurting for ammo in the bosston wasteland , but always hurting for caps  which in turn had me hurting for resources a lot.
THE UGLY:
Dumbing down - this came as no suprise , though i had really hoped bethesda was ready to stop dumbing things down. saddly they continue to push the boundaries of "how far can you dumb down a RPG before it is no longer an rpg?".  after a stint in FO4 i give bethesda 2 more games before they just say "screw it, this is not an RPG". Character leveling dumbed down,  Dialouge  dumbed down . really al these things could have their own subject topic  but tyring to compress them here so i'm not writing a novel.     I hate the dialouge wheel. It feels borrowed from bioware's mass effect, yet it offers less options than the game it was borrowed from. the leveling while interstingly approached  after some time i find myself missing the old system. the fact skills are tied into this system makes the game much more limted and less life like than previous outing. want to try to  pick a  lock even if you got fumble fingers?  well too damn bad you haven't picked the perk yet so you can't even attempt it.    just such a  back step from the old special/skill/perk system , now there's just special and perks and they are all blended togehter in one chart. i love the interface but that's about it.
No mods yet -  much of my complaints i could have completely overlooked if the game already had modding. How come it doesn't?   didn't skyrim launch with mod support already  ? corect me if i'm wrong.   that said after having just finished the  main story , i have no intention of firing FO4 up again until bethesda get's offical mod support in the game. And no i'm not looking to graphic mod ♥♥♥♥♥ it up, there are mods out there other than graphic mods, besides the game already pushes my system in certain areas.  Just there is no reason this game shouldn't have launched with mod support already in it. in fact the folks at nexus have already been doing some mods back door via ini file altering.
Don't get me wrong i know i got a lot of bad and ugly  stuff listed in this review. honestly this review barely covers the scope of every thing i wanted to mention and I am loving every minute of this game.  It's not a bad game, I just think it could have been much more than it is.  That said I give it a  80%. if you are a fan of Fallout games or open world rpgs get this game imidiately. if not i'd wait for mod support.  either way you won't be disapointed with the purchase the game is worth every penny it cost.

If you're interested in this, do yourself a favor and play literally any other Bethesda RPG on Steam instead.
When you judge Fallout 4 by objective merits, it stands above Fallout 3, Skyrim, Oblivion and whatever other release you care to refer to. It crashes a lot less, it looks a lot nicer,  it's a bit better balanced.
But we ask specific things of Bethesda. They make a type of game that nobody else does; the open-world RPG that lets you make and play your own character in your own way. And saying Fallout 4 fails at this would imply that they actually tried beyond token efforts.
The voiced protagonist and limited dialog ruins your own attempts to define your character. The plotline itself mandates you play a straight, married parent looking for their son whether you care or not (so screw you, gay people). Skill checks are now entirely the domain of the Charisma stat; if you enjoyed being able to put your tech, medical, or bartering knowledge into play to solve problems, sorry to say that's not happening, and it will hurt every time you see when it might. And as nice an idea as it might seem, the new character advancement system is clearly designed with a particular playstyle in mind; namely, the guy that wades straight in guns blazing. Sure, there's enough stealth bonuses that you can make a good sneaky character, but it's clearly not what the game wants you to do.
It is still a good game, and I'll still be playing it for a while. But the prevailing sensation I have is one of frustration and disappointment, at seeing a series I really like decide to deviate from all the reasons I liked it.

Here's a post-DLC support review:
Disclaimer: I am playing a devil's advocate for Bethesda. Like it or not, I played a lot of Fallout 4 and will continue playing it once I get a better computer because my Alienware is so outdated it can only just barely run this game. I believe that Fallout 4 wasn't a bad game. It's the current Black Sheep of the Fallout Games. If you feel "offended" deal with it. Bethesda ♥♥♥♥ed up, sure, but the community response, both before and after Fallout 4's release with the PS4 mods controversy are things I don't care about. Now onto the review.
I have played Fallout 4 the most out of the Fallout Games I own. Here's my personal gripe with people hating on the game: They literally went in to the Hype. For Bethesda, this was one of the hugest problems with Fallout 4, people expected so much. Too much. What they should've done considering the game was "mostly done" was either release it over the summer or released it when it actually had "Gone Gold" (translations done, game done, some bugs fixed, etc.) but the bugs have been 99% ironed out (I get as many Infinite Loading Screens as I did in New Vegas, which wasn't many, but I've played much more Fallout 4 than New Vegas, so results may vary).
Now the problems with Fallout 4:
-Immersion: Yeah, there wasn't much of it, that's a valuable tool for keeping fans intrested. When I played through New Vegas, I would fail a quest every quest I completed. "We want Mr. House's life preserving technology.", I want to beat him over the head with this golf club and I did, it was worth it. But the problems with some facotrs such as immersion is that too much overwhelms casual players and too little alienates the hardcore players, you'd need an equal amount of immersion to not overwhelm those casual players, and enough immersion to keep your hardcore fanbase happy, it's pretty hard to please both sides without hurting one side even a smidge.
-Dialogue: It could go one way most of the time. Even in some of the DLC's, there would be DLC that ended off with the same statement.
-Voiced Protagonist: Not a huge issue. In about 1-3 years from now, my guess is that people will replace Nate and Nora's dialogue with a text-to-speech program or their own voice. If you do that last one, do a good job. If you use something like Audacity, add a small delay so that if your mouse picks up your mouse clicks or anything keyboard taps, you can just edit the file and there goes that background noise. It's not a huge gripe, but it's one that had some effect on the Fallout Fans. In the future, don't have somebody spend 2 years voices your male and female, even if they're good. I didn't mind in Skyrim when I talked and didn't hear myself, or in Fallout 3, or New Vegas, so I don't think this was necessary, still cool.
-The Dialogue Wheel: Pretty self-explanatory, don't cross the ip's.
-The AI still sucks: Yeah, no comment there.
-The Engine: The Creation Engine is an upgraded Skyrim Engine. You had basically 4 years since Skyrim came out, surely a new engine would've been a good idea. Bethesda, it is with my opinion that before ESO 6 comes to see the light of day, that you should make a new engine, from scrach, or reworked, but upgrade it, by 2020, I'm expecting that games will look like Uncharted 4 at the least, or a little worse than Uncharted 4. After all, if your engine works as well as a car with no wheels, then why use it?
And now my nit picks:
-Named Enemies in Enemy Factions: This was my own gripe. The only person who is a Raider Boss that even bothered to talk to me, was Slag. Only. Slag. I think it would've been intresting to have a dialogue with Red Tourette or Tower Tom and then asking for Food or finding their sister, but then again, they're raiders. And what about the Gunners? Captin Wes would probably like to have Mr./Mrs. Main Character Power on his side.
-Codsworth: Out of the 1k names Codsworth says, he doesn't say a whole bunch that aren't some swear or pop-culture reference. And it's only Codsworth that knows your name. Not Preston, Nick, just Codsworth. Which is both understandable, but considering it sounds like you're giving your life story out, don't you think somebody would be like "Oh, hey, what's your name?"
-Weapon Design Changes: I get this is a new area, but the Flamer looks less like a combat weapon and more like a fancy blowtorch. Or the Gauss Rifle from Fallout 3? Not here either. Instead the Railroad has their own Gauss Rifle cobbled together. Or the Gatling Laser? Different Variant. Combat Rifle? Not even the R91 from 3. Assault Rifle? Different as well. And let's not forget the lack of a Chinese Assault Rifle from Fallout 3. It was in the files. And only until Nuka-World did you get an Ak-styled weapon.
Things I liked about Fallout 4:
-The Combat System: Better. Aiming down the sights isn't like leaing in your head a little closer to see your enemies, or up in your face so close that the recoil from the gun will give you a concussion. ADS was good, and leaning. And everything else, oh, except the AI could've been reworked.
-I could keep coming back to it, even if it was for an hour or two, I loved to come back and continue playing, heck, I am trying to get the rest of the achievements from the main quest specifically in a new playthrough!
-The areas: While Fallout 4 didn't give us 4-5 new areas with differences between them, whether it's how they look or how they were, I liked Far Harbor and Nuka World. Both had their own themes, new or not. Nuka Worlds was Raiders and Rollercoaster, but Far Harbor's theme was much more like Point Lookout.
-The colors: Fallout 4 has lots of color. I like to see that. Sure, it cuts down the grimy perspective that the Captial Wasteland's Wasteland City had, or New Vegas' Desert feeling, but I liked it. It felt like a 50's post apocalypse and not some washed out area where clouds were always in the sky.
And if I forgot to talk about any DLC's I'll put my reviews of them here:
Automatron: Felt very good, liked the armors, liked the robots, gets this if you've got Nuka World, you can put robot mods from that onto Automatron robots.
Wasteland Workshop: Settlement building stuff, was okay, liked concrete stuff, like neon lighting. Still could've been in the base game.
Far Harbor: Take Point Lookout, place it in Maine, throw in some references to older factions, boom. Did a good job with this concept, though.
Contraptions: Take a Rube Goldberg machine and make it in Fallout, could've been better.
Vault-Tec Workshop: Was pretty cool, but Vault Size felt small, I had to disable various debris in order to make it. So in the future, if you do make a vault, make it a huge, open space and allow us to build it as big as we want, no limits, especailly on PC. Also, a molment of silence to Clem, if you had him go back to the power cycle and he died, I'm sorry.
Nuka World: Was probably the best one out of all of them. It's a Disney Land with 2 old-school references thrown in, maybe more. I'm still playing through it, fixed Fallout 4's "You can only be a good guy" issue. You want to be raider, get this, and Automatron, since you know, Robot Parts.
Again, I love Fallout 4, that is my preference. You can say "I did not agree with your opinion." but don't take it as fact. I'm no robot. I'm human, just like you. Bethesda did ♥♥♥♥ up, but I sort-of know why it did ♥♥♥♥ up, and frankly, we're still at fault, as a community, we made so much hype, that it made this game dissappointing. So in the Future, for any game, don't join the Hype train, trust me, hype is what can make or break a game sometimes.

well 116 horus in and i finnally polished off the main story quest.  Not that they took me that long to complete , I just happened to poke around quite a bit, any way  a review is in order  , but where to start.
THE GREAT:
We are back in yet another open world RPG made by bethesda - and boy does it show.  huge land scapes  thousands of places to explore  the fun never stops.
The voice acting-  the VA in this one is superb. There are a lot of returning voice talent that you will recognize if you played any of bethesda's previous games  (such as  the guy that voices Valentine). But lo and behold Bethesda has also hired a lot of new talent that you may have heard in other games.  you'll recognize voices from actors that played parts in the  mass effect series (if you played that series) and the dragon age series . such as the main character's voice  (her name excapes me at the moment) , but she voiced Jack from ME 2 and ME 3. I also heard several characters that were voiced by Garrus' voice actor too.  That said there is a lot of good talent  and all the voice work is top notch.
The setting -  not only is the land scape big but in typical beth fashion the environments ooze character  and atmosphere. (love those radiation storms). also as a move away from previous fallout games  there are actual rain storms in FO 4 too.  I always felt it was stupid that there never was rain in FO games.  a nuclear war would not dry up earth's atmosphere especialy considering that the earth's surface is 70% covered in said water.  so the enviroments and the weather is a big plus in my book.
Weapon crafting -  This is just awesome. there are so many ways to customize a weapon  it's unbeleivable.  I love how the weapon's apperance actually changes to reflect the modifications too. really can't say enough about this aspect of the game.
THE GOOD:
The story -  It's top notch in this game as expected . Bethesda is good at telling a story. it will pull you into the game. not gonna say any thing else about it as i don't want to give any spoilers. however , a few things hold this bacvk from being great. for starters there seems to be less story pathing than say FO NV.  it does offer the same pathing ammount as FO 3 , but after NV I had hoped Bethesda would have upped their game for FO 4.  Suppose I shouldn't have expected that much. after all Skyrim also released after  NV and it's story has next to no actual story branching.
Settlement crafting -  This is awesome too, but you are probably wondering why I only marked this under "the Good"  section and not "the great" section.  while there are many things you can build and many options in the system it has some drawbacks.   first off there is a limit to how many objects you can place in a given settlement. if you try to go crazy detailed with every house, or try to build a large premeter fence (like i did at first), you will hit this limit fast.   Second you can't build every thing from the get go. You have to find those picket fences magazines to ad more stuff. that said the default  stuff you do get is quite extensive.  Overall it was a good addition to an already great game  and i suspect many gamers will just dive into settlement crafting and forget all about the main story.
THE BAD:
The graphics -  are they horrid ugly and festering?  NO.  are the dripping with uber next gen sauce? no there as well.  Do they get the job done and look pretty doing so.  Yeah, but for the experince  they use too many resources.  Don't get me wrong I really LOVE the graphics on this game. and they do have quite a few next gen features  such as tesselation, hair physics, and god rays. but being on the same engine as skyrim with just dx 11 updating  they don't impress as much as they could have. in places some textures are blurry, the hair styles are relatively short to shoulder length despiote having good hair physics in game (why cant they give us some really long hair styles?)  and in general ther are some really odd frame rate drops in odd places.  one minute I could be walking through a dense forest  fighting dogs and bugs at 46-60 fps,  then i would go into a city that had far less shadows casting, far less god rays and next to no enemies to fight in that spot,  but my frames would plummet to the 22-32 fps range. just weird. I did figure out if i turn shadow distance to medium , god rays to high and shadows to high I could keep the dips in the 27-35 fps range , more playable but still odd.
Lack of money and resources- this one was an odd one to me.  the game throws you all the ammo you ever need  constantly. by the end of my play i had 2000 something fusion rounds for laser rifles,  2000 something rounds of .45 weps and qutie a few plasma rounds as well.  what I barely ever had was caps , and building resources. it's an odd mis-balance i felt the devs could have did better with. they should have threw you a  good deal less ammo , and about double the caps they did give you and about 50% more resopurces and the game would have balanced much better.  as it stands , i am never hurting for ammo in the bosston wasteland , but always hurting for caps  which in turn had me hurting for resources a lot.
THE UGLY:
Dumbing down - this came as no suprise , though i had really hoped bethesda was ready to stop dumbing things down. saddly they continue to push the boundaries of "how far can you dumb down a RPG before it is no longer an rpg?".  after a stint in FO4 i give bethesda 2 more games before they just say "screw it, this is not an RPG". Character leveling dumbed down,  Dialouge  dumbed down . really al these things could have their own subject topic  but tyring to compress them here so i'm not writing a novel.     I hate the dialouge wheel. It feels borrowed from bioware's mass effect, yet it offers less options than the game it was borrowed from. the leveling while interstingly approached  after some time i find myself missing the old system. the fact skills are tied into this system makes the game much more limted and less life like than previous outing. want to try to  pick a  lock even if you got fumble fingers?  well too damn bad you haven't picked the perk yet so you can't even attempt it.    just such a  back step from the old special/skill/perk system , now there's just special and perks and they are all blended togehter in one chart. i love the interface but that's about it.
No mods yet -  much of my complaints i could have completely overlooked if the game already had modding. How come it doesn't?   didn't skyrim launch with mod support already  ? corect me if i'm wrong.   that said after having just finished the  main story , i have no intention of firing FO4 up again until bethesda get's offical mod support in the game. And no i'm not looking to graphic mod ♥♥♥♥♥ it up, there are mods out there other than graphic mods, besides the game already pushes my system in certain areas.  Just there is no reason this game shouldn't have launched with mod support already in it. in fact the folks at nexus have already been doing some mods back door via ini file altering.
Don't get me wrong i know i got a lot of bad and ugly  stuff listed in this review. honestly this review barely covers the scope of every thing i wanted to mention and I am loving every minute of this game.  It's not a bad game, I just think it could have been much more than it is.  That said I give it a  80%. if you are a fan of Fallout games or open world rpgs get this game imidiately. if not i'd wait for mod support.  either way you won't be disapointed with the purchase the game is worth every penny it cost.
