Bethesda's second Fallout title is a good game.  I simply enjoy the gameplay that they create, their style of game if you will.  This is another Bethesda title that has me addicted to exploring, what's over the next hill or around the corner?  It might just be an abandoned railroad car, or is something else going on there?  I almost never play thier game tho, don't really care about the plotline (sorry people who worked on the story).  Instead, I invent my own game within the sandbox they give me and they gave me a great sandbox with this one.
Less of a RPG and more of a FPS.  I'm not much on shooters but this one is enjoyable (and with VATS you don't have to be good at shooting all the time).  I'm also not a fan of complex RPGs anymore, so there is enough inventory management and character development to satisfy me without having too much logistics that interrupt or bog down the gameplay.
The crafting system is good, gives added control over the gear you take with you.  Unfortunately, it's not as varied as I was hoping (hundreds of different weapons they said), you basically have the same mods on all the similar weapons.  So you can add a sharpshooter stock to a 10mm pistol, or a pipe pistol, or a shotgun... but it's still just adding a sharpshooter stock to a gun.  Still, it's better than not being able to mod guns like in FO3.
The enemies seem to have slightly better behaviors than prev Bethesda games (sort of dodging around more often and taking cover)  but  you still get the "must have been my imagination" after shooting someone in the face, then hiding for awhile.  Not sure how this can be avoided really.  Yet, overall I find them more challenging and interesting.  The types aren't that varied, but the different environments tend to make you fight the same enemy differently.  Adding Legendary and more named enemies is another improvement.
Companions are still annoying, I tried to play a game with them but after a few hours I leave them at home.
Anyway, crack open an ice cold nuka cola and enjoy the game for what it is, fun to play.  I'm very happy with it and with mod tools coming (hopefully in the next few months) it will only get better.  The fact that Bethesda is fully supportive of modding is a great thing for gamers.

Despite what the haters say, this IS a Fallout game.
I know it is, because it has Mini nuke, super mutants, vault boy, S.P.E.C.I.A.L, Nuka Cola, Bobbleheads and God Damn Deathclaws.
More importantly, it has the same feeling of progression that 3 and New Vegas did - you walk out of that vault (or in the case of New Vegas your shallow grave) with almost nothing to your name, and you get owned. Then you craft and uild and explore, and sooner or later you can one shot the raiders that made you almost crap your pants when you were fresh out the vault.
I am playing on Hard, as a Glass Cannon/Genius/Trader/Crafter type character, and I am finding plenty to support my playstyle.
YES, they have taken skills away, or more accurately they have merged skills and perks into one streamlined system. For my money, this takes away little in the way of character customization/building. So for example, instead of putting 15 odd skill points per level into lockpicking so you can reach the next 25 point milestone that enables you to pick the next level of locks, you put the one perk you get per level into increasing the rank of a lockpicking perk.
So yes, this system is 'dumbed' down' in the sense that 1 is a smaller number than 15, but you're still putting points into lockpicking if you want to be able to pick locks - not exactly rocket science before or after.
The weapon and armor modding adds more complexity, which in my opinion makes or for the complexity taken away by the levelling system. You can take any weapon you like, and mod it so that it becomes a close range 'shotgun' or a ranged sniper rifle.
Honestly, I don't know why anyone wouldn't prefer this to finding the best shotgun ever that perfectly suits your playstyle, then giving up on it because you don't want to or can't find the 50 lesser shotguns that you need carry around with you to keep repairing the damn thing.
Personally, I love what Bethesda have done with the voiced protagonist, and the quest line feels much more personal. The story is good, I am engrossed so far (I'm close to the final stages of the main campaign, as far as I can tell).
For those that don't like being constrained to being a parent out on a quest for your baby, I say two things:
1. Every Bethesda game has some backstory to the player character - did you always like being a prisoner, or being on a quest to fine your father, or a courier out for revenge?
2. If you really don't like this particular backstory, feel free to pretend that you didn't actually know your wife/husband, and that the kid is actually not yours. Cryo sleep just messed with your mind, plus the case of PTSD you would probably get from witnessing the violent death of even a stranger, shortly before having your own life threatened, has given you the delusion that your husband was killed and your baby has been kidnapped.
Bethesda took out Karma. Well good for them. There are many moral philosophies, only some of which depend on some higher power or cosmic force keeping track of everything you do. There is still morality in this game, it's just contextual - based on who you are with, and what they are like.
This is more like how morality works in the real world.
I've spent most of my play-through with one companion, and the writing behind his character and dialogue reminds me of Mass Effect 2 (that's high praise).
There is plenty that has changed compared to the previous two games in the series. Some of it is for the better, and some things are features that you may miss.
But for my money, I can't bring myself to fault a game that sucks me in, and keeps me wanting more.
The Fallout series is, evidently, many things to many people. If you enjoyed the previous two installments in the series, and you are not deathly afraid of change, then do yourself a favor and buy this game.

After 70 hours of gameplay and finishing the main quest, I think I'm ready to give an honest opinion of Fallout 4. I will start by saying that it's a fine game, but at the same time, it didn't meet my expectations. The things I really liked, I really liked, and the things I hated nearly made me give it up.
For instance, the graphics are not as intensive as I thought. At medium settings they are still very good and I have yet to experience any kind of significant lag. In fact the game seems to have been vetted much more thoroughly than Bethesda's other releases. I also appreciated the inclusion of crafting and building towns. I spent some time creating my own homes for my residents and I didn't regret a moment. The one aspect of the game I found the most enjoyable was the inclusion of more companions. You literally have your choice of any type of companion you'd want and they will like or hate you, depending on what you do around them.
With that said, the things I hate are significant, and as I said nearly broke, or broke the game for me. The first is the main story line. It's an amazing story, until you reach the end of the first part of the main quest, then you feel so betrayed that you want to quit. The writing is so emotionally manipulative, you get the idea the author wanted you to have that shocked feeling you get from Game of Thrones, only it has none of the suspense. It's simplistic, plagued with questions as to why (or how) it could even have happened. In the end you quit for a few days (like I did) or just roll with it and say, "it's just a game." In no way do you enjoy it, and I mean I have not met a single person that liked the ending of the first main arch, it's abysmal. Without a doubt the worst quest in the franchise hands down and has the potential to actually ruin the reputation of the franchise.
I also felt that controls were clunky. It's hard to play at times and you end up having to move your hands off the mouse to hit the arrow keys A-L-O-T and it's annoying. Save yourself massive frustration and get a controller. Aiming can be hard to get down with a mouse, since it's very touchy, but after you do, it's not too difficult to get through normal difficulty, with only a few missions being a significant challenge.
Overall I liked the game, but I can't say this was the best release. The controls and story are not even near on par with the previous installments of the franchise and will definitely require DLC in order for it to feel as polished. With that said I would recommend the game, but I wouldn't advise anyone to get their hopes up. (3 stars out of 4).

Fallout 4 is a ROLE PLAYING GAME. Not a game that succeeds based on the difficulty of it. This game is designed to give the player an adventure, not a headache. I simply enjoyed the ride, no matter how long or repetitive it was sometime. People need to look at the fact that games arent always going to improve 200% on one of it's predecessors (may have spelled that wrong). It is an entirely new game and will have new aspects to it as well as some previous ones. Without playing the previous games i understand that i don't realize what's missing and what's "all wrong", but as someone who simply enjoys a good RPG i truly believe this game delivers. Fallout 4 has been a game I have been excited even before the announcement. I collectively have 200+ hours of gameplay between Fallout 3 and Fallout: New Vegas (Which some would consider to be a small amount) and I would like to consider myself somewhat experienced with the series. Please keep these facts in mind as I continue forward with my review. I’m also going to do my best to avoid bias from what other people have said, and keep this strictly based on my opinion.

To start off, this game has a MUCH better story than either 3 or NV. The characters are interesting and the voice actors are much more varied + much better voice acting minus a few characters here and there. The dialogue is much more engaging than previous games, and the conversations feel real, thanks to the new dialogue wheel. However, this dialogue wheel is a double edged sword. While it grants the addition of cut scene-like conversations, it will often leave you guessing what exactly your character will say. For example, a sarcastic option will usually be present, but it gives no hint of whether it will be positive or negative, and I usually just avoided as a result. Luckily, this flaw can be rectified with a quick mod install that makes the full dialogue of your choices appear in a similar fashion to the previous titles. I also enjoyed the romance aspect of having the ability to romance 1 of the many companions that you can have travel with you throughout the game. While on the topic of companions, they are so much more varied, interesting, and useful than before. They have their own backstories and personalities and have many funny/unique comments while exploring and during certain conversations. The variation also made it hard to choose just one companion. They are all very different people, and some are even robot or synth, yet all of them are so lovable and fun to have by your side. The increase in writing quality, as well as a much more interesting story are much appreciated..

Now on to arguably the most controversial topic about this game; the graphics. Personally, I thought they looked pretty good, even at lowest settings (need a better computer ;( ) and the somewhat low texture quality was not noticeable nor bothersome. However, there was some inconsistency with texture quality and some random frame dips while in areas with lots of lighting effects. Animations were impressive and top-notch, especially for Bethesda standards. Guns were powerful looking and the animations for them were detailed and fun to look at, especially with energy weapons. Facial animation was also impressive and really stood out during conversations. Some problems that I have been told about is that increasing the framerate above the 60 frame cap can cause physics and game-time bugs, and that some certain resolutions are not supported.

Moving onto the controls, if you have played Skyrim, you know exactly what to expect. If you haven’t played a Bethesda game since Fallout 3 or NV, then the menu system might take some getting used to. Instead of right click, R drops items, as well as a few other changes to the menu system. Sprinting and holding breath while sniping are also new features, and both of which drain your AP, which is nice to see AP being used for something other than V.A.T.S. The best part about the new controls is that the shooting is extremely satisfying. Guns have lots of power and kick to them, and V.A.T.S. system, which is a mechanic that slows down the game and lets the player target specific body parts of an enemy is totally redesigned with a new satisfying feel to it. Sprinting is also lots of fun, and there is a real sense of urgency in it, and using power armor makes you feel like a god stomping around the wasteland. The controls are much more satisfying and engaging than previous Bethesda titles, and the refined shooting is great for some fantastic fire fights.
Now if you know ANYTHING about this series, you should have a somewhat decent idea of what you do for fun. Most of the game is comprised of side-missions that usually follow the formula of
1.	Talk to person, they tell you to go kill raiders/ghouls/creatures
2.	Go to area, kill EVERYTHING in sight.
3.	Go and tell person that you made everything okay ;)
While the side quests are somewhat questionable in terms of quality, the bigger story missions are much more thrilling and entertaining, and the quests are not what drive this game, it’s the exploration aspect. Walking in any direction will quickly reveal half a dozen locations that are completely free for you to explore and usually have some interesting back story or NPCs in them. There is also little things as satisfying as killing a legendary raider or creature and their corpse reveals a new weapon or armor piece with a special stat attached to the item, like a damage bonus against certain enemies, or bleeding damage. Vaults are also super fun to explore and are just as twisted and creepy as usual.

However, the biggest surprise of this game, is the ability to customize just about EVERYTHING. Sure, things like making your own character and building their skills according to your play style are all par for course, however, what was completely unexpected was settlement customization and gun crafting. Crafting has always been a part of the fallout series, but never before has been this fleshed out or satisfying. Just about every part of every gun can be customized to have something else unique about it and serve a specific purpose. Don’t like the lack of short range capabilities of your sniper, put a bayonet on the barrel and build a barrel that has better hip-fire accuracy. Don’t want a plasma pistol and would rather have a rifle? Put a longer stock on it and make the receiver more powerful. Just about every single weapon can be upgraded and customized to make it totally yours and there are just so many different possibilities that it is almost over-whelming. To go along with this, you can also build up structures, such as walls, turrets houses, wooden bridges, gates, fences, electrical lights, and so much more. You could build entire towns and establish trading lines between them, set up markets that see meds, ammo, and just so much more. Build huge farms which then need to be protected from raiders, so you put turrets all over the place, and build hotels for your settlers to stay in and just so many more possibilities and it’s just so fantastic to open the crafting menu and basically build to your hearts content. And collecting these resources is not tedious in the slightest. You remember those paper weights sitting around everywhere in the previous games? Yea, well now that junk actually has purpose. Every carton of cigarettes, every baseball glove, every animals skin now has purpose thanks to this new crafting system and it’s just so in depth and has so much detailed and is so satisfying, and better yet, if you want nothing to do with building towns, you can just completely ignore it. The game will almost never force (a few side-missions require you to build a generator and a signal tower) you to interact with the crafting system, and it’s such a huge part of the game that is optional. The crafting and customizability of this installment are greatly appreciated and extremely well done. Bravo Bethesda, for making a crafting system more addictive than Minecraft.

With all of that said and done, fans of Fallout 3 will not be disappointed. This game is a worthy sequel and is a game that has nearly consumed nearly 60 hours of my life in less than 2 weeks of being released. While the game may have evolved with the new perk system and whatnot, but the gameplay is still the Fallout I know and love, and I wouldn’t have it any other way.
Verdict: 9.5/10

Fallout 4 is truly a worthy successor to Fallout 3 and New Vegas. Everything that those games did so well including character customization, player driven story, atmosphere, replay-ability, and straight enjoy-ability have all been improved upon and added to. Most notably would be the addition of settlement building.
After hundreds of hours logged onto fallout 3 on ps3 and pc combined, my opinion of this game may be skewed a bit, but what I do know very well is what a fallout game is supposed to be. The lore, combined with the atmosphere and generally dark humor of the game make Fallout very special and unique among the slurry of recent survivor horror and post-apocalyptic games.
And what I mean when I talk about the atmosphere and dark humor is that Fallout is one of the only games with such a grim setting that actually has me laughing. Actually laughing at events that may not even be scripted, but it is rather the satisfaction of a raider taking a point blank shot from a shotgun and completely exploding in front of me.
The gameplay is greatly satisfying, and stop talking♥♥♥♥♥♥about the graphics. They are very good, especially coming off of Fallout 3. Fallout never had, and will never have the state of the art graphics. If that is really all you care about, this game is wasted on you, and you should consider buying Black Ops Infinity.
With this said, the game is not perfect, and there are some aspects that deserve improvement such as facial animations in some situations, and some companion AI. With that said, you cannot expect tens of thousands of lines of dialogue to be perfectly lip synced to the player and NPC's. That is simply not possible for a game of this scope. The NPC AI can also be explained by the fact that the landscape is so vast and different, you actually need an AI. Not everything is flat corridors and stairwells. This game is far more dynamic and interesting in its settings, and so the AI must figure out for itself how to navigate. And it sucks that people only seem to focus on the one in hours of playing that the NPC's don't do the ideal thing a player would do.
This ignoring of context is the main reason people find such issue with the AI, graphics, animations, and whatever else ou have to complain about. A thouroughly generic FPS with limited RPG elements.
FO4 does most things well but there is nothing to distinguish it from other open world games (aside from a large marketing budget).
This game takes a huge step back from everything fallout new vegas accomplished. No longer do we have interesting 'evil' factions like the fiends, khans and powder gangers. Rather we have 'raiders' and 'gunners'. Typical bandits with no backstory, no interactivity, no reputation system and no personality. Simply human scale targets to shoot at. Wanted to be a bandit? Too bad, now go join the BoS.
We've left the days of a crated character behind. You are THE man looking for your son, you are THE general and within a few hours you can be THE absolute, power tripping leader of any of the games factions. Few choices are aforded to the character when it comes to the main quest.
The main thing that cripples the quests in this game is the dialogue system. Intimidations, SPECIAl skill checks and perk based conversation options are gone as are the morality specific choices from past games. Most conversations have one end point that was pre determined by bethesda. All dialogue options are also limited to four responses which often removes inquiry options present in past games. When you made a low intelligence or high charisma character in New Vegas that choice mattered and affected dialogue and descision making throughout the game. In fallout 4 you have little power over your speach choices and dialogue options are hugely limited. Again, perk and SPECIAL speach options have been removed completely.
Most main quests (although there are a few compelling side quests) boil down to glorified fetch/kill objectives and involve nothing more than clearing an area or obtaining an object.
The gameplay is a step up, but only when compared to previous games. Crafting, gunplay and settlement buildings are on par with modern games but only just that. Nothing about FO4's gameplay is unique. It's all been done before and done better.
The game still runs in gamebryo engine (nearly a decade old) which has led to numerous bugs and glitches that have already plagued bethesda games for years. The graphics are fine but texture quality often drops to levels I'd expect to see in a game from 2009 and performance is shockingly low for a game of this graphical fidelity. Crashes and freezing bugs are very frequent as well as horrible friendly AI pathing.
The user interface is an atrocious example of a console port. Mouse acceleration, low FOV and bugged mouse sensitivity must be fixed through ini files and are not in the game's options menu. The pip boy continues to show clear evidence of a console menu and lacks specific menus for notes and holotapes (this becomes more frusturating the more you play).
If you want a decent FPS with a lot of fetch/kill enemy quests FO4 is perfect for you. If you like RPGs, character building and compelling quests with good writing I recommend playing Fallout: New Vegas or even Fallout 1 or 2.

This review will have two parts: one with the vanilla game, and one with future content of both dlc and mods.
Vanilla game:
Fallout 4 is an immersive world with amazing visuals (don't listen to the other people) that has a lack of old fallout rpg elements, but doesn't bring the game down too much. The world and exploration is the best out of any recent fallout game. You will explore Boston, known at this time as the "Commonwealth" and believe me when i say it, exploration is easily the best part of any fallout game. While the graphics do look very nice, they may lack compared to most games that come out these days. Optimization, while not "unity bad," still will make mid end pcs struggle unless running on lowest settings (given you want 60 fps everywhere you go at least.) The game gives up the old skill system which many people loved a lot about the old fallouts. Instead of adding points to sneak, small guns, energy weapons, etc., you will go the "skyrim approach" and make the leveling a lot more simple. The perks are the big thing with leveling, like in old fallouts, you still choose perks that can have one level or multiple tiers. However, instead of having the skills, you now can add perk points to any of the S.P.E.C.I.A.L. abilities. There are a few bugs, but nothing that entering "tlc" in console can't fix. Finally, the companions are extremely buggy. 90% of the time when you try to trade or talk to them, they will walk away, making it impossible to interact with them. Instead of following behind you like the old bethesda games, they will often run ahead, going their own path. Finally, the dialogue is completely awful, the actual responses are fine, but the simplicity of the choices it lists is unbearable. Instead of full responses, it gives a few words and you have to often guess what your character is going to say. It's usually options of "yes, no, sarcastic, and information." Overall the base game gets a 7.5/10 (if bugs and optimization got fixed it would be 8.8/10)
The future of the game:
Just like any bethesda game, there will be dlc, and mods. The dlc hasnt been announced yet, but we could hope it would be something along the lines of 3 or 4 dlcs with a new map. Bethesda is also going to actively fix the game's bugs so that's something to look forward to. On the mod end, the creation kit hasn't been released yet, so a lot of the crazy things to do in modding aren't available. However, there are already mods fixing some of the issues in the base game, such as the one that displays what you're going to say fully. If all of the issues in the vanilla game get fixed by mods, this game is an easy 10/10.

Okay, though I enjoy the game more than less the difference is miniscule.
The sidequests get repetitive: go here speak to this person, go here kill these people, go back to this person get a reward (and for minutemen) go and speak to Preston to complete the quest and get another TEDIOUS quest.
The weapon drops are just.... bleh, the amount of pipe guns, Short Shotguns, Missile launchers, even FAT MEN just really makes weapon hunting pointless. Armours the same damn thing so many raider armors that (in my opinion) really suck, not to mention that no matter HOW you customize them they look EXACTLY the same.
Choices, what is the point of CHOICES!? No matter WHAT response you give the dialogue remains more or less the EXACT same and has absolutely NO effect on the story or alignment with other factions (unless you walk in with a certain companion).
POWER ARMOR!!.... I never really used, absolutely pointless, it really has very little use other than radiation protection and in early game carry capacity.
Companions are still absolutely useless (the only companion that was any good was Fawkes, EVER) and the amount of times I have seen ...... can't carry anymore was infuriating since there is NO indicator to how much your companions carry weight is. They also, as usual (unless you are Fawkes) die, in some cases even burn you up with a molotov or blow you up with a frag..
Settlements, nice idea but you have to arm ALL your settlers with armor, weapons AND ammo, unless you want them all to run around with pipe pistols or bare handed. Your shops make NO money, even if you make the 3rd level ones. The micro management of settlements is flawed, for example one of the settlements regardless of what I gave them plenty of beds, food, water, defense, power, I added shops and so on would ALWAYS be unhappy and settlers would leave! And there is just TOO MANY of these settlements, WAY too many. I ended up just focusing on Santuary, The Drive-in and The Castle.
And like Fallout 3 bugs, glitches and bull.... (enemies have the ability to shoot through walls in certain areas, game resets (in my case it also just flat out crashed) V.A.T.S is rubbish unless you make Perception, Luck build.
My BIGGEST problem with this game is the story doesn't really engage me in any way, I literally do not care about the kid (son), the illuminati kind of thing doesn't really work, as you know LONG before the actual development that you will have to destroy them.
I didn't really like any of the characters other than Hancock, and of course, Dogmeat in this game. I can't stand Preston or Dantse and the others are just very 'meh' (this includes all the storyline characters that you meet).
I am also the silent protagonist type, though the voicing isn't bad (in my opinion) I think giving the MC a voice removes a certain element from the players experience of the game.
The pros are few, but had an impact on me.
The BEST one I can say is that V.A.T.S no longer pauses the game, no more V.A.T.S to save my life before that last shot kills me.
Though the S.P.E.C.I.A.L is dumbed down it is a whole lot LESS convoluted, and makes a whole lot more sense, focus on this to unlock that, rather than put all your points into this and only after SO many points are put into this will you notice the difference.
Settlements, I liked the idea of helping people and creating settlements but it needs some serious refinements. Being able to build your own town is awesome probably spent about 9-12 hours building up my town, castle and making a little settlement in the Drive-in.
Customization I did enjoy crafting my weapons to my prefered style of play, I mean a 6 crank laser musket, with short barrel equals stupid damage but I love the incineration of my enemies.
Pointless stuff like abraxo cleaner, tin cans and junk has a relevence now and we all know there is way too much of this worthless stuff in Skyrim, Fallout 3 and to an extent Vegas.
Unlike many I also enjoyed the level scaling, though I like seeing my progress, I think going around killing enemies in one shot can get VERY boring VERY quickly.
ENEMIES: Rad Scorpions, they used to annoy me, they were everywhere and just a nuisance, but now there is less but still annoying for actual reasons (damn armored insects) Deathclaws now live up to their name, they WILL kill you more often than not and they look so much better! Legendary enemies! I like this idea but I think they need to chill on the mutation, not stop it, but make it so only a few do, also they need to deny the one shot V.A.T.S kill, they are supposed to be legendary after all.
The world, it's massive but unlike Vegas it isn't empty, there are so many places to go to, clear out and explore and it has a fair amount of surprises scattered around like the legendaries, a random deathclaw and if you are really lucky a Behemoth.
In all I like the game but for 7 years work it is lacking graphically, story wise, characters wise and quests wise. There are some improvements but not enough to justify the claims Bethesda made or the 7 years it took to make the game.

ORIGINAL REVIEW:
It's just... not great.
Go play New Vegas.
AMENDED:
Having beaten the game, I've changed my tune a bit on this one.  Almost from the moment you start Fallout 4, the game starts shoving a bunch of repetitive, pointless ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t in your face, and you might be fooled into thinking that repetitive, pointless ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t was all the game had to offer.  I sure was.  Oddly enough though, for all its Bethesda-ness, Fallout 4 differs from the norm by having a relatively engaging and somewhat lengthy primary questline.  Once I completely stopped giving a♥♥♥♥♥♥about building settlements, helping the dumbass Minutemen, or gathering garbage to attend to the above two things, the game got a lot more fun.
I'm not saying the game is good, per se.  I don't even think it's Bethesda's best. They did a whole lot of things wrong, but they did a few things way right.  If you can sidestep the tedious path they set you on and stay focused on the main story, you could have some fun with this.  Didn't run into much in the way of fun sidequests, though.  They might be out there and I just didn't look very hard, but I only found 1 or 2 and after tens of hours trying to lead the collective horses to water and watching them drown I wasn't much in the mood to go looking.
Looking forward to see if Fallout 4 follows the pattern of "Lackluster game, great expansion" that its predecessor held to.
Short version: If it's on sale, and you've got a moderate amount of time to kill, power through the main quest and spare yourself the shallow crust of a world that surrounds it.

Vanilla game:
Fallout 4 is an immersive world with amazing visuals (don't listen to the other people) that has a lack of old fallout rpg elements, but doesn't bring the game down too much. The world and exploration is the best out of any recent fallout game. You will explore Boston, known at this time as the "Commonwealth" and believe me when i say it, exploration is easily the best part of any fallout game. While the graphics do look very nice, they may lack compared to most games that come out these days. Optimization, while not "unity bad," still will make mid end pcs struggle unless running on lowest settings (given you want 60 fps everywhere you go at least.) The game gives up the old skill system which many people loved a lot about the old fallouts. Instead of adding points to sneak, small guns, energy weapons, etc., you will go the "skyrim approach" and make the leveling a lot more simple. The perks are the big thing with leveling, like in old fallouts, you still choose perks that can have one level or multiple tiers. However, instead of having the skills, you now can add perk points to any of the S.P.E.C.I.A.L. abilities. There are a few bugs, but nothing that entering "tlc" in console can't fix. Finally, the companions are extremely buggy. 90% of the time when you try to trade or talk to them, they will walk away, making it impossible to interact with them. Instead of following behind you like the old bethesda games, they will often run ahead, going their own path. Finally, the dialogue is completely awful, the actual responses are fine, but the simplicity of the choices it lists is unbearable. Instead of full responses, it gives a few words and you have to often guess what your character is going to say. It's usually options of "yes, no, sarcastic, and information." Overall the base game gets a 7.5/10 (if bugs and optimization got fixed it would be 8.8/10)
The future of the game:
Just like any bethesda game, there will be dlc, and mods. The dlc hasnt been announced yet, but we could hope it would be something along the lines of 3 or 4 dlcs with a new map. Bethesda is also going to actively fix the game's bugs so that's something to look forward to. On the mod end, the creation kit hasn't been released yet, so a lot of the crazy things to do in modding aren't available. However, there are already mods fixing some of the issues in the base game, such as the one that displays what you're going to say fully. If all of the issues in the vanilla game get fixed by mods, this game is an easy 10/10.

Okay, though I enjoy the game more than less the difference is miniscule.
The sidequests get repetitive: go here speak to this person, go here kill these people, go back to this person get a reward (and for minutemen) go and speak to Preston to complete the quest and get another TEDIOUS quest.
The weapon drops are just.... bleh, the amount of pipe guns, Short Shotguns, Missile launchers, even FAT MEN just really makes weapon hunting pointless. Choices, what is the point of CHOICES!? No matter WHAT response you give the dialogue remains more or less the EXACT same and has absolutely NO effect on the story or alignment with other factions (unless you walk in with a certain companion).
POWER ARMOR!!.... I never really used, absolutely pointless, it really has very little use other than radiation protection and in early game carry capacity.
Companions are still absolutely useless (the only companion that was any good was Fawkes, EVER) and the amount of times I have seen ...... can't carry anymore was infuriating since there is NO indicator to how much your companions carry weight is. They also, as usual (unless you are Fawkes) die, in some cases even burn you up with a molotov or blow you up with a frag..
Settlements, nice idea but you have to arm ALL your settlers with armor, weapons AND ammo, unless you want them all to run around with pipe pistols or bare handed. Your shops make NO money, even if you make the 3rd level ones. The micro management of settlements is flawed, for example one of the settlements regardless of what I gave them plenty of beds, food, water, defense, power, I added shops and so on would ALWAYS be unhappy and settlers would leave! And there is just TOO MANY of these settlements, WAY too many. I ended up just focusing on Santuary, The Drive-in and The Castle.
And like Fallout 3 bugs, glitches and bull.... (enemies have the ability to shoot through walls in certain areas, game resets (in my case it also just flat out crashed) V.A.T.S is rubbish unless you make Perception, Luck build.
My BIGGEST problem with this game is the story doesn't really engage me in any way, I literally do not care about the kid (son), the illuminati kind of thing doesn't really work, as you know LONG before the actual development that you will have to destroy them.
I didn't really like any of the characters other than Hancock, and of course, Dogmeat in this game. I can't stand Preston or Dantse and the others are just very 'meh' (this includes all the storyline characters that you meet).
I am also the silent protagonist type, though the voicing isn't bad (in my opinion) I think giving the MC a voice removes a certain element from the players experience of the game.
The pros are few, but had an impact on me.
The BEST one I can say is that V.A.T.S no longer pauses the game, no more V.A.T.S to save my life before that last shot kills me.
Though the S.P.E.C.I.A.L is dumbed down it is a whole lot LESS convoluted, and makes a whole lot more sense, focus on this to unlock that, rather than put all your points into this and only after SO many points are put into this will you notice the difference.
Settlements, I liked the idea of helping people and creating settlements but it needs some serious refinements. Being able to build your own town is awesome probably spent about 9-12 hours building up my town, castle and making a little settlement in the Drive-in.
Customization I did enjoy crafting my weapons to my prefered style of play, I mean a 6 crank laser musket, with short barrel equals stupid damage but I love the incineration of my enemies.
Pointless stuff like abraxo cleaner, tin cans and junk has a relevence now and we all know there is way too much of this worthless stuff in Skyrim, Fallout 3 and to an extent Vegas.
Unlike many I also enjoyed the level scaling, though I like seeing my progress, I think going around killing enemies in one shot can get VERY boring VERY quickly.
ENEMIES: Rad Scorpions, they used to annoy me, they were everywhere and just a nuisance, but now there is less but still annoying for actual reasons (damn armored insects) Deathclaws now live up to their name, they WILL kill you more often than not and they look so much better! Legendary enemies! I like this idea but I think they need to chill on the mutation, not stop it, but make it so only a few do, also they need to deny the one shot V.A.T.S kill, they are supposed to be legendary after all.
The world, it's massive but unlike Vegas it isn't empty, there are so many places to go to, clear out and explore and it has a fair amount of surprises scattered around like the legendaries, a random deathclaw and if you are really lucky a Behemoth.
In all I like the game but for 7 years work it is lacking graphically, story wise, characters wise and quests wise. There are some improvements but not enough to justify the claims Bethesda made or the 7 years it took to make the game.

This game is kind of different than 3 and NV. It is hard to say how, but if you put hours into those games you will see what I mean. It is like NV in the sense that the player has great affect on the world around him/her. In NV, the Courier gets involved in a political war between factions trying to gain control of New vegas as well as the Mojave wastes. In Fallout 3, The Long Wanderer is essentially forced into joining the Brotherhood in a quest to find and inevitably help his father. Fallout 4 is pretty in between when it came to this, and it is what I was looking for. NV's questline was very roleplay-y which a lot of people loved. I didn't mind it, but having an affect on the whole world didn't mean as much to me as the feeling that Fallout 3 gave me. When you play that game alone, you feel lonely. You feel for the Lone Wanderer as he was left by his father out of the blue and his sheltered life is quickly manifested by the corruption and ugly truth of the Capital wastes. Fallout 4 finds a way in the middle of the two ideas, which I suppose can cater to all people.
The building is a meaningful addition to the game, but it certainly does have flaws. Things don't really snap into place and it takes a lot of time and frustation to make a good looking build. The build cap does get annoying too. In addition, people don't feel like they are really involved in the world. I'd say I have 35-45 hours in the game and I somewhat agree. There is a lot of world to explore, but from what I have seen no Megatons or ghoul invasions on Tenpenny Tower. I still have a lot to see, so take that lightly.
Combat I think is fantastic, and weapon ugrading is cool as well. Each enemy has its own strengths and weaknesses (besides Mirelurk Killclaws, don't think they have a weakness besides their 1 pixel heads). Deathclaws are very scary, and are sold as these titans that are impossible to kill and are definitely worthy of that hype.
All in all, I think it is a great game. I am a Fallout fanatic and this game was all I've been waiting for. I don't think for me it tops Fallout 3 as of yet. People think New Vegas is the best of all, and I see why, but for me I loved 3. The best thing is the modding tools for this game will be great. I know some people have the sentiment that the game should not need outside sources to fix the game and make it better, but I am not a professional critic and don't care so long as I get the most fun out of the game. I think we should all have the feeling. because we are all going to get the mods and have a blast regardless.
I give the game a 8.5/10, probably higher than most will give but I really do like this game a lot.

Disclaimer: I was torn about hitting Yes or No on the recommendation, its not a bad game on its own, but it IS a bad game for the fallout series. If this was the first in the series, I would rate it higher, but my expectations based on previous installments lowered the score. Thing I will explain in the review.
I won't lie. Like most, I was hooked on fallout 4 after playing the first 2 hours. The game showed so much promise, but after beating the mainstory and starting my second play through, I realized, quite honestly, there was no reason for a second play through. Like most have stated, there is no choice system or karma system in this fallout. There are 4 endings, 3 of them end the exact same way, the only variance is which factions you dont wipe out at the end (which you dont get to chose, you make enemies of 2 of the factions based on which one you chose for the ending). Also, with no level cap there's no reason for a second character, unless you wanted to replay the main story missions with a different style weapon.
The game has its ups, but if you were looking for that 100hour+time sink that most people expect from a fallout game, you won't find it here.
the settlement building is a nice addtion, but the UI for it is atrocious, the rules seem inconsistent. I can scrap an entire house in sanctuary but ONLY IF ITS TOTALLY COLLAPSED, for whatever reason. Settlement locations are predetermined, with most being very small 2 person farms which you get by "clearing out those nearby pesky raiders/ghouls" every..single..time. Seriously there's about 5 farms like this and the dialogue is the exact same at every single one.
The graphics are great for the scale of the game, no issues there, and the combat is the most fun its been, which I think is why so many people played the first hour or two, and immediatly went to every social media saying this game lived up to the hype. I was that person, too. Until i finished the game and felt pretty hollow inside.
Atmosphere(graphics, environment, sound): 9/10
Combat: 7/10
Story: 3/10 (The story itself isn't bad, but compared to previous fallouts, the lack of choice, karma and effect, etc, it just doesnt compare, No replay value to the storyline, because you can do all the side quests for every faction before getting to the "point of no return" in the story. Outside of the 4 main factions I haven't seen many sidequests worth doing.)
Content: 4/10 (Settlement building was a nice addition, and you can do a lot with it, but there is no depth to it. your settlements don't tie into the main story and it doesn't affect the game at all to improve any of the settlements, whether your settlements are happy or not has no affect on anything other than the number of settlers there. Basiclly just a 3D version of the ♥♥♥♥♥♥ phone fallout shelter app. Weapon and armor customization is the best its ever been, and the addition of legendary equipment is nice.

I've never bothered writing a review before, but Fallout is a special game for me. The origonal Fallout was the very first non-pirated game (eastern europe ftw) I ever bough after skipping on lunch in school for some time. I was around 10 years old back then. I have played all the Fallout games since then and will likely do so with all the other ones that will follow. This is why I felt that I need to write this review in hopes that someone somewhere will see it and others like it and the later iterations of the game I really love would be better.
PROS:
- Crafting system for weapons and armour is fantastic!
- Settlement building is an awesome new addition that I personally enjoyed greatly. I might have spent more time with that than the reast of the game. It really does make a difference when you have built a place to call home and are coming back to it between missions.
- Loads of items everywhere! Great variety (sometimes to a fault)
- The wasteland looks a lot more appealing colour wise but still feels like a wasteland. I like that.
- Gunplay is a lot better, thank you very much! That really needed to happen.
- Some really cool locations to visit and NPCs to meet. Although, only a handful are really memorable.
- Atmosphere is great and keeps you hooked!
And that's about it for the PROS I guess. Now for the less awesome stuff.
CONS:
- Interface as awhole is a joke. It's pre-alpha console port quality.
- Local area map IS NOT USABLE. Who ever looked at that and said "yeah it's fine" needs to get disability benefits, just like the guy who came up with it.
- Dialogue system. Oh man, the dialogue system. "Yes", "No", "Maybe" and "Sarcastic" that generally lead to same outcome. And you never really know what your character is going to say! Worst-change-ever.
- New skill system is not that great, but I don't outright hate it. Let's just say it could use some improvement.
- Skills and perks do not affect dialogue, only Charisma. RPG much? No, really?
- No carma system =/
- Complete absense of any explanation to the settlement management. On top of that, the information about the things you can build is lacking. Like the trading posts - what is the difference, how much do they bring in, etc?
- No follower management system AT ALL! Considering followers are a big part of the game, I don't see how they completely ignored any interface for them. How am I supposed to remember where each of my followers is? How happy with me they are? What is the weigh they can carry? Really lazy, Bethesda.
- Controls are good in 1st person only.
- LOADING SCREENS EVERYWHERE.
- Bugs are totally present. Not gamebreaking (at least for me) and mostly it's just some visual glitch, but they do break immersion at times.
- Graphics are OK at best. Slight improvement over Vegas. I am running everything on ultra and at times it still looks like sh*t. This engine should have retired several years ago.
- Story is just "meh". Find who? Yeah yeah later, let me clean the forest first. Although some side quests are pretty cool! But becoming a knight of The Brotherhood Of Steel - waaay to fast. As an old fan that us just wrong to me)
- Never ending side quests that tell you to "go clean out (insert any enemy here) nearby that threaten our village" that at times are on the opposite side of the map. Those lack any kind of originality.
- Flying on a Vertibird is SUCH a dissapointment. First time you get to do it I expected some cool sequence (FC: BloodDragon comes to mind at the very least). Nope! And it's also not possible to order it to fly to a specific point that is not a settlement, so essentially it's a slow way to fast travel (lol).
There is plenty of other things good and bad with this game, but those are the ones I wanted to mention the most. Now, all that being said (and looking at the list of negatives), you might think it's a bad game. No, it's not! The game kept me entertained for tens of hours and I'm not even done with it yet! I totally got my moneys worth in relation to hours spent playing! But.. I wish that I would have more to say than that about one of the coolest franchises ever!
The RPG element of the game has been significantly decreased. It feels like it drifted from RPG to shooter and I really hope that this will not be the case going forward.  So far, I would rate it at 6.5/10 as an RPG. Slightly higher as a whole experience, 7/10. As to recommending this game - yeah, I would recommend it for sure despite the shortcomings, but not for 60 bucks. Get it when it's around 40. Plus there will be significant mods by then. Pity they have to count on the modding community to fix their mistakes.
Really hope you get your sh*t together for the 5th one, Bethesda!
P.S. Witcher 3 will mop the floor with your faces on this years GOTY as a best... well, anything really.

First of all I want to say that this review is, just like every other one, based on personal opinion and preferences. I'll try to be a little bit objective, but it's not possible to be 100% objective in a review. So take no offense if I say something you don't agree with.
The game itself is good, but not perfect.
The gaming community might have expected too much at some points, and this led to some disappointment for some people.
I'd say it's worth the money, however, be sure your PC meets the minimum requirements.
It's a bit sad, but I get the whole point some of the Fallout 1/2 fans talk about. Yes, the game and some of it's new mechanics like a voiced protagonist and the 4-lines take away a lot of the roleplaying in the game. For example, I tried to make a 1 INT melee mutant build, but the voice and speech options kinda ruined it.
Most of the time the voice is an awesome addition, and it's pretty versatile, but it has it's restrictions. It doesn't fit a dumb mutant, an awkward nerd or a charming transexual.
I honestly don't understand all the fuss about this. To me the graphics, the colours, the weather system, the lush environment, the gore etc. etc. are pretty damn awesome.
Sure it's not a 100% lifelike/realistic, but I don't think that was the intention of the game designers. It's a different kind of beautiful, just as games like Borderlands or The Wolf Among Us have their very own style.
A lot of the new game mechanics, for example crafting and settlements, are a godsend. It adds so much to the game, that even if you explored every square inch of the world, you'll still be able to spend hours&hours in the game.
Also there are some nice additions like the grenade/melee hotkey, better 3rd person view, layered armor and legendary equipment which make the game a lot more smooth and fun to play.
This might be an issue to give solid advise about, as the PC specs can vary a lot from person to person.
I myself recently upgraded my video/graphics card to a MSI R9-380 4gb, this might not have been the wisest decision as Fallout 4 is optimised for Nvidia cards. Besides that my CPU is a bit outdated, and clearly causes some lagging and (rarely) crashes at some points.
Most of the time the game runs okay, on high settings it mostly stays between 40-60 fps, however when entering the dense city it can drop significantly.
Sometimes the game crashes, but I'm unsure if this has to do with my CPU, my Radeon/AMD graphics card, or just the game itself. So I can't really draw a conclusion from this.
My advise, if your specs just barely meet the requirements, it's probably time to upgrade your PC first.
The game is not perfect, some of the changes might not be the best and the whole hype may have raised the expectations a bit too high.
But to me it's still a wonderful game, on which I will spend many hours with delight. Totally worth the money.

However the fact is that this game still suffers from the same issues as with Fallout 3, Fallout NV, & Skyrim.  That is, the pathing, false VATS % calculations, and collission detection.
1.  Pathing of Companions:  They improved pathing mechanics.  However, instead of improving the pathing of companions, they cheezed it by allowing companions to teleport to the player.  So, the pathing of companions are just as bad as Skyrim, its just they won't get lost now because they have the super power of teleportation.
2.  Pathing of Bullets/Grenades:  This was a major issue with FO3 & FONV that seems to not have been fixed with FO4.  Even if you have a direct sighting on a target, shots maybe blocked by the obstacle that you can see through.  Like railing... I can see through the railing at the target, but the railing still blocks my shots.  This is especially an issue with grenades and being in doorways.  Despite being able to see outside the doorway at your target, sometimes the grenade will hit the doorway instead and either richochet somewhere differently (grenades) or explode on you (molotovs).  Again, this was an issue in FO3 & FONV that should have been fixed.
3.  False VATS % Calculation:  Just as with number 2, this was a major issue with FO3 & FONV that was never fixed.  When aiming at a target with VATS a % may show up but you will still hit an obstacle 100% of the time.  This is especially infuriating with 95% shots still hitting walls that you are clearly shooting around.
I enjoy FO4 as I view it has quite a few improvements over it's predecessors.  However, I want to inform potential buyers on the issues that this game currently has.

I have invested heavily in Fallout 4 having bought the game for the PS4 and the PC.  The game plays well on the PS4 where I have already clocked up considerable hours of play.
The PC version, purchased through Steam, is glitchy on my PC in respect of the start up procedure (gaphics) which caused an initial Lockpicking bug where the game failed to show the lock, bobby pin and screwdriver required to complete the task. This bug was fixed by trying different graphic options upon start up.
I am now playing Fallout 4 more on the PC having mastered the glitch - not least because the game operates very smoothly on my PC and I am very pleased with the graphics.  My heroine looks much better on the PC than on the PS4; infact, the same can be said of the whole game.
I recommend Fallout 4 because it is a great ACTION based RPG; it's compelling and draws you into a dangerous "edge on your seat" world that I find challenging.
It's a game that allows you to play the way you want with plenty of excellent in-game modding and creativity.  And the many adversaries you can encounter are, for the most part, more tactically astute. (Raiders are not normally stupid enough to attack a well protected settlement, but be prepared, and hostiles can be good at ambushing and using cover.)
One warning, Fallout 4 could disappoint those looking for a deeper role-playing experience where conversations can have complex cause and effects including those relating to moral issues.  Social interplay is simplistic.  However, there is factional intrigue and there is humour and good dialogue to be found.
Meanwhile, knowing how well the modding community have enhanced my favourite game Skyrim and continue to do so, I look upon my PC copy of Fallout 4 as a great investment.  It's going to get even better.

Boy is this a hard review to do. I allready played it way to much, even enjoyed it more than i probably should, you see this is not the Fallout i had hoped for and why?
I´ll tell you why, this is a dumbed down version of Fallout 3, this I guess is because the game also is launched on consoles.
Some of the things I miss the most are the choice/consequence based gameplay from Fallout 3, in Fallout 4 it never seem that you choices have any consequences to them, and you are such a good guy, that for the most of the game you can be a member of each and every faction, without this having any consequences at all, everybody just seem to like you, and trust you regardless of your affiliations.
Another thing I miss are the hard choices, in F3 in some missions you had to choose between bad and worse, and you felt like♥♥♥♥♥♥♥for it, it felt real. In F4 you always feel like the good guy, there are no importent choices, no situations where you can talk your way out of, few choices that even have an impact on the story. Even the dialogue you have with the ones you partner up with are anything more than small stories within the story, to make you feel just a little closer to them, but no matter what you do or what dialogue option you choose, the only response is ´Piper liked that´or ´Piper disliked that´ no more, nothing seems to matter and regardless of your partner, they quickly start to feel like nothing more than a pack animal for carrying your stuff.
The map is also one of the things i dislike, everything seems so cluttered, you often find Super Mutants and Raiders living right next to each other, without the seem to notice. You never feel alone, and one of the things i especially loved i F3 was wandering through empty landscapes, exploring empty buildings, in F4 every explorable building has either Raiders, Gunners, Synths or Mutants, you never feel alone, and there is just way to much shooting.

The settlement building is fun, allthough a little under developed, graphics are a little outdated, but that really does not matter because there is so much to see and do.
In its own right F4 is a great game, even with my complaints it is still way better than most RPGs on the marked today, the amount of content is staggering, and that alone makes the game worth its price, and we all know that when the modders are done, everybody can have exactly the F4 the want.

I'll be brief. It's easier for me to point at flaws rather than good points, but I do recommend the game.
The good:
-Solid story. Solid side stories/quests.
-Beautiful graphics, that set the tone of the game well.

The bad:
-Bethesda decided to dumb down another good series (no skills anymore)

This is a great game.

Fallout 4 gives you an huge post-apocalyptic wasteland to freely explore at your leisure: whether you're following the main quest, doing favours for a faction or simply wandering around looking for new places there's always something to do in the Commonwealth.
-good art style, we're pretty much used to it by now but the iconic armour, weapons, dilapidated ruins and radioactive wastes are always great and detailed
-great soundtrack
-we get full voice acting, and the voice actors do a good job overall
-huge wasteland to explore and fight in, there's really alot of places to discover and most of them have their own identity, not to mention a backstory thanks to notes or terminals you find
-tons of loot to gather, armour pieces, weapons, junk for your settlements etc
-nice crafting system lets you upgrade and tailor both armour and weapons to your preferred combat style
-building and managing settlements is almost a game within the game and I lost quite a few hours creating structures, dressing up settlers and arranging stuff
-improved character creator lets you finely tune your looks
-the story is pretty good
-a varied cast of characters and companions, while they won't win any awards for depth most of them are quite interesting and believable
-new perk system works well and streamlines character customization
-gunplay feels improved and is way less reliant on VATS
-great length if you immerse yourself in the world rather than speeding through the story
-graphics are hit or miss, while they look pretty nice at times they can also often come up as lacking details
-new perk system won't sit well with everyone, same goes for the stats points you're given during character creation
-as usual with Bethesda we get a good amount of bugs, thankfully none of them are truly gamebreaking but quite a few of them are annoying ( random framerate drops, bugged settlement happiness etc)
-being very combat oriented you'll be forced to out at least a good amount of points into related perks if you want to survive
-NPC and companion AI is quite bad, settlers get stuck often and cant navigate places properly, companions will often stick too near you and block doorways, stealth can easily be exploited to clear rooms without too much trouble etc
-the narrative lacks punch and I didn't feel much of an emotional attachment to the people/ places you're supposed to care about
-ending felt a bit "meh" overall, and a bit too hurried in its wrap-up
-most of the settlers I've had looked the same face and hair wise, it felt quite weird and might be a bug
-radiant quests can quickly get repetitive
-lacking tutorials
-dialogue choices can be murky in their final results (there's a mod already out for that, thankfully)
-the settlement building interface can be finicky when placing things on uneven ground
I've put almost 100 hours in the game before I felt I had done enough to finally pursue the last quest line: most of the time I had a blast simply exploring around , clearing and looting places or doing quests for one of the factions you can ultimately join. If you enjoy the sandbox world style that made Bethesda famous you'll find lots to do in Fallout 4 and there'll be even more if you decide to leave a mark in it by building and explanding settlements.
The actual storyline is decent, starting out pretty strongly but eventually losing momentum halfway through and wasting some interesting ideas, but it's at least good enough to make you willing to see how things end. Just make sure you keep your armour and weapons upgraded and get at least a few combat perks or you'll suffer alot...there's not much space for diplomacy in the Commonwealth and you're expected to keep up when bullets start flying (which is basically always).
Fallout has changed alot during the years, some changes were welcome while others not so much but there's no denying Fallout 4 is a great game and the best fun I've had this year: if you can keep up with its shortcomings there's no reason not to pick it up.

This review comes from a player who has played (and owns) all Fallout games. I try to be truthful in this review, without bias.
Pro's
- Settlement building (fits to the game)
- Reactivity of enemies (like deathclaws, assaultron, sentry bot)
- Better shooting mechanics and overall feel
- Overall graphics are great
- Crafting system (weapons, armors etc..)
- AI (when it works)
- Map size is sufficient
Con's
- Soulless game, by that I mean places and people feel like they don't belong to the world.
I know, It is hard to build living and breathing world.
However Fallout 1, Fallout 2 and FNV succeed in it just fine!
- Most of the side quests are silly (go kill or fetch something)
- Main story (I won't spoil)
- NPCs (plastic faces and awkward movement, just awful)
- Dialogue wheel and writing. Very bad choice. I totally hate it. Fallout games have always been
heavy in dialogue (discovering interesting new places, people etc...)
(Fallout game is not Mass Effect)
- Legendary enemies and their drops (Fallout game is not Borderlands)
- Karma gone
- Reputation gone
- Unkillable NPCs (In older Fallout games or in FNV you can kill anyone if you wanted and so it
should be)
- New character system (jack of all trades, bad choice)
- Lots of bugs (those will be soon fixed)
- Voiced protagonist (limits gameplay and modding in general)
- Not caring about the lore
Conclusion
I wouldn't consider this game as a role playing game because almost all of the aspects which define a role playing game, in general, have been stripped off from it (i.e dumbed down). Such as meaningful (and deep) writing, karma, reputation, leveling system, choices with consequences.
So in overall this game is a bit better than Fallout 3 in my opinion.
Is this game worthy successor after FNV? No
Is this game worthy of Fallout title? Hell no
My score 5/10
Would I recommend this game?
As a RPG player I can't recommend this game. If you want good Fallout/RPG, then buy Fallout  1 or Fallout 2 or FNV.
I end my review with citation: (originally from steam user Jelly Croissant)
"This is not a game for Fallout/RPG fans. This is a game for people who don't care about either of them."

The good:
+ A _Real_ open world. Not like every other title that claims the same thing but ends up railroading you.

+ Lighting. Atmospheric and strategic. Snipers will learn to hate mornings.

+ Being able to blow the arms and legs off a ghoul and watch it just sit there growling at you.

+ Long-range scouting with a scoped rifle will not tell you what faction you're looking at. You can either get closer to try to figure it out, or hope that that's not a friendly wearing raider armor.
On the Fence:

Link it to crafting, and you should be able to fine-tune that plasma rifle you've been using for ages much better than someone who's been running around with a 10mm pistol forever. The comic books are a welcome bonus to the existing perk tree, though.
The bad:
- No longer an issue

I will preface this by saying I have played all of the Fallout Series, either on PC, PS2 (Brotherhood of Steel), or PS3.
I am thoroughly enjoying the game thus far and will go through my thoughts on the good, the bad, and improvements over other games in the series.
BUGS:
There are some glitches and bugs, but these have only been a few random game crashes, my gun becoming invisible for a moment, or an NPC glitching through a wall or ceiling.  None of these have been frequent or have prohibited me from playing.
CONS:
Some of the tutorial information is non-existent.  There may be pop-up text once which goes unnoticed, or there may not be an explanation at all.  With some of the new items, this can be a PITA.  I've had to pause the game and look up a few things like: Exiting Power Armor, Setting up a supply line, assigning workers, the difference between storing and scrapping, etc.
The HUD compass does not show nearby NPCs (either friendly or enemy) unless they are looking to fight you.  There may be a perk for this, but I haven't found it yet.  This lack of info makes the game more challenging when going through unfriendly territory but more annoying when in friendly territory.
You get Power Armor way too early in the game.  It is more like a vehicle, requires fuel and repairing, but still helps you be quite overpowered.
COMPANIONS:
In the series, I've always been a lone wanderer, and that's how I stay in my current strategy.  So, I have no input on Companions or their AI.
PROS:
Junk.  Lots of it.  This game is a hoarder's dream.  I'm not a hoarder, but I could become one.  Unlike previous games, you don't have to worry about the junk to sell vs. using as a component.  Nearly EVERYTHING is usable.  The only truly junk items I've found are burnt books and magazines.  Everything else should be picked up and stored so you can Mod your weapons and armor or cook up some chems.
Enemies are better.  From Ghouls to Mirelurks, the enemies have better movements, more variety, and an added difficulty.  Molerats are no longer simple enemies that you can kill before they get close.  They will now burrow and come up behind you.  Radscorpions and others do the same thing.
You can dismember an enemy without killing it.  For example, if you shoot a ghoul's leg off, the ghoul will fall to the ground, still alive.
Weapon and Armor deterioration is gone (with the exception of Power Armor).  Radiation is also treated differently. I'm not sad to see either of these changes.
Visuals are better.  I'm not running this on max settings (because my PC can't handle that), but I am running on medium-high.  Enemies and people have more seem to have variety.  Also, as New Vegas was a step up in color from Fallout 3, this is a step up from New Vegas.  The environments can still be bleak, but weather has been added and many places have more colors beyond the grays and browns of the wasteland.
Overall, I'm definitely enjoying the game.  I'm looking forward to a couple of patches coming out, but this isn't New Vegas where I had to stop playing for months because a bug kept me from entering the strip.

Boy is this a hard review to do. I allready played it way to much, even enjoyed it more than i probably should, you see this is not the Fallout i had hoped for and why?
I´ll tell you why, this is a dumbed down version of Fallout 3, this I guess is because the game also is launched on consoles.
Some of the things I miss the most are the choice/consequence based gameplay from Fallout 3, in Fallout 4 it never seem that you choices have any consequences to them, and you are such a good guy, that for the most of the game you can be a member of each and every faction, without this having any consequences at all, everybody just seem to like you, and trust you regardless of your affiliations.
Another thing I miss are the hard choices, in F3 in some missions you had to choose between bad and worse, and you felt like♥♥♥♥♥♥♥for it, it felt real. In F4 you always feel like the good guy, there are no importent choices, no situations where you can talk your way out of, few choices that even have an impact on the story. Even the dialogue you have with the ones you partner up with are anything more than small stories within the story, to make you feel just a little closer to them, but no matter what you do or what dialogue option you choose, the only response is ´Piper liked that´or ´Piper disliked that´ no more, nothing seems to matter and regardless of your partner, they quickly start to feel like nothing more than a pack animal for carrying your stuff.
The map is also one of the things i dislike, everything seems so cluttered, you often find Super Mutants and Raiders living right next to each other, without the seem to notice. You never feel alone, and one of the things i especially loved i F3 was wandering through empty landscapes, exploring empty buildings, in F4 every explorable building has either Raiders, Gunners, Synths or Mutants, you never feel alone, and there is just way to much shooting.
The shooting allthough is one of the things Bethesda did better this time round, the v.a.t.s. no longer pauses, but just slows time down, resulting in way more dynamic battles. I especially love the crafting, tons of guns and armor, both can be configured in a myriad of ways.
The settlement building is fun, allthough a little under developed, graphics are a little outdated, but that really does not matter because there is so much to see and do.
In its own right F4 is a great game, even with my complaints it is still way better than most RPGs on the marked today, the amount of content is staggering, and that alone makes the game worth its price, and we all know that when the modders are done, everybody can have exactly the F4 the want.
Buy it, you will not regret it.

I will preface this by saying I have played all of the Fallout Series, either on PC, PS2 (Brotherhood of Steel), or PS3.
I am thoroughly enjoying the game thus far and will go through my thoughts on the good, the bad, and improvements over other games in the series.
BUGS:
There are some glitches and bugs, but these have only been a few random game crashes, my gun becoming invisible for a moment, or an NPC glitching through a wall or ceiling.  None of these have been frequent or have prohibited me from playing.
CONS:
Some of the tutorial information is non-existent.  There may be pop-up text once which goes unnoticed, or there may not be an explanation at all.  With some of the new items, this can be a PITA.  I've had to pause the game and look up a few things like: Exiting Power Armor, Setting up a supply line, assigning workers, the difference between storing and scrapping, etc.
The HUD compass does not show nearby NPCs (either friendly or enemy) unless they are looking to fight you.  There may be a perk for this, but I haven't found it yet.  This lack of info makes the game more challenging when going through unfriendly territory but more annoying when in friendly territory.
You get Power Armor way too early in the game.  It is more like a vehicle, requires fuel and repairing, but still helps you be quite overpowered.
COMPANIONS:
In the series, I've always been a lone wanderer, and that's how I stay in my current strategy.  So, I have no input on Companions or their AI.
PROS:
Junk.  Lots of it.  This game is a hoarder's dream.  I'm not a hoarder, but I could become one.  Unlike previous games, you don't have to worry about the junk to sell vs. using as a component.  Nearly EVERYTHING is usable.  The only truly junk items I've found are burnt books and magazines.  Everything else should be picked up and stored so you can Mod your weapons and armor or cook up some chems.
Enemies are better.  From Ghouls to Mirelurks, the enemies have better movements, more variety, and an added difficulty.  Molerats are no longer simple enemies that you can kill before they get close.  They will now burrow and come up behind you.  Radscorpions and others do the same thing.
You can dismember an enemy without killing it.  For example, if you shoot a ghoul's leg off, the ghoul will fall to the ground, still alive.
Weapon and Armor deterioration is gone (with the exception of Power Armor).  Radiation is also treated differently. I'm not sad to see either of these changes.
Visuals are better.  I'm not running this on max settings (because my PC can't handle that), but I am running on medium-high.  Enemies and people have more seem to have variety.  Also, as New Vegas was a step up in color from Fallout 3, this is a step up from New Vegas.  The environments can still be bleak, but weather has been added and many places have more colors beyond the grays and browns of the wasteland.
Overall, I'm definitely enjoying the game.  I'm looking forward to a couple of patches coming out, but this isn't New Vegas where I had to stop playing for months because a bug kept me from entering the strip.

Fallout 4 gives you an huge post-apocalyptic wasteland to freely explore at your leisure: whether you're following the main quest, doing favours for a faction or simply wandering around looking for new places there's always something to do in the Commonwealth.
-good art style, we're pretty much used to it by now but the iconic armour, weapons, dilapidated ruins and radioactive wastes are always great and detailed
-great soundtrack
-we get full voice acting, and the voice actors do a good job overall
-huge wasteland to explore and fight in, there's really alot of places to discover and most of them have their own identity, not to mention a backstory thanks to notes or terminals you find
-tons of loot to gather, armour pieces, weapons, junk for your settlements etc
-nice crafting system lets you upgrade and tailor both armour and weapons to your preferred combat style
-building and managing settlements is almost a game within the game and I lost quite a few hours creating structures, dressing up settlers and arranging stuff
-improved character creator lets you finely tune your looks
-the story is pretty good
-a varied cast of characters and companions, while they won't win any awards for depth most of them are quite interesting and believable
-new perk system works well and streamlines character customization
-gunplay feels improved and is way less reliant on VATS
-great length if you immerse yourself in the world rather than speeding through the story
-graphics are hit or miss, while they look pretty nice at times they can also often come up as lacking details
-new perk system won't sit well with everyone, same goes for the stats points you're given during character creation
-as usual with Bethesda we get a good amount of bugs, thankfully none of them are truly gamebreaking but quite a few of them are annoying ( random framerate drops, bugged settlement happiness etc)
-being very combat oriented you'll be forced to out at least a good amount of points into related perks if you want to survive
-NPC and companion AI is quite bad, settlers get stuck often and cant navigate places properly, companions will often stick too near you and block doorways, stealth can easily be exploited to clear rooms without too much trouble etc
-the narrative lacks punch and I didn't feel much of an emotional attachment to the people/ places you're supposed to care about
-ending felt a bit "meh" overall, and a bit too hurried in its wrap-up
-most of the settlers I've had looked the same face and hair wise, it felt quite weird and might be a bug
-radiant quests can quickly get repetitive
-lacking tutorials
-dialogue choices can be murky in their final results (there's a mod already out for that, thankfully)
-the settlement building interface can be finicky when placing things on uneven ground
I've put almost 100 hours in the game before I felt I had done enough to finally pursue the last quest line: most of the time I had a blast simply exploring around , clearing and looting places or doing quests for one of the factions you can ultimately join. If you enjoy the sandbox world style that made Bethesda famous you'll find lots to do in Fallout 4 and there'll be even more if you decide to leave a mark in it by building and explanding settlements.
The actual storyline is decent, starting out pretty strongly but eventually losing momentum halfway through and wasting some interesting ideas, but it's at least good enough to make you willing to see how things end. Just make sure you keep your armour and weapons upgraded and get at least a few combat perks or you'll suffer alot...there's not much space for diplomacy in the Commonwealth and you're expected to keep up when bullets start flying (which is basically always).
Fallout has changed alot during the years, some changes were welcome while others not so much but there's no denying Fallout 4 is a great game and the best fun I've had this year: if you can keep up with its shortcomings there's no reason not to pick it up.
