Playing Fallout 4 is a joyous experience. Exploring and collecting loot is more rewarding than in Fallout 3 and the combat is great fun.
An important caveat: it takes time and effort before the game really gets going. Personally I was expecting to be wowed a bit more in the first two hours or so.
The ability to improve and customize weapons plays a big part in the latter. After a few hours of play and some effort, it's easy to create guns that suit a preferred playing style.
The world is filled with locations and quests and there is enough backstory to keep the game intriguing. The general design is interesting and pleasant. Some, if not most, simple side quests offer a lot of action.
The game has a few flaws. The animation isn't very good. This is a problem in conversations. The facial animation is both unconvincing and distracting and doesn't really convey emotion.
The mains story isn't bad in itself, but feels tagged on. After three traumatic experiences in the beginning of the game, experiences that would have broken most people, the protagonist seemingly shrugs any bad feelings of and continues to act as nothing has happened and nothing has changed. There is no sense of urgency and there are no emotional high and low points.
This is also true of relationships within the game. I had some fun flirting with my follower (I chose a female journalist and publisher named Piper) but at some point the relationship reached its conclusion and that was that. Mission accomplished and no consequences.
All this doesn't matter much, Fallout 4 is about exploring and experiencing a sense of wonder. But I do feel that the main story, in part because of poor execution, is a distraction rather than an asset. I would have preferred a character without a backstory. Or a better story that was told in a more convincing way.
The game looks pretty good, but a crisper look would have been appreciated. For various reasons the game looks a bit blurry. The fact that the FOV can't be changed is a bit disappointing.
As mentioned before, the world is filled with content, this is a huge game. But compared to games like The Witcher 3 and Bethesda's own Skyrim, Fallout 4 feels a bit small. It's an odd contradiction.
The optional settlement building is awkward. Yes, it's completely optional, but it feels underdeveloped and some functionality is missing.
Still, for me this is the game of the year. It's a great action RPG and a great open world game. Other games have better stories and tell them better, but the sheer fun I'm having playing Fallout 4 tips the scale for me.

This review is written only after completing the main story and some side quests. I have not finished the whole game.
After five years without a new Fallout game, our prayers have been answered. Is it worth the wait. Well, some people are saying "no". Me? I am saying hell yeah, it was worth it!
The story in this one is just as great as Fallout 3's story. It is full of excellent characters, and has a wide arrange of voices, unlike previous Bethesda games where you hear the same five voices throughout the whole game, and your character now has a voice. Players can also have their name spoken by NPCs, if you pick from a specific list of names. Mine isn't one of them, and it's just like every tourist attraction souvenier, all over again. And the graphics are beautiful, with a lot more colors than previous Fallout games.
Combat feels a lot smoother than 3 and New Vegas. Guns seem to hit a lot more than they used to, and can be customized. I literally had the same pipe pistol throughout the whole game, and I just kept upgrading it to become more and more awesome. In addition to that, you can also use them as a melee weapon if your enemy gets too close, so you can kill them without having to use a bullet. Grenades and mines don't have to be equipped as your main weapon anymore, but, unfortunately, you use them by holding the melee button, which is troublesome, since there were a few instances where I needed to hit someone close to me, but held the button a bit too long, and used one of my grenades. I understand why if you're using a controller, but this is PC, I have a keyboard, I should be able to put it on one of the many unused keys.
Power armor now feels like power armor. You build it from a frame and some scrap metal, and all sorts of different gadgets to it. It does affect how you move about, and feels much more tank-like than if you simply wear the clothes you peeled off of a raider's corpse. It also requires a fuel source, and pieces of it will need to be repaired, so you can't simply wear it forever, and be an indestructable badass amongst the average threats you'll find in the Commonwealth.
Building settlements is an interesting that many players will spend hours playing with, even though it's something I didn't spend much time doing.
Followers are a bit smarter than they were in previous games, but still do stupid♥♥♥♥♥♥that you don't want to. At least this time they aren't using a melee weapon, even though I told them to use a gun, and gave them plenty of ammo for it. You can romance a few of them, but wish there were a few more options (no sexy ghoul ladies, Bethesda?) They also can't die, so you no longer have to make the choice between losing progress, or losing a bunch of gear and a friend.
Speech is a bit more refined, and has players split on whether or not it's good. On one hand, I love how all dialogue is spoken, but on the other, I miss having many options of what I'm going to say to someone. This is something you're going to have to make your own opinion about.
This should be the best game in the franchise (well, at least the Bethesda games; I haven't put enough time into the originals to fairly judge them, yet), if it weren't for two glaring problems.
Karma is gone. I no longer know if I am post-apocalyptic Jesus, or the bringer of destruction. I don't even see why it was taken away. It was an excellent feature!
The RPG elements have been watered down, severely. In previous games, upon levelling up, you got a few points to dump into various skills such as lockpicking, speech, explosives, etc, then got to to pick a perk to go with it. In this one, everything is just lumped together into perks.
Hopefully, both of these problems will be addressed in the next game.
So, this is basically Game of the Year/10. Buy it. Buy it, now.

Kind of a mediocre shooter with a so-so story. Definitely a more "gentrified" version of the Fallout legacy, largely to its deficit.
My main gripe is that if you're going to go to the trouble of adding a "settlement" system into the game, why not take that concept to the next level and make it REALLY interesting. For example, adding Civilization-like strategy elements, or really thinking through some sort of substantive basis for having settlements in the first place. It always disappoints me when a game like this, which is so close to doing something truly outstanding and paradigm-shifting, doesn't go the full distance.
I won't rehash many of the common criticisms others have made (a mile-long bug list, somewhat shoddy PC performance, obvious balance issues that should have been solved in QA) but if I can pick one thing, on a technical level, that really bothers me it's the UI. Who the heck designed the menus and interactivity? It feels like they were dealt with dead last in the development process and pushed out the door in a very obviously unpolished state. For a $60 AAA game, having a UI as atrocious as this game's is inexcusable.
I enjoyed F4 on some level, and you'll likely enjoy it as well; but wait for it to go on sale, as there's really nothing in here that's going to blow your mind or that really justifies the high price tag.

This first point is the biggest reason I am giving this game the thumbs down.  If you are an "Explorer" type gamer you will not have fun with this game.  The enemies are zoned and each zone has a level range to it.  So zone 1 has enemies lv 1-5 and zone 2 could be lv 50-70 and they could be right next to each other.  This means you can't just pick a direction and explore.  You have to go to the zones that are in your level range or you will just find bullet sponges.  And there is no indication on your map where these zones are set up. I hate having to play a linear game.  I get Bethesda games so I can say "To hell with the main quest lets just go east and see what I find."  That is not possible anymore.
Point 2.  You can't play as YOUR character anymore either.  You are a person with a backstory, a voice, and a child to rescue.  Why bother with a character creator and giving name options if Bethesda just wants you to be this person.
Point 3.  You have to use VATS.  This was optional in F3 and New Vegas.  I hate using VATS.  Many animal enemies like the damn giant misquitos have such small hit boxes, move so damn fast, or burrow underground that you can't target manually.  Just go for turn based combat or quick time events at this point if you dont want me to interact during a fight.
Point 4.  The city builder has no tutorial.  Took me 18 hours to figure out how to connect power lines to objects that need them.
Point 5.  Your dialogue choses are Yes, No, Sarcastic, and Huh?.  No explaination of what you will actually say though.  Will sarcastic come off as an ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ or as a joker?  Is it any better than just saying yes or no?
Point 6. It is actually possible to have a bad character build.  This goes back to Points 1 & 2 really.  Basically if you do not play as a high damage (weapon mod perks) tank (Armor perks) then you're going to die.  Not just, oh combat is a bit harder but I can do this other stuff really well, you will just not get anywhere because of the Zoning of point 1.
I got the pip boy edition because I was a fan of the previous games.  I feel cheated.  This is not the game I paid for.

Leveling up just seems so unsatisfactory now.  You get one perk.  After leveling up a perk, you usually have to wait 10-20 more levels until you can level it up again.  And most of them are really uninteresting.  When I see the perks, I don't think "Wow that's so cool I would like that." I think, "Meh".  Most of them STR perks give you more damage (nothing creative like Skyrim had, like bleed damage on axes, stagger, zoom on arrows, etc), literally none of the charisma perks sound interesting, the luck perks are ok but they barely ever even happen (and this is coming from a maxed luck character), and then there's a bunch of perks littered around that give you access to more crafting or lockpicking or some ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t.  Just overall nothing that's really too exciting.  I don't feel like I am making any progress level to level and I just feel no motivation to continue playing.
Overall, there's just a lot less options.  Now, you need charisma to succeed with dialogue.  In Fallout New Vegas, you could rely on high skill levels, which dont even exist any more or you could use your SPECIAL points to win people over. Every thing is wasteland and really ♥♥♥♥ing depressing.  Overall you just have less options and less control over your storyline.  I would highly recommend waiting for the price to drop and mods to come out, or not just getting this game.

This review is written only after completing the main story and some side quests. I have not finished the whole game.
After five years without a new Fallout game, our prayers have been answered. Is it worth the wait. Well, some people are saying "no". Me? I am saying hell yeah, it was worth it!
The story in this one is just as great as Fallout 3's story. It is full of excellent characters, and has a wide arrange of voices, unlike previous Bethesda games where you hear the same five voices throughout the whole game, and your character now has a voice. Players can also have their name spoken by NPCs, if you pick from a specific list of names. Mine isn't one of them, and it's just like every tourist attraction souvenier, all over again. And the graphics are beautiful, with a lot more colors than previous Fallout games.
Combat feels a lot smoother than 3 and New Vegas. Guns seem to hit a lot more than they used to, and can be customized. I literally had the same pipe pistol throughout the whole game, and I just kept upgrading it to become more and more awesome. In addition to that, you can also use them as a melee weapon if your enemy gets too close, so you can kill them without having to use a bullet. Grenades and mines don't have to be equipped as your main weapon anymore, but, unfortunately, you use them by holding the melee button, which is troublesome, since there were a few instances where I needed to hit someone close to me, but held the button a bit too long, and used one of my grenades. I understand why if you're using a controller, but this is PC, I have a keyboard, I should be able to put it on one of the many unused keys.
Power armor now feels like power armor. You build it from a frame and some scrap metal, and all sorts of different gadgets to it. It does affect how you move about, and feels much more tank-like than if you simply wear the clothes you peeled off of a raider's corpse. It also requires a fuel source, and pieces of it will need to be repaired, so you can't simply wear it forever, and be an indestructable badass amongst the average threats you'll find in the Commonwealth.
Building settlements is an interesting that many players will spend hours playing with, even though it's something I didn't spend much time doing.
Followers are a bit smarter than they were in previous games, but still do stupid♥♥♥♥♥♥that you don't want to. At least this time they aren't using a melee weapon, even though I told them to use a gun, and gave them plenty of ammo for it. You can romance a few of them, but wish there were a few more options (no sexy ghoul ladies, Bethesda?) They also can't die, so you no longer have to make the choice between losing progress, or losing a bunch of gear and a friend.
Speech is a bit more refined, and has players split on whether or not it's good. On one hand, I love how all dialogue is spoken, but on the other, I miss having many options of what I'm going to say to someone. This is something you're going to have to make your own opinion about.
This should be the best game in the franchise (well, at least the Bethesda games; I haven't put enough time into the originals to fairly judge them, yet), if it weren't for two glaring problems.
Karma is gone. I no longer know if I am post-apocalyptic Jesus, or the bringer of destruction. I don't even see why it was taken away. It was an excellent feature!
The RPG elements have been watered down, severely. In previous games, upon levelling up, you got a few points to dump into various skills such as lockpicking, speech, explosives, etc, then got to to pick a perk to go with it. In this one, everything is just lumped together into perks.
Hopefully, both of these problems will be addressed in the next game.
So, this is basically Game of the Year/10. Buy it. Buy it, now.

This game is fun, but for a Fallout RPG it's kinda garbage.
Positives:
-Crafting system: The crafting system is very fun to use, it makes pretty much all the junk you find usefull.

Negatives:
-Choices: Rather than giving you plenty of choices like the old Fallouts, a lot of them are now just the illusion of choice. Mutiple times it will look like you can make a choice by saying  something completly different, but it ends up being the same thing.
-RPG Elements: The RPG elements in general have been cut down to be a simple shooter with a open world, it feels a lot like Borderlands in a way.
-Speech System: It's down right awful,  you can't even compare it to older Fallouts, it's like a crappy version of Mass Effect.
-Voiced Character: I can't stand the voice, sorry but for someone who loves RP, this is horrible, I can't imagine the voice I want now, and everything your character says sounds nice.
-Disappointing Graphics: Are you kidding me? This game does look pretty, but it could of been so much more, Bethesda shouldn't be rallying on modders to fix that.
-Lack of Side Quest: Fallout New Vegas had way more, almost everywheres you went there was one, in this it's a challange to find a side quest.

-Bad Optimization: The reason this makes me mad is because I will sometimes get low FPS for like 6 seconds, yet  this game has horrible textures. (I run this on ultra with a GTX 960, i7 Quad Core 4770k, and 12 gbs of ram.)
Conclusion: If you want a fun sandbox game, go for it. If you are looking for a good RPG ro RP in, you will be disappointed, and  I reccomend Fallout 1, 2, or New Vegas.

I'd like to preface this review by saying I've greatly enjoyed my time in fallout 4 so far. The chance to be re immersed in the fallout world has been wonderful. It's scratched an itch I'm sure we've all had since fallout new vegas. Fallout 4 is a fun game furthering the tales of this fantastic post apocalyptic world. The updated crafting system, the enemies, the new area to explore....
HOWEVER
As a Fallout title, I can not recommend. There are many things that are simply... wrong... with this game.
The ending, without giving any spoilers, leaves much to be desired. I'd expect these kinds of endings from a NEW title (graphics aside).  Previous games left you fulfilled when you reached a conclusion to any given storyline, while Fallout 4 leaves a sour taste in your mouth.
The building system. Now, this was my main draw to the game when I watched the unveiling. Build my own settlements? Heck yeah! the problem is, it's incomplete. The indie game RUST has a more complete building system. Within a half hour of starting to build, you'll notice there are ZERO physics implemented. I built a tower for all my settlers floating in the middle of each settlement supported by a set of stairs at the entrance. plant 50 Tatos underneath and set 8 turrets at the entrance, and welcome to your raider proof sky tower. It was funny the first time, after that it felt sad... This isn't minecraft after all.
While I have many more issues, My last for this review will be the Gimmicks. Codsworth saying your name (and one holotape). NEAT! but only if you have one of twenty or so names names (I was lucky enough in that regard) and nowhere else in the game. The Pipboy app for your phone, a cute little idea, but wears away after the first five minutes, and those were resources that could have been put into other aspects of the game to give them a proper polish. Oh! while I'm on that topic, that monstrosity of a cash grab they sent out with the Pipboy edition is repulsive. In person it looks cheap, Like a dollar store toy, and it's FLIMSY! I'm very glad I didn't order it myself, as the top dial already broke on my friend's Pipboy, along with the faux leather tearing at the seams even before he used it.
BOTTOM LINE
Was it a fun game? Yes. Did it deserve its price tag? Absolutely not! At this point I feel the LEAST that Bethesda could do would be to give the season pass free to anyone who made the mistake of pre ordering this wasted potential of a game. Do yourselves a favour, and don't buy it until GOTY makes it down to $40. I give Fallout for a 6/10, a good game to find in the bargain bin.

Fallout 4 is a game that many people feel very passionate about in both negative and positive ways. Rather than make unavoidably bold statements about this game and how it fits within the context of the Fallout franchise as a whole, I will simply share some facts. And one of the only things I can say with certainty, is that I like this game. I like it a lot. Here is what I like:
I like finding legendary equipment.
I like shooting off people's limbs and watching their heads explode.
I like Piper.
I like Nick.
I like a lot the companions actually.
I like the fact that choosing a faction was kind of stressful for me.
I like exploring, and finding items.
I like crafting, and building the best weapons and armor I can.
I like building my settlements, and making an armory for all my customized power armor.
I like how goofy this game is.
I like how dense the map is.
I like finding letters and clues and intersting terminal logs.
I like building up my perks and leveling up.
I like the atmosphere, and the lighting, even the (sometimes wonky) graphics and (very wonky) animations.
I like that I can turn on this game and always find something to do, even if it's jut ♥♥♥♥ing around.
And what do I not like?
I don't like overburdening.
I don't like that I can't talk to Elder Maxon after the end game due to a bug.
I don't like the other bugs that are similar to the one above, such as NPCs randomly telling me that a minor NPC was dead, when she wasn't, and was literally standing right next to them, what the ♥♥♥♥ Bethesda. THEY STILL THINK SHE'S DEAD.

Fallout 4 is simultaneously a great game and a disapointing one at the same time. I completed the campaign and have done about 10 hours of side quests so I feel like i know enough to write a review. In a quick pros and cons list ill talk about the good sides and the bad sides of the game.
Pros:
-the colour pallet in the game is much improved and the world has vibrance, no longer are the only colours♥♥♥♥♥♥brown and dull grey
-the voiced character turned out actually work and he gives some real emotion to the dialouge, despite some occasionally very cheesy writing
-interesting main story that gets the job done even though if it loses focus and aim often
-interesting characters throughout game
-companions implemented really well they feel like they are part of the story and are not just your thugs anymore
-huge engrossing world with so many awesome side quests, creepy and engaging locations and theres always cool little secrets and puzzles to find
-game really rewards exploration
-combat really really improved, and fighting outside of vats no longer feels like a chore. Though melee combat could be fleshed out a bit more
-so many weapons
-amazing modding system that allows you to customize your weapon any way you want
-cool base building mechanic that is actually pretty well fleshed out even if they dont give you really any motivation to do it, and worst of all there are no tutorials for this mechanic making everything really confusing at first

Cons:
-horrible UI really needs improving or a mod
-the radio stations are funny to listen to and have nice 50's music at first, but there is such a small collection of them you will probably hear the same song or news a 100 times and you will eventually just turn it off
-graphics are complete♥♥♥♥♥♥ low res textures, poor facial animations and despite all this there are constant framerate stutters that can go into the 20's in big open areas [and this on a pc that can run the witcher 3 on ultra and get a steady 50 fps] it is really unacceptable for this to happen Bethesda
-there are a ton of bugs and glitches ranging from funny to game breaking
-the dialogue wheel is terrible, they dumbed down dialogue so much where other characters have generic responses and your dialogue choices eventually come down to Yes/No/Maybe/Sarcastic

FINAL VERDICT:
The game sadly did not live up to the hype and was disapointing in many aspects. But when i look back at how much fun i had and how much more content and fun there is still to be had I realised this game is definitly worth your money.

Amazing game with very few bugs, I'll be mainly comparing it to New Vegas.
The main story line is great, maybe a bit generic compared to Fallout 3, but great nonetheless.
Graphics are a nice upgrade compared to New Vegas; better color pallet, improved animation and well optimized for PC.
The weapon- and armor upgradeability is easy to learn. Mods can be found scavenging the wasteland, or having enough materials in your workbench. There are over 700 mods, including scopes, barrels, stocks and more. You can mod a weapon at a weapon workbench. Legendary weapons/armor can be found troughout the game and deal more damage or have a special attack, rather than a regular weapon. Power armor is too easy to find, and personally I don't like using it. Mainly because it uses fusion cores which deplete quite quickly and has an annoying overlay in my opinion.
The biggest improvement since New Vegas has to be the ability to start your own settlements, building houses and powering/protecting them. To find resources for your settlement(s), you can scrap nearly any object in the world for parts - even entire previously built structures. The foundations for a well-functioning settlement are quite easy, having enough beds, food, water, protection and a recruitment beacon are all you need. A big tip is to link them together with a trading route, allowing all workshops to sync together (shared resources). In total there's 14 settlements you can own.
The weather system has also changed slightly, there's now rain/thunderstorms, and even random rad-storms which give a small amount of radiation with every lightning strike. Wandering around in the middle of nowhere with a rad-storm going on definitely adds to the sp00ky-factor.
Map size is good, not too big or too small. There are alot of locations you can discover and it feels like there's alot more to do/explore compared to the New Vegas map. Boston is a huge city and it's easy to get lost in all the different buildings. The Glowing Sea is an interesting area, as it is outside the map. In this area you deal alot of radiation, so a hazmat suit/power armor is recommended.
The camera in this game is good, and hasn't changed much since NV.
The radio stations are okay, but it's a shame Diamond City Radio used so many tracks from Fallout 3 (Galaxy News Radio). The OST in New Vegas was great with the perfect music choice for the Mojave. They should have put more effort into making Diamond City Radio good by adding a more diverse tracklist. Classical Radio does not have a DJ, but has some good soundtracks.
The conversation system is something different compared to NV and 3. You use the arrow keys to select dialogue options, negative point to this is that you can not see the line you're about to say.
There's alot of nice companions. Your household robot called Codsworth being my favorite one. You can get Codsworth at the start of the game, and have him stick with you until the end. Certain situations. building interiors or player actions triggers a funny quote/remark.
In general, this is a great game any Fallout enthusiast will enjoy and I can not wait until they start releasing the DLC's.

Fallout 4 is a great addition to the Fallout series.  I'm really enjoying the game, it's addicting.  Fallout 4 does feel a bit like Fallout + Skyrim.  The world delivers an excellent Fallout world experience... even better than Fallout 3 or NV.  If you are chomping at the bit for a Fallout experience and value dollar to hours played this game is worth retail.  I have only seen the game crash once in 95+ hours played.  If you like the Fallout universe pick it up now.
Combat can play a lot more like FPS than previous installments in the series.  I was skeptical of the difficulty system to begin with.  If you max difficulty at the start enemies will feel like bullet sponges.  I found that if you ramp the difficulty up as you go it feels much more natural.
How you ramp the difficulty will depend on how quickly you take damage or weapon mod perks.  I changed difficulty to very hard by the high 30's and bumped it up to survival in the mid 40's.  Survival difficulty creates a spread of enemies; some still go down fast, others become bullet spongy (but not bad if you have a lot of damage perks).  The best thing about survival difficulty is it really slows down your healing which forces you to use the environment a bit more for cover.  I like that the wasteland can offer challenging battles.
Perhaps the biggest negatives of the game thus far.
The game offers changes from previous installments of the series.
What felt the same since Fallout 3/NV.
What felt new since Fallout 3/NV.

I'd like to preface this review by saying I've greatly enjoyed my time in fallout 4 so far. The chance to be re immersed in the fallout world has been wonderful. It's scratched an itch I'm sure we've all had since fallout new vegas. Fallout 4 is a fun game furthering the tales of this fantastic post apocalyptic world. The updated crafting system, the enemies, the new area to explore....
HOWEVER
As a Fallout title, I can not recommend. There are many things that are simply... wrong... with this game.
The ending, without giving any spoilers, leaves much to be desired. I'd expect these kinds of endings from a NEW title (graphics aside).  Previous games left you fulfilled when you reached a conclusion to any given storyline, while Fallout 4 leaves a sour taste in your mouth.
The building system. Now, this was my main draw to the game when I watched the unveiling. Build my own settlements? Heck yeah! the problem is, it's incomplete. The indie game RUST has a more complete building system. Within a half hour of starting to build, you'll notice there are ZERO physics implemented. I built a tower for all my settlers floating in the middle of each settlement supported by a set of stairs at the entrance. plant 50 Tatos underneath and set 8 turrets at the entrance, and welcome to your raider proof sky tower. It was funny the first time, after that it felt sad... This isn't minecraft after all.
While I have many more issues, My last for this review will be the Gimmicks. Codsworth saying your name (and one holotape). NEAT! but only if you have one of twenty or so names names (I was lucky enough in that regard) and nowhere else in the game. The Pipboy app for your phone, a cute little idea, but wears away after the first five minutes, and those were resources that could have been put into other aspects of the game to give them a proper polish. Oh! while I'm on that topic, that monstrosity of a cash grab they sent out with the Pipboy edition is repulsive. In person it looks cheap, Like a dollar store toy, and it's FLIMSY! I'm very glad I didn't order it myself, as the top dial already broke on my friend's Pipboy, along with the faux leather tearing at the seams even before he used it.
BOTTOM LINE
Was it a fun game? Yes. Did it deserve its price tag? Absolutely not! At this point I feel the LEAST that Bethesda could do would be to give the season pass free to anyone who made the mistake of pre ordering this wasted potential of a game. Do yourselves a favour, and don't buy it until GOTY makes it down to $40. I give Fallout for a 6/10, a good game to find in the bargain bin.

Fallout 4 is simultaneously a great game and a disapointing one at the same time. I completed the campaign and have done about 10 hours of side quests so I feel like i know enough to write a review. In a quick pros and cons list ill talk about the good sides and the bad sides of the game.
Pros:
-the colour pallet in the game is much improved and the world has vibrance, no longer are the only colours♥♥♥♥♥♥brown and dull grey
-the voiced character turned out actually work and he gives some real emotion to the dialouge, despite some occasionally very cheesy writing
-interesting main story that gets the job done even though if it loses focus and aim often
-interesting characters throughout game
-companions implemented really well they feel like they are part of the story and are not just your thugs anymore
-huge engrossing world with so many awesome side quests, creepy and engaging locations and theres always cool little secrets and puzzles to find
-game really rewards exploration
-combat really really improved, and fighting outside of vats no longer feels like a chore. Though melee combat could be fleshed out a bit more
-so many weapons
-amazing modding system that allows you to customize your weapon any way you want
-cool base building mechanic that is actually pretty well fleshed out even if they dont give you really any motivation to do it, and worst of all there are no tutorials for this mechanic making everything really confusing at first
-so much content really worth your money
Cons:
-horrible UI really needs improving or a mod
-the radio stations are funny to listen to and have nice 50's music at first, but there is such a small collection of them you will probably hear the same song or news a 100 times and you will eventually just turn it off
-graphics are complete♥♥♥♥♥♥ low res textures, poor facial animations and despite all this there are constant framerate stutters that can go into the 20's in big open areas [and this on a pc that can run the witcher 3 on ultra and get a steady 50 fps] it is really unacceptable for this to happen Bethesda
-there are a ton of bugs and glitches ranging from funny to game breaking
-the dialogue wheel is terrible, they dumbed down dialogue so much where other characters have generic responses and your dialogue choices eventually come down to Yes/No/Maybe/Sarcastic
-they "streamlined" the skill tree and feels like they watered down the role playing aspect of the game- it was really dispointing
FINAL VERDICT:
The game sadly did not live up to the hype and was disapointing in many aspects. But when i look back at how much fun i had and how much more content and fun there is still to be had I realised this game is definitly worth your money.
8/10

I've been playing this game a lot for the last few days, and although my steam only says I've played it for 54 hours, I've played it for about 80 hours on my first character.
This game is amazing but has a lot of flaws, like any other good game out there.
It's two huge steps forward feature-wise, but a huge leap back roleplay-wise.
With this being said, I still found it quite easy to immerse myself, if not easier. The only lack was the sort of customization the skill-based progression offered. The graphics are mediocre, but the art style is amazing and the animations are suprisingly good for a Fallout game.
The gunplay has been improved MILES and I actually enjoy going into combat - the gunplay is really solid, and feels amazing. As a result, I rarely ever use VATS - which has been improved quite a bit. The "Slow-motion" rather than "No-motion" is a great addition for a fast paced game. What I especially like is the fact that you can leave VATS whenever, wherever.
The environments are huge leap forward. They don't feel recycled and every area/zone feels different. They also introduced the good ol' "rubberbanding" aka "unleveled world". That's a good step in the right direction (It was standard for old school RPG's), if we want to have games that are more challenging.
The power armor system is one of my personal favorite. The armor actually feels like a suit of power armor, designed for combat, instead of a lousy armor you put on like any other. The first time I stepped into the power armor I felt very powerful. However, in late game areas, you'll discover that power armor doesn't make you a space marine, rather a tool to keep you alive in places you normally wouldn't be able to last a minute. The armor increases your damage reductions by ♥♥♥♥tonnes as well as radiation resistance, making you capable of traveling into heavily irradiated areas without dying within seconds.
The new settlement system is an awesome distraction from the dangers of Boston. It's a huge system that allows you to create small towns and settlements around the wasteland, in areas made specifically for it.
I love the system, but it honestly feels very clunky as if it was ported from the consoles (which it probably is lol)
The audio in this game is amazing and visceral. Everything feels so alive and it's one of the things that contribute to this games amazing ability to immerse you. The soundtrack stays true to the Fallout genre, with focus on colonial twists, like in New Vegas, where it was focused on western elements.
My only real complain about the audio is the fact that a lot of the music is recycled, and that "Diamond City Radio" has horribly few lines. It's the same old "hearing the same ♥♥♥♥ing song or dialogue over and over concept"
The voiced protgonist was something I was initially worried about, but it actually turned out to be an amazingly talented voice actor.  My character is addicted to Psycho, only because I love the lines that are exclaimed after using the drug. Nothing like going all "♥♥♥♥ING KILL" in your power armor with a super sledge.
The general voice acting is really good for a Bethesda game, and there are some familliar voices hidden out there in the Commonwealth.
The companions are fantastic, and the voice acting is really solid. They're some of the best written characters in the franchise. I actually feel attached to many of the character, even some that are not companions in esque to the Mass Effect characters.
The game has a lot of bugs, however, but that's to be expected for such a huge game.
TL:DR: Amazing game with a lot of bugs and flaws, but in the end, it's a solid lifetaker.

The character design in this game is nothing short than spectacular, now NPC's dont look like clones of eachother! My review of Fallout 4. It's good. Get it.
In all seriousness though, it took what was great about the previous Fallout games (3 and New Vegas) as well as take some lessons learned from Skyrim, and then added more on top of that, and there you have Fallout 4. Gunplay is far more engaging and fun compared to previous games. The leveling system is much like Skyrim's which is a damn good thing because Skyrim's leveling system is one of the most superior progression systems out there. The world may initially look smaller than Fallout 3 and NV's maps, however it is far from small. It is however, indeed smaller than Skyrim's map but it makes up for it by how dense the city of boston (basically the center of the map) can get, many hollowed out building you can go through and explore as well as many skyscrapers you can traverse. Fallout 3's Washington DC was bleh to me because the entire city was disconnected from each other and only consisted of patches of locations. Boston is far different, far more open and seamless. Graphically the game looks amazing in my opinion, people saying it looks the same as the other bethesda games are high off their gourds. One negative thing I can come up with for this game is, while I really enjoy the new voice actors for your main character, I do not enjoy how much the dialogue options have been cut back compared to previous Bethesda games. However the introduction to a fully voiced character does allow you to easily get attached to your main character much better than in the past. The story is very interesting as well, far more interesting to me than Fallout 3's. I would say 8 or even 9 out of 10 for Fallout 4 is more than a fair general score for this game.

They could have spiced up the story line a little more but the further along you get in the game the more interesting I found it to be.
I wish the choices of dialog when speaking with NPC's wasn't so lame. The fact that you can't really change the direction in which the conversation leads to is very disappionting, it just allows you to click through the dialog without having to worry about the consquences ...
I was excited about the build mode when it was first introduced but now that I've mastered that I find it somewhat disappointing, I'd like to see them expand a lot more in the tools that we have to work with.
Overall I would say that it's still a great game and I would recommend it, I just wouldn't call it the best game of the series.

I waited a bit to write this, I now have about 100+ hours in the game. I have not finished the main story questline, my character is approaching rank 50. I was glad to read that there is no rank cap. Some of what I say may be in response to various current reviews, and my own opinion on the game has fluctuated over time. Short review is that I think the game is similar enough to prior games (FO3/FO:nv) to say that I like it, the same way I liked those games.
There currently are some technical issues for me, which may get patched over time. The game did not allow full keyboard rebinding, mostly concerning the numpad. My review of Fallout 4. It's good. Get it.
In all seriousness though, it took what was great about the previous Fallout games (3 and New Vegas) as well as take some lessons learned from Skyrim, and then added more on top of that, and there you have Fallout 4. Gunplay is far more engaging and fun compared to previous games. The leveling system is much like Skyrim's which is a damn good thing because Skyrim's leveling system is one of the most superior progression systems out there. The world may initially look smaller than Fallout 3 and NV's maps, however it is far from small. It is however, indeed smaller than Skyrim's map but it makes up for it by how dense the city of boston (basically the center of the map) can get, many hollowed out building you can go through and explore as well as many skyscrapers you can traverse. Fallout 3's Washington DC was bleh to me because the entire city was disconnected from each other and only consisted of patches of locations. Boston is far different, far more open and seamless. Graphically the game looks amazing in my opinion, people saying it looks the same as the other bethesda games are high off their gourds. One negative thing I can come up with for this game is, while I really enjoy the new voice actors for your main character, I do not enjoy how much the dialogue options have been cut back compared to previous Bethesda games. However the introduction to a fully voiced character does allow you to easily get attached to your main character much better than in the past. The story is very interesting as well, far more interesting to me than Fallout 3's. I would say 8 or even 9 out of 10 for Fallout 4 is more than a fair general score for this game.

They could have spiced up the story line a little more but the further along you get in the game the more interesting I found it to be.
I wish the choices of dialog when speaking with NPC's wasn't so lame. The fact that you can't really change the direction in which the conversation leads to is very disappionting, it just allows you to click through the dialog without having to worry about the consquences ...
I was excited about the build mode when it was first introduced but now that I've mastered that I find it somewhat disappointing, I'd like to see them expand a lot more in the tools that we have to work with.
Overall I would say that it's still a great game and I would recommend it, I just wouldn't call it the best game of the series.

Some of what I say may be in response to various current reviews, and my own opinion on the game has fluctuated over time. Not understanding  a part of gameplay and doing things wrong does not make for a fun experience. After several days, I have figured out a lot of it, and it does not bother me as much as it did at first. It may get better with patches and mods, and it will be better if someone just posts an actual good explanation of all aspects of crafting and settlements.

First of all let me start off by saying this. I HAVE PLAYED ALL THE FALLOUT SERIES AND NO, I AM NOT A FANBOY. That said, let me start off with an honest review, and not some batched hatred/loved filled review like the rest of these idiots.
The Fallout series is an AMAZING and the most spectular series to play in the history of gaming. Fallout is a post apocalyptic role playing game, where all your factors are taken into your own accountability, where all your decisions are affected by your actions, where all your insticts are taken into a survival count, and where all your Role-Playing skills come into play on how you choose to do that, with the first three games (Including New Vegas). Now for the Review.
In all honesty, Fallout 4 lives up to the Hype train and the promoted game trailer now, let's take a logical look here.
If, you look at the game from a perspective of a person who hasn't played the Fallout series it's super fun and interestingly awesome! to play. Now, if you look at the game from a person's perspective of someone who has played the whole Fallout series, then it's also super fun to play and interstingly awesome! except, for the fact that you want to see what has been implemented or removed or added within the game. Now, for this sake let me just say that from both perspectives yes it's fun and yes it's enjoyable. Although, if you are a Fallout fan like me and enjoy, all the little details that fallout 3 had (roleplaying, freedom, karma system, skills) then you will notice the small details that Fallout 4 has that the developers  had possibly  removed from the game that makes the game "uninjoyable" which I can understand. Even though, that all of that has been removed the game is still pretty damn fun. So, for this review if, you're a person who likes FPS with a little bit of decisions and a little bit of roleplaying then this game is for you, although if you're a person like me who loves role-playing to the max and wants everything to be taken into accountability then this game might not be for you. Yes, don't get me wrong it is fun as hell, but for a person like me who wants actual role-playing and  the things where your decisions affect all your actions in every little detail then this was disappointing. So, therefore I WILL ( notice how I said will) give credit where it's due.
6.0/10 - Exceptionally okay (RPG guy like me)
9/10- Casual Gamer(Loves Shooting stuff, not so much into RPG)
In turn this game has been fun, and this game deserves credit where credit's due. Although, for me I'll just let the series rest and see where it evolves, for now I am going back to Fallout 3.

-The dialogue wheel seemingly over simplifies things. But to be honest, as I've played I've learned that our protaganist better establishes themself through their actions, rather than their dialouge. The main flavor the dialouge offers is your characters paradigm and stance on matters. Still would be nice if there were more options, or ways of previewing dialogue before selecting.
Yeah there are a handful of bugs, most of them graphic/physics based goofs in the games algorithms, but there are a good few hair pulling bugs and annoying hiccups in how the game processes progress and completion on certain quests. This is a problem that can be patched, unlike the next problem.

Those are Standards-based cons. The bugs and design choice of using a dialogue wheel with crummy options is a step back from the standard.
Here is a Expectations-based con, meaning, this con doesn't make the game worse in a universal sense, its just something that I, personally thought should have been done differently.(take this for a grain of salt.)
The only personal scripe I have with the game( this isn't nessesarily a design flaw) is the fact that most of your character's backstory and some of his/her views are already decided for you. No matter what, you can't change the fact that:
-You(male) joined the army and are proud of it
-You(female) have/had dreams to become a lawyer and had trouble going through with it
-You are a family-oriented person
-You are willing to get married
-You are willing to have a kid
-You are heterosexual(or at least that's how you started)
-You prefer(ed) the comfy suburban life
There is a lack of open endedness to your character. What if I wanted to play as a character who saw the events of the beginning as an opportunity to start a new life, without a family tying me down? Its hard to do that while my character won't shut the hell up about MY SON SHAUN!
Don't get me wrong, if this game wasn't designed to be a role player's delight than that's fine. This is why I call this a personal scripe, rather than an actual design flaw.
It's a great game, it surpassed its standard. The phrase,"it didn't live up to my expectations", is stupid. So what? Bethesda's goal isn't to live up to the expectations of Daryll, living in Tustin, CA, in his parent's basement who freqents Kotaku and Buzzfeed. Their goal is to make exceptional games, take risks, and try new things, and they did that with FO4.

Pros:
The companions were great! Even if I thought Piper was a horrible and pretentious writer with spelling troubles, she actually came across as a person through her dialogue, which triggered organically when we were out adventuring together--and occasionally giving me candy? Gold. I actually had genuine emotion for the character. The companions in this game are so much better than in previous Bethesda Games Studios titles, I've gotta give them some praise. Haven't tried the romance, so no comment.
Settlement building was a really ambitious step, and sometimes you fall down when you're learning to walk. I'll give it a pass simply because it's there and it wasn't before. I probably spent forty hours of my sixty hour run building up my settlements.
All the little things. Man, there's so many tiny gameplay improvements it's difficult to list them all. They gave us most of the necessary controls for playing a first person shooter! The only thing I found myself wishing for was the ability to go prone when I needed to be extra small. But when you come across a gang of raiders duking it out against a group of supermutants, or two vertibirds deploying their contingent of brotherhood troopers into a hostile LZ to murder feral ghouls and raiders, you'll know what I mean when I say there's some cool stuff that can happen in this game, that were simply unfeasable in FO3 due to resources and the engine.
Cons:
Without getting into spoilers: The story is awful. The game could literally be made better by removing it wholesale, leaving it as a platform for free-form exploration and modding.
User Interface is just straight up shameful.
Diplomacy is practically nonexistant and I hope you saved before initiating this conversation, becuase it's based on an RNG, not how much you've invested in Charisma. Also, the dialogue wheel and the voiced protagonist limit modding and play choice. That said, I liked the female VA's work from an objective standpoint; it simply doesn't mesh with what gives Bethesda games their infinite replayability.
Lockpicking & Hacking still use the exact same terrible minigames. Thankfully, mods will be around to remove them entirely, becuase that's an improvement, too.
Combat is a constant slog and a grind, with enemies that can soak multiple missiles like they're a gentle tickle on the chin, and little in the way of reward. Clearing out a raider nest isn't worth it, unless you happen to come across a Legendary, because outside of materials, he's got the only loot you care about. There's little in the way of weapon diversity, and the simple mechanical superiority of certain weapon mod choices simply obsoletes the others. And if you're hoping for depth in modding melee weapons? You'll be disappointed.
Immersion is pitiful. There's supposedly civilizations in game, but the biggest cities are a row of shops and maybe a dozen people. They're no better than Megaton was in Fallout 3.
Settlement Building. Yes, I said it was a great part of the game. And it was! But when you spend fourty hours building up your towns only for it to mean literally nothing to the game and the story? It's a slap in the face for your efforts.
This game is a solid rent-don't-buy until the modding tools come out: In a couple of years, maybe modders will have released the kind of game that gives several hundred hours worth of gameplay.

Like all of Bethesda's products, the glimmer of a good game is apparent in Fallout 4. The Modding community will turn this glimmer into a shining example of Open World gameplay in time.

I will refrain from talking about the gameplay balancing, story and graphics, as these are not what makes or breaks an open world game. Minecraft shows that these elements are really not necessary for a open world game to thrive, but are nice additions to the formula. Let me begin by saying that I want to like Fallout 4, just like I wanted to like Skyrim. However the highly apparent bugs, the lack of interactivity with the world in general, and the inability of the developer to create UI's, creates a product which I cannot get invested or absorbed in.
First of all, lets discuss bugs. I have not completed the main storyline, nor have explored all of the playstyles. In fact I have seen very little of the world in general. However the parts I have seen shows bugs in the most crucial places, which dampens any optimism for the state of the game in general. In the introductory sequence alone, the game contained bugs which even small developers would not let be released. The voice acting would cut-out mid sentence, to combat this I turned on captions. this was to no avail though as they became trapped on a single line of dialogue, refusing to proceed with the conversation.
The game will sometimes refuse to boot, requiring multiple attempts to warm-up.
The scripting of the descent into Vault 111 also fails on occasion, creating situations such as your character having to cut in line to get his Vault-Tec gear in a very unbelievable fashion, derailing other NPCS motions. There was even some unfortunate implications when my character (Walter Evergreen, I like common sounding names) and his wife Nora, both quite caucasian poeple, someone managed to have a black baby. I like to imagine that he and his wife have a very open relationship, with several poeple, as this would explain his lack of concern at this development.
From this list alone, I cannot imagine what the game will become in the end, where developers typically spend less time and money making. I do expect that his son will somehow become caucasian however, cause baby's skin colour is like hair colour right?
I know the response that I will likely recieve to this complaint (and the baby comment). Bethesda make very large games with lots of small parts, it is therefore expected that bugs will occur. This I feel is misleading, as it makes the bugs in Bethesda's product seem like bizzare edge cases from the combinational explosion of interactive parts. I can forgive misbalanced item combos, or odd edge cases, but these bugs are part of the basic functionality of the game. This makes it appear that Bethesda has not tried at all to QA their product.
Every time an obvious bug is found it yanks the player from the experience, reminding them that it is just a game. Like unkillable crows, its the little things that count in connecting the player to the world.
Fallout 4 suffers the same problem that Skyrim had. The world is Dead, but not in a good way. The Commonwealth is decayed and outwardly forboding, but this is not shown in the game mechanics. There is no danger to the player from the environment itself. The Rad Storms are not as terrifying as they really should be. The radiation from water is laughable, creatures (apart from Deathclaws) do not present enough of a threat, and nightfall is meaningless.
In a wasteland where opportunties for the player to push against the world can be far and inbetween the world must push against the player instead, or else tedium will set in.
Bethesda seems to acknowledge this with the Fast Travel system, because the only reason you would need to instate such a system, is that the world does not make it enjoyable to actually travel. I refused to use Fast Travel as I find it belittles the Commonwealth of scale. However its presence is a indictment on their world.
All in all I think the crows of Fallout 4 are a good example of the interactivity of the game. They look nice, but you may as well be a ghost to them as they do not react to your presence, and you cannot act upon them.
The final annoyance in this product is the god awful UI they have created. Common features such as "loot all" buttons on containers, and the inability to selectively loot without going into a Inventory is just the least of the problems. The UI for the settlement system is incredibly clunky and slow, requiring the use of the arrow keys. a set of keys which are not required for any menu (as they can be controled with WASD, which your hand is probably already on when playing). Building can be a right royal pain in the rad ghoulies as wall snapping is sporadic at best, and placing items (like turrets) on structures (like guard towers) is outright impossible.
The inventory quickly becomes completely chaotic as there is not a way for the player to sort the items in a meaningful manner. However the most egregious UI error of them all is in the character customisation. There is no randomise option. I sincerely beleive that any character customiser without this all-important feature is not fit for use. Not everyone wants to make themselves in the game (not that i tried. -cough- -cough-) and just want to play as a unique random dude(tte).
In short, through the tireless efforts of its community, Fallout 4 will become a great game in about a year, which is why I give it a thumbs up. However at this time it is not great, just mediore. The world lacks connection to the player and then player cannot interact with the world in important ways.
Everyone will mod the game to buggery, adapting it into a game that they will actually enjoy. Then praise Bethesda for making a great game, forgetting that its the mods that made Fallout 4 (or Skyrim) great, not Bethesda.

It was really hard to decide between recommending and not recommending this game. I don't normally play FPS or RPGs (I prefer rogue like, rts, civ, and casual) but since I built a new computer I thought it was a good chance to check out the newer AAA games and see what was up.
I'm glad I bought it and saw what was going on and I did play enough to not feel like I got ripped off or anything, however the whole mechanic of picking up little things for scraps to build mods and then dealing with how much weight you carry was just annoying. If it was a permenant death game then I could get into that since all those little things add to the desire not to die. In Fallout, dying meant I had to go pick up some scraps again or quicksave all the time which feels like cheating. Fast travelling back and forth to organize my scraps, buy ammo, and fix my suit feels like busy work. There is just not enough continuous action and too much inventory management.
All that said, I had some real fun. Some of the battles were really epic.  It's just the inbetween busy work and the kind of average storytelling that made it not fun.

It was really hard to decide between recommending and not recommending this game. I don't normally play FPS or RPGs (I prefer rogue like, rts, civ, and casual) but since I built a new computer I thought it was a good chance to check out the newer AAA games and see what was up.

If it was a permenant death game then I could get into that since all those little things add to the desire not to die. In Fallout, dying meant I had to go pick up some scraps again or quicksave all the time which feels like cheating. After finishing the main quest after 80 hours of exploring, side questing and base building I feel as if I have enough experience to give my thoughts on Fallout 4.
Gameplay
+FPS inspired shooting mechanics
+Power armour acts more like a mech suit than clothing
+Base building
+Crafting weapon and power armour mods finally gives purpose for picking junk up
+Legendary and boss type enemies
+Challenging early game
+Armor pieces instead of one entire outfit
+Unique and easy character customisation
+New VATS and critical hit system
-Clunky UI
-Base building is messy (again more a UI issue but really affects base building)
-Lack of weaponry ( I know you can craft weapon mods but just compare the list of weapons from New Vegas to 4)
+-Removal of skills and focus on SPECIAL
+-No karma system
Story, quests,dialogue and characters
+Brotherhood of Steel back to their roots
+Nick Valentine
+Location lore is plenty through reading notes and terminals
-Established role means role playing is limited
-Dialogue wheel and not being able to see what the player says
-Poorly done intro section
-Main quest drops in quality after act 2
-Majority of companions aren't interesting
-Factions feel forced
-Lack of ways to complete a quest
-Lack of Fallout's dark humour
-Lack of evil choices
Technical
+Lighting is beautiful
+Improved animation makes it feel like your charcter actually has their foot on the ground and not just gliding
+Least bugs I've experienced in a Bethesda game
-Occasional fps drop
-Occasional bugs
-Graphics and textures are poor compared to other AAA open world games this year *cough*Witcher 3*cough*MGSV*cough
Fallout 4 to me is still an addicting game despite it's many flaws (it's writing especially) . If you loved Obsidian's take on Fallout New Vegas, you might be a bit disappointed with this. However I'm still going to recommend you play Fallout 4 at some point in time as it does bring many new and cool features.

Now let's start off by addressing gameplay. The storyline although short, as a whole didn't fall short in my opinion. The ending on the other hand could use some work, and I definitely feel that bethesda could have put more effort into it.
Now for the graphics and FPS; I don't get all the complaints I've been hearing about graphics. I have ultra settings on and the game looks great IMO. I get a constant 60 FPS except for the very occasional times when I fast travel and the world has a little stutter loading in.
The game environment is huge. Bethesda really went all out on creating the FO4 map, and did a great job studying boston. Even at just under 50 hours played I still have barely discovered 1/3rd of the FO4 map.
Bugs; For myself the game has crashed 2 times ever and the game quicksaves so much it wasn't a big deal. I have heard of other bugs but all of them are fixable and nothing is game breaking.
Selection of guns armor and misc; While the clothing and armor category falls short of variety for previous fallouts such as NV and FO3, I still think they did a pretty good job. There are less gun options than in the other Fallouts, but the huge array of customization available to these guns makes up for it in a huge way.
Overall I give FO4 a 8/10.

OK so we all Fallout 4 is the game we've wanted for since New Vegas salivating for the continuation of the mastercrafted FPS Fallout series.  I'm just going to say, yes, this game was worth paying full price ( they deserve it after incredible amount of work put into it ) and I would absolutely recommend it.
Now for a few "cons" that I think are pretty glaring :
1) For Bethsada to improve weapon modding,  and make all the new crafting stations... WTF is the ammo mods that were in New Vegas?  It boggles my mind why they left out such a incredible improvement over fallout 3 and great feature of NV. Dumb, Dumb, Dumb.
2) The weapon modding itself seems like they took an easy way to not have to brainstorm new weapons ( of which in reality there are few of ) and instead put in a piece-meal system.  Really poor choice and goes right along with having no ammo mods. Dumb. Dumb. Dumb.
3) The Quest system seems so over saturated with crap missions like " go clear this building of enemies " or " retreieve this item " it like they fired the writers of fallout 3 and hired semi-intelligent monkies.
The Un-original ideas above really irriate me because if completly takes away from being in the wasteland exploring for the sake of exploring, not for " go fetch " reasons.
I know they're shooting for the moon and the game is absolutely beauitiful on my 980 ti w/2600K @ 4.7Ghz with 16GB ram, but im not sure if they tryed to hard, got publisher pushed or what, but the vibe of the first few weeks of Fallout 3 AND New Vegas were much more entertaining imho.
Still, all in all a classic, hopefully some nice patches/DLC will come and fix whats been left out or tweaked way too much ( NPC's anyone? )

I don't really do reviews or care enough to do them a lot of the time, but I've been hyped for this game for a good while and feel making one would be nice. So here I go, take this with a grain of salt, it's my opinion and it's basically a circle jerk to not enjoy this game, so yeah. (I just kinda went through all of the big issues with the game, didn't take time to make this some super special review)
Two step forward, one step back. It's a fun game, could use a lot of fixing and changes, but it's still fun to the average person which is what Bethesda was going for, I guess. Lacks a lot of lore and story elements that other Fallout games used and were amazing for. Bethesda basically scrapped everything that was great about 3 and NV, added FPS features and took out RPG elements. Yeah, there are some good things but I wouldn't say this game wasn't a let down. (Which seems weird since I have 100 hours in 2 weeks.) The game is fun, but if I had to rate it as a Fallout game, the score would be below the rating I'd give it as an action/FPS game with a bit of story added to it.
Honestly this game could be created into a better Fallout game with time, with mods and plugins later on. But for now it just isn't what 3 and NV were, which is odd for Bethesda to be honest. Bethesda is known for creating RPGs with amazing worlds and lore, but Fallout 4 doesn't feel like it was made to fit that genre. It takes lore from past Fallout games and throws it in the trast to appeal to more people and even change the game, Bethesda has always ignored lore from the very first games but this is a whole new level. I could make lists with loads of proof, but not worth the time. The game feels different than the other games, which is a real let down to people who were hyped for the reason of loving the other Fallout games.
Didn't really go into it much, but Fallout/Elder Scrolls have always been big on player freedom and character creation. Fallout 4 lacks both to a point of just making this game not even an RPG anymore. Yeah yeah yeah, the character creation menu is pretty fun to mess around with, but this time around you're forced to be a character with a set background and set family. I'm not one of those idiots who in uproar because I can't be a gay, transgendered, anime furry girl. I'm just saying it's a huge change into the facts that this time around it feels more like an action fps game. One last thing that I wont go into much but, you cannot be evil in this game. There is one way to do things 99% of the time, I cannot be an evil person even if I wanted to, unless you count being sarcastic and being witty evil in the standards of a Post-Apoc ''RPG'' like Fallout.
I see no problem with graphics, you can and thats good for you, but I don't care enough about them. The game actually runs pretty well for me and most people I know. Big step up from Bethesda, who's Fallout 3 PC port barely worked with mods and hours of work. Goodjob, keep the well made PC ports up. There are a couple texture issues, but they can be fixed easily.
Is Fallout 4 dumbed down? Yeah, yeah it is. A lot actually. Combat is pretty good honestly, but is that really something you want to be the main feature of an RPG? Everything about speech checks and skill points from the other games is gone. You might have the option to be a snarky little♥♥♥♥♥♥every now and again, but never a medical check or even an explosive way to do something. The scroll wheel is bad, yeah. But if you use a mod that changed it to show all you say, it shows it really isn't too bad. I still don't think it's better than the past system, but it is dumbed down. There's a lot more I could go into, but I wont because it'd spoil things and I think i've♥♥♥♥♥♥on this for one day.
So they added some new things to the game, eh? Settlements? Weapon modding? New style of crafting? That stuff is pretty cool, honestly. Does it fit in Fallout? Eh... some of it, sure. Something I actually enjoy is these new features, they're fun and I've wasted a lot of time doing it so far. Not much to say about it, it's just a fun thing to pass time with and something i'll probably do a good bit once more mods are added for it. *cough* UI *cough*.
I could go on for a lot longer, but I made my point clear and will get to the point and give my final thoughts. The game is fun and would be worth maybe $40 if you just want a game with good FPS combat and loads to do. $60? Maybe, but I don't think so. Now if you want to buy this game because it's Fallout? Nope, wait until GOTY or cheaper than $40 during a sale. I know I sound like some edgy kid who's hating to be cool, but i'm not hating it, really. I think it's fun, but not worth it's price and it is a huge let down to the hype I had for this game. I'm done now, just my opinion. Thanks for reading.

It was really hard to decide between recommending and not recommending this game. I don't normally play FPS or RPGs (I prefer rogue like, rts, civ, and casual) but since I built a new computer I thought it was a good chance to check out the newer AAA games and see what was up.
I'm glad I bought it and saw what was going on and I did play enough to not feel like I got ripped off or anything, however the whole mechanic of picking up little things for scraps to build mods and then dealing with how much weight you carry was just annoying. If it was a permenant death game then I could get into that since all those little things add to the desire not to die. In Fallout, dying meant I had to go pick up some scraps again or quicksave all the time which feels like cheating. Fast travelling back and forth to organize my scraps, buy ammo, and fix my suit feels like busy work. There is just not enough continuous action and too much inventory management.
All that said, I had some real fun. Some of the battles were really epic.  It's just the inbetween busy work and the kind of average storytelling that made it not fun.

Bethesda has done it once again: a game that is wonderful and engaging and flawed.  It's by no means perfect, but improves upon Fallout 3 in many important and meaningful ways.  Interesting enemy differences, shooting mechanics that feel 'right', and a twist on the SPECIAL system that tries something new without throwing everything you loved in the trash.
My only major complaint is the voiced protaganist.  While we'll all have to wait and see how it turns out, I suspect this is going to affect the community's ability to create compelling questlines.  While I also question many of Bethesda's choices in balancing and pacing, these are the types of 'problems' that modders will revel in 'solving' and gives us a lot to look forwards to in the near future, and especially once the creation kit is released.
EDIT:  I should mention the horrible dialogue system because it is the biggest ding in Fallout 4's resume.  The Yes, No (Yes), Maybe (Yes), What? (Yes) is the stuff of memes and is no understatement, it literally works like that.  I don't think it's as terrible as it's made out to be, the voice over work is fine, but it is the number one complaint about the game and will hurt replayability.  However, if you overlook it (and you should) for your first playthrough, there's a lot of good stuff to enjoy.  Hopefully some industrious modders will come to the rescue on this one.

I have to recommend this because, frankly, it's fun. It looks good, it plays well, it has a lot of what you'd expect from Fallout 4 given what 3/NV and such provided.
But with that said, I had some really big hang-ups. I tried super hard to ignore them and just keep going and told myself it'd surely pan out but.. it didn't.
First off - unarmed, I thought it'd be fun to go with the fisticuffs, and ended up with one single weapon from level 22 to 52 that I never found anything better than.. That's kinda lame. :( The mod system in general is fun and neat, I loved it! But I would have liked to see more, especially for the melee/unarmed side of things. I also was a bit disappointed to not see more new/different weapons in general, I understand needing to get a lot of what we'd expect to see.. but only seeing what you expect leaves very little room for excitement.
But my biggest, biggest grump has to be the latter part of the game and the 'story' and such. I don't want to spoil anything, but.. Well, I was sad that the whole settlement thing affected almost nothing. I expected some kind of grand overarching purpose to raising and managing numerous settlements.. but no, nothing. Not a thing at all. That was a giant disappointment. And towards the end there's a moment where I knew I was getting close but I kept going and suddenly I was presented with an extremely arbitrary choice that forced me very, very heavily and in a way that I really disliked. I want to say more but I would hate to spoil anything major for those who still have yet to pick up the game and play it and might read this. :\ Just.. I dunno. These games are supposed to give you choice, wer'e supposed to have options, the ability to find middle ground, to talk our way around things, to shake it up a bit, not just.. A, B, or C, pick one and screw the other two completely.
And lastly, the dialogue.. I positively cannot stand the changes. First off, simply shifting it to not really 'lock' you into dialogue means having to mash the button multiple times to engage someone, and sometimes they aren't even really 'engaged' and you don't know if they have anything to say.. more a technical issue, but still dumb.
But then, ah yes, the lovely cliche of the "dumbed down" conversation wheel. Why? Just.. why? Numerous times in the game I chose an option and it was totally different than I'd expect. And what the hell is "Sarcastic"? You can agree and be sarcastic and you can disagree and be sarcastic. You can't just have a conversation and yell "SARCASTIC" or something. That's not how it works.
Having such a limited number of dialogue options while also having them obfuscated just about ruined the entire dialogue aspect for me, and that makes me sad. There are almost ZERO options to trigger perks/skills in dialogue, science etc., and that frustrates me. Oh, what's that science guy? My 10INT and max Science perk mean nothing and obviously all your science talk is way over my head? Okay, sure, that feels right. :\
I get that it's an easy control scheme for consoles and stuff but come on.. it's really hampering the ability for us to have a good number of options and to understand what we're even saying in the first place. Is there really a need to keep taking steps backwards with regards to dialogue and conversation and whatnot in games?
Ultimately it's fun, I guess. Running around and shooting stuff and talking to people and all that but.. the entire story and setting just crashed and burned for me when it all came down to it. I almost feel like I don't even want to finish it because the choice to be made is so painfully shallow and arbitrary and gives so few options and so little flexibility to us as  players. Making no choice feels like the only real smart choice.
Maybe the DLC will be better, I guess. I'm just disappointed, and I'm not even an oldschool fallout lover. :( It was good, it could have been way better. It doesn't deserve GoTY and all that stuff it'll surely get, and I hate to say that, but.. the story was just a complete and total failure in my opinion due to the very sudden and arbitrary direction you're forced to take, especially when coupled with the lack of using neat features (all the settlement building and such ends up having essentially no point at all.. I was rather shocked by this. :\ )
Fallout 4 has a world that feels larger and populated by a wider variety of environments and entities, with a cool variety of character options and weapons and armor and all that, but I gotta say.. Witcher 3 made me far happier with its story, choices, and consequences of it all. It felt far less hamfisted and arbitrary. I just can't go all in on a game like this that falls apart so hard towards the end when you're in the moments that it should be coming together in ways you hadn't even anticipated.

I'm going to jump on the F4 bad feels train here and say this is a total disappointment for me as a person who has gleefully soaked up hundreds of hours playing the console versions of F3 and FNV and another hundred on the PC port of New Vegas. I feel that the games narrative - at least in the beginning - is weak, and I felt that it was difficult to adjust to a character whose entire story is basically set out for them. It doesn't help that all four(seriously?!) dialogue options are either "I'm a very concerned father" or "Yes, I'll do all you ask." in variation. You can pick the most negative responses possible and still get pushed into that quest you don't want to do.
Oh, there's also a total lack of weapons. No, the rather extensive weapon modding does not make up for it. The game feels way too cramped (maybe that's just the FOV talking...) with a tiny amount of real content and I've already discovered about half of the map's locations, all of which felt simply uninteresting and more of a bland slog with no context or story to it. Most places were just filled the molotov-spamming raider cockholsters, weak mutants and
ghouls that lay on the floor whenever they attack you.
Did I mention that character stats have been thrown out the window now? Y'know, a thing that dated back to the original Black Isle Fallout games. Instead of a perfectly fine system that worked well, they decided to put in a hopelessly generic open-world-game perk system. It feels tacked on and unnatural for a Fallout game, and is a reminder of the saying; "If it ain't broke, don't fix it." With the removed level cap, every character - with enough time spent - will all become the same stats-wise(though you'd need to get to around level 70 first), There are also a few perks which basically fill the bottom-half of the screen with some shoddy animation accompanied by some silly sound, this isn't very helpful when trying to kill a room-full of face-planting ghouls.
I feel that the graphical improvements have taken away the rough and gritty style of the game, and it doesn't help that even when all my settings are minimal I can barely get above 40 FPS. The HUD is much more... clean? It's too clean to look good in the Fallout setting I feel, and the default colour is ugly as hell. Menus are obviously console-oriented and a total pain to use, I often had to leave the mouse alone to navigate the menus, especially the Pip-Boy and workbench menus. Suddenly, TREES ARE EVERYWHERE!!!
I'll also point out that Fallout 4 is still running on the Gamebyro engine, and seems to use the modified version Skyrim had. It's an engine that's long outdated and has poor performance, but if it works, it's alright. The thing i'm not alright with though is the fact the game looks and plays just like Skyrim... but with guns. It feels more like a total conversion mod than an actual game, to be honest.
You know in Fallout: New Vegas the whole 'Hoover Dam' and 'New Vegas' things were all hyped up in-game? It was all for a good reason, the places were absolutely massive and full of life and history. Turns out that Diamond City received similar treatment and all it was was a slightly less boring Megaton. When I finally arrived, I spent about ten minutes walking around and attempting to interact with the locals before I walked off.
Overall, this game felt like a waste of my money so far. I'll update it when I complete the game a few times, but I think my opinion won't change. I guess if you've never played a fallout game before, it won't be that bad; but to me and many other players out there it feels like a slap in the face with a critical strike on my wallet.
4/10 for now.
