Oh, where to begin? (This is my second review, the shock and awe wore off after a while)
The list is pretty big, so big in fact that it would be impractical for a paragraph style review.
Pros:
-The game is great fun. The power armor makes you feel like a walking tank
-Settlement system is great if you know how to optimize it for yourself
-Weapon/Armor Modification system is a brilliant feature that was well implemented
-The story is pretty good (IMO) for a Bethesda game, with a great and unexpected plot twist that will make the hardcore RP's think again about their choices.
-Several "Holy Sh*t" moments in the game in the form of insane boss battles or just randomness. It will surprise you and kill you everytime if you aren't ready for it.
-Companions are much more fluid. They react faster than in Skyrim, and you can choose what they wear/use
-Glowing Sea. Never has there been such a bad♥♥♥♥♥"No Man's Land" in a Fallout game. Fallout needs more of this.
Cons:
-Repetitive quests (lots of them, some are infinite like in Skyrim)
-The game slows down - a lot. If you wish to upgrade your power armor to be absolutely amazing, you have to be at least level 41 (Jet pack). This takes a LONG time if you don't spend days on end in the game.
-RPG features are okay at best. It just doesn't feel like a good RPG
-Not a good Fallout game. I know it is a different setting, from a different dev, but come on. Fallout and Fallout 2 were about ♥♥♥♥ing sh*t up and saving people. Not hunting down your son while helping absolutely everyone and their mom (although the "intro" with the deathclaw is awesome)
-Not a lot of good exploration. There is 1 main city thus far (55+ hours, with the majority in side content). The main enemies are Raiders and Super Mutants. Synths, BOS, Wasteland Creatures, and Gunners are secondary enemies
-Not a good variety - in general
-Locations look the same most of the time, with the typical Skyrim dungeon level design
-(Not a big gripe but,) Graphics are really bad in some cases. Like Super Mutant feet. They look like they were ripped from Fallout 2 or 3 and upscaled.
-Lip Syncing looks like it was made by a child, with poor vision. While blind folded. And tied to the floor (need I go on?)
-Dialogue is fine, but in some cases it is too simplified. Every once in a while I would need to reload because my character said just the wrong thing while I am RP'ing.
-Technical Performance is♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ As expected by a Bethesda game
-No Modding tools yet. I don't have a clue how people are making mods already but they have their ways.
-So many cons yet the game is still praised to no end
All in all the game is fun, but not the long term enjoyment that I and many others have come to expect from Bethesda. The game has some ups, but many more downs. I don't think I would buy the game full price if I ever had the option to do so.
Would I recommend this game? Yes and no. To a long time fan of Bethesda, maybe. But to a long time fan of Fallout and/or RPG games, no. I would recommend Fallout New Vegas more. New Vegas has so much going for it; even though the project was nearly doomed with a 2 year deadline.

I mean, yeah its good. We all know the good things in the game, so im going to go over the unimpressive things in fallout 4.
This fallout has the least amount of contenet and it is the most linear (compared to 3 and NV). Not many side quests, and the "continual" side quests are just "go here, do this, come back". Very boring and gets old quick. There were 2 dectecive quests which were very fun with uncovering the mysteries and i just wish there were more. Base building is okay but ultimatly it accounts for nothing. The game felt short, even though it took me 62hrs to complete (along with all or most of the side quests), it just didnt feel satisfying. The map is smaller than what i expected, and to account for this they jammed in 32140985139258 quest markers in a tiny space to make it feel like there is a lot. Dont get me wrong, it is probably the best designed fallout map, but i feel like it wasnt enough. I dont know what it was but fallout 4 just didnt live up to its hype or expecations for me. I think its because of the lack of content. I was kind of dissapointed but not really. It's like going home with a 10/10 babe, only to realise shes actualy an 8/10. Youre dissapointed but youre still gonna bang and be happy about it.
I just hope future DLC's can unlock more content because the game lacks content. It does many things right but ultimatly it feels very shallow and lackluster in content. I would have liked 30+ more side quests that are INTERESTING not go here, kill this, come back.
All in all, a great game, but when it comes to the greats we have to pick it apart. 8/10 might replay again (probably will).

Oh, where to begin? (This is my second review, the shock and awe wore off after a while)
The list is pretty big, so big in fact that it would be impractical for a paragraph style review.
Pros:
-The game is great fun. The power armor makes you feel like a walking tank
-Settlement system is great if you know how to optimize it for yourself
-Weapon/Armor Modification system is a brilliant feature that was well implemented
-The story is pretty good (IMO) for a Bethesda game, with a great and unexpected plot twist that will make the hardcore RP's think again about their choices.
-Several "Holy Sh*t" moments in the game in the form of insane boss battles or just randomness. It will surprise you and kill you everytime if you aren't ready for it.
-Companions are much more fluid. They react faster than in Skyrim, and you can choose what they wear/use
-Glowing Sea. Never has there been such a bad♥♥♥♥♥"No Man's Land" in a Fallout game. Fallout needs more of this.
Cons:
-Repetitive quests (lots of them, some are infinite like in Skyrim)
-The game slows down - a lot. If you wish to upgrade your power armor to be absolutely amazing, you have to be at least level 41 (Jet pack). This takes a LONG time if you don't spend days on end in the game.
-RPG features are okay at best. It just doesn't feel like a good RPG
-Not a good Fallout game. I know it is a different setting, from a different dev, but come on. Fallout and Fallout 2 were about ♥♥♥♥ing sh*t up and saving people. Not hunting down your son while helping absolutely everyone and their mom (although the "intro" with the deathclaw is awesome)
-Not a lot of good exploration. There is 1 main city thus far (55+ hours, with the majority in side content). The main enemies are Raiders and Super Mutants. Synths, BOS, Wasteland Creatures, and Gunners are secondary enemies
-Not a good variety - in general
-Locations look the same most of the time, with the typical Skyrim dungeon level design
-(Not a big gripe but,) Graphics are really bad in some cases. Like Super Mutant feet. They look like they were ripped from Fallout 2 or 3 and upscaled.
-Lip Syncing looks like it was made by a child, with poor vision. While blind folded. And tied to the floor (need I go on?)
-Dialogue is fine, but in some cases it is too simplified. Every once in a while I would need to reload because my character said just the wrong thing while I am RP'ing.
-Technical Performance is♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ As expected by a Bethesda game
-No Modding tools yet. I don't have a clue how people are making mods already but they have their ways.
-So many cons yet the game is still praised to no end
All in all the game is fun, but not the long term enjoyment that I and many others have come to expect from Bethesda. The game has some ups, but many more downs. I don't think I would buy the game full price if I ever had the option to do so.
Would I recommend this game? Yes and no. To a long time fan of Bethesda, maybe. But to a long time fan of Fallout and/or RPG games, no. I would recommend Fallout New Vegas more. New Vegas has so much going for it; even though the project was nearly doomed with a 2 year deadline.

Let's jump right into the pros and cons and then I'll give my verdict.
Pros:
Great gameplay
Crafting is fun and adds to the game
Power armor is more fun than in the past
Voiced protagonist adds a cinematic, entertaining feel to the game
Good variety in companions
Lots of quests to play for hours upon hours
The perk tree allows you to easily craft your playstyle without jumping through hoops
Interesting and entertaining characters
Gunplay and Vats is decently improved, hindering the gameplay
Cons:
Map atmosphere is somewhat bland and makes the world feel a bit small
terrible framerate issues are annoying and ruin the flow of the gameplay
Base building is rather clunky and restricts creativity unless you can work around it
Story predetermines your character's personality leaving little to imagination
Story is also too similar to past Fallout games and becomes very predictable
Perk tree removes uniqueness of character builds after awhile, moving a step back  from the RPGness of past games.
Dialogue replies are somewhat limited and become very similar and repetitive throughout dialogue sections.
Graphics are somewhat outdated while not being terrible, they are a bit underwhelming
All in all, Fallout 4 is a great game but not perfect nor near perfect. If you can get past the flaws and enjoyed past games that Bethesda has done then this should be a great game to spend hours upon hours on.

Fallout 4 is a huge advancement in several ways since Fallout 3 released in 2008. While the main quest is a let down to some extent, offering only a few ending cutscenes, none of which reflect on your actions during the game, at least you get to continue the game after you beat the main story without having to buy a DLC expansion like bethesda's previous iteration of the series. On the other hand the destination is not as important as the journey, which Fallout 4 does an amazing job of making very enjoyable, with massive improvements to melee combat and most importantly the gunplay, the game finally feels like a modern shooter by todays standards. All in all, worth the price if you can deal with poor optimization in certain areas.
-TL:DR-
Pros:
-Great gunplay
-around a dozen companions, each with their own backstory
-Heavily customizable weapons, armor, and base building
-mods are already available (though in limited gamechanging capacity)
-small but enjoyable map, little to no rubble filler like the capitol wasteland
Cons:
-Limited dialogue options
-Poor optimization in some areas (20,000-30,000 draw calls per frame)
-lots of bugs that break immersion (very few can be gamebreaking, such as companions completely vanishing)
-dissapointing ending/lackluster story
I think if you can deal with all the negative things mentioned in these reviews i would definitely recommend you purchase this game. i have over 75 hours so far in the game, and with the continued release of mods, and the inevitable release of official DLC expansions, i will be playing this game for a very long time to come.

Fallout 4 brings back all the fun of the post-apocalyptic wasteland. This time, were heading up north, to the Commonwealth of Massachusetts. More specifically, Boston. All of you're favorite things (I.M.O) from Fallout 3 and New Vegas are back: V.A.T.S (now slowing time instead of stopping it), and A.D.S. Play as the Lone Survivor, emerging from Vault 111, hellbent on finding a person very dear to you're heart. As you roam the wasteland, you encounter many familiar landmarks such as Concord and the Institute of Technology. Discover strange new lands while gaining XP and choosing perks to aid you in you're quests. WARNING: Game is slightly buggy/glitchy and CAN/WILL break, though these are far and few between. So it can be overlooked. Graphics can be dissapointing at times as well, but if you can forgive this game for that aspect, then get this game immediately. Worth every penny.

Just hit >70 hours and finished main story line. A lot of side quests to do, which I'll get back to shortly.
For me, the game turned out to be an absolute blast - about 50 hours in the last 5 days should tell you all.
So, after all the adventures, is it worth a buy?
Graphics-wise, the game is deffinitely an evolution over last two titles. It's the best looking Fallout so far, and best-looking Bethesda game to date. I haven't encountered many graphical glitches, which is a good result considering size of the world involved. I also didn't have any issues performance-wise - the game ran on acceptable FPS levels on my old gaming rig which didn't even meet minimum requirements. The new gaming rigt didn't even break a sweat, providing outstanding performance majority of time, with only few FPS drops here and there.
Few words about the engine: it is still capable of delivering good looking game, but only thanks to Bethesda programmers' spectacular work of juicing all the ooze out of it. Still, it must be said - this engine seems to be at the very limits of its capabilities and I don't see it running next Bethesda game, not if it wants to compete with other games.
The game's atmosphere is wonderful - once again we're back to urban environment, with lots of buildings, bridges, tunnels and the like, surrounded by suburban outskirts of houses. Although not everyone's fond of F4's color palette, I find it believable - let me just remind you that pre-war Fallout world is based on 1950's, where pastel colors were trendy. Personally, I think the more colorful world fits the Boston area well, but as usual - that's my opinion, your may vary.
I like the fact the main protagonist is now voiced!
Despite the fact I am enjoying this game, I cannot say there aren't issues. I'll allow myself to punctuate here:
1) Downright insulting console port: forget FOV slider in settings, forget fully bindable keyboard (some binds are hardcoded so you may change one function, while the other is still assigned to the key, example: R for reload and for loot all - works flawlessly during combat where many corpses lay around). Thank God we can actually activate some more power-hungry graphical options! This game was made for controlers (because consoles, f**k you PC gamers!), ported to PC and slapped "ready!" sticker.
2) Dumbed-down response description - no longer are you able to tell what your character will precisely say, responses are limited to the sort of "yes", "no", "sarcastic" and the like, occasionally changing into different options when dialogue is longer, or key to main story line, only making it more difficult. This made me feel like I have no influence on what's happening as a result of my decisions.
3) Main story line - just like with Fallout 3: written on a tissue during coffee break. At times, delivers that nice feeling of being actually surprised by a plot twist, then fails utterly when you become a person who should lead certain faction as their leader-and-decision-maker, and yet you have no influence on avoiding oncoming bloodbath (sorry, can't give more details to avoid spoilers :) ).
4) The world doesn't look like 200 years after nuclear war. It more looks like 40 years - I've seen abandoned cities in real life being more consumed by wildlife in 20 years, than this game's environment was in supposedly 200. And that's not an issue with environment - this game's scenario seems to be badly thought out in general.
So, is this game worth a buy?
If you're in for a Fallout-themed shooter with minimum of RPG elements, rich and interesting environment to explore and to immerse yourself in background story told by all the terminals and notes left around - you're in for a treat!
If you didn't like Fallout 3/New Vegas and expect some outstanding story-telling, you may be disappointed.
I certainly enjoyed, and still am enjoying, the game, so for me - it's a positive.

FO4 has taken the industry by storm, and the internet has been buzzing about Bethesda's return to the franchise. Everyone called out of work (Or at least quipped about doing so), other gaming companies have referenced it, and reports say that it's breaking sales records.
I recommend it, especially if you're a fan of the revival of the franchise. Despite this, the game is not without flaws.
Now, I'm a very chill player. My panties did not become twisted over the power armor rehaul, the early deathclaw attack, the graphics (I'm just happy it can even run on my badly prebuilt computer). the odd dialog system (Which I find a little irritating) and even the perk system doesn't bother me too much. If anything, it's just remniscent of their work on Skyrim (Which people are still playing four years later).
But you may hear tales of how... punishing FO4 is compared to its predecessors.
New Vegas had its own "Hard" areas. Namely that if you went straight north as soon as possible, you'd run right into a quarry of deathclaws. FO4 boasts that the farther south you go, the harder the enemies become. This doesn't seem to translate that well into the game. Starting on Easy difficulty, one of my first quests is to get to the main city: Diamond City. A mere twenty minutes into my game, skipping the settlement tutorial quests (I just wanted to see the world and was not about to waste two hours in one town - I got into that much later), I ran into a gunner gang and died immediately. Reloading save, I evaded this encampment and ran into a super mutant takeover that's right in front of the bridge to Diamond City. Dieing again, I blasted my way through them (Knowing what to expect) only to be detroyed by a measily raider armed with the Fat-Man, a nuke-launcher.
There's "beef gates", difficulty levels, and challenging. All of this? Was downright unfair to a gamer's first two hours into the game.
I understand the need for a certain learning curve but I was gunned down and torn apart on the upper third of the map. I died dozens of times before coming into my own.
I will say things go a bit more smoothly as the game trucks on as you gain access to various faction quests. Even the radiant quests (Similar to Skyrim's unlimited questing) help you get the lay of the land while supplying you with the necessarily resources to build on your weapons.
My point is, after a while you start to get a 'feel' for the game and it quickly becomes obvious why everyone you know has gathered several dozen hours on the game.
I just want to warn anyone I can to be very, very careful. Regardless, the game is certainly worth it if you're a fan of Bethesda's work in general. Skyrim. With guns.

*NO SPOILERS*
Ok, this is a bit of a long one, so if you're planning on reading this buckle up.
Now, I'd say that I'm a long standing fan of the fallout series, but only in terms of the Bethesda / Obsidian entertainment, I've got 500+ hours on both NV and 3 on my xbox, (Long gone are the days of my console peasantry - I apologise) and I've just hit the 60 Hour mark on Fallout 4, does this make my opinion better than a new player? No, each to their own, but, it does give me a good grounds for comparison.
Now I'll do this like any average review and split it into numbered pros and cons list.
Pros:
1. ♥♥♥♥ing Excellent gameplay:
The game is just ♥♥♥♥ing great to play, there are a variety of guns to use, a variety of armour and wacky clothes to equip and just generally a lot of quests to play through, currenly I'm level 44 - 45 and while I've completed the story, I still have a lot of side quests to find through the thousands of zones I've not yet visited, while guns and weapons are limited to just under 60 weapons, the amount of customization you can do to them make's them completley different guns to play with, as well as the 44 unique weapons hidden around the world.
it offers a variety of different difficulty settings that go "Very easy, easy, normal, hard, very hard, SURVIVAL," which offeres different levels of play styles and difficulty and rewards those that play on harder difficulties with better chances to get legendary weapons.
2. ♥♥♥♥ing beautiful:
A lot of people are complaining about the graphics and I really, really don't know why, I play on the lowest settings and barely scratch 60fps, and I can play fine and happily with how the game looks because even on low, it looks great, sure, textures are a bit awful, but they're better than Fallout 3 / NV by a long shot, even the general look of outside feels more apocalyptic with it's washed out look, abandoned burnt down buildings, rustic civilizations of scrap metal, feral and tame abominations of radiation riddled creatures, even zones like the "glowing sea" all really capture what you would expect from a nuclear disaster perfectly.
3. settlements:
Now this was something that had me practically grasping at my balls and tugging on my meat during the initial reveal trailer, and while in reality I find myself rarely using this feature of the game because I prefer blood filled rampages of shooting things, it is nice to come to a place to build a home for myself and/or others, maybe even trying to set up a town and trade routes, it's implemented as something in a world of fast paced shooting, you can just take your time with and relax while listening to some classic old music.
My only recommendations of improvement on this are:
-Remove height cap.
-Improve the clip feature, it's a bit ♥♥♥♥♥♥ at times.
4. Replayability:
I've played this game's main story through once, and I'm still not done exploring the rest of the game and it's many side quests, there is however, still a lot for me to go through in regards to the alternative endings, I could save at a specific point and do all the different endings from there, but, personally I'd prefer to start again and do the different endings with different companions following me, the game is set up incredibily well for at least 4 or more play throughs if you are someone who has a lot of time on their hands.
5. Companions:
Companions are extremeley well done, they all have a backstory to them that are slowly revealed as you earn their trust, they all have dislikes, hatreds and loves for actions of the player, and they all have thoughts and feelings towards current event's of main quests and side quests, I love practically every one of the companions, especially the dog - who you can even dress up with bandanas or dog armour.
Cons:
1. Limited speech options:
Yes I know, this is a con that's already been shoved down your throat with a billion other reviews but it's just something that needs mentioning, NPC's that aren't shop keepers just seem usefull for only one thing, and that's quests, you speak to someone, you choose from your limited options and you're told only what you need to know, sometimes you can dig for bits of information regarding the quest, but that's it, after completing the quest, the most you get out of a NPC is a passive sentence after you call their name.
In Fallout 3 / NV it was completley different, you usually had a wide array of options to choose from that didn't limit themselves, you could talk about stuff other than the quest and more about the area and the secrets it holds, and after you had done a quest, you could talk to the quest giver again except maybe this time the npc was happier or angrier with you depending on how you did their quest.
Overall I just think it was something that could have been a bit more fleshed out.
This however, does exclude companions, I'll talk more about them later.
2. Lack of Karma:
Now this is one that even I will agree is an argueable subject as to whether it's truely needed in the game, but, it's just something that made fallout for me.
The game in it's current state is set up very much like Skyrim, anything you do in the world is regarded in any way shape or form as positive so that the player feels good about themselves, personally I feel that this is a step back, if I murder all of Diamond city, I want to feel like an ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, have people scared of me, have children run away in fear by my presence and be known as the "Diamond crusher."
Instead I get an empty city, maybe a companion who is♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥off at me (If they were their to witness said culling,) and nothing to show for it other than whatever I loot off of peoples bodies.
3. Survival mode = ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥:
Ok, this is probably my most hated part of Fallout 4, Fallout: New Vegas did one thing Very well, and that was Hardcore mode, you had to eat, sleep, drink and limit your bullets, as they actually weighed something, it added a survival aspect to the game that intensified the difficulty and made it a lot more interesting.
Survival mode on Fallout 4 on the other hand, is just... No.
It's not survival, it's just "extremeley hard," enemies do more damage, have more health, take less damage, are more likely to be legendary and drop more legendary weapons, that's it, there's no mode to include anything actually "survival" or what we expected to be survival, other than "don't get killed by the guy/creature with the weapon!"
A recommendation for the devs: renamed survival to "extremeley hard" and reiterate survival as something similar to Hardcore mode.
4: Critical hits are pointless:
Through the 60 hours that I've been playing, I've found that I'm never using my VAT's unless I'm fighting something extremeley annoying to hit, such as "stingwings" or "bloatflys" and critical hits are set up so that they can only be used during VAT's, I personally find that slowing down the game, to hit a specific point on a target, to do a critical hit, is another downgrade.
Critical hit's should have stayed the same as they were in fallout 3 / NV, a critical chance was a percentage based on your luck, and whenever you were to shoot a creature or humanoids, without VAT's, there was at least a chance it would hit a critical, I wouldn't have to open up VAT's to do it or build it up over time, it just happened.
It's a unique twist on criticals, but it's just one I don't use.
TLDR:
Pros:
-Good gameplay.
-Good Graphics.
-Good implementation of settlements
-At least 4 playthroughs (without upcoming DLC)
-Companions are fleshed out and fun.
Cons:
-Boo! 4 dialog options
-No Karma system
-increased Difficulty = MOAR HELTH, MOAR DAMAG
-Critical hits = pointless

Just hit >70 hours and finished main story line. A lot of side quests to do, which I'll get back to shortly.
For me, the game turned out to be an absolute blast - about 50 hours in the last 5 days should tell you all.
So, after all the adventures, is it worth a buy?
Graphics-wise, the game is deffinitely an evolution over last two titles. It's the best looking Fallout so far, and best-looking Bethesda game to date. I haven't encountered many graphical glitches, which is a good result considering size of the world involved. I also didn't have any issues performance-wise - the game ran on acceptable FPS levels on my old gaming rig which didn't even meet minimum requirements. The new gaming rigt didn't even break a sweat, providing outstanding performance majority of time, with only few FPS drops here and there.
Few words about the engine: it is still capable of delivering good looking game, but only thanks to Bethesda programmers' spectacular work of juicing all the ooze out of it. Still, it must be said - this engine seems to be at the very limits of its capabilities and I don't see it running next Bethesda game, not if it wants to compete with other games.
The game's atmosphere is wonderful - once again we're back to urban environment, with lots of buildings, bridges, tunnels and the like, surrounded by suburban outskirts of houses. Although not everyone's fond of F4's color palette, I find it believable - let me just remind you that pre-war Fallout world is based on 1950's, where pastel colors were trendy. Personally, I think the more colorful world fits the Boston area well, but as usual - that's my opinion, your may vary.
I like the fact the main protagonist is now voiced!
Despite the fact I am enjoying this game, I cannot say there aren't issues. I'll allow myself to punctuate here:
1) Downright insulting console port: forget FOV slider in settings, forget fully bindable keyboard (some binds are hardcoded so you may change one function, while the other is still assigned to the key, example: R for reload and for loot all - works flawlessly during combat where many corpses lay around). Thank God we can actually activate some more power-hungry graphical options! This game was made for controlers (because consoles, f**k you PC gamers!), ported to PC and slapped "ready!" sticker.
2) Dumbed-down response description - no longer are you able to tell what your character will precisely say, responses are limited to the sort of "yes", "no", "sarcastic" and the like, occasionally changing into different options when dialogue is longer, or key to main story line, only making it more difficult. This made me feel like I have no influence on what's happening as a result of my decisions.
3) Main story line - just like with Fallout 3: written on a tissue during coffee break. At times, delivers that nice feeling of being actually surprised by a plot twist, then fails utterly when you become a person who should lead certain faction as their leader-and-decision-maker, and yet you have no influence on avoiding oncoming bloodbath (sorry, can't give more details to avoid spoilers :) ).
4) The world doesn't look like 200 years after nuclear war. It more looks like 40 years - I've seen abandoned cities in real life being more consumed by wildlife in 20 years, than this game's environment was in supposedly 200. And that's not an issue with environment - this game's scenario seems to be badly thought out in general.
So, is this game worth a buy?
If you're in for a Fallout-themed shooter with minimum of RPG elements, rich and interesting environment to explore and to immerse yourself in background story told by all the terminals and notes left around - you're in for a treat!
If you didn't like Fallout 3/New Vegas and expect some outstanding story-telling, you may be disappointed.
I certainly enjoyed, and still am enjoying, the game, so for me - it's a positive.

Mods good. Game dull. Mods make very limited game very good game.  Done.

As ever with Bethesda, something that many of us oldies loved and keep buying in the hopes it will regain its former credentials seems to be dying a death that seems likely due to it being designed for a console and so unable to develop beyond the limitations of where it is.  Perhaps Fallout 4, like the consoles the designers had in mind cannot evolve to take advantage of new hardware to give us a bigger more immersive experience because the consoles it is designed for cannot upgrade and evolve.  However, even with that in mind this is not much of an upgrade from fallout new vegas or another Bethesda game if your an acomplished modder. In fact, you might find it more limited for want of a GECK.
The ultimate reason to buy it, you can mod the hell out of it.   Yes I can, technically overcome the limitations of console heritgate and turn it into something post 2006 to some extent.  But, the basic underlying game should not have to rely almost purely on that.   Poor field of view as standard is sub standard if you got a PC not a console.  Would it have hurt so much to design for a wider field of view?  This is a classic Bethesda issue in general and should not be happening.
This really sums up my thoughts on this game from the technical perspective of engine, graphics immersion and compatibility .I can patch it, I can mod it I can take it out the back where no one can see and beat it half to death only to have it come back using 8 gigs of VRAM in an attempt to make it look pretty.  The open moddability of the thing is truly appreciated.  But why should anyone do that out of the box to make it playable?  Field of View and other basic elements that should just be there?
In terms of gameplay, the environment feels more sterile than past games and the charm has been lost in a sense.  This is fallout 4, Urban Warfare. There is a lot of city type combat though those areas are done very well. However, there is not enough wasteland to wander outside of this for me making the game feel small at times. . On the subject of the wasteland. It does not have the same feel at all.  This is not a technical issue, it is a design issue.  Hendon high street is more dangerous, not to mention Cologne.   Bearing in mind they had limited space, they couldnt put actual wilderness in so it really is very much and urban story.  I would have liked to see the wasteland expanded in proportion to the large city to give a greater sense of scale and freedom and I really dont care if that would melt consoles to plastic slag.
One  new and very welcome feature/enhancement is the ability to construct a settlement. However, it is as though this was a concept that ran out of time and was never implemented properly.Once more, enter the modders. (No thanks to Bethesda who couldnt be bothered to release the construction kit it so badly needed with the game).
Graphics are still stuck in console realm and at times it looks positively ugly unless you get modding.  The character models.... omg.  Anyone over 12 years old can look like something out The Walking Dead.
Modded, the settlement aspect is truly a thing of beauty and I can spend countless hours on it.  It was one of the only real innovations with this title but modders picked it up and really ran with it and it is great fun.
Again, given that mods are essential.... wheres the creation kit?
On the very positive side, at least they give you a full game for the money, make it moddable and only then sell you DLC.  That is appreciated.

I've been a fan of Fallout since the beginning. I've played every title (except for that stupid looking console one, BoS) and every single title in the series has been great for what that game was trying to do.
Fallout 1 and 2 are clearly the best in the series for RPG elements.
Fallout Tactics was a great squad based strategy game.
Fallout 3 was a fantastic action/adventure game
Fallout: new vegas blended the action/adventure with better elements of RPGs like that of the first two
And finally, Fallout 4.
None of the series has a better view on the Fallout universe. The attention to detail in the environment and world is at a S.T.A.L.K.E.R. level of greatness, and is easily the best Bethesda has done yet. Everything in Fallout 4 behaves the way you would've imagined it would've back when you were playing Fallout 1 and 2. It may be lite in some of the RPG elements, but so are most of the games nowadays that claim to be RPGs. Fallout 4 does everything you'd hope it would and more. The combat in Fallout 4 is more solid than the majority of today's dedicated First Person Shooters. The gun play is great, the enemies are great, combat feels natural and fresh with every battle.
I'll admit, the building settlements is a little less than i was hoping for, but a simple concrete slab with out the wooden floor is all id ask for so that i may smooth out the land.
People obviously complain about the dialog. Yes it's not as well written as Fallout 1 and 2, but Arcanum was the only other game i've played that has had that level of dialog. Mass Effects dialog is ten-fold less interesting than Fallout 4's, but everyone is cool with that because you can have sex with aliens? The voice acting feels less like acting and more like natural responses. I mean, when you are skipping dialog, you character will occasionally say 'mhm' 'yep' 'uh-huh' like you do when you yourself are actually ignoring someone, now that's attention to detail my friends!
There is just so much to love about Fallout 4, because there is so much to it, and so much in it. The level design is absolutely amazing, you're almost always going to find something you didn't see the second time you pass through. It is with all these things taken into consideration, that Fallout 4 is easily the greatest Fallout game in the series.
Fallout 1 and 2 were fantastic, but trust me, if you were to play them now, or even if you played them back then, you'd have been wishing for a fraction of what Fallout 4 has to offer.

If you played Fallout 3, Fallout 4 is very similar in most if not every aspect.
To start with things I didn't like:
1. First thing I noticed is optimalisation. It's rather poor for a game looking like this. I had some irritating fps drops while using weapon's scope and sometimes in a bushy/tree dense regions. After lowering some options the game worked fine, but I noticed how ugly this game can actually be.
2. This ain't the rpg game for sure. All your dialog options are like: yes, ♥♥♥♥ you (no), tell me more and dull sarcastic jokes also they're very boring, predictable and add no interesting information about the lore. The story has many logical gaps which shouldn't happen, especially in rpgs. You can't roleplay your character as you wish, good people are always more rewarded.
3. Map is boring. I lost my exploration desire very quickly. You won't find any unique places, enemies, things when exploring. Literally nothing, everywhere dull, barren wasteland. I'd complain about map's size as well, but seeing how bad this map is designed, I'm happy that it is small.
4. Weapons. This one has a good and bad points. The weapon arsenal usable in a game is very small, every weapon looks very similar, sound very similar, but there are many weapon mods. You can have two same weapons customized in a different way. Weapon upgrades are made really well, same goes to power armor. Shotting is pretty fun, kinda enjoyed slaughtering all those ghouls and mutants.
5. Enemies or actually lack of them. You'll encouter some raiders, ghouls, mutants and crazy mosquitos and their different kinds. That's pretty much it and gets boring to see 100th camp being raided by one of them.
6. Side quests are... infinite. Whenever you enter a settlement you'll receive a random generated quest to go somewhere, kill something or collect something and bring it back. It's nothing, you'll just click it through and go to slaugter, but I had fun doing them over and over for some hours. After that I just went for a main quest.
7. Special and perks are decent. I know they screwed up by removing previous fallouts' character development, but this one wasn't that terrible. I enjoyed doing mentioned side quests to level up my character and I liked that. Still I wish I had something more to spend than one perk point per level.
8. There are lots of bugs, but I guess you'd be surprised if there weren't. It's Bethesda. There was no patch yet when I'm writing it and it'll probably be fixed in upcoming patches or when modding tools are released.
9. Some people complain about AI. You can go past them and they won't see you, react. Personally I didn't mind that. Was a stealhy ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ anyway ;)
10. Sims mode. Quite nice, but it's not really my thing. You can build some decent settlements in it. Probably enjoyable if you don't wanna kill monsters all the time and chill for a bit. I only wish there were more raids with stronger enemies.
So this is it. Fallout 4 is rather bad game as vanilla. The only thing I enjoyed for some time was doing those side quests and killing random enemies over and over again with my customized weapons. The rest is sad. It's definately not a rpg game, so if you're looking for something of that kind go buy Wasteland or check old fallouts instead. I'd call Fallout 4 decent shooter, though there are better out there. The main story was cheap with errors.
The only things that may make this game interesting are mods, once modding tools are released. Community tend to do crazy things with bethesda's games and It'll definately be interesting to check this game with mods, otherwise I suggest waiting for sale/mods. Vanilla is disappointing

*NO SPOILERS*
Ok, this is a bit of a long one, so if you're planning on reading this buckle up.
Now, I'd say that I'm a long standing fan of the fallout series, but only in terms of the Bethesda / Obsidian entertainment, I've got 500+ hours on both NV and 3 on my xbox, (Long gone are the days of my console peasantry - I apologise) and I've just hit the 60 Hour mark on Fallout 4, does this make my opinion better than a new player? No, each to their own, but, it does give me a good grounds for comparison.
Now I'll do this like any average review and split it into numbered pros and cons list.
Pros:
1. ♥♥♥♥ing Excellent gameplay:
The game is just ♥♥♥♥ing great to play, there are a variety of guns to use, a variety of armour and wacky clothes to equip and just generally a lot of quests to play through, currenly I'm level 44 - 45 and while I've completed the story, I still have a lot of side quests to find through the thousands of zones I've not yet visited, while guns and weapons are limited to just under 60 weapons, the amount of customization you can do to them make's them completley different guns to play with, as well as the 44 unique weapons hidden around the world.
it offers a variety of different difficulty settings that go "Very easy, easy, normal, hard, very hard, SURVIVAL," which offeres different levels of play styles and difficulty and rewards those that play on harder difficulties with better chances to get legendary weapons.
2. ♥♥♥♥ing beautiful:
A lot of people are complaining about the graphics and I really, really don't know why, I play on the lowest settings and barely scratch 60fps, and I can play fine and happily with how the game looks because even on low, it looks great, sure, textures are a bit awful, but they're better than Fallout 3 / NV by a long shot, even the general look of outside feels more apocalyptic with it's washed out look, abandoned burnt down buildings, rustic civilizations of scrap metal, feral and tame abominations of radiation riddled creatures, even zones like the "glowing sea" all really capture what you would expect from a nuclear disaster perfectly.
3. settlements:
Now this was something that had me practically grasping at my balls and tugging on my meat during the initial reveal trailer, and while in reality I find myself rarely using this feature of the game because I prefer blood filled rampages of shooting things, it is nice to come to a place to build a home for myself and/or others, maybe even trying to set up a town and trade routes, it's implemented as something in a world of fast paced shooting, you can just take your time with and relax while listening to some classic old music.
My only recommendations of improvement on this are:
-Remove height cap.
-Improve the clip feature, it's a bit ♥♥♥♥♥♥ at times.
4. Replayability:
I've played this game's main story through once, and I'm still not done exploring the rest of the game and it's many side quests, there is however, still a lot for me to go through in regards to the alternative endings, I could save at a specific point and do all the different endings from there, but, personally I'd prefer to start again and do the different endings with different companions following me, the game is set up incredibily well for at least 4 or more play throughs if you are someone who has a lot of time on their hands.
5. Companions:
Companions are extremeley well done, they all have a backstory to them that are slowly revealed as you earn their trust, they all have dislikes, hatreds and loves for actions of the player, and they all have thoughts and feelings towards current event's of main quests and side quests, I love practically every one of the companions, especially the dog - who you can even dress up with bandanas or dog armour.
Cons:
1. Limited speech options:
Yes I know, this is a con that's already been shoved down your throat with a billion other reviews but it's just something that needs mentioning, NPC's that aren't shop keepers just seem usefull for only one thing, and that's quests, you speak to someone, you choose from your limited options and you're told only what you need to know, sometimes you can dig for bits of information regarding the quest, but that's it, after completing the quest, the most you get out of a NPC is a passive sentence after you call their name.
In Fallout 3 / NV it was completley different, you usually had a wide array of options to choose from that didn't limit themselves, you could talk about stuff other than the quest and more about the area and the secrets it holds, and after you had done a quest, you could talk to the quest giver again except maybe this time the npc was happier or angrier with you depending on how you did their quest.
Overall I just think it was something that could have been a bit more fleshed out.
This however, does exclude companions, I'll talk more about them later.
2. Lack of Karma:
Now this is one that even I will agree is an argueable subject as to whether it's truely needed in the game, but, it's just something that made fallout for me.
The game in it's current state is set up very much like Skyrim, anything you do in the world is regarded in any way shape or form as positive so that the player feels good about themselves, personally I feel that this is a step back, if I murder all of Diamond city, I want to feel like an ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, have people scared of me, have children run away in fear by my presence and be known as the "Diamond crusher."
Instead I get an empty city, maybe a companion who is♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥off at me (If they were their to witness said culling,) and nothing to show for it other than whatever I loot off of peoples bodies.
3. Survival mode = ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥:
Ok, this is probably my most hated part of Fallout 4, Fallout: New Vegas did one thing Very well, and that was Hardcore mode, you had to eat, sleep, drink and limit your bullets, as they actually weighed something, it added a survival aspect to the game that intensified the difficulty and made it a lot more interesting.
Survival mode on Fallout 4 on the other hand, is just... No.
It's not survival, it's just "extremeley hard," enemies do more damage, have more health, take less damage, are more likely to be legendary and drop more legendary weapons, that's it, there's no mode to include anything actually "survival" or what we expected to be survival, other than "don't get killed by the guy/creature with the weapon!"
A recommendation for the devs: renamed survival to "extremeley hard" and reiterate survival as something similar to Hardcore mode.
4: Critical hits are pointless:
Through the 60 hours that I've been playing, I've found that I'm never using my VAT's unless I'm fighting something extremeley annoying to hit, such as "stingwings" or "bloatflys" and critical hits are set up so that they can only be used during VAT's, I personally find that slowing down the game, to hit a specific point on a target, to do a critical hit, is another downgrade.
Critical hit's should have stayed the same as they were in fallout 3 / NV, a critical chance was a percentage based on your luck, and whenever you were to shoot a creature or humanoids, without VAT's, there was at least a chance it would hit a critical, I wouldn't have to open up VAT's to do it or build it up over time, it just happened.
It's a unique twist on criticals, but it's just one I don't use.
TLDR:
Pros:
-Good gameplay.
-Good Graphics.
-Good implementation of settlements
-At least 4 playthroughs (without upcoming DLC)
-Companions are fleshed out and fun.
Cons:
-Boo! 4 dialog options
-No Karma system
-increased Difficulty = MOAR HELTH, MOAR DAMAG
-Critical hits = pointless

Good and bad changes since Fallout 3 and Nev Vegas, but ultimately the good outweighs the bad. If you are gameplay focused like me then the improved combat, which is more fluent and satisfying compared to FO3 and Vegas, is the saving aspect of the game. But as somebody who enjoys RP a lot as well I am sad to see the system becoming terribly one dimensional. There is little room for RP, your character (the male one at least, haven't tried female yet) sounds way too timid even when you try to be hostile. There are some choices but they can almost only be found within the main story line. Many of the characters could have ben made better as well, with longer and more intricate dialogues so the player can investigate the history, motives and personaleties of those inhabiting the world. This, and that textures could be a bit higher resolution for the PC version, are the only real critiques I could hold against the game.
Without spoiling too much I will say that I find the main story quite interesting, you are caught up in a struggle between some major factions and plenty opportunities for betrayal and acting as double agent is given. Unravelling the mystery of your missing son is also an entertaining aspect of the story. In the end it is your personal view on morality that will decide the future of the Commonwealth.
A few small points: The skill system of the old fallout games has been compressed with no real effects on actual gameplay. Power armour is now quite powerful but also entirely option if you feel it makes the game too easy. Humour can be found in abundance in true fallout spirit. Companions feel more interesting compared to earlier games. Base building is great if you are into that sort of thing. While graphically unimpressive the art style of the game still makes it a pleasant sight for the eyes.
The game is also abundant in content and probably contains 150 - 200 hours of playing if you intend to 100 % it.

I've waited five years for this game.
It was well worth the wait.
Fallout 4 has exceeded all my expectations, it's graphics, while not the best, are still visually appealing, even on medium-high levels. There is much more color in the game that in Fallout 3 or New Vegas, which does a good job of helping immerse the player in the world around them.
The combat is much more fluid, Fallout 3 and NV had janky animations, an annoying weapon degradation system, and strangely innacurate ADS mechanics. Fallout 4 has improved upon these flaws GREATLY. The animations now look more human, the AI actually takes cover and tries to dodge bullets being spewed at them, and aiming down sights is much more accurate. Not only that, but V.A.T.S is no longer a makeshift pause button. Now, V.A.T.S only slows time to a crawl, forcing you to make quick decisions on where you want to focus your shots, giving combat more excitement than in the previous installments.
In addition to those points, the weapon and armor modding is AMAZING. There are so many options when it comes to modding your weapons, including things like larger magazines, automatic recievers, and even receivers that change your weapon's caliber. Armor modding is similar, requiring parts looted from junk around the wastelands used to craft your modifications. And with the new layered armor system, you have to scavenge for each leg/arm guard, instead of just picking up a jacket, and finding an additional helmet, boots, and pink panther thong inside. This pushes the player to explore every location, just trying to find that left shin guard that'll give you the best protection.
As for story, the dialouge options have been streamlined into something similar to the Witcher series, which gives the player an outline of what the protagonist will say. This is useful because the main protagonist is voiced now, which I find causes me to be more invested in the dialouge, instead of just skipping through at the click of a button. In terms of actual storytelling ability, Fallout 4 is one of the few games where I fear the consequences of my actions. The game's story is structured so that you will have to make contact with the main factions in the world, and then later on decide which ones you want to still be apart of.
It executes this very well, in this spoiler, I will give an example of this, so read at your own risk
The game is FULL of decisions like that, making for a special playthrough each time you make a new character.
There are many more aspects of this game that I would like to go into detail about, but I won't, for sake of time. So, should you buy this game? Yes, do it RIGHT NOW, if you like a huge open world full of immersive characters and locations, then do it, buy it TODAY.

As another review said, the reason there where an overwhelming number of negative reviews on launch day is because the people who were having a blast with the game were too busy playing it to write a damn review. I was so worried by all those bad reviews, that I canceled my pre-ordered Pipboy edition of the game, and just bought the $60 Steam version instead.
I think I'm only 13 or 14 hours into the game at the time of this review, but let me tell you that this game is epic. I have been a die hard Fallout fan, and this game blew my expectations out of the water. There are a few things I found dissapointing, but very few.
Pros-
Graphics- A lot of people are complaining about the graphics being "last gen", but the environments are truly beautiful. I think the textures are amazing as well, but if they aren't to your expectations, I'm sure a Hi-res texture mod will be out in a matter of months.
Immersion- I have never been this immersed in a Fallout game, and that's saying a lot because I find all the games very immersive. This one is different though... Without giving any spoilers, I found myself clearing an area as a radiation storm was rolling in. The sound in the air was ominous, and the world became very...uncomfotable. I checked around this place, finding some booby traps and checking for general security, and then slept in a sleeping bag to gain a little health. All of the time you are having to make tactical decisions. You can't be greedy. You have to use your environment more. It really feels like survival.
Sound/Gunplay- I'm doing these together because it's how they work together that make them so great. The gunplay is improved a 1000%, and the way the guns sound is so freaking awesome. All types too, even energy weapons sound so badass. This was definitely a weakness in the earlier versions.
Usefulness from useless items- rollerskates, clipboards, duct tape; it all has a purpose now. Now it is even more challenging to try and balance out what to pick up or not pick up as you reach your maximum weight.
Building fortresses- You can spend far too much time doing this, and it's incredibly fun
Cons- if it seems like I am listing far more cons than pros, that is just because I can't possibly list all the good things about this game. It is incredible.
Dialouge- I am not actually a fan of the new dialouge feature. It makes it sort of seem like your character has a certain forced personality. Sometimes it also just seems like it doesn't matter what you say, you are going to get the same outcome, or they are going to make you say everything by going through every choice anyway.
Stimpaks- Just using a stimpak heals a cripled limb, and I even just "walked it off" after cripling a leg on a landmine. Literally, I hobbled for about 10 seconds, and my cripled limb was healed without using anything for health.
Karma- unless I am missing something, it seems like the whole Karma thing is gone now. You may have to take what I say here with a grain of salt, because I may be missing something, but I don't really see where your choices effect the game at all as far as a Karma level. I've noticed that things you do may effect how a companion thinks of you, which may cause them to not follow you or something, but other than that I don't know. This is dissapointing to me, because I always liked to have a character that is pretty virtuous, and then another that is plain rotten evil.
Companions- the companions are clumsy piece's of♥♥♥♥♥♥that get in your way all the time, trip booby traps causing everyone to die, etc. There are a few nice little features, such as having them search for any items you may have missed, or Dogmeat dragging a Ghoul onto the ground while you pop it in the dome with your pipe-pistol, but I have thought several times about just dismissing all of my companions.
Guys and gals, I feel like I did a really ♥♥♥♥♥♥ job writing this review, but my fiance just quit playing the game to go take our real life Dogmeat (no her name isn't really Dogmeat sadly) for a walk, so I feel like I need to take back control of the computer. Not checking for typos, because no one cares about typos in the wasteland.

I've been a fan of Fallout since the beginning. I've played every title (except for that stupid looking console one, BoS) and every single title in the series has been great for what that game was trying to do.
Fallout 1 and 2 are clearly the best in the series for RPG elements.
Fallout Tactics was a great squad based strategy game.
Fallout 3 was a fantastic action/adventure game
Fallout: new vegas blended the action/adventure with better elements of RPGs like that of the first two
And finally, Fallout 4.
None of the series has a better view on the Fallout universe. The attention to detail in the environment and world is at a S.T.A.L.K.E.R. level of greatness, and is easily the best Bethesda has done yet. Everything in Fallout 4 behaves the way you would've imagined it would've back when you were playing Fallout 1 and 2. It may be lite in some of the RPG elements, but so are most of the games nowadays that claim to be RPGs. Fallout 4 does everything you'd hope it would and more. The combat in Fallout 4 is more solid than the majority of today's dedicated First Person Shooters. The gun play is great, the enemies are great, combat feels natural and fresh with every battle.
I'll admit, the building settlements is a little less than i was hoping for, but a simple concrete slab with out the wooden floor is all id ask for so that i may smooth out the land.
People obviously complain about the dialog. Yes it's not as well written as Fallout 1 and 2, but Arcanum was the only other game i've played that has had that level of dialog. Mass Effects dialog is ten-fold less interesting than Fallout 4's, but everyone is cool with that because you can have sex with aliens? The voice acting feels less like acting and more like natural responses. I mean, when you are skipping dialog, you character will occasionally say 'mhm' 'yep' 'uh-huh' like you do when you yourself are actually ignoring someone, now that's attention to detail my friends!
There is just so much to love about Fallout 4, because there is so much to it, and so much in it. The level design is absolutely amazing, you're almost always going to find something you didn't see the second time you pass through. It is with all these things taken into consideration, that Fallout 4 is easily the greatest Fallout game in the series.
Fallout 1 and 2 were fantastic, but trust me, if you were to play them now, or even if you played them back then, you'd have been wishing for a fraction of what Fallout 4 has to offer.

Overall Rating: ★★★★☆ [4/5}
Story: ★★★☆☆

★OVERALL★
Many things have changed since New Vegas, for better or worse; the interface, dialog, power armor, perk system, VATS, unkillable companions, and the waiting system. Other things have improved; the graphics, sound effects, enemy AI, weapon customization, no level cap, free-aim viability, character customization, and cooking. And even some new features like a weather system, moon-phases, a real crafting system, a bazillion armor customizations, legendary enemies, unique item abilities, building settlements, useful junk, and radiation affects.
Now, let's talk about what's been removed; the repuation system, karma, old-style dialog options, weapons holstering on characters, and weapon/armor durability (personally, I'm glad that's gone).
This is by no means a complete list of everything that has changed, improved, added or removed. Whether these things are good or bad is entirely up to you. Personally, I think we've gained far more than we've lost in Fallout 4.
★STORY★
For the first time, we get to witness "when the bombs fell" instead of just hearing about it. And the time leading up to it feels tense. A sense of urgency to flee is immediately felt. And as an adult that understands the importance of family, the protagonist's loss and sudsequent purpose is much more relatable to me than the previous Fallout games. When you first immerge from the vault into the wasteland, it's apparent that you're in way over your head. Fights are difficult, ammo is sparse, and the world is rotting away. Everything feels hopeless, dead and destroyed. Then, slowly but surely, you get the hang of things. You forge alliances, make enemies, and ultimately have an impact on the Commonwealth. Predictable in some places, surprising in others, but overall a good story nonetheless.
★GAMEPLAY★
Gunplay is spot on. Free-aiming makes firefights feel more tense. Sniping with scopes is more realistic, as you now have the option to hold your breath, thus steadying your aim. Night-vision actually helps when it's dark.
More advanced enemies will take cover, flank you, shoot your grenades in mid-air, predict your shots and dodge them. Crippling limbs has a huge effect on enemies and yourself. Shoot their legs, they will fall to the ground and stop shooting. Shoot their arms and they'll drop their gun. And headshots are extremely satisfying. This can also work against you. If you're shot in the head, your focus will wane and your vision becomes blurry. If you're shot in any of your limbs, you'll be slower moving, reloading, or aiming becomes more difficult.
Ghouls are fast and will come at you in swarms. Super Mutants are tough and rarely wander the wasteland alone. The new, legendary enemies are tough to beat. And Deathclaws, well, you'll find out about them early on.
★SOUND★
The very first thing that I noticed was the sound of gunfire. Whether it was the close and personal firefights or the echos of battles far off in the distance, it sounds much more realistic than in previous games. Bullets have a pop-hiss sound and wizz over your head. Shell casings clink as they hit the pavement. It's very satisfying to use ballistic weapons.
Then there's the other ambiant sound effects. Rain drops thunking hard on your power armor, thunder cracking in the distance, the ominous and eerie sounds of radiation storms. And, of course, the music is exactly what we've come to expect from the franchise. Whether you're listening to the Silver Shroud on your radio or just the background music, it sounds fenomenal. This is the area of the game that gets five stars in my opinion.
★BUGS★
Fallout 4 ended up being way more polished than I expected. I experienced no game-breaking bugs, as is usually expected from their previous titles in this franchise. Only once did my game experience a crash-to-desktop, but it had auto-saved recently so I didn't lose anything. And for almost 90 hours of gameplay, I think I can let one little glitch slide. The bugs I did encounter more often were minor annoyances like mesh clipping, laggy weapon draw, frozen quest progression, and insta-deaths via falling through floors. These occurrances were infrequent and easily solved thanks to the autosave and quicksave functions. However, I am aware that other people are having some serious issues with the game. Bethesda has addressed those issues and is already working to fix them.

New Review 1/6/16
Tl,dr;
Great game, terrible Fallout game/ RPG in general, Deathclaws and Power Armor are forced down your throat at the beginning to try and disprove the latter, but any die hard fan looking for another Fallout game will be sorely dissapointed. May I suggest Wasteland 2 as an alternative. However, since I really don't care about franchises or genres in particular, I just like playing good games, which I feel this classes as.
Pros
- Far improved first person combat (while being a fan of the older games, I also happen to like the new formula)
- The first vaguely good looking Bethesda game on release
- Performance issues are now gone (I couldn't play for several months after release due to a speed up in gameplay tied to the framerate)
- Companions are better and more fleshed out than ever
- New power armor system is far superior to the older, clothes based system
- Interesting world, far more detailed than 3 or NV and even Skyrim
- Best script yet- I laughed a lot especially at Deacon (a companion) and even the player character's own dialogue (nothing on The Witcher, but a move in a good direction)
- Updated engine (finally Fallout has moved to creation engine in a much needed update)
- Settlement building
Cons
- Reduces the RPG elements substantially
- Character is given a full background
- Voiced protaganist (I'm not hugely against this one, but it would be better in a Saints Row        style, i.e; pick a voice)
- Perks are put together with skills which makes for a very 1 dimensional system
- Dialogue options, however good the dialogue is, is still a terrible system, very non-descript
- Storyline is ultimately flawed, with all factions involved either having little purpose, or being sidelined later on. The script is good, but the writing overall is pretty crap
- Morality system has gone :( You are now judged by your companions which is slightly odd
- Still little recognition for your actions in game (in regards to the game world evolving)
- Talking about cons, there's a settlement that needs your help, let me mark it on your map for you
- Crap Fallout game
- Its a first person open world shooter, not an open world RPG
- Modders are having to pick up a lot where the devs left off

Okay so I'm writing this review after spending 50 hours in the game
The gameplay is everything you can expect from a Bethesda Game; almost seamless (dungeons) Open World map with a lot's of points of interest to discover. I've played the game 50 hours and I haven't even touched the story after the tutorial and the exploration is immense, it just doesn't end, there is so much to discover and to look for. Quests don't offer much however, much of them have been a some kind of delivery quests; like go to a place X to recover item B and deliver it to NPC A, so not quite the Witcher 3 level experience (Emmentaler). Shooting mechanics and controls however has been improved from FO3 and NV, controls are slick and accurate and shooting mechanics feels like straight out from an FPS game and that is good, but melee feels somewhat off and throwing grenades are sometimes hazardouz for your health because of clunky design. The crafting system is okay, you just have enough skills and enough resources and you have it all. Customization is good, you have many armor bodyparts to choose from and many level-up-perk-rewards. With each level up you can pick up a perk you want if your level is high enough. I haven't touched the base bulding thingy at all so I can't say a word about that.
8/10
I have to say this, but the graphics are the one thing I don't rate in games, because I play them for good gameplay and story.
Texture filtering and texture quality are nice once you set some things up from Nvidia Control Panel, textures looks crisp and clean, but there is however some low detailed textures all around in the places that are hard to see (maybe because of the consoles). The effects look good overall, but there is some filtering tobe noticed sometimes and God Rays look good. The level of detail doesn't leave any reasons for hate, this game draws the world beautifully (at least on GTX 970] without pop-ins. AA is needed, the jaggies are there wheter you like it or not, I had to download SweetFX to make the game look the way I wanted in the terms of AA. All in all Graphics are okay after a short tweaking and setup. Slightly OC'd i5 4670k, slightly OC'd GTX 970 and 16 GB 1600 MHZ ram ran this game on Ultra settings about 45-60 fps.

Fallout 4 is without a doubt the best game of the year.
tl;dr : rpg is still intact, and its even been improved. Best game world ever created. Buy the game. you won't regret it. Ever.
Everyone who is giving this a bad score is just complaining because they are so hung up that Bethesda "changed" the rpg elements in Fallout. However, they DID NOT simplify it at all in any way. In fact, in the previous Fallouts it was quite easy to level up mid game (not end game/late game) to the point where the skills and perks didn't even really matter, because you had everything already. Every skill was above 75 and you had all the perks that you would have wanted. In Fallout 4 the game really makes you think strategically about "who you are" and what kind of wastelander you are stiving to be. The choices you pick through Fallout 4's rpg system WILL matter and make every difference in its world (depending on who you want to be).
Overall the game itself is a masterpiece. The visuals are unexpectedly spectacular. People nagged saying the graphics are outdated, but imo I thought the visuals were triple A 2015 status. (It's breathtaking..honestly it is. People must be blind) Con: When you load a new area it takes a while for the textures to come in but tbh its no big deal.
This game is the first game that made me FEEL like the world was TRULY ALIVE. 36 hours in and I have not met a single npc that "obviously" used the same character model/voice actor. But the game's storytelling, pacing, dialogue, and the ability to put all of that together depending on YOUR choice of what you want to do? is...was...and will forever be flawless. I ditched the mainstory but I can't even tell what the mainstory even is anymore. The WHOLE WORLD feels like the mainstory. Side quests (no matter how rinky dink the scope of the quest) is fully fleshed out with dialogue that matters, a story, and new characters with no obvious recycling of character models. You hear npc's talk to each other about something over the course of 10 ingame hours. And then later that npc comes to you talking about the same thing except now something went wrong and boom the quest starts. Everything in Fallout 4 is so organic, real, and truly makes this game worth well over 60 bucks.

Gonna be honest: I love this game. I love pretty much all games Bethesda releases. But is Fallout 4 perfect? No, there are flaws. I'll illustrate both the things I like and dislike in the game, but ultimately, this is a game I whole-heartedly recommend.
(I have kept this as spoiler-free as possible)
+Gameplay is much better than Fallout 3/NV and Skyrim. It's more responsive, interesting and actually feels fluid, which is something I haven't experienced in previous Bethesda titles.
+Enemies are smarter, use cover and aren't half-blind. Stealth is difficult, which ultimately makes it more rewarding.
+Character customisation is vastly improved over previous games. Mods will hopefully improve upon the quality even further.
+Weapons and armour have a nice degree of customisation and usefulness. All junk items in the game have purpose, as you build the weapons with them.
+Animation quality is far superior to previous titles. Seriously, just look at Piper's animations when you first meet her - so much better than Skyrim's animation.
+Base building is rather expansive for a game that is delving into the new territory. While admittedly it doesn't add much in terms of gameplay, it's still a lot of fun to create and manage a base.
+Much more interesting and diverse world than previous Fallout games. You've got the suburbs, the city, the coastline, the forests, the Glowing Sea, marshland, subways, and more to explore at your leisure.
+Main quest is mostly interesting and polished, despite being rather railroaded towards the end. Some people have complained that the main missions are cliche and poorly written, and that may be true, but it's still engaging enough to be enjoyable.
+Fairly unique faction missions which is good for replayability.
+The game doesn't end after completing the main quest. Always a plus.
+Interwoven character interactions, which make the world feel much more believable. Seeing your companions work together without intervention is certainly an appreciated touch and helps to establish the fact that humanity has built itself up again after the Great War.
+Graphics are better than previous Bethesda games, even though it's not the best for a 2015 release. Mods will fix it in time.
+Atmosphere is on point.
+Good music tracks, such as the battles with Deathclaws.
+Mod support. As always.
-Music is repetative and radio stations are generally annoying (might come down to personal preference).
-Dialogue is overly simplified and often meaningless, as your choices usually end up with the same result.
-Difficulty is a measure of how much health an enemy has. Higher difficulty settings make enemies bullet sponges, which is not fun at all. I recommend getting a mod that sets the damage multipliers to x1.5 for both player and foe, at the very least.
-A lot of armour and weapons (the vast majority, actually) become redundant very quickly, as newer equipment with far superior stats become available.
-Almost no interactive animations between characters. After seeing the protagonist pet Dogmeat at the first meeting, I was expecting more interaction between my character and others - handshakes, gestures, perhaps a friendly pat on the back - but it's simply missing.
-Characters are generally uninteresting. Romance is flat.
-Lip-sync stuffs up a lot. Some lines of dialogue get cut-off mid-sentence in favour of the next one.
-Repetitive, boring radiant side-missions. Don't get me wrong - some side missions are great. However, the radiant ones (such as, "rescue my friend"), are almost identical every time.
-The ending of the main quest is lacklustre, and faction choices don't make much difference in the chosen outcome.
-Framerate dips in cities and other cluttered areas. Reduce your shadow settings to improve performance drastically.
It might look like there are a lot of flaws (there are), but that doesn't detract from the overall experience of Fallout 4. Re-read the pros section of the review if you feel like I've soured your opinion by stating the negatives.
Get the game, whether that be now or in the future; you'll have fun. Especially with mods.

The more I play Fallout 4, the more disappointment I feel.  Fortunately, someone else has already put into words what I was starting to form an impression around.
"Bethedsa tried to do what's usually left to modders, and in the process stripped the R out of RPG in what's otherwise a great line of games.
The game is enjoyable, but it feels more like I'm playing a cross between Saints Row and Mass Effect, not Fallout.
It's a good game, but I can't recommend it as a Fallout game." - Taken from a review by Maki ★
Or, as I was starting to think; it's been dragged down into the knuckle-dragging depths of the likes that Assassins Creed inhabits.  It's fun, no doubt, but it's remarkably plain and utterly without depth.  Conversation options no longer even hint at allowing you to pick your sides anymore, unlike in New Vegas which I consider the pinnacle of a Fallout Role Playing experience given that you could side with the utterly brutal, not very friendly, slave driving Legion, the NCR, House, or even completely Independent .  Basically this leaves a supposedly open world to a remarkably linear story, which isn't Fallout.  And so much for a wasteland, really, the map's (comparatively) tiny and absolutely full with locations and victi...  'People'...  Hardly any 'waste' in the wasteland, certainly in terms of space and those who inhabit it are provided as little more than targets as opposed to providing additional flavour to the environment (unless you're a cannibal).
Yes, you can wander about in a mostly open world, yes you can attempt to approach things with your own twist (which in itself is largely limited to 'run in and gun it down' or 'attempt to be a sneaky ninj but fail due to the limits put in place by the new systems), but you can't have anywhere near the impact on that world as you could in previous games and you can't define your character nearly as well largely in part due to the new trait system.  The mechanics behind the game seem deliberately designed to remove thought an consideration from much of the content.  It should not be a foregone conclusion that you can get everything and be the 'best' at it all.
If anyone who hasn't already got it is swithering about getting this as a 'Fallout' game, don't.  That's not the experience you're going to have here.  It is fun, it's worth playing, but it's not Fallout.

Everyone who is giving this a bad score is just complaining because they are so hung up that Bethesda "changed" the rpg elements in Fallout. However, they DID NOT simplify it at all in any way. In fact, in the previous Fallouts it was quite easy to level up mid game (not end game/late game) to the point where the skills and perks didn't even really matter, because you had everything already. Every skill was above 75 and you had all the perks that you would have wanted. In Fallout 4 the game really makes you think strategically about "who you are" and what kind of wastelander you are stiving to be. The choices you pick through Fallout 4's rpg system WILL matter and make every difference in its world (depending on who you want to be).
Overall the game itself is a masterpiece. The visuals are unexpectedly spectacular. People nagged saying the graphics are outdated, but imo I thought the visuals were triple A 2015 status. (It's breathtaking..honestly it is. People must be blind) Con: When you load a new area it takes a while for the textures to come in but tbh its no big deal.
This game is the first game that made me FEEL like the world was TRULY ALIVE. 36 hours in and I have not met a single npc that "obviously" used the same character model/voice actor. But the game's storytelling, pacing, dialogue, and the ability to put all of that together depending on YOUR choice of what you want to do? is...was...and will forever be flawless. I ditched the mainstory but I can't even tell what the mainstory even is anymore. The WHOLE WORLD feels like the mainstory. Side quests (no matter how rinky dink the scope of the quest) is fully fleshed out with dialogue that matters, a story, and new characters with no obvious recycling of character models. You hear npc's talk to each other about something over the course of 10 ingame hours. And then later that npc comes to you talking about the same thing except now something went wrong and boom the quest starts. Everything in Fallout 4 is so organic, real, and truly makes this game worth well over 60 bucks.

Is it a great fallout story? . . . not really.
. . . but is it a fantastic game? YES.
As a huge fan of Fallout 3, I immediately noticed the lack of depth in dialogue and interesting choices. Some of the RPG elements have been removed, and I lament their loss.
However, my lamentations pretty well ended when I actually hit the downtown boston area. All of a sudden, the Fallout game I thought wasn't living up to its name. . . lived up to its name. Exploring the commonwealth, looting buildings, and creating a meaningful homebase where I mod out my gear is surprisingly fresh, compelling, and just plain insanely fun.
The random epic moments are still here, and they are random and they are epic. I was running between skyscrapers after a brotherhood of steel vertibird targeted me and decided it wanted to end my life (the brotherhood hates me since I decided to kill a backtalking piece of♥♥♥♥♥♥member early in the game). After I hit the vertibird with a rocket it lost control between buildings, spun into one, and exploded in burning flames to the ground. When I turned around I realized I had been running from the vertibird so hard I was now in the middle of a super mutant encampment. When the Brotherhood paladins emerged from the vertibird wreckage in their powersuits they were immediately engaged by the super mutants. The pure chaos of the extended fight reminded me just why I loved Fallout 3 so much, except. . .
It was even better than Fallout 3.
