There comes a time in every Bethesda game (or perhaps open-world games in general) when the game is 'broken'. I don't mean in terms of bugs or gameplay hindrances (though those do exist), but rather the fact that adventuring and discovery become rote and uninteresting. As a gamer, you have totally 'figured out' the game and the process of actually playing bears similarities to the effects of repetitive strain injury.
For the record, Fallout 4 is a very good game, but not because it's innovative or particularly exciting. It's good in so far as six hours will go by and you'll wonder why your backside aches or how Pringles crumbs accumulated so heavily on your winter sweater. There's nothing new to Fallout 4. Indeed, Bethesda's engine feels quite dated, though improvements have been made in the first-person shooter department.
I for one am not bothered by the radial dialogue system. Let's face it: Bethesda's take on the Fallout series has not exactly trended toward Planescape Torment territory. I've always thought the dialogue options were rather basic anyway. The real drawback is the lack of the added threat of a Karma system that punishes or rewards you for your dialogue choices. If you're really bothered by not having a string of text detailing exactly what your character is going to say, download the mod. One does exist.
The game is a pleasure to look at, even if it feels very Bethesda-y. Character models are slightly laughable. I get a kick that NPCs still sleep in their clothes on top of beds. It's a bit of an immersion-breaker, to be honest. Though, maybe sleeping like a wooden stick on a plastic bed is something others do and I'm the odd one out.
Crafting is fun, but ultimately tedious. I like improving armour and weapons, but I resent the manner in which I have to save every bit of junk. They need a 'save all' option when dropping junk off in trunks (etc.) to avoid the tedium of manually clicking EVERY SINGLE ITEM. 'Take all' is there. Given their new take on collecting a bunch of junk, it makes little sense why 'save all' or 'store all' is not.
Anyway, I could go on, but if you've played Fallout 3 or New Vegas, you've played this. If you want to relive those gameplay experiences, go for it. You probably won't be disappointed - until about 30 hours in when you realise that there is more unpredictability in toasting a piece of bread than wandering around the wasteland.

Fallout 4 is perfectly ok for a Fallout game.
It should be much more. "Perfectly ok" is not something we deserve after Fallout 2, and although Fallout 4 is a significant improvement over Fallout 3, it is still very much of the same what was introduced in Fallout 3 and New Vegas.
The shooting mechanics have gained a much needed improvement, but the user interface is rather poor and and obviously ported from consoles. Not all keyboard settings can even be remapped, something which should not be a thing in anything which has been published for anything else besides a Commodore 64.
I could complain about the character models which are still robotic and barely any better than in Fallout 3, or about the graphics which I do not think are anything spectacular, but I do not think anyone expected them to be. The story is horrendeously bad, but I doubt anyone expected it to be good - Bethesda hasnt scraped a single good story together after Morrowind. Fallout 4 is very "Bethesda" - painfully mediocre and riding on our love of the subject matter. The weapon modding, though fun and well made, should have been in Fallout 3. The constructing and interior design introduced in Fallout 4 can be fun, and also painfully annoying as some components can be unrealistically difficult to find.
What I do appreciate in Fallout 4 is the lack of the skill system. I do not like the perk system in Fallout 4 as much as I enjoyed the skill system in Fallout New Vegas, but I can appreciate the courage Bethesda had to change something so fundamental for Fallout.
I am stillf hoping for a fully turn based 3D world fallout game, something we will certainly never receive. Completely turn based system would enable much more options in combat as the players options wouldnt be hindered by time and the limitations of console controls as much. Completely turn based game would also be a much harder sell and not as mainstream, which is not in Bethesdas interests, clearly.
IF you are starving for some Fallout action the game is tolerable, but I would reccommend waiting for some mods which imrpove the user interface.
Maybe not as good as New Vegas, but I'm enjoying it a lot more then Fallout 3.

Generic, dumbed down and repetitive is all I can really say about this game.
The removal of the skills and perks system to replace it with a hybrid is frustrating, it comes across as a cheap way to artifically lengthen the game because you are going to be constantly looking for ways to get as much XP as you can to get that single perk point to spend towards obtaining what would rightfully of been classed as a skill, or a perk, in the previous installments of the franchise, from Fallout 1 to New Vegas.
But then, are you going to buy that skill, that perk, or are you going to spend that valuable point on your stats? Which means you have to trawl more dungeons, dig through every part of the wasteland, customize your skills to be the most beneficial to gaining experience points so you can get what you actually want. Not that the game doesn't have enough exploitable bugs to turn you into a demi-god in less time than it takes to get through the prologue, and that's without touching the command console.
The settlement management is also horrific. After you spend about half an hour scouring every pixel of the settlement limits to clear up all of the junk, you are still left with a good sized chunk of the build limit that you can't use because of structures that are frequently unable to be re-purposed or replacedwhere you then have to try make the best settlement possible with what you can, heavily fortified with turrets as guard posts are of very little use, and the traps being extremely situational as well as reliant on a power source that can easily be damaged, rendering them useless. Yet even if you create a defence network for your settlement that could slaughter an entire present day military in all its glory, you are still going to have to travel to every settlement that is under attack to finish the job yourself before its counted as defended.
Do you want to achieve maximum happiness in your settlement? Don't go far then, as frequently it will come up that the entire settlement has lost water, food and power when you check up on them with your Pipboy, the happiness plummeting as a consequence till you fast travel there to see that absolutely nothing is wrong at all. After spending well over an hour catering to every single possible one of my settlements needed, from more food, water and beds than a small present day town could ever use, with dozens of varied stores, and enough turrets to get the American military hot and bothered, managed to get the settlement up to 95% happiness. I then went off and spent about an hour on questing to progress in the game, for the happiness to nosedive down to 61%.
Of all the NPC's in the game, including the recruitable ones, the only ones with any real flavour and character to them are Codsworth, a Mr. Handy thats humorous to start off with yet quickly becomes tedious and annoying, and Nick Valentine, a synth thats a throwback tribute to the old noir style detective stories. Everyone else just comes across as a bland stereotype without any depth to their character. The fact that companions are immortal as they never die, they just sit on the floor waiting for a stimpak, and possessing infinite ammo for their default weapon also takes a lot away from the game, you can just provoke combat, let your NPC run in to take care of the situation then follow after them to give them a stimpak when they go down, to rinse and repeat.
Now while you dont have to abuse that system to make the game even easier, the fact that it can be done so easily detracts heavily from the overall gameplay.
The central point to the story though, is that your child has been abducted, so as a parent, you are forging out into the wasteland in a quest to get your son back and punish his kidnappers. This very rapidly becomes pushed to the wayside and can be easily forgotten about as it has very little bearing on the majority of the game, you're parent driven to rescue their child at all costs gets distracted from this easier than the dog from Up when squirrels are concerned.
Many of the side quests are also quite repetitive, following the same formula as each other with minor tweaks, with many enviroments just coming across as lazily recycled locations.
Much of the game feels like its going to be left to modders to fix and improve, not including what they cram into the most likely, many DLC packs, which says a lot when we all know just how well established a developer Bethesda is, with the resources they have to throw into development. Its lacklustre and uninspired trading on a brand name, its comparable to Apple even, it isn't Fallout 4, its Fallout 3S.

Please note: just because 20% of people like it dosen't mean it is bad, it just means they yell very loudly.
Personally, I have very little complaints, and the ones I do hear have no real merit to them. My complaints are very minor and will be fixed with mods soon enough: settlement limits (already has a fix), more power armor variants/asthetics, ammo crafting (already a mod) and things like that. As a vanilla game, however, it is really good and has surprised me many times. The AI has vastly improved - deathclaws and the like will zigzag, human enemies will take cover and make tactical retreats, robots are just reckless and will charge head first at you.
I've played the entire series, and actually really enjoyed the old games - this if anything gives the old games justice compared to Fallout 3 and New Vegas. Power Armor actually feels the way it was meant to be, making the wearer a juggernaut compared to those not within it, which was how I felt it was in Fallout 1. I'm not understanding the arguement of "It's not Fallout". It has everything to qualify as a "Fallout" game besides baseless argueing from people who don't like change.
This brings me to the changes. First I will admit, the Dialogue wheel is a bit dissapointing sometimes, I would like to see more varied dialouge and see what I'm actually saying. But it does it's job, theres still plenty if dialogue when you ask questions and makes it pretty clear when you're making an important choice, which is actually a nice benefit.
I'm hearing a lot about "Forced Backstory" and that makes me chuckle. Every Fallout game has had a "Forced Backstory" if you've played the series at all. Fallout 1 you are a vault dweller sent out to get water to your Vault, there was a damned time limit if you ignored that story. Fallout 2 you were a freakin tribal whose tribe worshiped the Fallout 1 player character. Fallout 3 is literally the reverse of Fallout 4. Even New Vegas had a lot of forced backstory if you paid attention, especially in the DLC.
The gunplay is beautiful, if you complain that it's too much like "Call of Duty" now and not an RPG, well I'm sorry you don't enjoy improved gameplay mechanics and you probably would also complain if someone offered you free food, so that's a moot point. It's an improvement, plain and simple - there's no step back here. The crafting is also very well done and for once in an RPG, the value of items to currency actually seems to make sense.
With every Bethesda game, there's a few bugs - but to be honest I was expecting way more. I encounter the weapon swap glitch rarely and that's about the only gameplay affecting one.
Overall, it's fun. Complaining about this game is like slamming your head into a padded wall and complaining that it dosen't hurt.

For those familiar with the Fallout franchise, the baseline hasn't changed much.   This is still very much, post apocalyptic America and it still has all the horrible nasties and intriguing locations ripe for you to find.   This particular installment had quite a bit of divide between folk on whether or not it is any good.  I will try to lay it out as best I can without rambling.
First off.   The Graphics.   For a computer that runs a i5 2500k with a Nvidia 760 GTX with 8gig RAM, the game saw it fit to run at High settings.  Even at High settings, the game looks crisp and never washed out.   The grey-brownscaling shouldn't be a complaint since this is, after all, a wasteland.  Not many colors to behold save for how many colors you can find on the insides of your foes.   The contrast of colors depending on the time of day is beautiful and there is even fog at times.  And no I'm not talking N64 era fog.  Weapon effects and explosions are very nice, though it's a bit disheartening to see that the mini-nukes do not seem to follow a random pattern that I can see.  The bigger the explosions the more effect they have around you.  The screen will actually 'white out' with some of them.  I actually am pleased with the graphics, although you can tell there is a difference between the pre-rendered FMV.  But the Pre-Rendered movie at the beginning did not bother me so much since I'm used to PSX era FMVs sometimes being longer than some of the gameplay segments.
Next up,  Sound.   The sounds this time around are crisper and feel cleaner to listen to compared to Fallout 3 and New Vegas.  The way the weapons sound are very satisfying and feel like they genuinely have some power to them.   Explosions are also satisfying.  The ingame music can be a hit and miss at times but generally fit the mood.  Something about the music in Sanctuary doesn't flow right with me.  I suppose I've been listening to the Radio too much.
Controls here.   Many seem to complain about the handling of the character feeling like they were on Ice-Skates.   I do not seem to have this issue.  Fluid and very responsive.  Though the rework of Melee seems to take some time to get used to, though, more on that in Mechanics.   I don't have any complaints.  Agreeable and smooth.
Game Mechanics.   Here we go.  I'll be honest.  I was very skeptical of plenty things.  The Power Armor, the looting, the towns, weapon and armor crafting.   But suffice to say, I was pleasantly surprised with how well everything seemed to fall together.   Although my only complaint with the settlement point, is assigning settlers to specific tasks such as harvesting or guarding.   But those should only be a one-time thing.  The Power Armor feels like you're actually in power armor this time around.   Walking tank.  Destructor of faces and it's nice to know it has a limit on it now.   If you use it a lot you'll be needing to know when you should think about the Core.  The weapon and armor modification is a pleasing get-away from just searching for something with higher DT.  A very nice detraction from the usual, although the amount of compatible clothing that can be layered is disappointing.  The weapon crafting really doesn't begin to open up for you until you get to Rank 2  in the perspective talents.  But it seems to be quite the treat to play with so far.
And here is the portion that everyone was disappointed about.  The speech being dumbed down.  While yes, it's out of place and dumbed down, I feel that ultimately it doesn't detract too much from the core gameplay.   I am still sore but that hasn't stopped me from taking it out on raider scum.
The biggest change however is one that I'm still having to get used to but I have no quarrel with.   The Overhaul of SPECIAL and Perks.   This is a hard subject to explain for me since I've yet to discover anything that's helped or ruined the game for me.  It seems set up so that you will gradually get what you need when you absolutely need it if you set yourself towards it.  Given that there's no level cap, a perfect character is definitely possible.
Fun Factor.   My personal enjoyment on the game is evident with how many hours I've put into it from time of purchase.  I work Overnight/Graveyard shift and this leaves me with very little time to myself.   That said, I find myself sucked in and I can't help it.   I really enjoy it, often I find myself either shouting at enemies or quietly whispering to myself as I'm going through the wasteland.  I haven't even started much of the main questline but I'm eating this up all the same.  I say it's a fun game.
Overall?  I'd say this is a definite purchase if you're willing to overlook the heavy detractions of the changes in SPECIAL and Speech.  There's enough there in the game itself to keep you busy for a while.  I never try to rush through and I find myself fiddling with things longer than I should.  But...That is only part of what defines a decent game doesn't it?

I originally posted a glowing review of this game, and I think that was still in the "honeymoon" phase of release, when I was convinced this was the best game ever.  But now that I've REALLY put time into it, I think I'm ready for a real review.
I LOVE Fallout.  Ever since I pulled Fallout 3 off the shelf in January 2009 and booted it up for th first time I loved it.  Since then I have put a huge amount of time and energy (and money) into the franchise.  I own all the games, I own the Pip-boy edition of Fallout 4, I own a vault-tec T-shirt, and a Vault-tec sweatshirt, among the countless art pieces and backgrounds I have used as screensavers and desktop backgrounds (and even phone backgrounds).
However, Fallout 4 disappoints me in a way that really...depresses me.  I have been waiting for a new Fallout game since 2010, so when it finally got confirmed, I was over the moon.  I watched EVERY little piece of gameplay I could, read every article, saw every interview and little bit of speculation until FINALLY, the game came out.  The day it came out, I installed it and quickly rushed up to a buddy of mine's room in our dorm.  We played from 10 AM to 10 PM, stopping only for food and the bathroom.  It was incredible.  I couldn't get enough.  I probably hit 50 hours in this game faster than any other game I played, and probably hit 100 and 150 faster than any game I ever played.
But now that the game isn't brand new, I see it more for what it is.  It's not a BAD game...but it's not particularly good, and it's definitely not a good FALLOUT game.
I think a few things contribute to that.
1. The atmosphere: One of the best parts about Fallout is how the game doesn't take anything to seriously.  Much like Robocop, it satirizes American culture and has a humor that is blacker than soot.  So many witty jokes and twisted circumstances that really engross you.  However, Fallout 4 doesn't really have any of that.  There is some really hamfisted diologue which tries to point the finger at American life, but it doesn't come across as ironic or sarcastic, but like they are actually trying to say something deep and meaningful...which seems...bland.
2. The story, quests and characters:  This is probably the part where most people know what's coming: "another settlement is under attack, I'll mark it on your map."  Remember how people criticized Skyrim for having dumbed-down missions, because many of them revolve around going somewhere and killing draugr?  This is the same thing, but worse, because you literally can't avoid them.  The moment you're within earshot of Preston (or even some settlers) you get the stupid quest thrust onto you.  Involving the story, I don't mind the whole "baby kidnapped" thing, that can be good, but I do have to say one thing: who didn't see the twist coming? I mean seriously, thats a plot in most things involving cryo freezing.
Now I get into the main meat of this, the characters and diologue:  This was a massive falling of the game.  The Mass Effect style of diologue is a stupid idea, and it INFURIATES ME that they decided to go with it.  Not only are you limited to 4 options (In previous games you had so many different ways of doing things) but they all lead the same way, no matter what you say involving quests, it still ends the same damn way.  Also voiced protagonists really messes with the idea of "make your character your way" because my character will always sound like some guy who's kid is missing and is out of place, no matter what he looks like, how he acts, and what he does.  Thats why the very first mod I installed got rid of the voiced protagonists.  Speaking of no options with diologue, what the hell happened to skill checks and stuff like that?  I think I can count the number of "skill checks" in the game (that aren't involved in asking for more money) on one hand.
3. The overall "streamlining" of the game:  This means how they removed skills, and how they removed weapon conditions and stuff like that.  No longer do you have to add skills to stuff to make your character good at stuff.  There is no point.  You can probably beat the game, on survival difficulty, with 1 point in all of your SPECIAL areas, and no perks...and probably pretty easily too.  In Fallout 3 if your character had bad small guns skill, expect to miss like crazy, and do barely any damage at all.  If you had bad speech, expect to♥♥♥♥♥♥people off and never get your way.  Regarding weapon conditions, I know not everyone liked this, but to me it made sense.  These items are either 200 years old, or are made from scrapmetal by random settlers and survivors, of course they aren't going to be shiny and new.  I liked that if you didn't take care of your weapons, they'd jam and do less damage, and eventually be unusable, it kept you from just using the same weapon or armor all the time without ever changing.
and finally #4, probably my biggest reason: REPLACING STUFF WITH CRAFTING INSTEAD OF ADDING TO IT WITH CRAFTING.  Let me ask you a question:  How many MAJOR settlements (not dinky 2 person farms) can you name in Fallout 4? and how many in New Vegas? and how many in Fallout 3?  Without doing ANYTHING faction related except the opening missions, Fallout 4 has Diamond City, Sanctuary, Goodneighbor, Covenant, Vault 81 and Bunker Hill...so thats 6 towns/settlements.  The rest are nothing but little family farms that don't do anything until you build them up.  Fallout 4 added crafting and settlement building...but they added them as a replacement to having actual settlements and items.  This means that instead of having all the towns and settlements in Fallout 3 where every NPC had a name and a purpose in town, you now have a settlement filled with 30 people named...settler...and they all did pretty much nothing.  You made them farm, or patrol, or sell♥♥♥♥♥♥ but they never did anything, and never had a personality.  So instead of having towns like Megaton, Arefu, The Republic of Dave, Underworld, The Citadel, Big town, Little Lamplight, Andale, Oasis, Paradise Falls, Rivet City, Tenpenny Tower and even Girdershade (thats 13 right there, and I doubt that's it) you've got 6 real settlements, and countless basically unnamed ones that you need to make yourself, to fill with nameless NPCs with no backstory.
In the end, this game kind of ends up being a faceless, soulless version of Fallout.  No interesting characters, no interesting places, and barely the heart that made Fallout Fallout...
I found myself practically dragging myself to continue playing, forcing myself under the guise of "its Fallout, I must like it, I'm just not getting into it, but I know I have to like it"
but in the end, I just can't like this game...I find myself starting it up, playing for 10 minutes and going "eh" and leaving again.  I play it again for 2 days every time a new expansion comes out, and drop it again the moment the DLC is done...

Nonstop exploration in a vast open world with many many buildings that have hidden secrets inside.
I'm nearly 90 hours into this game and there is still so much more for me to explore and discover.
Story:
I was pretty much excited with how the story was in the beginning, it was exciting and made me curious, yet I wasn't very captivated to do them right away. I just wanted to explore every bit of this apocalyptic world and didn't care much for the story. It's a good story, but there it's no where as near satisfying as exploring the game - 7.5/10
Gameplay:
Where do I start? Fallout 4 has really solid gunplay and overall the combat system is just well refined. The combat just never feels boring and you could always spice it up by trying out a gun that you've never used or a melee weapon that has a unique stat. I found this baseball bat that has a chance of sending enemies flying in the air when you hit them and as you do that, you'll hear a croud cheering for you because you gave that mother f'ing ghoul a homerun. How majestic can this game get? Besides combat, it feels really nice both in first and third person, I switch alot between the two (indoors/outdoors), and it's also a way for me not to get bored with only one type of playstyle.
The dialogue system is something that does irritate me because you never know what your character might blurt out, but thankfully, modders have already implemented a mod that shows you the whole dialogue options instead of the small versions of them (Yes, No, Sarcastic).   -  9.5/10
Audio:
The music score in this game is just amazing. Inon Zur, the composer that made this score is just an absolute genius and truly makes Fallout 4 feel very real and immersive thanks to his beautiful music. I've tried listening to the radios and while they could be fun, they just aren't as intense and immersive as the games music score. Sounds from the weapons, either melee, ballistic, or energy are just awesome and very satisfying. The voices in this game are good. The voice actors aren't the best, but they certainly do make the game feel alive. My favorite voice so far is Codsworth, he's one hell of a companion as well just because the things he says are ridiculous.  -  9/10
Graphics:
This is a big deal and probably one of the most talked about thing when you bring up Fallout 4. Yes, the game doesn't have the best graphics, and certainly it is no match when compared to the other AAA releases in this year. However, that does not mean Fallout 4 is a bad looking game. It is a very beautiful world when you forget about all the other games and appreciate it for the sake of its style, the post apocalyptic setting. I've never had an issue where I felt that the game could honestly look better, infact, I just walk around the game and tell myself how pretty this game is. If you're holding out because of this issue, don't. This game is infact very beautiful and has a very distinctive art style from other games, which I believe should be appreciated.   -  8.5/10
Performance:
It's Bethesda.
I know that's no excuse for any game but you'll have to make an exception for these guys. Their games run like♥♥♥♥♥♥and have a LOT of bugs, but man do they make awesome games. I've had a very little amount of bugs into my game, I guess I'm one of the lucky ones. I did play the game with all ULTRA settings except Shadow Distance at MEDIUM. The game runs very smoothly and apart from the jittery movements every once in a while, it doesn't have many problems. Some areas are bound to have some frame drops, but it should hold up fine and stable most of the time.   -  7/10

Die-hard fallout fan here, never played F1 or 2 (I need to though), but i've put a ♥♥♥♥-ton of hours into 3 and NV, as well as Oblivion and Skyrim, so i'm generally a big Fallout fan and a Bethesda fan in general. They have their flaws, but if I didn't like them I wouldn't play their games.
After about 70 hours I think this game is probably to F3 and FNV what Skyrim was to Oblivion.
Huge upgrade in certain areas, massive downgrade in others.
Pros:
- Great story, probably the best of any Bethesda game i've played so far (haven't played Morrowind but everyone says that game's storyline was really good), wasn't expecting it to be very good (bethesda games don't normally do) but this game's story gives New Vegas a run for it's money, and that's saying something.
- Story has alot of morally grey areas, four different endings and choosable factions you can side with/against.
- Combat is the best it's ever been, i've also been using VATS more, which I barely ever did in previous games.
- The settlement system is amazing, really well detailed and I love it.
- Companions are excellent, might actually give New Vegas another run for it's money, which is again saying something. Piper, Curie and Nick are my favourites btw, also Nick is voiced by Stephen Russell (Garret from Thief). I also liked seeing Macready again.
- Mother♥♥♥♥ing useable vertibirds, oh my god yes, they have no practical ♥♥♥♥ing usage whatsoever but they're SOOOO FUN.
- The Constitution quest, oh ♥♥♥♥ing go there it is one of the best in the game. Without any spoilers, word of advice, join the robots, don't side with the scavengers side with the robots. You'll know what I mean when you get to that point.
- Feral Ghouls and Deathclaws are legitimately terrifying.
- Power Armor FEELS LIKE POWERED INFANTRY ARMOR. You just stomp around inside it and it feels amazing.
- Relatively few bugs on launch (by Bethesda standards anyways).
- The art style, I can't really articulate why but it feels much more like "Fallout" than 3 did, everything has this very "50's" look to it and I love it.
- Settlement building, I love it.
- Far Harbor, absoloutely AMAZING, it's everything this game should have been.
- The Brotherhood's arrival in the Prydwen. Just. Wow.
Cons:
- STREAMLINING
- The new leveling system, it's arguable whether it's even a ♥♥♥♥ing RPG anymore, where are my ♥♥♥♥ing skills Beth? wtf is this? Also I have no desire to go back and play through the game again with a different SPECIAL configuration. You can start out somewhat specialized, but then by late-game you're just amazing at everything. At level 80, my sole survivor "Shauna" has gone from a ♥♥♥♥ing lawyer to a lockpicking, hacking, settlement-building, minutemen army commanding extremely charismatic brotherhood/railroad/institute triple-agent masterfully manipulating all 3 of them for her own gain, and for the gain of the minutemen.
- Console port, you can tell from a mile away this game was made for ♥♥♥♥ing consoles first, I particularly hate the ridiculously small build limit on settlements (it's easily fixed with mods but i'm still holding them accountable for it). The new dialogue wheel makes no ♥♥♥♥ing sense on a mouse and keyboard, and speaking of that...
- The new dialogue system, oh god, no, there's waaaaaay too much to cover here, but basically they ♥♥♥♥ed everything up here, i'll try and summarise it, why do we only have four options at a time? Where are my ♥♥♥♥ing speech checks, seriously the speech checks suck in this, they can all be pretty much summed up as "gimme moar money", they're very basic, and skill/SPECIAL/Perk speech checks are gone, remember that guy in F3 who tried to mug you? and how you could tell him the gun's not loaded if you had high perception? A fairly fun FPS game with a bit of story brought to you by the most lazy developers I've seen. While Ubisoft might make up lies about low FPS being better these guys don't even seem to have a lie about why an old crap engine is still being used or why it runs like garbage on rather good rigs.
From weird minor bugs to game crippling ones it's a pretty ugly game that feels very bethesda as you play. The Settlement system is a horrible joke and is about as deep as anything else bethesda has done, which is to say it's not deep at all. If you want to follow a fairly large questline you'll be stuck babysitting a bunch of helpless drones that refuse to join your larger encampments. In the end if you team up with a certain faction you'll even be asked to take food from some of your settlements as an optional task. All that is wrapped up in the most lazy attempt at a modular building system I've ever seen (I can't think of an indie title that has done worse, DayZ mods did better).
Often there feels to be no choice regardless of what you say when it comes to quests. You might not really get more or less options to choose from than in previous games but you get less impact for sure. From the intro to the end of the game I was nothing but sarcastic and a complete jerk to everybody and still ended up joining factions, running missions and being hailed by the NPCs as the most impressive person alive. I took every chance given to me to try and be an evil monster and still turned out to be neutral "maybe" in the end.
For the stupidly high profit they'll no doubt make off this game it feels like they put in the least amount of effort and will make the most amount of gains possible. While the game isn't unplayable it feels like you're playing an unfinished game if you do ANYTHING other than roam around gunning things down enjoying the FPS element.

There comes a time in every Bethesda game (or perhaps open-world games in general) when the game is 'broken'. I don't mean in terms of bugs or gameplay hindrances (though those do exist), but rather the fact that adventuring and discovery become rote and uninteresting. As a gamer, you have totally 'figured out' the game and the process of actually playing bears similarities to the effects of repetitive strain injury.
For the record, Fallout 4 is a very good game, but not because it's innovative or particularly exciting. It's good in so far as six hours will go by and you'll wonder why your backside aches or how Pringles crumbs accumulated so heavily on your winter sweater. There's nothing new to Fallout 4. Indeed, Bethesda's engine feels quite dated, though improvements have been made in the first-person shooter department.
I for one am not bothered by the radial dialogue system. Let's face it: Bethesda's take on the Fallout series has not exactly trended toward Planescape Torment territory. I've always thought the dialogue options were rather basic anyway. The real drawback is the lack of the added threat of a Karma system that punishes or rewards you for your dialogue choices. If you're really bothered by not having a string of text detailing exactly what your character is going to say, download the mod. One does exist.
The game is a pleasure to look at, even if it feels very Bethesda-y. Character models are slightly laughable. I get a kick that NPCs still sleep in their clothes on top of beds. It's a bit of an immersion-breaker, to be honest. Though, maybe sleeping like a wooden stick on a plastic bed is something others do and I'm the odd one out.
Crafting is fun, but ultimately tedious. I like improving armour and weapons, but I resent the manner in which I have to save every bit of junk. They need a 'save all' option when dropping junk off in trunks (etc.) to avoid the tedium of manually clicking EVERY SINGLE ITEM. 'Take all' is there. Given their new take on collecting a bunch of junk, it makes little sense why 'save all' or 'store all' is not.
Anyway, I could go on, but if you've played Fallout 3 or New Vegas, you've played this. If you want to relive those gameplay experiences, go for it. You probably won't be disappointed - until about 30 hours in when you realise that there is more unpredictability in toasting a piece of bread than wandering around the wasteland.

I've always thought the dialogue options were rather basic anyway. The real drawback is the lack of the added threat of a Karma system that punishes or rewards you for your dialogue choices. If you're really bothered by not having a string of text detailing exactly what your character is going to say, download the mod. One does exist.
The game is a pleasure to look at, even if it feels very Bethesda-y. Character models are slightly laughable. I get a kick that NPCs still sleep in their clothes on top of beds. It's a bit of an immersion-breaker, to be honest. Though, maybe sleeping like a wooden stick on a plastic bed is something others do and I'm the odd one out.
Crafting is fun, but ultimately tedious. I like improving armour and weapons, but I resent the manner in which I have to save every bit of junk. They need a 'save all' option when dropping junk off in trunks (etc.) to avoid the tedium of manually clicking EVERY SINGLE ITEM. 'Take all' is there. Given their new take on collecting a bunch of junk, it makes little sense why 'save all' or 'store all' is not.
Anyway, I could go on, but if you've played Fallout 3 or New Vegas, you've played this. If you want to relive those gameplay experiences, go for it. You probably won't be disappointed - until about 30 hours in when you realise that there is more unpredictability in toasting a piece of bread than wandering around the wasteland.

Same ol' day-waster, this time with more crafting, improved game engine, and repeatable missions. Really, aside from the story, which I'll try to avoid spoiling any of, it's not far from the previous titles.
Where does it improves:
-Dynamic conversations you can leave any time, although can be rudely interrupted now.
-Repair is all but gone aside from damaged settlement stuff and power armor.
-Charisma and Luck now have some important uses.
-Third dimension is more explorable and visually pleasing.
-Environment has fewer must-go-into-seperate-instance-for-every-mission, lots of the game (most ruins) are entirely in the main world. Fewer loading screens is always good.
-Player has a voice, as opposed to silent text.
-Older titles seemed to have only two AI for combat (melee run at you, ranged take cover and fire), whereas there's unique combat for most enemies (bloodbugs disable you, deathclaws dodge automatic weapons, feral ghouls bodyslam you and fall down, etc)
-Character models are much improved, big step up from the Oblivionesque F03 + FO:NV.
-Perks aren't Oblivionesque anymore either, no more 100 levels for each skill. Single point system that levels up a primary stat or a skill that falls under one.
Where it's the same:
-Gameplay is true to FO3 + FO:NV, VATS and normal combat are very stable, and rewarding.
-People have been saying there's too much go-there;do-that, but that's been consistantly the model for gameplay in the Fallout series. The only thing they've really changed in missions is that most of the escort NPCs can't die, making it a little less frustrating.
-Most aren't gamebreaking, but some people have gotten a few bugs that totally halt progress. You're going to have at least one where you have to load a previous save or google a solution.
All in all, the game is tremendously better than previous Fallout titles, and while it falls short of Skyrim in terms of explorable area, it's gameplay was much more enjoyable. However, here are my few remaining gripes:
While the game does reward you for time spent building settlements, and can be a nice distraction from the normal roaming grind, it's a pain in the♥♥♥♥♥for the most part. You can always ignore the Minuteman quests, so I guess it's kind of a mute point, but everytime I imagine running a second character and restoring those 20 settlements AGAIN... it pretty much guarantees I'm rolling the biggest ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and ignoring the Minutemen. Maybe if the prefabricated buildings were more practical, and building up a base (assuming you have collected enough resources already) took 5 minutes, multiple 'good' characters would be more viable.
And WOW, Bethesda did not learn their lesson with endings in this series at all. FO3 it was acceptable that you'd have a lack of choices, because they were just starting to get the hang of Fallout as an FPS. New Vegas had a step up, where you could include or exclude factions, and craft somewhat of a custom main story ending. But in FO4...
------(HORRIBLE, TREMENDOUS SPOILERS AHEAD)(HORRIBLE, TREMENDOUS SPOILERS AHEAD)------

B. Support the synth-sympathetic Railroad. Don't get any perks. Destroy Brotherhood and Institute.

Remember how devastated the Commonwealth is and how much tech from the Institute could help grow food and make medicine? Think maybe you could take it over as opposed to destroying it? Too bad.

Cons
-Graphics are either great or horrible looking creating an inconsistent feel.

-One companion at a time felt oddly limiting and wasted a good chance to have interactions
-Could have used a bit more choice in the way things played out
-Needs a much better settlement UI for assigning settlers
-For me personally it felt a little to easy, so much so I avoided using vats even on Survival.
Personal Experience: I had a blast with FO4 and managed to net every ach / explore nearly every major location / reach the mid 90s without getting burned out. It was a great experience and although perhaps not as memorable or engaging as the Witcher 3 it was still worth every penny I spent on it.
Final Thoughts: This is a very solid entry in the Fallout franchise and is a huge step up from Fallout 3 in most regards.

Fallout 4 is a fantastic game... if you're already a Fallout fan. Let me qualify this by saying that Fallout 3 is my favorite game of all time and I've probably put 30-40 days of playing time between PC and console. Having said that, Fallout 4 feels basically the same. There are a few changes to the gameplay mechanics--VATS now slows time way down instead of stopping it, weapon and armor condition are gone, most weapons and armors can be modded--but ultimately there isn't much improvement over Fallout 3. That's not to say it's a bad game, as it certainly isn't lacking anything Fallout 3 had, but it's more of the same in a different packaging. It's a Bethesda game, so you've still got your tedious fetch quests and your buggy gameplay mechanics in a top notch, holy-crap-this-is-awesome open world map.
As someone who adores the Fallout universe, though, I'm thoroughly enjoying this game. Ignoring the obvious gaping flaws, it's genuinely a lot of fun to spend my time collecting sweet rolls and making people explode. The map is massive and much more diverse than the Capital Wasteland. The trademark Fallout wit is still there, as well. Basically, Fallout 4 has all of the things that you loved about Fallout 3, but more of it. Play this game if you're a Bethesda/Fallout fan, stay away if you're expecting anything beyond glitchy fetch quests and/or you like remembering to eat.
All in all, 7/10 as an objective critic, 9.5/10 as a sweet roll enthusiast.
Side note (And kinda sorta spoilers):
The minutemen settlement quests go on forever, so if you have OCD and you like to keep your quests clear, do not continue to take them. I spent two straight days refusing to eat and turning down sex before I googled it and realized they weren't going to end. Ever. What's a Fallout game without a borderline unhealthy dose of masochism?

After having spent aprox. 90 hours on the game (as of this time when I'm writing this review) and having completed the main quest + a♥♥♥♥♥♥ton of side quests and exploration, I can fairly give my honest opinion and review of the game. I will not spoil the story or anything (Small spoilers will be writen with black spoiler code) in this review, but I will be talking about the new game mechanics, and how they work or don't work. So let's just get to it.
Fallout 4 starts with you being in the year 2077, right before nuclear war ends the entire world. This is basically the prologue where you create your character, pick a name and choose your S.P.E.C.I.A.L. stats. You choose either to be the husband or the wife of a family with a son, whose name is Shaun. It's more or less a cinematic introduction, as you don't really do much other than walk around and look at stuff while your character talks. Then certain events happen, and you're forced to take shelter in an underground vault with your family. SPOILER!
Let's start with the most important part for most people, and that is gameplay. In Fallout 4 the gameplay is epic! It's a really huge upgrade from previous titles in the series, and combat is better than ever. Shooting feels great, the guns have actual recoil and the sounds are awesome. You can also finally sprint using your AP, and there is now also a grenade key. You can power bash with any weapon, and VATS has been redone and now slows down time instead of stopping it completely. You can now also tag multiple quests at a time, as opposed to only one at a time in previous Fallout games. Almost every perk in the game can now be upgraded with several ranks, and skill points have been completely removed. There is a much bigger focus on your S.P.E.C.I.A.L. stats this time, which I think is a step in the right direction. Weapons also have full stats now and they can all be modded, both standard, legendary and unique, with a big selection of several mods to choose from. Everything from scopes, muzzles, barrels to ammo clips and much more. This of course has an effect on your weapon and it's not just cosmetic. Armor can also be upgraded now (though only the layered armor pieces and a few selected outfits) and they can be improved with not only giving more dmg resistance, but also things like more carry weight, faster movement speed, bigger hit chance in VATS and so forth. The same goes with your power armor, which is now also divided up into several pieces. The new character creater, where you simply sculp your character's face, can be tricky to use effectively, but can yield wonderful results. The added facial features are great, but I still think there's a lack of hairstyles to choose from. Your bodyweight can be modified as well. The map size is much smaller than expected though. It's about the same size as Fallout 3's map. The game also has a surprisingly low amount of bugs and crashes, compared to previous Bethesda titles. But on pretty much every aspect of gameplay, Fallout 4 is an improvement over previous titles and it definitely deserves credit for that.
I have mixed feelings about the graphics. While they are an improvement over previous titles, they don't really stand up to today's standards in graphics. Textures looks blurry up close, character animations are still clunky, lip synching, for when the NPC's or the player character talks, is still not very good and sometimes it goes out of synch. Lighting looks REALLY good in the game, thanks to the addition of their fully dynamic volumetric lighting, also known as "godrays" which adds atmospheric depth to the game. Unfortunately, it uses a lot of GPU power and will result in FPS loss most of the time, if you don't have a really strong graphics card. I had to turn godrays down to low instead of high, as my Nvidia GTX 970 couldn't even pull out a decent fps with this option on. I gained like 10-20 fps in areas with a lot going on just by turning it down to low. The fps loss is not worth the good-looking lighting. Also the new weather effects is a bit dull. The rain is really weak and dosen't really give the sense of it actually raining. It's more like it's "dripping" a bit. The radiation storms, which sounds like a cool concept, are poorly executed. They don't really add much danger other than giving you 5 Rads every now and then and a constant +1 Rad, while turning the sky green and adding some heavy wind sounds. A more hurricane like feeling and a higher radiation pr. second would have given this weather effect more depth.
With the addition of your character having a voice, the roleplaying element of the game has been severely reduced. The character's voice makes it hard to seriously roleplay as any specific kind of character other than the "concerned parent". Anyone who wants to roleplay as a ♥♥♥♥ed up evil psychopathic killer will be disappointed. The new dialogue wheel makes it difficult to go in a specific direction with your character when you interact with NPC's. The game has become more Mass Effect-ish in its roleplaying (you can also romance companions now), limiting player freedom. Sure you can still do whatever you want and kill whomever you want, but your actions are less believeable and rewarding, in terms of roleplaying, as it was in previous Fallout titles. Also on a side note, you can no longer see your holstered weapon in 3rd person, which completely destroys some of the immersion. The karma system is also gone and that's a matter of taste really, but I personally think it's a good thing that it's gone. Choices are no longer black & white, and there are very good reasons to do specific things in the game. There is no longer a good and evil. It all depends on your and the NPC's point of view. Some might like what you do, while others might dislike it. It depends on the situation, the context and the people involved. Companions now respond to your actions, either liking or disliking you more because of it. It makes it more realistic and adds more depth to the overall experience.
This feature doesn't quite live up to its expectations. There is basically no tutorial given as to how different things work, and you'll often find yourself frustrated when building something or trying to get something to work. Took me hours to figure out how to get electricity. The system is also clunky and lacks a few features, such as more decorations or smaller misc items. Also, running brahmin caravans between your settlements doesn't really add anything to the overall experince and feels like a complete waste. Settlers that you either recruit or show up to your settlements, often bug out and doesn't do what they're told. Sometimes they'll even spawn on the roofs when you fast travel back to your base and they won't come down. There is also a limit as to how much you can build in your settlement and how many settlers you can have.
- Is Fallout 4 worth getting? Yes.
- Is it worth getting if you're hoping for it to be exactly like the previous fallout games? No.
Fallout 4 draws heavy inspiration from games such as Bioshock, Mass Effect and even Dead Island when it comes to game mechanics and story/dialogue. It's clear that Fallout 4 is more of a heavy story driven game, with more focus on gameplay rather than roleplaying. Future mods may fix the game's mistakes, but only time will tell. In my opinion, Fallout 4 is still an outstanding game, but it lacks all the little things that made the previous games so memorable.

Fallout 4 is the most dissapoining game of 2015.
There are few improvments :
- FPS mechancis are better, but still i can not call them good because we can't do such simple and essential things like leaning or go prone
- Enemy AI is a little bit better, still melee enemies will charge in your face, other then hide in a cover and waiting for you to come closer
- Weapon and armor crafting is a nice addition
- New Power Armor mechanics
And it is pretty much concludes my list of things i liked, Fallout 4 features that i did not liked:
- Boring and predictable main story, which does not envoke absolutely no empathy from the player, one would think that after The Last of Us other game developers learned something good, but one would be wrong.
- Terribly written and simplistic dialogues
- Crippled social system, remember how in New Vegas you could use a variety of skills and you SPECIAL score? Heal someone with medic? Intimidate someone with high strange? Notice something with Preception? Every skill was used in dialogues, not only Speech. If you role-playd your character, dialogues were helping you with it.
In Fallout 4 all is gone, the only SPECIAL you will use is Charisma and it's use is as deep, as a puddle after 5 minutes of moderate rain.~
- Unbeliveble game world due to horrendous enviromental design, The Great War happened 210 years ago yet the game world looks like it happened on the previous week. Every human settlement is filled with debris, people's houses often have unbarred/uncovered windows, leaky roofs, some location are even have a human skeletons in them! One example, the Diner near Sanctuary Hills where a lady named Trudy does bissness, behind one of the tables there is a skeleton! It is like that lady moved to that Diner just 5 minutes ago and did not had the time to sort the mess.
I tried to find atleast one human settlement that looked believeble but i failed.
- Disrespect to Fallout's Lore, both Lore establish by Black Isle and even by themselves, the Bethesda : Vertibirds that you saw in the pre war prologues is one of many examples.
- Dumb and boring quests : The absolute majority of quests is boring, in a typical Bethesda way : Go there, kill a few dozens of creatures/people, return back to me for another quest like this. And i am not talking about randomly generated quests! The majority of main story quests are like this as well!
Now to the dumb quests - there are a few of them, but story of a ghoul kid who was trapped in a fridge for...210?! How it is even possible? Ghoulification takes years to develop! How he survived those years in that fridge? How he did not go mad after the 1st week? And there are a few quests like this in the game.
- Not only the quests are dumb and boring - there a very few of them, whe Fallout 4 wiki is far from complete, but i think Skyrim had atleast 10 times quests then Fallout 4!
- Uninteresting "dungeons" : Remeber dungeons in Skyrim? Each of them had some kind of story behind, you could meet friendly NPCs there and explored it together, gain some unique items or even spells by doind so! (flaming familiar for example). Fallout 4 "dungeons" (interior cells) are painfully boring and repetetive, they are no friendly NPC for you to iteract, no puzzles to solve in the absolute majotiry of them, is it a vertical corridor with dozens of repetetive enemies and in the end there is one or two mega enemy type NPC, legendary raider or legendary super mutant! Oh my, so exiting! They probably drop a chest piece which cost almost no money and provide absolutely useless effect! The most exiting thing you will find in 99% of interior cells are fusion cores. Yes you heard me right, finding the battery for your armor is the most fun you will have. Unlike Skyrim, there you could find a new unique dragon words, inique weapon or armor.
- RPG system. It just work! No.It is not. No traits to choose from, no skills, there are only perks now and many of them are useless. The joy of leveling up is greatly reduced now, when the only thing you do is to decided what perk to unlock.
- Very few base weapons, there are a lot of mods, but it does not make up for unique weapon models.
- Very few unique weapons : Unlike New Vegas, there are very few unique weapons in is game, in fact i found only 3 : Broadsider, Alien Blaster, and Shishkebab.
- Boring and generic rnemies : Two words. Legendary Radroach.
- Two dimensional companions, the only two companions i could understand some motivation into following me in danger are : the robot and the dog. The rest of them joins you for no reason and for no reason they suddenly initiate a conversation with you, by talking about things out of the blue. They are terrible written and executed, even New Vegas companions look much more alive then these homunculi created by Bethesda.
- Legendary loot : New loot system is horrible, there are freezeing knives now, nocturnal pipes, junky baseball bats, armor that offers protection against certain types of enemies...it made a little bit sense in the Elder Scrolls game, but not in Fallout.
- Oudated game engine: Gamebryo has to go, i don't care how do you call it's next iteracion, super duper creation engine or whatever, but is has to go.
- Bad graphics : while inside buildings the game does not look that bad, when you come outside...oh boy.
I cried after i climbed on top the Trinity Tower, cried because my eyes were hurting of that terrible LOD distance, those mirky water and landscape textures. In a year where a game like Witcher 3 was released, that level of graphics is unacceptable.
- Terrible UI, it maybe works for consoles (which i doubt), but it won't do for PC.
- Bad optimization and techincal decisions : Locked frame rate, low FOV, the game stutters and drops frame even on a very powerfull PC's. In my Steam library when i launched Fallout 4 about half of the time it stops working. I have to close fallout4.exe process and launch it again, there are many more techincal problems with this game, search for it if you are interested.
All and all, Fallout 4 is an average game at best, and undoubtly the worst Bethesda game since Redguard, how after an exelent game like Skyrim they could made such a monstosity, is beyond me.
If you really want to play it, wait until it drops to half a price, there will be some decent mods by this time already.
In my opinion, Fallout 4 must be compared to three games. It's current rival, the game of the same genre - The WItcher 3. To the previous Fallout game - New Vegas. And to the previous Bethesda game - Skyrim.
And in all of this comparisons Fallout 4 fails miserably. This game just is out of other league, in boxing terminalogy, out of different weight category. While those threee game are heavy-weight boxers, Falloit 4 is a light-weight boxer, and a lousy one at that.
The worst thing about this game however, is that it already made a ton of money. No way now the next Elder Scrolls Game will be much different from Fallout 4, it will be as silly, boring and simplified as Bethesda's recent reimagination of post apocalyptic USA.

I hated the weapon condition system in the other games and they threw out the old leveling system, which I love. I'm glad they added sprinting and the ability to make settlements. The power armor is so much more useful in this game than any of the others although I hadn't found any in the original fallout games and I don't even know if I can. Still, the game is amazing and it was worth the wait.

LONG VERSION
I have to admit that i fell victim to the "overhype" during July 2015 and i've preordered the game.As a result,i've been expecting too much;i'll try to provide my point of view on those introduced new mechanics in order to point out what i didn't/did like.
What i didn't like:
1-New dialogue system
It's primitive and subject to any kind of abuse as you can make a strong save file while into the speech options menù and try all the dialogue options in order to achieve that one that you fancied/your companion fancied the most. Even having a high Charisma stat won't help that much because you'll be encouraged to flip the coin several times until you'll be able to nail that dialogue option you were looking for. Even your counterpart's reactions won't be realistic: being an ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥,a wuss,a british gentleman often won't lead to any remarkable results. Moreover,there aren't quests' endings locked behind some strong speech abilites...and that's a shame!It would have been cool to get a whole new ending for a side quest by just reasoning with people or playing smart...but no.
2-Settlement building
The only thing i don't like it's the fact that it gave me the impression that this feature was literally thrown to us at the last moment; key tutorials are missing even when they're essential. Examples? Do you know that if you deposit all the materials and junk you've found so far into your workbench they'll be automatically recyled? HECK NO,i had to ask a friend for that! Do you know that light bulbs don't need any electric wire to be fully operative?OF COURSE NOT,i had to read 5 pages of building tutorials to know that.Another thing that turned off my interest for this very cool feature was the incompleteness of it: you don't have to use water to get your plants growing,you can't destroy old rubbles to rebuild an entire settlement (YES,Sanctuary Hills will look bad anyway with its rusty houses),you can't build walls with windows' holes inside it,you can't build radio stations or REAL,SIGNIFICATIVE,REALISTIC city improvements.The numerical quantity of things you can create is huge,but the variety of it is insignificant. Building a huge settlement with supply chains will be useful only if you've previously spent 6+ points on trading skills,otherwise...it will just be a cosmetical thing to do to pleasure your eyes.Even making your citizens happy it's a joke;they can even sleep on improvised beds/rooms with no consequences at all,even if bathrooms are absent. Also,raiders won't attack your cities if you place enough sentries to defend your borders,making the survival elements of the game very faded or absent.
3-Bad optimization,bugs,loadings
You'll get constant 60FPS only during enclosed dark areas,deal with it. Framedrops are terribly common,even changing the camera with your mouse/stick will slow your game in a significative way. If you wish to play in the open areas,prepare to fight and run with 30-50 fps that will never be constant. Just to make a good comparison : check a MGS5 gameplay video and one related to Fallout4. There's an ocean between them.Bugs are infinite: you can order to to your companion to carry a mountain on his/her back and they'll obediently do it like docile donkeys; weapons and people will vanish from time to time,double headed cows will climb your roofs like Catwoman and Batman only would do,quest marks won't be often showed or when they do,they'll be put in the wrong place. And...i tip my hat to Bethesda for this one....some good side quests aren't completable. And...imo...let's show the worst thing...those loadings. They're long,common and pointess. We are in 2015: Batman Arkham Night didn't have any sort of loading as well as The Witcher 3,unless you decide to enter another region.Let's imagine that you have to talk with 2 people located in 2 different biudings...WHY THE HELL to do i have to WASTE.and i repeat...W-A-S-T-E 5 minutes just to be able to do my "fourhuehuehuedialogueoptionsFML" dialogue sections?! Enough. Next time,just bring the tow ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s near eachtother,so you don't have to climb a Everest's made of boring loadings and they can shitetalk themselves as much as they want.
4-Awful enemy and gear variety
There are too few types of enemies and gear available,no matter if you have 4 points on blacksmithing,science and armorcrafting. You'll find yourself surrounded by the same enemies over and over again and those enemies,with FEEW exceptions,will try to kill you using the same gear over and over again. This is a post-nuclear world and yet...we don't see any enemy improvements/new mechanics. Now...how cool it would have been while exploring some old abandoned factiories to see some unique or heavily mutated monsters? Nah,how about ghouls,mutants,raiders,roaches,deathclaws,robots,sentries and mirelurks all the time?
5-Loot absence and dull gear improvement
Your loot is replaced by junk. Find junk,recycle junk and make your junk-made weps stronger and more filled with junk. I honestly...got sick of that not because of the concept itself,but because isn't any variety attached to it. I would have enjoyed this feature more only if this randomized junk loot would have been followed by some chest loot filled with good and immediately equippable loot. Even if there any level restriction to the gear you can use...it actually is.You'll often find new gear right after you've unlocked smithing skills,as happened in Skyrim.That's not cool;if i have the freedom to build my stats and perks...why do i have to spend points there at all costs?! The real loot you can actually get are the Vault-Tec bobbleheads,the Comic Books and Magazines,which will grant you a passive cumulative bonus or a new little perk everytime. It would have been MUCH better to add some unique blueprints and schematics to the loot drop,or even some more already 100% granted rare S.P.E.C.I.A.L. magazines,just to boost up a little bit your character progression. The gear improvement is dull,as it will only improve your gear stats in one way most of the time. It would have been much nicer to have some gear improvement that wasn't all the way positive like : "Mmhh...should i get a bigger grip or an enchaced reload speed,knowing that one will exclude the other?"
6-Main story and endings were rushed and they will actually prevent factions' side missions.
The endings are totally related to the factions you decide to work with. The ending itself isn't original,isn't innovative...it's not anything worthwhile after spending 80 hours into this game.Fallout 3 and NV had a sort of ending story recap including your previous choices. This isn't showed in Fallout 4.
What i've liked:
1-Companions
Companions have their own mind,psychology,prefereces and thoughts even during the smallest side quest you'll decide to do with them; making particular choices will affect your affinity in a good and really mature way. This is the best thing Bethesda did with this game; the best side quests i had in FL4 were those ones related/with my trusted companions. Good job,really,you really nailed it in the right way.
2-Women's asses in Vault Suits
SHORT VERSION
This game offers many low quality hours of gameplay full of bugs,crashes,hideous face modeling,low enemy,dialogue and gear variety and most of all showing that it's not important how many features are introduced in a open world game; what's important it's that those features must be meaningful and really,really well "sewn" with the other game mechanics. This is not the case: Fallout 4 look like a quick photo collage where you have to put yourself very distant to grab the real picture.If there's one.
Verdict : 5/10

CONS:
Idk if I'm the only one that feels the same way. Its a great game don't get me wrong, however i'm really disappointed with the limited dialogue choice you get from a selection of 4 choices. Also the fact that a majority of these choices lead up to the same conclusion of what happens next. The game's aspect of choosing what your character is able to say is a disallusion to what Fallout really stands for and basically the endings are almost one in the same.
FO3 and NV definitely made you feel that it was important to choose your answers wisely and that you could even fight off opponents using words. FO4 has few of those moments, and I feel that the dialogue wheel was a huge step backwards to the franchise...
As for the end game, once you finish the main story missions as well as the side missions that may or may not be aligned with the main quests there really isnt much to do end game. Rather, you're stuck in the wasteland trying to find unique NPCs to talk to in hopes that they will offer you a job so you may continue to keep busy and have a said purpose in continuing to play the game.
There are alot of bugs that are very noticable, and many will say that it is afterall a "Bethesda game". But it shouldn't be an excuse as Bethesda is known in the past for releasing buggy games. This cannot be helped though since it is afterall an open world game that will have many unpredictable bugs that players will come across, but there will be alot of noticable ones too. Such as trying to enter your power armor from the front but you get stuck in an animation unable to get out of it unless you reload the game, or being stuck in an elevator, a terminal, etc.
There are a limited amount of armor choices to choose from, notably ones that are stat worthy at least. I went through my first playthrough utilizing at least 3 armor sets and only 3.
PROS:
There are good aspects in the game that do deserve praise however. The single button grenade toss is now included in the combat mechanics as well as a sprint that utilizes your AP which is also used for VATs.
You can now layer your armor up with individual set pieces and every set piece of armor is either craftable or upgradable from the crafting station.
The forge mechanic is a nice plus, optional but still a nice plus. You are now able to build settlements/bases and fortify their positions using materials that were otherwise useless in previous titles. Same can be said with weapons which can be improved upon.
Companions are of variety and are very likable. Each having their own loyalty mission as you gain their trust in time, and you can develop more then one relationship with one character which is a nice touch, regardless of your character's gender.
BUY?:
With this all said and done, I would still recommend this game for the $60 price tag. If you take your time with all the side missions and story quests, I can say for certain this game can last you to about 80 or so hours depending on your playstyle. But note, this game is far from perfect.
A 8.5/10

Incredible game with an amazing world. The main story is very well made and the side quest simply while may be simple and repetitive after a while, are still entertaining due to the vastness that's left to explore in the world (which is very diverse). And a good side note, even if you haven't played or read any of the Fallout lore, this is an awesome game to pick up, since it doesn't follow the story of Fallout 3 directly (even though, if you are familiar, you will get "not-so-relevant" references to the other Fallout games).
The workbench that allows you to modify weapons and armor is very well designed and allows you to develop a weapon you find at a low level and make it a high level killing machine; that is of course, unless you find a better weapon that drops from a legendary creature. And the combat is very smooth too, even though VATS is awesome, I found myself not using it much except for the unusually hard fight in which I needed the stored critical. While melee is different from other games, it's still not the forte of the game, but it's a good option to save ammo and have some fun ripping heads clean off.
The complanion system is very good, even though they can drag behind at times or get stuck (I hope Bethesda will get a hold on that), and they are well scripted as far as dialogue goes, as well and can come very handy.
There's a main difference in the way you customize your character in terms of abilities and perks. There are no more skills, only perks. For those unfamiliar, in other Fallout games, you had points to spend on skills like Lockpicking or Guns or Medicine, etc. Now you only have Perks, based on your S.P.E.C.I.A.L. you can pick up perks and make the decision of picking a new perk, develop one that you have already or add a point to your S.P.E.C.I.A.L. Any of the ones you pick, you have to think it for a while, since you can't go back, the way you pick your perks, can define how your character develops, from a sneaky ninja sniper, to a walking tank that beats people to death, to an all-around, to whatever you decide.
Perhaps the only complaint is that the settlements aren't quite explained other than tips that pop up when you open certain things you can build, but you'll get the hang of it soon enough, since it's not that complicated. And you're not required to built and maintain all settlements you run into, they are mostly quests, but there are plenty other more that you can use to fill that missing XP.
Overall, this is an incredible game to pick up and one that it's worth every penny and more. Even now after I've played over 50 hours, I still want to play more and explore more and start a new story with a different set of skills.

There's a TL;DR at the bottom of this, unless for some reason you want to read the whole thing.
I've put roughly 150 hours combined of both Fallout 3 and Fallout New Vegas (this review will be mostly making comparisons to those two games.), and I can say with absolute confidence that the combat is
much more satisfying. The guns feel fantastic, each one different than the next. Melee combat has also improved immensely, but I'd have to say that Skyrim's melee is still better. (but that's to be expected, Skyrim doesn't have any guns.) I absolutely adore the new combat system, it makes the game feel so much more like an FPS (which in this game's case is a very good thing), than in 3/NV, which was basically a means to an end.
Now, the Power Armor. If I'm even sort of honest with myself, this is pretty much the biggest reason I pre-ordered the game (and the pip-boy edition at that) a week after it was announced. The Power Armor (from now it will be referred to as 'PA') is such an upgrade from 3 and NV. You feel powerful, as you should be. Raiders just become annoying instead of actual threats, and if you invest heavily into a PA build, eventually so will everything else. There's also the Jet Pack, but I've only just unlocked that. It's honestly the funnest thing to go around stomping in the PA, slaughtering everything that fires back at you. The Deathclaws are also much more scary. In the earlier levels whenever I encountered a deathclaw, I'd panic and pull out my minigun and begin shooting as many bullets as possible before it got close. The removal of fall damage whille in PA is also pretty amazing, because you can just air drop wherever you want, from any height.
The settlement building is definitely an important part of the game, and I enjoy just being OCD as I try and remove any and all useless junk off the workshop sites. But, it can be a bit of a pain to try and find those rarer materials as you try and build your PA garage. It's also fairly challenging, because if you don't leave any defenses, it becomes harder to defend your settlemenst from unwanted raiders. It's not required by the game for you to build settlements, but I highly recommend you do it either way.
I remember a lot of people complaining about the graphics from the E3 trailer. Now, they aren't any Arkham Knight level of detail, but they sure are incredible. I'm able to run most of the settings on Ultra without lag, but occasionally the menu screens act like a slide show, but not the actual game, for some strange reaason. I've yet to figure that out, but the only actual lag I've encountered when in-game is while I'm in a vertibird and looking down on Boston. That causes the most lag whenever I play, but the rest of the time it's a steady 60 FPS.
As well as that, it's also one of the most stable Bethesda games I've ever played. Considering how many times 3, NV, and Skyrim crashed, this game is incredibly stable. I just hope modding it to bits once the modding kit releases doesn't change that.

This is one of the greatest game ive ever played, Fallout 4 is an engrossing game that lures you in with mystery and the promise of adventure. Its wretched wasteland can be captivating, and you never know what odd person or settlement lies around the next bend. Fallout 4 uses its dark world as a canvas for exciting combat and gripping stories, and when you dig deeper into its post-nuclear-apocalypse version of Boston--defending yourself from violent scavengers and using your wits to climb social ladders--you become attached to the new you, and ultimately invested in the fate of your new world.
You transform into an influential wasteland warrior over the course of a multitude of dangerous quests, but this is difficult to imagine at the start when you're a well-to-do citizen of 1950s-esque Boston. The game begins on a peaceful morning at home with your spouse and child; a robot butler provides upbeat banter and a glimpse at what America might have become if the World's Fair era of invention and optimism from the 1930s persisted into the 21st century. Life is pleasant, until a distressful television broadcast. Your family is quickly rushed underground. It's within Vault 111 that you spend the next 200 years, frozen in cryogenic-stasis until your eventual rude awakening in the year 2277.
