As much as I try and enjoy this game it really is quite the dissapointment. Despite being a devout Fallout fan since the originals, I don't think this is a case of me expecting too much either.
Credit to Bethesda for wanting to try new things, and some of these things have come off really well. The crafting system is great, as is being able to create and restore towns. People complain about the graphics, yes they are very hit and miss when it comes to some things like frame rate, textures etc (signs of a rushed project IMO) but overall they are fine. Between crafting, modding weapons and armour, rebuilding a farm etc; it really is immersive. The map is quite large as well, and what I have enjoyed is moving around and just playing F4 as a combat/exploration game. AI has also come leaps and bounds, combat in general is much better. So at 25 hrs, I have enjoyed myself but its only for these reasons.
But this is an RPG, remember? So its not too much to expect some quality control when it comes to the rest of the content, some would say its equally or even more so important. The character voice narration is terrible, ok I can see how they want to go a more cinematic and place more control on the story. But the narration (at least of the male) is dry, boring and unconvincing. Personally I feel forcing the voice narration on players removes a great deal of the immersiveness from the previous games. It would not be so bad, but the characters responses a short, flat and boring. The NPC voice/dialogue are just as bland for the most part, and the whole 4 choice system is rubbish. Ok, fine, simplify it but far too often the availible choices progress no where at all. The dialogue has completely been dismissed.
The story line seems thrown together and really struggles to make you want to invest in it, for reasons stated above. Considering the set up of the game, and then considering the outcome of the initial sequence of events, its a bit of a let down and quite short sighted. You'll have more fun just paying it off and doing your own thing. But even the side quests are generic errands. The Fallout tradition of choice/consequence/reaction is vacant from this game. Recycled radio songs from F3 and FNV (I have not heard one new song yet). Hideous bugs and glitches (have a look on Youtube) that are so consistent you have to wonder if the entire development crew was boozed up for 5 years making this. So maybe we could get past this is if the rest of the game could stand of its feet? But it can't.
If you love this game and are reading this, take a minute so consider the quality of GTA V, Bioshock Infinite, Last Of Us or some of the other big hitters of the last couple of years, then consider if what we are playing here is up to scratch.
The whole thing feels rushed by at least 6 months. I would give this 2/5 and say its only worthwile buy at this price if you are new to the series, otherwise wait for a special. I don't think Bethesda can come back from this and as much as people say they love this game, there are obivious issues that need to be addressed if a top tier company can think releasing a game in this state is acceptable. I can't wait to see what the modders do with this and I hope they give the reigns back to Obsidian for the next Fallout game.

TLDR;  A mediocre non-RPG shooter with great modding potential.
But even as it is the Fallout 4 is not a bad game. It is quite buggy but entirely stable and the plenty of the issues should be very easy to fix. Turning this game into an actual Fallout game will take a lot of time though as in it's current state this is more like Sims With Guns. For the most part does not even feel like an adult game and the target audience is probably around 15 years old despite the mature rating.
All the controls in this game are obviously made 100% for consoles (even the key binding for PC is flawed and has actual bugs too). UI for the most part is pretty bad, inventory management is among the worst ever and conversations are cut down into trees where you always have only 4 options and at least in my case the options are bound to movement keys making you occasionally give a totally random answer when someone ambushes you with a dialogue. Your answer is whatever direction you happened to be moving at that time. Basically all this should be redone and I am sure modders eventually will but not sure if Bethesda cares at all about these kind of things.
Settlement management is also a disaster in terms of UI and with the key binding bugs I can't even move in build mode and I need to keep opening and closing the damn menu all the time. Also there is no management screen for your 'settlers' where you could assign them jobs or anything. You can just give them commands in a similar system you can use on your followers except that with the key bind issues it may easily take 10-15 minutes to get one single settler to do the job you want him/her to do.
Companions are typical Bethesda companions in terms of AI and generally speaking cause far more problems than they are worth. They have a preferred weapon (hidden in the inventory) that spends no ammo but you can give them any weapon you like along with the ammo rquired. The 'custom' weapons work just fine for them in open terrain but in many situations the ammo efficiency is catastrophic and your companion will keep hitting anything but their tagets and can easily waste 100 rounds of ammo without doing any major damage.
Skills are gone. Completely gone. Fallout 4 isn't much of an RPG anymore and the new perk system that replaced those skills is mostly boring and extremely hollow. Leveling up is barely worth a yawn. Sure, some perks are good and some are ok, but most of the time you are just spending your perk points on either rather useless perks or SPECIAL stat points that these days just seem so weak. Partly because none of the perks now require more than one stat whereas in earlier games many good perks required a combination of stat points. Also with the CRIT system completely ruined luck does not seem very interesting stat at all. Criticals no longer have a % chance but you fill up a bar that once filled allows you to manually select when to fire your critical shot. After more than 50 hours I haven't used a single crit yet as I have decided to ignore this completely futile mechanic.
As a rather simple and mediocre non-RPG shooter this game is not that impressive in it's current state. With some fixes and some DLC this may change quite a bit but MODS are real thing that determine how long this game will be played and how much you can enjoy this. As it is the game deserves about 75/100 points and I expect it to go somewhere around 90 during the next 6-9 months. I can take a couple of years before the truly great mods start pouring in. So even if you are planning to buy this game: THERE IS NO RUSH.

*It will take many, many months before this game is properly fixed'
TLDR;  A mediocre non-RPG shooter with great modding potential.
But even as it is the Fallout 4 is not a bad game. It is quite buggy but entirely stable and the plenty of the issues should be very easy to fix. Turning this game into an actual Fallout game will take a lot of time though as in it's current state this is more like Sims With Guns. For the most part does not even feel like an adult game and the target audience is probably around 15 years old despite the mature rating.
All the controls in this game are obviously made 100% for consoles (even the key binding for PC is flawed and has actual bugs too). UI for the most part is pretty bad, inventory management is among the worst ever and conversations are cut down into trees where you always have only 4 options and at least in my case the options are bound to movement keys making you occasionally give a totally random answer when someone ambushes you with a dialogue. Your answer is whatever direction you happened to be moving at that time. Basically all this should be redone and I am sure modders eventually will but not sure if Bethesda cares at all about these kind of things.
Settlement management is also a disaster in terms of UI and with the key binding bugs I can't even move in build mode and I need to keep opening and closing the damn menu all the time. Also there is no management screen for your 'settlers' where you could assign them jobs or anything. You can just give them commands in a similar system you can use on your followers except that with the key bind issues it may easily take 10-15 minutes to get one single settler to do the job you want him/her to do.
Companions are typical Bethesda companions in terms of AI and generally speaking cause far more problems than they are worth. They have a preferred weapon (hidden in the inventory) that spends no ammo but you can give them any weapon you like along with the ammo rquired. The 'custom' weapons work just fine for them in open terrain but in many situations the ammo efficiency is catastrophic and your companion will keep hitting anything but their tagets and can easily waste 100 rounds of ammo without doing any major damage.
Skills are gone. Completely gone. Fallout 4 isn't much of an RPG anymore and the new perk system that replaced those skills is mostly boring and extremely hollow. Leveling up is barely worth a yawn. Sure, some perks are good and some are ok, but most of the time you are just spending your perk points on either rather useless perks or SPECIAL stat points that these days just seem so weak. Partly because none of the perks now require more than one stat whereas in earlier games many good perks required a combination of stat points. Also with the CRIT system completely ruined luck does not seem very interesting stat at all. Criticals no longer have a % chance but you fill up a bar that once filled allows you to manually select when to fire your critical shot. After more than 50 hours I haven't used a single crit yet as I have decided to ignore this completely futile mechanic.
As a rather simple and mediocre non-RPG shooter this game is not that impressive in it's current state. With some fixes and some DLC this may change quite a bit but MODS are real thing that determine how long this game will be played and how much you can enjoy this. As it is the game deserves about 75/100 points and I expect it to go somewhere around 90 during the next 6-9 months. I can take a couple of years before the truly great mods start pouring in. So even if you are planning to buy this game: THERE IS NO RUSH.

I've been with fallout for quite a while now, i played the first two games when bethesda announced they were working on 3. I loved 3 and loved even more new vegas, and while 3 wasn't as lore friendly, it was still an enjoyable game with a great atmosphere.
Now here we are with 4, and with complaints and all, it's overall a fun game. Combat has been improved dramatically, it still feels like a role playing game and like a fallout game for that matter regardless of the countless complaints people have had. While the system is a simplification of the skills in previous entries, it still feels complete and full of choice, getting all the skill can take it's time and even when people complain that you can max everything out, it was fairly easy to exploit the system in previous games.
To take a note, people have made a meme out of a fake ending that says the ending is two sided, when it's faction based sort of like new vegas, people have used this fake ending as a con saying the game only has 2 endings based on the bad guy and the good guys, which just isn't true.
Now taking off the nostalgia goggles like everyones seems to use to judge the game:
Pros
-Companions feel more complete, almost always saying something about the location you are on and even participating in conversations you have with other characters. Dogmeat feels like a pointless gimmick, and his AI is specially bad compared to other companions, expect frustration from them getting stuck on walls. But the commands make things sometimes easier and more straight forward compared to the wheel in NV.
-Game difficulty has increased since previous games, i'm having a harder time when playing on hard on new vegas. You actually have to rely on different tactics and the AI will do the same too, sometimes flanking you and using grenades.
-Enemy variety has increased too, many different types of enemies to add some spice to the fight.
-At first glance the removal of weapon condition system looks like it will ruin looting, but it just replaces the usage of the guns you pick up, as mods are a more important part of the game
Meh
-The dialogue system is not as complex and fun to ♥♥♥♥ with as in previous games, it still gives you enough choice to play with, the voice acting is pretty good too.
-Graphics aren't the best but not the worst either, the game looks pretty as ♥♥♥♥ at times and just straight ugly in others, it depends on location.
-The map, it's not as big as in other bethesda games, or it might be but it doesn't feel like it. The map has an insane amount of things to do, but some empty space would be nice, i liked traveling in general in previous games, also i dislike discovering locations out of nowhere because i might forget about them while i'm doing a quest.
-Setlement building while fun and great, it needs some tweaking and some extra stuff, or maybe i'm just missing some perks that open my options further, so far i had my fun, but ♥♥♥♥ add some noclip to the walls.
Cons:
-Some weird as ♥♥♥♥ performance in cities, it's all over the place with shadow distance to ultra, after looking at afterburner the game refuses to use resource properly at times, leaving my cpu and gpu at 50%.
-Some weird bugs that required me to reload at times, quicksaving is also a little ♥♥♥♥y at times, sometimes giving momentum to enemies once you reload.
Overall a great game, if you love fallout it's a great entry into the series regardless of the cries of "not a fallout game, bethesda ruined the loreeee" All you need to enjoy is to take off the nostalgia goggles.

I wanted to love this game, truly I did and although it has a hell of a lot going for it, in a few ways its less captivating than Skyrim. They say they want to make games where you can be whoever you want and do whatever you want but there is a big backstory in this one that is forced on you and after playing for about 50 hours with a couple of different characters there really isn't much choice about how to act either. You can pick 'sarcastic' responses but these just stop people from wanting to interact with you, there is no great big moral choice like in FO3 deciding the fate of Megaton. There's just different factions to choose from and although that gives it some replay value it doesn't feel like you have much freedom in terms of character development. In the Elder Scrolls games you can choose your sex, your race and as a history with an unknown past, make up your own back story, in this you're either a male ex soldier or a female lawyer - with a young child. Is this truly even an RPG? Yes, ok it is but not one with the same freedom to make yourself as we've been used to in Bethesda games.
The engine hasn't been updated enough. Retexturing has been done (but oh my god hurry up with the HD texture pack, some of the textures look horrific) but it feels the same. Gun play is good, melee is bad. I don't know why anyone would want to play melee in this game when your character takes so damn long to throw a punch. Its ridiculous.
The armor system is not great either. OK so you can update your vault suit with bits of leather, or metal later... but this is supposed to be a massive RPG - why does my character look basically the same after many hours of play, can I really not find anything better? You might find your wear your vault suit all the way through the game and that's not something I like.
Still there's lots to explore and lots to see although you should avoid the main quest for as long as you can (even though all the factions tie in to it so you can't progress in them without doing the main quest - another unwelcome addition) because after doing that the rest of the game might seem kind of pointless. I need to start again, and pick a different faction. Hopefully the DLC will be amazing.

A much improved version of Fallout 3.
Pros:
- World is much better realized. The map is completely open, unlike Fallout 3 where particularly the city was highly linear.
- Quests, locations and story also much improved. The themepark feel of F3 is mostly improved, with better connection between locations. There are large quest-chains to complete beyond the main story. You can join various factions and complete multiple stories, many linking areas together. Less emphasis on a sort of slapstick feel that F3 had, more serious.
- Crafting. Huge complex crafting mechanics added. Settlements add a bit of spice to the gameplay. Makes it feel more like a world as you can call for aid in the form of artillery and fighters from settlements.
Cons:
- Easy to gimp your character. I wish RPGs with big crafting mechanics would separate crafting and combat. A level up should give you 1 perk to spend on crafting, and 1 for combat. Make the perk sheets separate so we can actually enjoy CRAFTING AND COMBAT in the same game. Instead the game essentially forces you to choose one over the other unless you greatly lower difficulty.
- Bethesda game. In fact F4 is much closer to Skyrim than F3 was to Oblivion.
- VATS is still horrible. Usability improved, but still it is often clumsy.
- Inventory is horrible and clumsy. Particularly as you are picking up far more stuff than you used to.
- Aspects of crafting aren't well realized. Particularly cooking is a mess. Far too many recipes, which make a mess in the inventory. Never used food as it is a pain to sort. Simple usability things like making multiple meat recipes fall under the same category would vastly improve usability. So various creatures meat can be cooked into a generic "cooked fallout steak", instead it separates many of them out, without any particular gain. So many of the recipes give similar effects.
Essentially it is a director's cut version of Fallout 3. If you didn't like that game, it is unlikely F4 will change your mind. The mechanics are very much the same, they have just been improved upon.

Fallout 4 – Short review – Minor Spoilers
Fallout 4 is set in the wondrous location of Boston, USA. It is unique in giving you a glance to the past before all of the bombs hit, though it is only a short glimpse it's still interesting to see. It then of course sees you treading through the wasteland to find your son after a nuclear fallout, and let me tell you- it’s a wild ride that’s filled with lots of good and lots of bad.
I will admit, I have been waiting for Fallout 4 for a long time, ever since Fallout: New Vegas was brought out I was imagining a new Fallout and now it’s here. As much as I want to praise this game to high heaven I just can’t bring myself to do it, though I did enjoy myself throughout some of the main story at least.
This is the first fully voice acted Bethesda game, with this being the first time the main character has been voiced at all. It will probably take some getting used to but I’m sure that it was a step in the right direction- with only a few minor complaints about only having one voice for each gender. I do however feel both voice actors did well, though the female voice is noticeably better.
I will say this is Fallout. You will know that it’s Fallout. Nothing has changed so much that the game is no longer recognisable and while big companies were expecting so much more, I will say that this is what I wanted and what I had expected.
Many things have been improved over the last few installations in the series, starting with the gameplay. It has been refined and tweaked to near perfection, so well in fact that I find myself referencing its FPS mechanics to Call of Duty, which is in no way a bad thing. It’s not perfect by any means, but it’s a significant step in the right direction.
VATS has been tweaked, where in the old games it stopped time completely, here it only slows time allowing for a smoother transition in and out with the added bonus of having tension as the battle hasn’t stopped completely. Though you may think with the FPS mechanics being refined that VATS isn’t needed or not as crucial as other games, I can tell you it is most certainly worth using. It’s certainly easier to use it to single out enemies in the massive battles that the game offers you. The new critical mechanic also allows you to bank your critical hits and use them whenever you need to, with there being perks allowing you to bank more than one.
The addition of sprinting was also another welcomed change, it most certainly makes running to locations more bearable (though it does use your AP, which is used for VATS).
The settlement building is another new mechanic that I have not spent too much time with, though it does offer a wide array of things to do and build in a variety of locations.
The main thing that I find myself in awe over is the locations and the art style. I must say they really have done a fantastic job making this game a lot more pleasing to look at as opposed to previous Fallout games. The very start of the game shows this sleek, gorgeous looking world before it becomes the wasteland you will be exploring for the other 99.9% of the time you spend in the game. This glimpse shows you the contrast of the before and after allowing you to get first-hand experience on the desolation of the location that you’re exploring. It’s always been easy to get lost in exploring in a Fallout game, and this one certainly is no exception. Pick a direction and wander that way in the hope that you will find something interesting, that is how many people say this game is played and I couldn’t agree more.
However, while this game does those things so very well, I will say that there are some things that I really didn’t feel like it did enough of, or well enough.
The main story feels lazy and too narrow. It feels as though you’re not really playing an RPG of sorts, but more an action adventure game. With the addition of player voices and the storyline being so linear, I can’t help but wonder what they were thinking.
You start by being cryogenically frozen, with your son being taken and you needing to get him back. Right from the get-go you’re forced into a parent role in a game where people are being slaughtered left right and centre. This was a turn off for me in the biggest of senses, I didn’t want to have my character told to me, I didn’t want my character to have the ONE objective that honestly I didn’t really care about… Why would I care about a baby that I saw only one minute of, and better yet, why do I have to care in a game that’s about creating my OWN character?
While people are having different experiences with this game it all remains the same, everyone has to do the same thing to get to the same place albeit for a different ending. I feel like no matter my decisions or chat options my character does and says things that I didn’t want them to say, the best being all 4 of my chat options being focused on my son, when really, I don’t care too much for him.
I will admit some story points were really enjoyable, but that doesn’t shake me feeling like I was forced into playing the role of a character I didn’t want to, and in a world where I create my own character- is it really acceptable to have the Witcher 3 have better decisions that change the story more than it does here? This really is a step back in Bethesda’s shoes, with New Vegas being the pinnacle of RPG-player choice.
Whilst the story provided at least an objective for me to accomplish, the faction quests are so bland, so lacklustre that I put my head in my hands on several occasions when I got the same objective in the same place more than once to accomplish. This is the problem with repeat missions, and I was more than disappointed with it. I felt forced to complete these boring repeat quests in which you defend a settlement or clear a location, they were just the same thing over and over.
In a world you’re told to explore, there really aren’t enough unique quests laying around for me to find quickly enough before I get tired of wandering around finding nothing. Now, I won’t admit to finding everything there is to find, but struggling to find things to do in a game like this shouldn’t be happening, at least to me.
The settlement building is a forced mechanic, you HAVE to do it for some quests, even if you don’t want to. While this mechanic can be fun if you put the time in, I get people telling me “the game is made for more than one play through” so why spend so much time building a really cool settlement that you’re only going to scrap when you start a new character? The repeat quests are not enough to keep me involved long enough to want to dedicate time to building something that won’t be used for the most part anyway. Even if I did use it, it would be lost when I start my new save.
All in all, I like this game, mechanically and visually it’s lovely. It’s a massive step in the right direction in terms of the engine and at least in terms of locations. If Obsidian got their hands on this engine (my god a girl can dream) then I can only imagine how incredible that game would be. Alas, right now, this is a good base for modding and the like.
+Good Gameplay
+Good Locations
-Dull Story
-Repetitive quests
-Base building feels pointless

If you're going into this game expecting graphics on par with the Witcher 3, you'll be sorely disappointed. But it was never said that Fallout 4's graphics would be able to compete in the first place. Now that the elephant in the room has been addressed, let's move on.
The best part about Fallout 4 is that it's satisfying to play both as a fan of Bethesda's Fallout series, and as a newcomer. That being said, if you're looking for a great RPG experience you'd be better off playing Fallout 1 and 2. If you're looking for solid and exciting gameplay you should play Fallout 3, Fallout: New Vegas and Fallout 4. Let's list some pros and cons:
Pros:
- Gunplay: A solid improvement over Fallout 3 and an expansion upon New Vegas. An expansive amount of weapon modifications make for great customization.
- Replayability: The factions you encounter in the game are very different from one another and allow for a lot of replayability.
- Power Armor: It's definitely more immersive and offers a great temporary bonus to defense and offense when coupled wth the minigun.
- Mods: The mod system is already in full swing and seems to be a lot easier to create yourself than ever before, even before the G.E.C.K.
Cons:
- Dialogue: The voice acting is a nice addition, but for people who prefer the way Fallout 3 and New Vegas handled things it's very unwelcome, and Bethesda should have added an option to disable the voiced protagonist. The dialogue wheel itself is alright, but I feel it should have come with more than four options. Most of the options you can select also seem to lead to the same outcome, which is "yes, I will help you", even if you don't want to.
- Loading times: They can vary pretty wildly, but I can get up to 45 seconds of load time just going from an exterior to an interior on a pretty decent laptop.
- Pacing: The introduction seems to go a bit too fast, and you obtain your power armor within the first hour and a half. I understand that Bethesda wanted to start the game off "action-packed" but it just feels like you're not really rewarded for playing, you're rewarded for purchasing.
- No skill checks: New Vegas' best feature was the skill checks, for example to heal a soldier you had to pass a Medicine check of 50 or you'd kill him. Those days are gone, and we have Charisma checks now. It was a welcome and beautiful addition that never made the transition from Obsidian to Bethesda.
Overall, even though I listed more negatives than positives, I would recommend this game. HOWEVER I wouldn't recommend it NOW. Wait a few months for Bethesda to roll out some bug-fixing patches and for the modding community to release a few fixes of their own.

I've been with fallout for quite a while now, i played the first two games when bethesda announced they were working on 3. I loved 3 and loved even more new vegas, and while 3 wasn't as lore friendly, it was still an enjoyable game with a great atmosphere.
Now here we are with 4, and with complaints and all, it's overall a fun game. Combat has been improved dramatically, it still feels like a role playing game and like a fallout game for that matter regardless of the countless complaints people have had. While the system is a simplification of the skills in previous entries, it still feels complete and full of choice, getting all the skill can take it's time and even when people complain that you can max everything out, it was fairly easy to exploit the system in previous games.
To take a note, people have made a meme out of a fake ending that says the ending is two sided, when it's faction based sort of like new vegas, people have used this fake ending as a con saying the game only has 2 endings based on the bad guy and the good guys, which just isn't true.
Now taking off the nostalgia goggles like everyones seems to use to judge the game:
Pros
-Companions feel more complete, almost always saying something about the location you are on and even participating in conversations you have with other characters. Dogmeat feels like a pointless gimmick, and his AI is specially bad compared to other companions, expect frustration from them getting stuck on walls. But the commands make things sometimes easier and more straight forward compared to the wheel in NV.
-Game difficulty has increased since previous games, i'm having a harder time when playing on hard on new vegas. You actually have to rely on different tactics and the AI will do the same too, sometimes flanking you and using grenades.
-Enemy variety has increased too, many different types of enemies to add some spice to the fight.
-At first glance the removal of weapon condition system looks like it will ruin looting, but it just replaces the usage of the guns you pick up, as mods are a more important part of the game
Meh
-The dialogue system is not as complex and fun to ♥♥♥♥ with as in previous games, it still gives you enough choice to play with, the voice acting is pretty good too.
-Graphics aren't the best but not the worst either, the game looks pretty as ♥♥♥♥ at times and just straight ugly in others, it depends on location.
-The map, it's not as big as in other bethesda games, or it might be but it doesn't feel like it. The map has an insane amount of things to do, but some empty space would be nice, i liked traveling in general in previous games, also i dislike discovering locations out of nowhere because i might forget about them while i'm doing a quest.
-Setlement building while fun and great, it needs some tweaking and some extra stuff, or maybe i'm just missing some perks that open my options further, so far i had my fun, but ♥♥♥♥ add some noclip to the walls.
Cons:
-Some weird as ♥♥♥♥ performance in cities, it's all over the place with shadow distance to ultra, after looking at afterburner the game refuses to use resource properly at times, leaving my cpu and gpu at 50%.
-Some weird bugs that required me to reload at times, quicksaving is also a little ♥♥♥♥y at times, sometimes giving momentum to enemies once you reload.
Overall a great game, if you love fallout it's a great entry into the series regardless of the cries of "not a fallout game, bethesda ruined the loreeee" All you need to enjoy is to take off the nostalgia goggles.

after about 50 hours or so with Fallout 4, I'd like to provide some simple point-by-point reviews for anyone still on the fence about it...
Game Stability - like most bethesda open world titles lately (Fallout 3, Skyrim, and now Fallout 4) the game is competently stable for my own experience.  While Fallout 4 has every single problem that the previously mentioned titles have always possessed (quest completion disjunction due to non linear questing, AI moments-of-idiocy, record keeping anomalies, and many others) those bugs crop up rarely, and are usually work-around-able by dropping to a previous save, zoning, reloading the program, or switching between a variety of in-game modes (for example, from time to time, the visuals for my weapons will disappear - switching to my pipboy and back usually fixes that)
all in all, I've found the game satisfyingly stable - not perfectly stable, but no significant problem that was unexpected or uncorrectable
Visuals - graphical fidelity (detail of textures) is perhaps 1 step below modern top-of-the-line, I still find it quite good looking overall.  Bethesda seems to have addressed many of the issues of visual aesthetic that cropped up during fallout 3 and Skyrim (namely, everything being grey), and have still managed to create a believable and interesting wasteland while utilizing a more colorful and varied palette
certain details are VERY pretty, others are a little less detailed, but overall, not only am I finding it very nice to look at, but I'm finding the choice of aesthetic (use of color and terrain details and lighting and so forth) to be mostly satisfying.  I'm a little disappointed in their choice of weapon aesthetics (weapons have gotten very chunky and knobby), but they still fit the haphazard construction motif of the Fallout wasteland fairly well
Story - while I've been fairly careful to balance my pursuit of the main story against general exploration, I've found the story to be mildly interesting, but not compelling enough to really draw me AWAY from general exploration.  If you're fond of strong, dramatic story, the Fallout 4 story may not be enough for you - but, if you're mostly looking for a mildly dramatic excuse to travel the post-apocalyptic wasteland of Fallout, kill, explore, loot, and build - you've hit the jackpot!
Game Mechanics - there are so many, my attempt to be brief having already failed...
Gunplay - gunplay is solid - sounds are excellent, and playing on the middle level of difficulty, things seem mostly balanced - like many games, Fallout 4 suffers from supernatural AI grenade throwing skills (distance and accuracy are ABSURD), but combat behavior beyond that seems well balanced
VATS is mostly a secondary system - the FPS gunplay is solid enough and the limitation on VATS usually make it a one-shot or two shot effort during most battles - it's still useful - it just has mostly an assist presence on the field rather than a major feature
LEVELING UP AND SKILLS AND PERKS - While many people have complained about the changes to the skill system, overall, I feel it does very well - you level up quite frequently, so you can expect to be able to accumlate a LOT of the skill points - the skill points also have much more satisfyingly significant upgrades point-for-point
The game continues to have skill books as well - but instead of adding to your perks, MOST of the skill books add small bonuses to perk-like features associated with the books specifically (technically providing you with another set of perks)  A *few* of the skillbooks add small bonuses to abilities that ALSO get big bonuses from the standard perks (for example, stealth perk gives you 20% and upwards bonuses to sneaking, and sneak skill books add 5% increments seperately)
combine that with bobbleheads (more perk-like advantages) and you have a fairly wide range of ability to upgrade your character for quite a long time
overall, I've enjoyed the levelling up system, and MOST of the perks seem to be pretty useful, depending on playstyle, so there's very little there that is obsolete
WOW - that's my attempt to be brief - and I'm not even done - but I wanna go play some Fallout 4 now - hope this might answer a few questions people might have...

I reccommend this game, but with several caveats.  First off, this is clearly, from both tone and writing style, a direct sequel to Fallout 3.  If you enjoyed New Vegas' quirky humor, or Fallout/Fallout 2, there isnt' going to be a great deal here to remind you of those games.  Your character has a defined background, so there are sharp restrictions to your play that can really break immersion for those used to the very broad sandbox of FO/FO2/NV's style.
If you're looking for essentially Skyrim with worse melee combat and guns, this is your game.  Most of the quests are, like Skyrim, just simple murder in assorted terrain, and quite linear.  Further, the factions appear to be of the 'gotta join 'em all' variety, so no worries about locking yourself out of a questline by choosing the opposite side so far.
Be aware also that this is -very- much a direct console port.  The FOV is narrow as if you will be playing from across the room, and the keyboard controls are more than a bit unintuitive as they are just roughly remapped controller buttons.  The mouse is the worst part, with the filters to it making it feel like a floaty thumbstick.  Most of this can be fixed with simple configuration changes, however be aware that this is a game that will require modification to give the best experience on PC.
It's been fun enough to keep me involved, despite the above.  Buy it, but unless you're a huge fan of the series like I am, wait until it goes on sale.

There's a good number of companions, though unlike New Vegas allowing you to run with 2, you are only allowed to have one with you at all times, a small draw back, but it makes it easier, still careful since you companion can sometime kinda pull you into conversations in the midst of combat which makes for humorous moments or they kinda ♥♥♥♥ you over in trying to disarm traps and just walk right into them, otherwise, gathering them is worth your time because most of them have a great sense of charm and you'll easily become attached to a few of them.
The change to the Power Armor mechanics as it to being more akin to a knight set over your normal wears without it on can make all the difference in some battles with what you decide to tackle head out and can be helpful to help you collect junk in the wasteland to mod weapon parts, armor parts, settlements and other things such as repairs to the armor itself.
There ARE side quests, you just have to look out for them, can't really miss them, you get pretty good loot and benefits for your labor to completing them.
You'll level up pretty fast in this game verus the other Fallouts, which can seemingly take forever, forcing you mostly to complete quests just to level up most of the time compared to grinding, which makes since, Fallout is not a grind heavy game compared to a game like Monster Hunter is. And with leveling up faster having no level caps like the other Fallout does, the leveling system is far better beyond compare as FO 3/NV, the cap was LV 30 if you didn't have DLC, which only brought the cap up to LV 50, making it a bit more punishing on try to get the right build you want to run with.
The settlement/building system was a mod in pervious Fallout games, like NV that people made, Bethseda has added such a system to bring that very idea to this game and it's great, because now the junk in the wasteland suddenly no longer becomes junk, it's junk you need to support your settlements to keep them supplied and well defended.
Overall, Bethseda did a great job with this game, it's a great game and despite the few flaws and bugs, which can easily be fixed via performance issues. you can easily look past all of it. If your a fan of Fallout, get this game, it capitalize on a lot the other vanilla Fallouts didn't have unless you had mods added to them.

At over 100 hours, the base game is very substantial. I played through the main story without mods or console commands on normal difficulty, and had a great time.
I now have about 20 mods turned on along with god mode, creating the most crazy towns and weapons while delivering carnage accross the commonwealth.

Okay since I've beaten the game and played about 100 plus hours, I'll have to be honest here and say the ending was a big disappointment. I expect some closure for the fate of the Commonwealth and the decision you've made over the main quests especially the factions you decide to help out. But you get absolutely nothing beside your character's brief speech in the end. I wish they put in more time in the story as well as the factions because you have no choice but to join one and you have to kill almost everyone you know, which really sucks. Also the faction quests are nothing more than side quests that just becomes boring overtime. For the story side, it's not that great and sadly New Vegas beats them down in this area big time.
As for the gameplay wise, I'll say it's really good and a big improvement over the previous Fallout 3 and New Vegas. The gunplay is responsive and smooth as well as the including iron sights for the weapons, which makes the gunplay more awesome. The weapon mods and weapon variety is not that great, which I hope future DLC content adds more weapons or when the GECK comes out, we can finally see some new and shiny toys to shoot with.
The perk system works almost how Skyrim perk system works, except it's much more simplier. It works to some point, but once you reach higher levels, they become useless and there are some that are purer garberge. I do kinda wish they keep in the Skill System because it made the game much more interesting especially the speech challenges, which in Fallout 4 doesn't have it.
The Building system is what got me spending most of my game time because in my opinion this is one of the best feature for Fallout 4. The options to build what kind of base you want is beyond awesome. You can build from small outposts to fully-sized fortresses in matter of minutes or hours depending on the scale.
Overall I still recommend Fallout 4 to anyone that have played previous Fallout and Elder Scrolls games while it does lack in content and variety at the moment, it's still bring in that old school feeling that Fallout always have. It's a good game, but it is a good Fallout game? That's for you to decide because I really haven't played the old Fallout games yet, but maybe my opinions will change once I boot up Fallout 1 and 2.

I reccommend this game, but with several caveats.  First off, this is clearly, from both tone and writing style, a direct sequel to Fallout 3.  If you enjoyed New Vegas' quirky humor, or Fallout/Fallout 2, there isnt' going to be a great deal here to remind you of those games.  Your character has a defined background, so there are sharp restrictions to your play that can really break immersion for those used to the very broad sandbox of FO/FO2/NV's style.
If you're looking for essentially Skyrim with worse melee combat and guns, this is your game.  Most of the quests are, like Skyrim, just simple murder in assorted terrain, and quite linear.  Further, the factions appear to be of the 'gotta join 'em all' variety, so no worries about locking yourself out of a questline by choosing the opposite side so far.
Be aware also that this is -very- much a direct console port.  The FOV is narrow as if you will be playing from across the room, and the keyboard controls are more than a bit unintuitive as they are just roughly remapped controller buttons.  The mouse is the worst part, with the filters to it making it feel like a floaty thumbstick.  Most of this can be fixed with simple configuration changes, however be aware that this is a game that will require modification to give the best experience on PC.
It's been fun enough to keep me involved, despite the above.  Buy it, but unless you're a huge fan of the series like I am, wait until it goes on sale.

Fallout 4 is a fun RPG-shooter that has a lot of flaws, though many can be fixed.
First off, after leaving the vault I use my usual "Is it really Open World" test and go in the opposite direction of what's clearly been signalled for me to do. I then get met with the edge of the map already, "You cannot go that way" - suffice to say, not a good first impression.
My second impression of the game after leaving the vault was... why are all the houses "barricaded"/not made? It screams rushing/lack of detail to me.
Then I give in a little and try to play it as a more railroad(coincidence Bethesda?!?))ed type of RPG , and it worked surprisingly well.
Fast forward to the ending and I had enjoyed the stories and world a lot, despite substantial barriers the game sets up that keeps it from becoming excellent, to just being good.  And as for the ending itself, let's just say it was very underwhelming and anti-climatic.
List of pros and cons (extra spoiler warning):
Pros:
Combat is excellent
Level design (when it's there) is great
Variation of enemy types is good
Weather, lighting and water are good looking
Dialogue options aren't as bad as you could fear. Personally I'd like a more nuanced system than both F3/NV and F4, but if we compare the two I'd say they're different, but not necessarily inferior to one another.
Factions both new and old are interesting and give you choice and variation
Power armor is better than ever
Weapon and armor customization is simple, yet detailed
Settlements as an idea and the options provided are great
Cons:
There needs to be some kind of easier loot-management system. I don't play an RPG to stare at an interface for hours and do mental math, that's for strategy games. The store all junk function in the workshop is nice, but you're still left with sorting and scrapping all the rest through a cluttered and small interface. For example, who had the bright idea that non-armor apparel can't be scrapped at the armor workstation but has to be manually stored in the workshop for its components to be usable?
Settlement building is terrible and clearly made for consoles. It's a misére of endless snapping, no control and rigid limitations.
Just to make it clear... remove the damn settlement size limit for PCs.
Only one type of player voice (I know it's a huge undertaking to record that many lines, but they could have at least processed the audio to make a few variations)
Textures are way too swingy in quality, with a majority being really mediocre to bad
Some textures sometimes fail to load completely (I'm looking at you, Proctor Ingram's upper body power armor piece).
It can be overlooked, but from start to finish there's major clipping issues.
The destructible environment system and physics are underwhelming. Fallout 4 would have been a great game for a much more permissive destruction system.
Unless you really grind, you only get the marketed Power Armor Jet Pack AFTER you actually "complete"  the game. And it's really just... crap. I can't think of one upgrade that isn't better than it, plus it wastes fusion core power on short "farty" bursts of air.
I got increasingly higher loading times as I progressed farther through the story. There's some optimization needed.
Occasional lack of choice in main story questline. The good guy narrative,  whomever you might be good towards, is somewhat forced. I'm really missing a NV-like "third option".
Companion commands need to be smoother and more intuitive to do.
Power Armor... it's powered by a fusion core. Don't you think there could be some sort of makeshift propeller to ascend underwater instead of walking like a snail on the seabed?
Give me my GBs back.
60 hours... Just starts main story!

I purely enjoy running around and gunning raiders of whoever to jaunty classic tunes. Something about it is just cathardic to me. So when i saw that Fallout 4 was basically an updated version with prettier graphics and some new/revised elements, I was all in.
Nowadays, i try to not over-hype myself by reading every new piece of info that crosses my eye. As i have learned from other games, it will only lead to disappointment. I will say that i could not get enough of the half hour demo from E3 as i watched it practically every day leading to launch.
When the day finally arrived and the reviews started pouring out, I knew that there would be those who immediately hated it and those who barricaded in order to defend it.
Do i think it deserves a 1 out of 10? no

I do love the crafting system, the settlement building, and the upgraded Power Armor that actually feels like goddamn Power Armor.

Does it have a fair share of bugs/performance issues? indeed- depending on gameplay sessions, the game will ocassionally crash. it does not require a system reboot but it is annoying above all. that is why F5 has become my friend.
Bottomline, i love Fallout 4. it feels fantastic and looks great considering how sizeable the world is. Sure it could look even better, but i am satisfied with it. I think why alot of people are♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥off is because they were expecting an entirely brand new presentation and approach. With 3, they slated their approach that all other Fallout games were going to follow. So in essence, they succeeded in their goal and added some welcome aspects.
And on a final note, if you do not like it, then simply do not play it. Just because you may/might not like it does not mean somebody else cannot find enjoyment from playing it. I play because i enjoy it and love me some Fallout action.

I just want to kick off this review by saying that this is an excellent game, and has surpassed all standards I set for it before playing. It absolutely has my recommendation, and there's no way that that could possibly be revoked.
Graphically it is stunning. Some people complain about it being oversaturated, or too dull, but I found it to be the perfect post-apocalyptic blend of browns and brights. The character design is a huge step up from recent Fallout titles, with creatures and other NPCs looking more detailed and lifelike than ever. That being said, the graphics are certainly not without their downsides. While the model and texture detail is absolutely stupendous, I must say the animations for these works of art are sadly lacking. Mouths move, if you can believe it, worse than I think they did in New Vegas, eyes are all but emotionless, and there are a lot of issues with the dynamic conversation camera snapping too close to objects. On top of this, I find it just a bit odd that Bethesda is a step away from requiring an absolute top-of-the-line rig for the content they have; it seems to me that, had they focused on optimization a bit more, they could have left room for so much more content on a much wider array of rigs than what they currently have, as beautiful as it is.
As far as the quests go, I was definitely not disappointed. I found myself pondering the repercussions of my actions, and feeling my heart wrenching out of my chest at several of the bigger decisions I was required to make. This game managed to make me FEEL a lot more than any other recent RPG has managed to do. I'm not going to spoil anything, but if Bethesda's goal was to make an excellent story with points at which you can feel the weight of a world upon your shoulders, then they certainly excelled.
Audio is as good as ever, almost like Fallout 3, New Vegas, or Skyrim with their respective ambient noises mods; however, what makes it really interesting, is rather than just hearing a nonexistant gunfight every so often rippling through the wastes, there are actually many faction wars raging on in the city practically nonstop. The Brotherhood of Steel will be hunting down their enemies, Supermutants will storm Raider camps, and Diamond City guards will encounter squads of Gunners looking for some energy cells.
This brings me to my next topic, crafting. The crafting system is pretty cool, though the novelty of it quickly wears off once you realize what a struggle it is to get certain resources. Forget the settlement object cap, for a minute, because I rarely ever have a problem with that. My main problem with crafting is the abundance of some of the resources that you always need. Some of them you can make, i.e. adhesive and oil. However, metals become increasingly rare as you progress through the game. Some of them are stockpiled in respawning factories, such as steel, but aluminum and copper seem to almost run out at some point, and are needed to repair top-tier power armor. This may not seem like such a big deal at first, but considering companions can also chew through power armor like crazy, it almost seems as though the amazing functionality of it has its shining moment in the sun and then burns out as you progress further. Post-ending, I am often leaving my power armor behind at my favorite settlement just because it almost becomes more of a burden than its usefulness allows.
Last but not least, there are companions. This has to be my favorite game for them; to a point. They each have their own fun questlines and little backstories. However, I do have a few big issues with them. Their AI can get pretty annoying, with them constantly taking charge and running in the way of your precious shots. I have also encountered bugs galore with them repeating conversation paths ad infinitum every time I walk by them, as well as some with special items that seem to overencumber them when they're replaced. Overall, I want to say they're not worth it, but that's not entirely true because I think they should at the very least be played with until their questlines are finished.
So again, overall, I highly recommend this game. Even if the minor bugs and nitpicks I have were never fixed, in my own opinion there's no possible way that it could be considered a bad game. It might not be what everyone expects, but I think everyone should be allowed to get their own experience out of it, and have their own story.

I am re-writting this review after playing this a lot more.
There are two ways to view this game and that is why I am re-doing my review.
The first way is if you have never played a fallout game before.  You have no expectations at all from this game.
If this is the case, then this is a good game.  It is not a great game, but it is quite good.  It is an open world and there is a lot ot explore and there are many ways to build your character.  There is a fair amount of content to find and every once in a while you will run into an interesting story to experience.  It has a fairly good crafting system which is made much better if you installl mods, and you can even build your own settlements although this is mostly pointless as it doesn't really help you in game.
The second way to view this, which is what motivated my original review, is to view this as a sequel to a fallout game.  A series of games you are famillair with and you are most certainly bringing some expectations to this game.
With that in mind, this game is an abomination.  It is almost a total failure as a fallout game.  It is just a generic open world game set in the fallout universe.
At least to me, the major theme / point of a fallout game is your story as a player going throughout the world making your choices which have a real impact on the world.  You meet certain people and do certain things and affect the world in both grand and small ways.  You meet companions which have thier own agenda and quests.   When you finish the game, you get a summary of what your choices were and how things turned out.  If you met a dozen people and played a role in thier life, in the end you would get a dozen summaries on each person's life.  Certainly you would get one on the major choices you made.
None of that is in fallout 4.  Your choices really do not matter.  There are no companion quests.  There is no summary of things you did and the impact it had on the world.  You get the same generic ending no matter what your choices were.  It doesn't even both to mention the big choice (the faction you chose to support) in the ending sequence.
You could go on a killing spree and kill everyone in Diamond City and it wouldn't matter.  It is all pointless.
Then there is the introduction of the radiant quests.  If you have played elder scrolls games you may be famillair with these.  Basically they are randomly generated quests.  Go here and kill everyone.  Go there and recover an item (that wasn't there the first time you went).
These are terribly boring and they send you to the same places over and over.  I do not just mean the same NPC gives you the same quest again, but of the many NPCs that give their version of these radiant quests send you to the same places again and again.  Oh, go to the auto plant AGAIN and this time put up a listening device or recover some old world techology or just murder everyone there (even though you have done this 4x already).
It is all very generic.  The whole world.  There are some speical areas and questlines here and there, but they really tried to create a bunch of quest content via this radiant quest system.  It has nothing like the amount and quality of quests you got in Fallout NV and Fallout 3.
The converasion system is also just stupid.  It has been made to a set of 4 choices and here is the kicker, that 90% of the time your choices to do not matter.  There was one conversation I went through.  I could pick the easy path and make it to some conversation option, or I could pass 3 increasingly difficult speech checks and then end up at the exact same spot as the easy choice left me.  At best is just nets you some xp or sometimes a tiny bit more information.  However, once in a LONG while you can make a choice which does have some real (but not very significant) impact in the world.
To sum it up, Fallout 4 is just a very generic, somewhat bland open world game.  It is not really a fallout game, and if that is what you are really looking for then you may have to wait for fallout 5 because no amount of DLC or mods will turn this into a proper fallout game.

(note: I have actually played close to 50 hours of this game, mostly on a pre-release version)
It has been seven years since Bethesda last tackled the Fallout series, with the excellent spin-off sequel New Vegas being developed by Obsidian instead. One might expect in that time span Bethesda would have made an effort to work out some of the rather glaring wrinkles that made Fallout 3 and New Vegas feel so clunky. In some respects, they have; the shooting feels much better in Fallout 4, meaning that VATS is a sort of fallback option rather than your primary means of engaging enemies. They have also added some crafting elements that help incentivize exploration, which remains the best part of the game. However in most other regards, Fallout 4 is the same semi-broken, super ambitious open world game that Bethesda has been making since Oblivion; it has received a patchy new coat of paint and a few nice gameplay additions, but ultimately, it won’t change anyone’s minds about Bethesda’s brand of RPG.

Okay, let's get this out of the way.  Yes, this game has the usual Bethesda bugs.  Random texture issues, glitchy object awareness, even the occasional crash to desktop.  But, I will argue, the bugs aren't nearly as prevalent as in previous Bethesda games--here's lookin' at you, New Vegas.  Instead, what you're getting is a game with some bugs and a whole lot of really fantastic gameplay, woven throughout an engaging and thought-provoking story.
The Commonwealth is in kind of rough shape, what with the rampant raiders, Super Mutants, rumors of something called Synths supposedly sent by the shadowy Institute...but what really matters is much more personal.  You're a dweller from Vault 111, and within the first few minutes of gameplay you're struck with a terrible loss.  Now the only thing in your mind is to find those responsible, but in the meantime the whole of the Commonwealth seems to be crying out for your help.  What will you do?  Who will you be?  Can you recover what was lost, or will you need to try and begin again?
I'd recommend it wholeheartedly.

I just want to kick off this review by saying that this is an excellent game, and has surpassed all standards I set for it before playing. It absolutely has my recommendation, and there's no way that that could possibly be revoked.
Graphically it is stunning. Some people complain about it being oversaturated, or too dull, but I found it to be the perfect post-apocalyptic blend of browns and brights. The character design is a huge step up from recent Fallout titles, with creatures and other NPCs looking more detailed and lifelike than ever. That being said, the graphics are certainly not without their downsides. While the model and texture detail is absolutely stupendous, I must say the animations for these works of art are sadly lacking. Mouths move, if you can believe it, worse than I think they did in New Vegas, eyes are all but emotionless, and there are a lot of issues with the dynamic conversation camera snapping too close to objects. On top of this, I find it just a bit odd that Bethesda is a step away from requiring an absolute top-of-the-line rig for the content they have; it seems to me that, had they focused on optimization a bit more, they could have left room for so much more content on a much wider array of rigs than what they currently have, as beautiful as it is.
As far as the quests go, I was definitely not disappointed. I found myself pondering the repercussions of my actions, and feeling my heart wrenching out of my chest at several of the bigger decisions I was required to make. This game managed to make me FEEL a lot more than any other recent RPG has managed to do. I'm not going to spoil anything, but if Bethesda's goal was to make an excellent story with points at which you can feel the weight of a world upon your shoulders, then they certainly excelled.
Audio is as good as ever, almost like Fallout 3, New Vegas, or Skyrim with their respective ambient noises mods; however, what makes it really interesting, is rather than just hearing a nonexistant gunfight every so often rippling through the wastes, there are actually many faction wars raging on in the city practically nonstop. The Brotherhood of Steel will be hunting down their enemies, Supermutants will storm Raider camps, and Diamond City guards will encounter squads of Gunners looking for some energy cells.
This brings me to my next topic, crafting. The crafting system is pretty cool, though the novelty of it quickly wears off once you realize what a struggle it is to get certain resources. Forget the settlement object cap, for a minute, because I rarely ever have a problem with that. My main problem with crafting is the abundance of some of the resources that you always need. Some of them you can make, i.e. adhesive and oil. However, metals become increasingly rare as you progress through the game. Some of them are stockpiled in respawning factories, such as steel, but aluminum and copper seem to almost run out at some point, and are needed to repair top-tier power armor. This may not seem like such a big deal at first, but considering companions can also chew through power armor like crazy, it almost seems as though the amazing functionality of it has its shining moment in the sun and then burns out as you progress further. Post-ending, I am often leaving my power armor behind at my favorite settlement just because it almost becomes more of a burden than its usefulness allows.
Last but not least, there are companions. This has to be my favorite game for them; to a point. They each have their own fun questlines and little backstories. However, I do have a few big issues with them. Their AI can get pretty annoying, with them constantly taking charge and running in the way of your precious shots. I have also encountered bugs galore with them repeating conversation paths ad infinitum every time I walk by them, as well as some with special items that seem to overencumber them when they're replaced. Overall, I want to say they're not worth it, but that's not entirely true because I think they should at the very least be played with until their questlines are finished.
So again, overall, I highly recommend this game. Even if the minor bugs and nitpicks I have were never fixed, in my own opinion there's no possible way that it could be considered a bad game. It might not be what everyone expects, but I think everyone should be allowed to get their own experience out of it, and have their own story.

Let's start with a short review with the big questions people might be wondering.
Does it live up to the hype? No.
Is it fun and enjoyable; can I sink many hours into it? Absolutely.
Is it worth the money? Yes, it is.
Is this Fallout 3.5? No.
Is it a good game? Yes.
8/10.
---------------------------------
Still here? Okay, let's move on to a more detailed list of pros and cons.
Pros:
+Generally Fun Gameplay
+Some Great Characters
+Great Exploration
+Character Customisation ROCKS. (Though... come on. I wanted purple hair.)
+Brilliant Companions (Apart from Preston.)
+Innovative in some areas
+Improved AI from Fallout 3. It's still kinda bad, but a whole lot better.
+Improved animations from Fallout 3. They're still kinda bad, but a whole lot better.
+Improved 3rd Person from Fallout 3. It's still kinda bad, but a whole lot better.
+Settlements feature is surprisingly fun and immersive.
+Immersive Graphics (If not next gen, they're still good. The graphics are NOT bad.)
+New Pip-Boy rocks. Has some charming animations with sounds to go with them, too.
+Dogmeat rocks. So does Codsworth. (Speaking of Dogmeat, you can make him equip bandanas and dog armour. Brilliant.)
+Some hilarious and original areas/events to find
+The 'Legendary Enemies' system is actually pretty great.
+Quicksaving. A real godsend feature.
Cons:
-Less Roleplaying
-Voiced protagonist. You don't feel like you're playing YOUR character.
-Some Awful Characters
-Game feels very linear AT TIMES - (NOT ALL THE TIME.)
-Poor PC Controls/Optimisation
-Feels a little rushed and incomplete
-Disgusting lack of Resolutions for a Triple-A game. Honestly.
-Feels 'dumbed down' in general. (Can be a Pro if you're more into action over immersion.)
-Minutemen quests feel so... ugh. UGHHH. It's like they're talking to a three-year-old how to do stuff just UGH.
-They removed skills. No. Bad Bethesda.
-You find POWER ARMOUR and a MINIGUN at the start of the game. Wow. Seriously? Like... seriously? Thanks for removing that element of challenge and excitement for when I finally get the super-awesome badass power armour. Dear God... whoever scripted that needs a word.
-My character doesn't speak like a dumbass when he has 1 Intelligence. I was really hoping for that to be a thing.
----------------------------------
Anyway. Let's get down to a real review. If the rules of 'TL;DR' apply to you, go away. And let me get one thing straight for some of the salty members: I am NOT a fanboy of Bethesda. This is just an honest review.
So, as I'm sure we'll all know, this game started off with a bunch of negative reviews regarding to everyone being dissapointed with the bugs, voiced protagnist stuff, and generally it not living up to the hype. It's a real shame what 'hype' can cause - because if they realised this game out of nowhere (or through a fairly quick deadline with little trailers), I'm sure people would love this game.
And yes, Fallout 4 does have bugs, but it's rare to get some that are gamebreaking. Most of the time they're just funny as hell and will make you mutter 'Oh, Bethesda...' to yourself with amusement. Such as my dog grabbing a raider and somehow making said raider ascend into the heavens then fall to his death. The lack of resolutions is utter garbadge on Bethesda's part, and I'm hoping they can do their best to fix that.
The game also feels somewhat... unfinished. It's almost as if it's been rushed a little. Serious reviewers who are going giddy with the '10/10 flawless game'♥♥♥♥♥♥♥need to get their head out of their arses. It IS a good game. But come on! It's not flawless, and 'mods will fix it' is not a valid excuse.
The voiced protagonist CAN be garbadge. But sometimes (those few moments I cherish dearly) the voiced protagnist says stuff how I want him to. And he can even say funny stuff now and again! But yes, in general, the voiced protagnist isn't really something anyone will hold dear. It's almost as if they were desperate to add some sort of NEW FEATURE to make this game classed as ooooh 'Next Gen'. I haven't tried the female voice actor yet, so that's my opinion on the voice acting on the male voice actor's part.
They also removed the karma system. ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥te. Like seriously, if there's one thing I'm super salty about, it's the removal of the karma system. I'm sure many feel the same way as me. Like... wow. Seriously?! You REMOVED the KARMA SYSTEM from FALLOUT? Holy♥♥♥♥♥♥ I remember actually feeling a little bit bad because of that sinister sound when I stole something. But now, when someone turns their back - ooh - I'll have that duct tape. Literally no consequences if they don't see you do it.
Some die-hard Fallout Fans who loved getting immersed and roleplaying as THEIR character will be deeply dissapointed in this game. But you have to accept the facts that the roleplaying elements have really been dumbed down. As for the story... pah! The story isn't anything special or whatever but it's enough to give you SOME motivation.
But hey. In terms of rushes of fun, combat, and a sense of progression and accomplishment - this game nails it.
The combat is sleek, with VATS making a re-appearance. Whilst VATS doesn't freeze time in an insanely overpowered way anymore, the feature is still useful and gets you out of many sticky situations, whilst it isn't enough to save your life in the most dire of situations anymore. The new critical system is also pretty dang good, with Luck being a perk I actually kind of want now.
Unlocking new perks is exciting and entertaining, and levelling up feels damn great. There are a TON of ways to build and play your character combat-wise, which is a nice touch. You can go for an all-rounder, or really specialise in one part of combat and suck at the rest. It feels 'new' and 'fresh' from Fallout 3, which is why I scoff when people suggest this game is Fallout 3.5. Sure, Fallout 4 could've had more time and love put into it, and perhaps they shouldn't have gone with an early deadline, but this game is a HUGE leap from Modless Fallout 3.
Stealth is also REALLY improved and much more fun to specalise in. Raiders panic when they see their dead friends, and will often nervously converse with each other whilst you're skulking around. Don't get me wrong, Raiders still possess around 80IQ, but they can now flank, do more battle tactics, and really catch you out with grenades and molotovs. Melee combat is also much better, with raiders taunting, feinting, blocking, etc. Melee duels feel great on this game - much better than on Fallout 3 where you were just tapping one button over and over again, occasionally using VATS to enlighten your experience somewhat.
The gore also rocks and feels great. Blowing someone's head up in a Fallout game got around... 43% more satisfying, I'd say.
You know what? I think I'll end it here. I've said what needs to be said, and if I carry on, I'll just end up making one of those crappy 10/10 jokes everywhere. The game is an 8/10, with less RPG, more Action than Fallout 3. It's a huge leap up from Fallout 3 (mostly for the better, though I can't stress how BS the removal of Karma is), with some great new features, a great and well-designed new area, better graphics, and general improvements in most combat fronts.
It's a great game, and 93 out of 100 people WILL have fun. You can sink a lot of hours into it, and if you the follow the rule of £1 = 1 hour of gameplay, I'm sure you'll get your money's worth.
You might be dissapointed somewhat initially, but you'll get over all the BS, adapt to Bethesda's new rules (as BS as some of them are), and have a bloody good time. See you in the wastes, wanderer.

My experience started out terribly. It took me 2 days to figure out how to get the game running. [The game doesnt run in fullscreen mode, apparently] But aside from technical difficulties at the start, my experience has been wonderful.
I am a huge fan of TESV: Skyrim, and I had extremely high hopes for this game, expecting a story as rich as Skyrim's without the bugs and clutter. So far, very few bugs, everything clips fairly well, unlike Fallout 3, which was a nightmare for me, being a graphics enthusiast. The game is very resource intensive, but my gaming laptop scrapes by on the high setting with 50 fps. The graphics are great, far exceeding default Skyrim graphics, and just shy of my modded Skyrim graphics. The only bothering graphical glitch is if you approach an object (usually doors or buildings), their texture will remain in the low-quality state it is shown as from a distance. Another minor glitch is that the PipBoy light does not create any shadows. Aside from this, Fallout 4 has few bugs, and has resolved issues seen in Skyrim. I did find it bothersome, and quite obvious, that Fallout 4 uses the exact same engine as Skyrim, with some environmental improvements, such as improved shadows, and what appears to be a built-in ENB preset, where light shows density and depth more clearly.
My experience with Fallout 3 was disastrous because of the cluttered, incomplete, and compact Pip-Boy interface. Fallout 4 was little better. Unlike skyrim, item stats are not shown when mousing over objects, and the inventory lacks advanced sorting techniques. However, the HUD and damage system is much clearer and simpler than in Fallout 3.
Power armor, although more immersive now, is a nightmare to repair and properly use. You can no longer pick up all the pieces, there is a frame, which cannot be picked up. All the armor pieces, without the frame, are useless. So if you frequently change armors to adapt to various situations, avoid power armor. I will applaud the shift from armor to vehicle, and the new power armor HUD that shows damage to each part, as well as various guages. Very immersive, but hard to manage.
Stimpaks. The bane of my existence. Carry 30+ at all times, they go quickly. Although more effective than in Fallout NV and Fallout 3, they still lack the ability of a heal-all-cure-all remedy. There is an animation for using a stimpak now, and they are administered after exiting your inventory, so if you apply them just before taking a lethal blow, you will still die. Although this is significantly more immersive, it has moments of irritation inducing failure.
Love the new crafting system and settlement system. The only issue is that I always seem to carry more clutter than I would in any other Bethesda game. Leave no wonderglue behind. Leave no clutter untouched. Pick it all up and store it in a workbench. You WILL need it eventually. The repair system has also been removed, instead weapons do not break or decrease in quality over use, but you can modify them to have bayonets, sights, grips, etc. Creative crafting system, but messy.
Intro cutscene was powerful. It blew me away in the best ways.
This installment of the Fallout series is special, because it gives a glimpse of life before the bombs drop. A world locked in a whimsical 1950's future comic, nuclear powered everything, and of course the shadow of communism in the far east. Without giving any spoilers, your character is a resident of Boston, in 2077, you get to design your character, and briefly explore your house, before a rude interruption. More dynamic and informative than Skyrim or Fallout 3, as far as intro sequences go.
Character creation is the Skyrim system but more direct. No more bars, just direct pull and push and sculpting. But the one thing that has bothered my through every Bethesda game I have ever touched: There are only like 10 hairstyles and theyre always the same. Come on, Bethesda, you've had so long to give us good hairstyles.
The story is very good, well developed, good characters, great voice acting coupled with interesting locations and quests. Nothing to say specifically, as to not spoil the story.
After my experiences with Skyrim and Fallout 3, I must say that Fallout 4 exceeded some of my expectations, and alone it is a great game with exceptional framework. This being said, the game's wide spread of new details adds complication, and the game lacks in significant variability from other Fallout games. Bethesda has come such a long way, but if they want to make an award-winning game in the future, they will have to beat this one.

Fallout is a franchise I grew up with. I played original Fallout and loved it. That's when it all started. I was enchanted by the vision of 50's USA burned to a crisp by nuclear missiles, with it's population still struggling, forming communities, preserving as much civilisation as they can. When Fallout 3 came around the artistic vision was realised in an even more vivid form. I explored Capital Wasteland through and through. Of course it had its flaws. Same with New Vegas. Now playing Fallout 4 I have a feeling, concept of post-apocalyptic RPG was realised to the fullest. Gameplay is greatly improved upon previous instances of the game. It's more dynamic and player feels more flexible, especially when you discover there is actually a cover system implemented in the game. Voicing the player character added a lot of depth to the story, which is quite engaging. Side quests retain great quality. It's hard not to mention the addition of building mode. You can build and maintain your own settlements which adds tons of fun to game already insanely rich in content. You can also mod your weapons and customise power armor. Game runs alright even on weaker PC's. My Lenovo Y580 runs it on low settings and it still looks good. My desktop PC on the other hand runs it on high without hiccups. It's certainly one of the best games in the series and a strong contender for the title of the best game of 2015.

Things I like and dislike.
I like that it's a fallout game. I'm a fan of the series. It still had elements of the "fallout formula." Such as large, open world, and choices to make. However, the game's core design in SPECIAL is dumbed down, skills are now just put a point in it and you're good to go. There is no tagging of skills and the amount of special points assigned is less. Additionally, there is no reason to replay the game. There is no karma mechanic. There is no low intelligence mechanic. The way you choose to play the game is totally up to you, but no matter how you play the game, the dialogue will be exactly the same.The marketing team for Fallout 4 did an astounding job. It was well met, and well hyped through the release of the Fallout Shelter App for mobile platform and the usage of the Pip-Boy App. They definitely deserve a raise. However, the newest rendition of fallout caters to a wider, more diverse crowd as shown through a lot of original mechanics that were available in Fallout 3 and Fallout New Vegas have been drastically dumbed down. Unfortunately, this results in little to no meaning to creating a new character.
All in all. It's still a great game and enjoyable to play. At least the first time through. If I was allowed to leave numbered reviews, it would be a 7/10.
