This is the most sandbox sandbox game in vanilla form. Sure, Skyrim with a couple hundred mods might contain more 'sand' if you will, but Fallout 4 on it's own is a step up over Fallout 3 in virtually every way.
The biggest improvement is the gunplay, the makers brought in some developers from Halo to give all the guns a nice heft, and sound, and it clearly shows from the very beginnging. The first gun you get is the 10mm, despite being the first gun it's bulky and scary looking with a great sound. In other Fallout 3 it kind of felt like you were playing airsoft the first dozen hours, but that is gone.
VATS took a giant step in the right direction. They nerfed it (Time doesn't stop like it did in FO3) but it's more than ok for how much more polish it has. It's no longer the incredibly OP end all mechanic, it's the slightly OP mechanic that looks way cooler, and I am more than OK with that.
The leveling system is vastly improved compared to FO3, and rivals the FO2 leveling system which has been near and dear to my heart since I was but a wee child. FO3 used a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ized version of the FO2 leveling system, which was overly streamlined to the point of High Intelligence characters maxxing all their tagged skills around level 4 or 5, and a perk every 3 to 4 levels. Now you get to choose between stats and perks EVERY level, and the skills are now pure byproducts of your stats, and cannot be leveled directly (sorry sneak and small arms, we had some good times).
The cons don't come close to outweighing the vast pros to this game, but for some of my friends the bugs I faced would be game ending. As with all tremendously massive Bethesda, more bugs than usual slipped through the cracks compared to your average game. This wasn't my first rodeo, hell, I even remembered the no clip consle command from Bethesda RPGs of old. Unfortunately for me, most of the bugs I encountered were at the very end, and severely dampened the final experience for me.
However, these kinds of games are far more about the Journey than the destination, and this Journey is an absolute must for anyone looking for a modern, immersive RPG experience.

In a word, tedious. I am accustomed to Besthesda's open-world games to FEEL open, but Fo4 is by far the most claustrophobic and repetitive of any of their games I've played. In the 70+ hours I put into this game, I never got a sense there was a genuine or satisfying diversity of playstyle - essentially every fight in this game is a horde, Dragon Age 2 style, and after the first 20 hours it gets to be a real slog. Navigating is painful since debris is used extensively to narrow your routes, and I -hate- this design choice. It's suffocating.
I never go into a Bethesda game expecting good writing, but for me to walk away from 70 hours with absolutely no emotional investment in anything for the entirety of it is really inexcusable. Every character and questline I followed was bland at best, and utterly nonsensical at its worst. I had a very hard time considering anyone I encountered in this game to be a fully fleshed out character with believable human qualities. Bethesda has never been good about this, but it's time they address this issue because it's hard to feel immersed when no one I encounter has any real emotional range whatsoever.
On the plus side, they finally hired more than 2 voice actors, and the crafting for weapons was pretty cool. Armor was sort annoying in terms of what you could wear at once time and what you couldn't (this is especially unclear when purchasing pieces from shops which have no indication of what can have pieces worn over it and what can't). Town building should have been A++ addition for me, but I found it to be a huge chore and one of the least rewarding crafting/designing experiences I've ever had in any game. It's not enough that everything is hideous, it's that your options are sorely limited, and if you play the game the way they want you to and rebuild every town perfectly you're going to be scavenging like a beast... which is another obnoxious feature. It gets incredibly tedious to try and haul back every single knickknack with a weight limit just to be able to build something that is going to look horrible regardless. And the rewards? There weren't any, so far as I could tell, unless you're the type of person who feels gratified to have placed enough shacks to get his village numbers up. Construction wise it's far too limited to give you the satisfaction of doing something creative.
The biggest dealbreaker for me, though, was how personally unrewarding it felt to explore. In Skyrim, exploring was the main draw. You weren't just exploring for loot, you were exploring for entire experiences. You won't find that in Fo4, because all your experiences are going to be the same: you go in, you shoot 50 guys, you leave. Nothing is visually, thematically, or emotionally engaging in the slightest. Between the constant resource gathering and the
I genuinely felt like I was playing an MMO without friends. By the end, I was in a rush to finish this game and never play it again. This game should've at least been "good." I can't call it that. It will probably be good when the modding community fixes it, but if you need your playerbase to make your game *playable*, you're doing it wrong.

I have real mixed feeling about this game. In many ways it's a huge improvment.
The combat is fantastic, added with modding, you'l want to go to a big battle to see how your new toy work, and you want to improve your wepones so you can enjoy the big battles.
The armor system is interesting and maybe the only part the got more complex. There are now 3 layers of armor - clothing (that can't be modded most of the time) body armor (Skyrim style, can be modded) and if you want (And you do) power armor. The power armor is now a tank, I think this is a fantastic choice that fit the lore and make it so much more fun wearing them. People will be aware of it in dialog wich is a nice touch.
My problome is that it is a very thin game. You can see they put lot of love into it, but they may put it at the wrong place. It's an open world RPG - the meat of the game is less the combat and mainly exploration - so the world must be full of fun quests and interesting location, and sadly it dose not.
Don't get me wrong, when you do found a good quest or a place with backstory - it is fantastic and well made. But it's so hard to found any of them. Most of the time you get fillers - some randome ruin #402 with enemy faction #6 , or even worst - fetch quests.
Fallout 3 might have a small game world, but it felt alive (well...dead, but you know). Every location is here for worldbuilding and every quest is something crazy to do that can take hourse.
None of that in here.
So in short - better gameplay but the fun factor is rarely there. It can be fixed with DLC and moddings - but if you ask me it should come in the vanilla, But if you going to buy it -and you should - don't shy away from modding as you get most of your game from there.

In this game, you cannot kill anyone.
Obviously that's an exaggeration, but Bethesda didn't bother to flesh out alternate routes based on killing people who are related to questlines, which is an issue they've always had, but here it at least seems worse than ever before. They don't even give you the chance to screw up and lock yourself out of quests by killing people or by having allies die. The central narrative is what drives the game, as opposed to freedom of choice and failure.
Honestly, this doesn't make it an outright bad game, I'm sure that the vast majority of people who played New Vegas favored the NCR and always tried to get the most
positive outcome, while not killing anyone important that they're not told to. It wouldn't be surprising that most people are not bothered by these limitations. However at many moments it stands to hinder it greatly and break immersion completely.
Take a situation like when you first enter a certain town:  You can just murder the first person you see because they're an ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and they tried to rob you. However, while the NPCs will react to this action, this is the only major interaction with this character and killing them or not doesn't change much of anything. Later when you enter into the bar, you will come across a mercenary speaking with a pair of thugs. Even more ridiculous that the mercenary gives you a quest to go kill them not long after this exchange.
The endings are shallow and samey and nothing that you do seems to really feel like it matters.

In a word, tedious. I am accustomed to Besthesda's open-world games to FEEL open, but Fo4 is by far the most claustrophobic and repetitive of any of their games I've played. In the 70+ hours I put into this game, I never got a sense there was a genuine or satisfying diversity of playstyle - essentially every fight in this game is a horde, Dragon Age 2 style, and after the first 20 hours it gets to be a real slog. Navigating is painful since debris is used extensively to narrow your routes, and I -hate- this design choice. It's suffocating.
I never go into a Bethesda game expecting good writing, but for me to walk away from 70 hours with absolutely no emotional investment in anything for the entirety of it is really inexcusable. Every character and questline I followed was bland at best, and utterly nonsensical at its worst. I had a very hard time considering anyone I encountered in this game to be a fully fleshed out character with believable human qualities. Bethesda has never been good about this, but it's time they address this issue because it's hard to feel immersed when no one I encounter has any real emotional range whatsoever.
On the plus side, they finally hired more than 2 voice actors, and the crafting for weapons was pretty cool. Armor was sort annoying in terms of what you could wear at once time and what you couldn't (this is especially unclear when purchasing pieces from shops which have no indication of what can have pieces worn over it and what can't). Town building should have been A++ addition for me, but I found it to be a huge chore and one of the least rewarding crafting/designing experiences I've ever had in any game. It's not enough that everything is hideous, it's that your options are sorely limited, and if you play the game the way they want you to and rebuild every town perfectly you're going to be scavenging like a beast... which is another obnoxious feature. It gets incredibly tedious to try and haul back every single knickknack with a weight limit just to be able to build something that is going to look horrible regardless. And the rewards? There weren't any, so far as I could tell, unless you're the type of person who feels gratified to have placed enough shacks to get his village numbers up. Construction wise it's far too limited to give you the satisfaction of doing something creative.
The biggest dealbreaker for me, though, was how personally unrewarding it felt to explore. In Skyrim, exploring was the main draw. You weren't just exploring for loot, you were exploring for entire experiences. You won't find that in Fo4, because all your experiences are going to be the same: you go in, you shoot 50 guys, you leave. Nothing is visually, thematically, or emotionally engaging in the slightest. Between the constant resource gathering and the
I genuinely felt like I was playing an MMO without friends. By the end, I was in a rush to finish this game and never play it again. This game should've at least been "good." I can't call it that. It will probably be good when the modding community fixes it, but if you need your playerbase to make your game *playable*, you're doing it wrong.

I have real mixed feeling about this game. In many ways it's a huge improvment.
The combat is fantastic, added with modding, you'l want to go to a big battle to see how your new toy work, and you want to improve your wepones so you can enjoy the big battles.
The armor system is interesting and maybe the only part the got more complex. There are now 3 layers of armor - clothing (that can't be modded most of the time) body armor (Skyrim style, can be modded) and if you want (And you do) power armor. The power armor is now a tank, I think this is a fantastic choice that fit the lore and make it so much more fun wearing them. People will be aware of it in dialog wich is a nice touch.
My problome is that it is a very thin game. You can see they put lot of love into it, but they may put it at the wrong place. It's an open world RPG - the meat of the game is less the combat and mainly exploration - so the world must be full of fun quests and interesting location, and sadly it dose not.
Don't get me wrong, when you do found a good quest or a place with backstory - it is fantastic and well made. But it's so hard to found any of them. Most of the time you get fillers - some randome ruin #402 with enemy faction #6 , or even worst - fetch quests.
Fallout 3 might have a small game world, but it felt alive (well...dead, but you know). Every location is here for worldbuilding and every quest is something crazy to do that can take hourse.
None of that in here.
So in short - better gameplay but the fun factor is rarely there. It can be fixed with DLC and moddings - but if you ask me it should come in the vanilla, But if you going to buy it -and you should - don't shy away from modding as you get most of your game from there.

I am new to the Fallout franchise, so unlike many other reviewers I am coming at this with a fresh set of eyes.  I also consider myself a casual gamer so I don't have the expertise that many other reviewers have.
First off, the game is stunning.  I find it vividly beautiful and rank it up there with Skyrim.  Would I say that the graphics are better then Skyrim? Maybe.  To be honest I can't much tell the difference and it really doesn't matter.  Character design and detail is better than Skyrim.  Although there are some lip syncing issues this is a minor nit to pick at.  Overall it looks good.
As for gameplay, I am a fan.  The gunplay aspects and VATS are strait forward and easy to understand.  The RPG elements are at the level I like, some customization but I am not overwhelmed trying to optimize a character perfectly.  The game is easy to understand and gets you right to the story instead of fiddling with a whole bunch of piddly things.  I don't much care for the base construction at this point but I could see its appeal after completing the story.
Speaking of story, having only put about 13 hours into the game at the time of writing this review I cannot comment on the whole thing.  What I can say is that the story and world are engrossing.  there always appears to be something to do and I have not yet felt that nagging feeling I generally get in longer games of 'Why do I care again?' or 'Do we really have to go through these steps?'.
All in all I would say that if you are new to fallout as I am, you can't go wrong with this game.  I am also hoping that any DLC really adds to the story, but we will wait and see.

I love all the Fallout and Elder Scrolls games, and while I would say I love this game also, because there is still so much good things in it, I just can't give this game the thumbs up because of the direction Bethesda has gone with it, and it makes me fear the future of the series and even more the Elder Scrolls series.
There are many improvements to the game in my opinion. The world and the environment are the best and most interesting yet I have seen in a Bethesda game. The world have got a great colorful style and feels extremely good designed, I would say this gameworld is just below to Rapture in  Bioshock in regards to design.
Combat is also improved and I feel that the companions are more lifelike and involved then before, commenting on things and feeling like real characters (even though they can be in the way sometime)
Now what I have a problem with (and many many other people) is the dialogue system and the voiced protagnoist. The Bethesda RPG games have always stood out from the competition, in the regards that their games have feelt like true RPG:s. There are many other games with the RPG label on them, like Mass Effect and The Witcher etc. But these games are still very streamlined and I would not say that they are an RPG on the same level as a previous Elder Scrolls or Fallout game. Now with Fallout 4, it feels very much like instead of continue to do their own thing, Bethesda is trying to ape after these games. And the result just does not work. You feel extremely limited in what kind of character you can make and what you can say. There is simply not much room to go outside the "predefined" character in this game. Forget to try to play an evil character. Also the voiced protagonist makes it even worse since it can be totally immersion breaking every time you see your character speak if you try to have a character that is anything else then a goodie goodie father.
To have had the voiced protagonist work, Bethesda would have had to record at least 5-10 different voices for each gender that you could pick from depending on what kind of character you would want to play as. You could have the goodie-goodie voice over, or the killer, or the geek, etc etc.
I really don't like the direction this is going. Even though the game in all other regards is great and I will spend hundreds of hours in it. Bethesda should continue to be unique in the industry. They really lost something and I just hope they understand that this is not the way to go. Currently the user metacritc score for this game is around the low 5-6.
I honestly don't think that people think the game is that bad, it is though a very strong indicator that many many people are very displeased and worried by the direction Bethesda seems to be going with this game.

The easy review would be to say if you liked Fallout 3 (the base game), you'll like Fallout 4. That's probably a general truism but a game like this deserves more. So read on....
Overall Opinion: Good but not great
Caveat: I once lived in Quincy, MA and I am familiar with the area. Thus I'll get certain jokes (Fallon's Basement is a take-off of Filene's Basement which is a famous local shopping landmark) and certain areas have a natural appeal to me because I lied there. YMMV. Of course, I lived in Washington DC as well so I got much of the inside stuff in FO3.
- - - - - - - - - -
Fallout 4 is a pretty flawed product for so many reasons.
- It's very combat-heavy, even more so than FO3. Thus it's often less of a RPG and more of a bad shooter at times.
- The pacing is off and early in the game you often have only a couple of quests to work on. You really don't get going in the game until you hit Diamond City, which is going to take 10+ hours of gameplay to get to for many people. As such, the intital areas can feel aimless and it's enough to put you off. 10-15 hours is a pretty big investment of time just to get things really going.
- It does a poor job of explaining both how and why to do certain things (like building your Sanctuary and other little towns). I've had to look up the key just to exit my power armor. I still don't understand what benefit I get out of building these villages (and boy does that get REPETITIVE after a while).
- Some things (like the aformentioned Sanctuary) feel more like a bolt-on to the game and weren't well integrated.
- The interface is awful for the PC. I didn't think Bethesda could make a worse UI after trying to muck with Skyrim's. I was wrong. This one is worse.
- The world building is certainly an achievement but I don't feel it's as good as the - Capital Wasteland in FO3 and pales in comparison to the monumental world-building achievement of Skyrim. Because it's very urban, you don't often get the breathtaking vistas of prior games. There's too much tramping around in shut-in areas or narrow building corridors and a lot less wide open exploration.
- Because of the base building, you need to keep looting junk and therefore run into the incredibly annoying encumbrance limits (to the point that I used a console command so I could carry more weight).
- Voiced protagonist/dialog options - I always think that having a voiced protagonist is a mistake in these games because it limits the dialog options and removes RPG aspects. FO4 is no exception. So not only do I get shorter dialog options but I have to listen to someone else acting it out rather than hearing my own character in my mind. So for instance, during a critical, emotional confrontation about 20 hours in, I had to listen to a voice actor screaming lines whereas I had pictured and played my character as someone who goes almost ice-cold in such situations. It's incredibly jarring.
- Furthermore, the dialog options are presented as a summary and at times what is said isn't what I really thought would be said by the summary option selected.
Other people have decried performance issues, bland companions (they didn't bother me though they weren't Bioware-quality), the new skill trees/SPECIAL system and so forth. I didn't have any issues with these but I can understand their opinions.
Ok then, why recommend it with all of these negatives? Because it's still Fallout. It's still a massive achievement in world building and it greatly rewards exploration (which is my favorite part of games like these). It still tells a decent and often compelling tale of a wasteland wanderer. There are more quests later, which help provide direction in the mid-game. FO4 still compels me to see what's in the next building or around the next corner. I remain engaged in this interesting, weird and depressing world that is the USA stuck in the 1950s with the technology of the 2070s. I care about this universe...and FO4's faults aren't bad enough to make me not care.
In addition, Bethesda has added some cool things to the game.
- There are a handful of set-piece encounters in the game that are thrilling to fight. Walk into a certain park in the middle of Boston and you'll find out what I mean...
- Enemies are smarter and some of the ways they spawn are really interesting. No longer are ferals just wandering around. Instead, they might crawl in through windows, down walls or stir when someone comes into a room. These small touches make the world more fun and believable.
- The world is beautiful. As I said, it's not magical in the way that Skyrim was but it is an incredible achievement.
- The sound is even better. From far-off gunshots to groans to hearing the "I Don't Want to Set the World on Fire" song again (by the Inkspots) or "Butcher Pete" (Roy Brown), this is easily the best sounding Fallout game.
- The crafting system is pretty cool. I like being able to tailor a weapon to specifically fit my style of play. The armor system isn't as good but it's still a step up.
- The radiation storms are really neat...I'd love these to be far more dangerous though.  :)
I imagine DLCs will only help to improve this game with more focused content areas (The Pitt in FO3 was excellent in this regard) and of course you know the mod community will have a field day with it. But as it is, I don't have any regrets about buying this at full price.
PS - I also got the Prima Survival Guide for FO4. It's not bad but it's not as good as the ones for FO3 or New Vegas.

I doubt my review will ever be seen by anyone, but my long standing love affair with bethesda demands that I put effort into this review.
I have mixed feelings about F04. So many parts of this game are brilliant, and I feel like bethesda has a team with some of the most gifted individuals in the industry. And I feel like the rest of the team is trying desperately to hold them back.
TL;RL The environment, effects, and sound design are ♥♥♥♥ing brilliant. The game systems are generic, unfun  and dissapointing.
+The world is massive, and so many locations in it are beautiful. If you have the machine to let it do its thing, the game is absolutely stunning.
+The people who designed the world are obviously talented, gifted level designers. Interesting scenarios, small precious bits of interaction (when you step on a scale, an otherwise meaningless piece of junk, the internal wheel actually spins and changes) are everywhere.
+Combat FEELS better. Shooting things feels much less plastic, and the combat related effects and animations are (still off) great for a bethesda game.
But the GAME systems themselves are rubbish. This is not an RPG. This is a first person shooter with stats. Your chracter is railroaded down one of several faction quest lines, you have no moral freedom, and no matter how you build your character, no matter what stats or perks you take, you always play the same character: The guy who kills stuff for other people. It is literally impossible (for the first time in any bethesda game ever to my knowledge) to make a non-combat character. All of the combat is put into the unsatisfying (albeit better) gunplay. With no skills, and level requirements on the perks that replaced them, you can hardly even specialize your character.
This game is well made in many respects, and so much of the team deserved the wanton praise that it is recieving, but the game designers do not. This is a good game. This is a shockingly bad RPG, especially from the company who has been paving the way for true RPGs in the public eye for fifteen years.
RIP bethesda RPG IP.

I’ve decided to rewrite this review because I’ve played Fallout 4 more extensively and my opinion of it changed.  Steams stupidly small review length is why this doesn’t feel more fleshed out.  Sorry.
This is not a game for Fallout/RPG fans.  This is a game for people who don't care about either of them.
I paid around 150 USD for this game and wanted to get my money’s worth.  Apparently this is not possible.  This is one of the most insulting video games I’ve ever played, and a slap in the face to anyone who has played a Fallout game before.  Bethesda decided to pander to the casuls who like the same generic garbage they got last time, instead of improving on their tired old formula.  Fallout 4 is not an RPG.  It’s not a Bethesda game.  It’s not a Fallout game.  It’s generic cliched FPS open world farcry shooting game #489, and it barely even works that way.
Do you remember when Fallout games where RPG’s? Where your choices had a real effect on the world around you? Do you remember when the choices you made during gameplay actively affected quest lines and companion interactions? Do you remember when you could end a war with a tyrannous  faction using words and emotion rather than brute strength? Well, Bethesda decided to forget all of that.  There are no choices to make in Fallout 4.  All options eventually lead the same way.  You have absolutely no say in where the story goes, and this is made even worse with the addition of the dialogue wheel.  Each option: “YES”, “NO”, “SARCASTIC”, and “WHAT?” all mean yes in Bethesda’s eyes.  No matter what you choose, the game will FORCE you to play it the way it WANTS you to play it: As the good guy.
Even worse, you can’t roleplay as YOUR character.  The character you play as already has a voice, a wife, a history, and a mission.  What’s the point of even letting us make our own character? We can’t be him.  We can’t make our own decisions because the game won’t let us.  There’s a reason why New Vegas’s story was so short, because it wasn’t important.  What was important was how YOU the PLAYER interacted with the world, and the main quest just showed  how the world would eventually end up due to your actions.  Your actions don’t mean♥♥♥♥♥♥in Fallout 4 despite the fact that the game forces you to make them.  Nothing you do has an effect on the world around you.  When the game tells you to help settlements, it will respawn enemies in the same place for you to kill all over again, so what’s the point?
I didn’t mind the dialogue wheel at first.  I assumed Bethesda was making it easier for console players and controller users to make their selections easier during conversation.  Unfortunately, Bethesda ♥♥♥♥ed that up, and instead we get 4 options that are all the same.  And why are the explanations so short?  Why should I have to GUESS what MY CHARACTER is going to say.  What the hell does SARCASTIC mean?  Is that positive or negative? Am I going to be rude to them or make a joke? This would be a huge problem, unfortunately, the game doesn’t make what you said matter so it doesn’t mean anything in the end anyway.
The combat is fun at first glance.  But due to the fact that every quest is the same, “Go here.  Talk to someone.  Go there.  Talk to someone else.  Go there. Shoot things. Go back. Talk to the guy again.” , it gets monotonous very quickly.  It’s casualized to the point where it feels like Bethesda ripped ideas from other games instead of coming up with something unique and new.  Hitmarks, grenade prompts, orthodox sprint options, etc.  The game stops becoming fun when all you’re doing is the same thing over and over again.
The glitches and graphical options and slowdowns and poor performance don’t bother me that much.  What does bother me, is that people will defend♥♥♥♥♥♥for absolutely no reason, when there is nothing to like here.  Nothing new.  Nothing original.  Please don’t defend garbage like this because you don’t agree with my points.  Defend it when you can actually back them up.  This game is a letdown because it fell short of what was ALREADY ACHIEVED SEVEN YEARS AGO.
This game is a tragedy.  It makes me very upset to even think about it, because they hyped this game up so much.  They promised so much.  “No loading screens”, “Your choices matter”.
“Their most ambitious RPG to date”.
It’s disappointing when you consider the fact that it took them 7 years to take something that was great and stripped everything that was great out of it and didn’t replace it with anything.  This is a framework.  There’s no substance here, no soul.  It doesn’t have staying power.  I can guarantee that if this game didn’t have the fallout title attached to it it would have disappeared into obscurity because there isn’t anything new here.
It’s the same♥♥♥♥♥♥we’ve been getting for years.  Please don’t buy into the hype.  It isn’t worth it.  It certainly wasn’t for me.

It's only been a week since Fallout 4's release date, yet the question millions of gamers have asked themselves was, is this better than Fallout 3 and New Vegas. Fallout 3 is still my favorite game over New Vegas and Fallout 4, and I will cover the reasons why Fallout 4 doesn't quite live up to the expectations in comparison to its predecessor.
Slightly Restricted Freedom:
While Bethesda's highlights at E3 swore commitment to complete freedom at the player's discretion, Fallout 4 feels more restrictive in minor changes of gameplay. A particularly reason is how you are unable to kill certain NPCs because they are essential to a quest. In Fallout 3, the only ones you couldn't kill were children for legal reasons. While this change is fairly minor, it is extremely disatisfying not being able to kill certain NPCs for the hell of it. (No references for spoiler purposes) While Fallout 4 may have added more minature quests to complete, the vast majority of them are so quick to clear that it does not feel beneficial or well worth to go out of your way and hunt down these quests. Many just involve clearing a building which I would have done anyways for exploration purposes. Exploration in Fallout 4 retains the same joy as Fallout 3 with end game goals of finding every single location in the Fallout 4 map. The addition of improved graphics, and actual changing weather immerses you in the world which was a definite plus. The biggest con for me in player freedom was the disadvantage of player level. In Fallout 3, you could max Small Guns, Sneak, and Medicine and be completely fine throughout the wasteland. You would essentially be able to "live off the land", selling guns found in replacement for stimpacks and ammo. However, in Fallout 4, you are essentially restricted from exploring areas of the new wasteland particularly of the scarcity of ammo, stimpacks, and RadAways. The weapons you pick up, hardly fetch a sustainable price without maxing barter perks. In doing so, you sacrifice all other potential perks. The worst part about this is the fact that exp granted from discovering buildings or killing enemies is a fraction compared to what it was in Fallout 3. Exploring and hunting down enemies actually leveled you far beyond most story related quests. This is the complete opposite in Fallout 4. Essentially, I felt a bit forced to continue through the storyline because leveling any other way felt out of pace in the game.
Weapon Customization and Legendary Weapons:
The weapon customization in Fallout 4 is definitely an improvement over Fallout 3. The variations of custom barrels, stocks, and muzzles add to the freedom aspect of the game. I also enjoyed the idea of making everything in Fallout 4 useful in some way in terms of material collection. Legendary weapons at first seemed like the perfect solution to players like myself to scavenge the new wasteland and find every single Legendary item in the game. However, Legendary items are at best, hardly better than their counterparts which dilutes the desire to find them. Legendary items are essentially normal weapons or armor with a slight buff to stats, resistance, damage, or VATS usage. These definitely do not compare to the Legendary weapons found in Fallout 3. As a player who found every single unique weapon and armor in Fallout 3, the same satisfaction does not apply to these "Legendary" items because they are not special. The addition of insane damage or mechanics such as the Experimental MIRV Fatman was and still is the most satisfying weapon to use in any game i've played to date.
Power Armor:
Power armor in Fallout 4 came to be a bitter sweet experience. In truth, Fallout 4 corrects what power armor should've been throughout the Fallout series, big, clunky armor that is not self sufficient. The requirement of fusion cores felt like another necessity in order to continue through the game, but of course, they are quite expensive for the playtime rewarded through them. I found myself just ditching the armor for the majority of the game because I lacked the caps to sustain my fusion cores. Personally, I liked how Bethesda added more customization to power armors with paint and modifications, but it fails to beat Fallout 3 once again because any power armor besides X-01 does not feel exclusive. Power armors are pratically handed over to you left and right whereas in Fallout 3, certain power armors were fun to find especially the Prototype Medic Power Armor.
Conclusion:
Fallout 4 feels like a different game than Fallout 3 while keeping the unique aspects of it. I guess it should be like this since there would probably be a public outcry if Fallout 4 felt like another DLC to Fallout 3. Overall, Fallout 4 was a nice improveent to Fallout 3, but I would not call it the best of the Fallout series. I definitely recommend this to anyone who has or hasn't played the Fallout series despite all the bashing. Fallout 4 lived up to its name, but not over Fallout 3. Note: I played Fallout 3 and New Vegas originally on the 360, so don't expect hundreds of hours poured into them. I hardly mentioned New Vegas because New Vegas felt like an extension of Fallout 3.
Edit: As I have later discovered, there has been the introductions of unique weapons in Fallout 4; however, as I stated before, the difference is hardly noticable from the original on most unique items. Also, I did not mention anything about the new wasteland settlements because it is uncomparable to Fallout 3. This of course was a nice addition, though the limitation of select settlement spots hinders its potential.

The easy review would be to say if you liked Fallout 3 (the base game), you'll like Fallout 4. That's probably a general truism but a game like this deserves more. So read on....
Overall Opinion: Good but not great
Caveat: I once lived in Quincy, MA and I am familiar with the area. Thus I'll get certain jokes (Fallon's Basement is a take-off of Filene's Basement which is a famous local shopping landmark) and certain areas have a natural appeal to me because I lied there. YMMV. Of course, I lived in Washington DC as well so I got much of the inside stuff in FO3.
- - - - - - - - - -
Fallout 4 is a pretty flawed product for so many reasons.
- It's very combat-heavy, even more so than FO3. Thus it's often less of a RPG and more of a bad shooter at times.
- The pacing is off and early in the game you often have only a couple of quests to work on. You really don't get going in the game until you hit Diamond City, which is going to take 10+ hours of gameplay to get to for many people. As such, the intital areas can feel aimless and it's enough to put you off. 10-15 hours is a pretty big investment of time just to get things really going.
- It does a poor job of explaining both how and why to do certain things (like building your Sanctuary and other little towns). I've had to look up the key just to exit my power armor. I still don't understand what benefit I get out of building these villages (and boy does that get REPETITIVE after a while).
- Some things (like the aformentioned Sanctuary) feel more like a bolt-on to the game and weren't well integrated.
- The interface is awful for the PC. I didn't think Bethesda could make a worse UI after trying to muck with Skyrim's. I was wrong. This one is worse.
- The world building is certainly an achievement but I don't feel it's as good as the - Capital Wasteland in FO3 and pales in comparison to the monumental world-building achievement of Skyrim. Because it's very urban, you don't often get the breathtaking vistas of prior games. There's too much tramping around in shut-in areas or narrow building corridors and a lot less wide open exploration.
- Because of the base building, you need to keep looting junk and therefore run into the incredibly annoying encumbrance limits (to the point that I used a console command so I could carry more weight).
- Voiced protagonist/dialog options - I always think that having a voiced protagonist is a mistake in these games because it limits the dialog options and removes RPG aspects. FO4 is no exception. So not only do I get shorter dialog options but I have to listen to someone else acting it out rather than hearing my own character in my mind. So for instance, during a critical, emotional confrontation about 20 hours in, I had to listen to a voice actor screaming lines whereas I had pictured and played my character as someone who goes almost ice-cold in such situations. It's incredibly jarring.
- Furthermore, the dialog options are presented as a summary and at times what is said isn't what I really thought would be said by the summary option selected.
Other people have decried performance issues, bland companions (they didn't bother me though they weren't Bioware-quality), the new skill trees/SPECIAL system and so forth. I didn't have any issues with these but I can understand their opinions.
Ok then, why recommend it with all of these negatives? Because it's still Fallout. It's still a massive achievement in world building and it greatly rewards exploration (which is my favorite part of games like these). It still tells a decent and often compelling tale of a wasteland wanderer. There are more quests later, which help provide direction in the mid-game. FO4 still compels me to see what's in the next building or around the next corner. I remain engaged in this interesting, weird and depressing world that is the USA stuck in the 1950s with the technology of the 2070s. I care about this universe...and FO4's faults aren't bad enough to make me not care.
In addition, Bethesda has added some cool things to the game.
- There are a handful of set-piece encounters in the game that are thrilling to fight. Walk into a certain park in the middle of Boston and you'll find out what I mean...
- Enemies are smarter and some of the ways they spawn are really interesting. No longer are ferals just wandering around. Instead, they might crawl in through windows, down walls or stir when someone comes into a room. These small touches make the world more fun and believable.
- The world is beautiful. As I said, it's not magical in the way that Skyrim was but it is an incredible achievement.
- The sound is even better. From far-off gunshots to groans to hearing the "I Don't Want to Set the World on Fire" song again (by the Inkspots) or "Butcher Pete" (Roy Brown), this is easily the best sounding Fallout game.
- The crafting system is pretty cool. I like being able to tailor a weapon to specifically fit my style of play. The armor system isn't as good but it's still a step up.
- The radiation storms are really neat...I'd love these to be far more dangerous though.  :)
I imagine DLCs will only help to improve this game with more focused content areas (The Pitt in FO3 was excellent in this regard) and of course you know the mod community will have a field day with it. But as it is, I don't have any regrets about buying this at full price.
PS - I also got the Prima Survival Guide for FO4. It's not bad but it's not as good as the ones for FO3 or New Vegas.

Now what I have a problem with (and many many other people) is the dialogue system and the voiced protagnoist. The Bethesda RPG games have always stood out from the competition, in the regards that their games have feelt like true RPG:s. There are many other games with the RPG label on them, like Mass Effect and The Witcher etc. But these games are still very streamlined and I would not say that they are an RPG on the same level as a previous Elder Scrolls or Fallout game. Now with Fallout 4, it feels very much like instead of continue to do their own thing, Bethesda is trying to ape after these games. And the result just does not work. You feel extremely limited in what kind of character you can make and what you can say. There is simply not much room to go outside the "predefined" character in this game. Forget to try to play an evil character. Also the voiced protagonist makes it even worse since it can be totally immersion breaking every time you see your character speak if you try to have a character that is anything else then a goodie goodie father.
To have had the voiced protagonist work, Bethesda would have had to record at least 5-10 different voices for each gender that you could pick from depending on what kind of character you would want to play as. You could have the goodie-goodie voice over, or the killer, or the geek, etc etc.
I really don't like the direction this is going. Even though the game in all other regards is great and I will spend hundreds of hours in it. Bethesda should continue to be unique in the industry. They really lost something and I just hope they understand that this is not the way to go. Currently the user metacritc score for this game is around the low 5-6.
I honestly don't think that people think the game is that bad, it is though a very strong indicator that many many people are very displeased and worried by the direction Bethesda seems to be going with this game.

I have both positive and negative thoughts on this game, but mostly Positive because hell, it's a Bethesda game!
To describe it, Like most of their games AND New Vegas, it's Very addictive, like Jet or Skooma for a example. While it does look and feel like a Fallout game, it's taken alot of good elements from Skyrim, including weapon modding, armor pieces and even sprinting. Some people complain about it not feeling like an RPG anymore, while it's RPG element is still there, it's been simplified leaving fewer choices in the dialogue, but it doesn't bother me much, there's even a Mod to change it! Speech-checking still functions the same, it uses Charisma now instead of Speech but it still makes sense! But one thing i also really like is.. we can finally romance companions, it may not be big but it helps us bond with them better. You ladies ever wanted to F**k a handsome ghoul? Now you can! Without even needing a mod! Also talking about companions, Nick. Goshdarn. Valentine! He's an incredible character that Bethesda introduced and his story is really cool to me, He's like a robot Sherlock Holmes. But the main reason I love it are these to keep it short: Base Building, Legendary weapons, Immersive makeshift weapons, Power Armour is more powerful, Weapon Modding, an Intact Roleplayable Vault Home (Vault 81) Brotherhood of Steel on a friggin Zeppelin, cool Console Commands, Dogmeat is actually really useful now, He and Codsworth can wear some accessories and more! And the DLC hasn't been announce yet but will introduce even more great stuff! Just like Fallout 3's 2/3 out of 4 DLC that I favoured,
I could go on, and even about the negatives everyone fussing about but I'm sure we all heard them before. Most people are just disappointed it didn't live the hype and not end up as good as their "precious" New Vegas and Fallout 2. (No offence to those who love those games, I do too)
Well if you want a more simple, modern and near bug-free Fallout game you think you have specs to run, Yes it's the best in awhile and I really love it, but if you care too much about story, characters, mods, lore, humor AND you know how to use mods, Stick with New Vegas. It'll be your choice and i'll accept it.
My final rating for Fallout 4 is a Solid.. 7.5/10! Worth a buy!

I've been playing this almost non-stop for about 7 and a half days now. Here are a few Pros and Cons to take into consideration.
-PRO-As far as I'm concerned, they took the old gameplay aspects and jammed about 20 vials of Psycho into it because I have never actually played a Fallout game the same as this one, as in using my head instead of using my hammer. In FO3 - FONV I mainly just played the tank and dove straight into combat and killed pretty much anything. In FO4 if you try that they'll be scrapping your balls off the ceiling within a mater of seconds. A perfect example of this I found was the Deathclaw. In FO3 in the later levels they were a nuisance, but they were far from anything I'd call a threat. The first time I saw a Deathclaw in FO4 I got my♥♥♥♥♥handed to me on a silver platter... and I still try to avoid them best I can out of sheer terror for the damn lizards.
-CON-Yes the graphics aren't amazing but you should take into consideration that graphics aren't everything when making a game. For those complaining about the graphics I'd have to tell them to just go to the store and get a ♥♥♥♥ing painting. That should be enough to satisfy you for a few years yeah?
-PRO-The voice actor I found makes the dialogue options much more interesting as now you don't just have a few lines of text to go off of, you also can hear the emotion in the words to convey much more feeling... especially whenever you click the 'Sarcasm' option. Those who don't like the voiced player, guess what? There's a mod. Problem solved yeah?
-CON-It's a little bit buggy, one that I found to occur often was the infinite loading screen while fast traveling to certain places, as well as the classic 'Hard Crash' where your walking somewhere and the game has a heart attack. No doubt the modding community will work tirelesly to fix these minor stutters. No game's perfect after all.
-PRO-Some people feel like the RPG levels are toned down... maybe so. But I don't feel like it's ancestors were that much RPG deep either. In FO3 you were a kid looking for your father. In FONV you were a delivery boy... a ♥♥♥♥ing delivery boy. And people complained that being just 'A father looking for your [SPOILERS]' is a bad thing. Why? I'm genuinly confused. From what I've seen the RPG is as strong as ever, and then some.
-CON-This is just a personal quirk. I didn't like how they handled the companion system... it's really nothing other than I want to be able to once again take 2 companions. One human/main companion. One pet/side companion. Nothing much but I suppose the modding community can help me out here.
All in all I'd say this game advances the series in a way I can definitely agree with.

Fallout 4 PC Review by Draul
Genre: Action , RPG
Publisher: Bethesda, Developer: Bethesda
Fallout 4 has been a game fans have been waiting to play for awhile. Sure there was New Vegas but that wasn’t developed by Bethesda and it wasn’t Fallout 4.  Personally I enjoyed New Vegas a lot. Almost more than Fallout 3.  I made a comment about how I felt the game was over-hyped on twitter and someone said I was out of my mind because the game was only announced earlier this year. Well that isn’t entirely true. People have been expecting it for awhile. A perfect example is Halflife 3. That game is extremely hyped and isn’t real yet. If and when it does get developed and announced all of that hype is still there.  So lets get real.
First and foremost I love Bethesda games. Every single Bethesda developed game is full of bug after bug. A lot of game breaking bugs at that. People say oh it’s okay because it’s Bethesda, we expect bugs. Well It’s Not Okay. Not even a little bit. A game in development as long as Fallout 4 (Claims being 5-7 years). It shouldn’t have the bugs it has. From followers glitching above levels or on top of buildings to npc pathing causing you to fail an escort mission because they get stuck on the map clutter and then teleport away. Or you being teleported 1500 feet into the air and falling to your death.  Heck there is an awful glitch of a follower getting into a suit of power armor.
Again, that is just not okay.  These are just a very small portion of the bugs in the game. Let us not forget about the graphics of Fallout 4. The game looks like an Xbox 360 game even on PC. Immediately I was upset after seeing the actual game itself. With games like Witcher 3, Dragon Age Inquisition out. I feel that Bethesda needed to compete and it just did not. There are two things I can think of when I see the graphics. Did Bethesda just not have time or want to put the budget to update the game to modern systems after it had been developed and decided to go for the inevitable cash grab ? Or Was it that they were like… Well someone is gonna mod it anyway so it’s okay. Welllll let me tell you… It’s NOT OKAY!
Moving onto the story of Fallout 4. Don’t worry this is a spoiler free review.  As I played the game I started realizing I cared very little about the lives of the wasteland survivors. As I did side quests it was all just rinse repeat content. Here is a settlement, clear it out. Here is a mission go to building and clear it out. There were times where I would go to these places and fight the copy paste raiders in those areas. Then one time I saw a group of them that all looked exactly like the generic character in the screenshots of the game that you play as. So the ” Cannon ” character.  Then aside from that I found the voice actors spoke with no emotion. Again I thought is this because in the future no one has emotion anymore?  I couldn’t tell really which….. says a lot.  Then you have the main character whom is trying to find his son.  He has no emotion when talking about his son. Look at movies or shows like Taken. Where the bad♥♥♥♥♥whom has a “particular” set of skills gets emotional and uses his aggression. Even when he was talking you could feel the urgency in his voice. But not in Fallout 4. Plus your character gets told about factions, events, or things in the game over and over. Every time he is told he is like huh ? what? It just gets so annoying after awhile.  I started skipping dialogue if it wasn’t in a main story cut scene and even then I just read the subtitles and moved on.
The gameplay of the game is the best parts. When it works. Though you will find a lot of illusion of content. IE a inventory weight system to make your game time pad to make it seem like you got more out of your game. The addition of the settlement mod from past Fallout games was cool. Next to useless which again is Illusion of content. Though It was interesting building my first settlement or two. After that I realized how pointless it actually was. The gun-play was said to be modeled after Destiny. I don’t see that, and it felt nothing like it at all. I loved Destiny and played almost 1000 hours in the game so I would know. That said the action was still fun. Just don’t try to be melee in third person. Your choices don’t seem to matter nearly as much as past Fallout titles though.
The most stand out point of the game for me was how they immediately have you using power armor and fighting deathclaws. These were things you normally did end game of past Fallout titles. So the further you went into the world, the further you got into the story you found new things to fight and areas to explore. There are a few random triggered events by doing certain quests or dungeons. Such as doing Vault 75 triggered a UFO event. So no spoilers are there I wont continue but that was one of the best parts of Fallout 4.   The addition of crafting was neat. It was similar to another mod from past Fallout titles as well. If you played the game How to Survive you will find the modding/crafting in Fallout 4 to be very similar. Especially when it comes to the pipe weapons.
The modding tools aren’t available yet for Fallout 4. There are still a few mods being made. Most of them just ways to cheat. Once more mods are available then I would definitely be going back to the game. At this point I have about 50 played hours in the game and have explored “Most” of the Commonwealth. I have finished the main story and I was mildly entertained. Still entertained though. I did enjoy playing the game. I do have the season pass pre-ordered for now. Lets see where Bethesda takes us for the remainder of the Fallout 4 journey.
Pros:
-Fun Gameplay
-Unique world events
-Crafting/Modding System
Cons:
– Outdated Graphics
– Emotionless Dialogue
– LOTS AND LOTS OF Bugs

After finally beating the game 50 hours in i can say that fallout 4 is a good game but also a dissapointing one coming from a massive fallout 3 and new vegas fan. Bethesda is continuing their tradition of dumbing down their new releases further and further. From morrowind to oblivion to skyrim, i don't even consider skyrim an rpg it's an open world action adventure game with rpg elements and they have done a similar thing to fallout 4. I do think that fallout 4 is an rpg just a very dumbed down one and it honestly didn't feel like one in the first 30 hours.
I started getting bored of the game around the 30 hour mark because i felt like i wasn't making an impact in the world enough and everything i did felt meaningless. This was very depressing considering i easily put over 100 hours in 3 and new vegas in multiple playthroughs and was never bored. After beating the game i do not see myself putting more hours into it exploring the rest of the world like i was planning. Maybe i will in future but not anytime soon i wanna move on to something else.
When i got to the second half of the main story the game picked up big time and it started giving you meaningful choices that effects the world. The game is missing the karma system and you can't really be evil in this game either. I think those additions would have made the game much better.
The shooting is not clunky anymore it feels fluid and the ai is better then the previous games but on the other hand i found no reason to use vats at all on the pc because the aiming is so smooth with the mouse and keyboard. However on console you will still probably use it cause aiming on controller is awkward.
In the other games i was using vats all the time i rarely shot a bullet without it because the shooting was so clunky but that was the charm of the game because if i wanted to play a shooting game i would go play the hundreds of them out there on the market and thats not why i play fallout and sadly fallout 4 fits into that category of shooters. This opinion is very personal and subjective and its totally ok if you disagree because the shooting itself is better in this game and i understand if you like it more because of that.
The weapons/armor don't break in this game, I simply dont get why they did this other than to appeal the game more to casuals and further dumb down the game
I really like the crafting i think its a great addition from building settlements to upgrading weapons and armour its very well done. I love how looting is in real time and you don't have to go into a menu anymore to pick something up it's the best improvment the game has made for me.

The story is better then fallout 3's and it holds up pretty well with new vegas too its just the little things that makes the other fallout games better to me. There's many other reasons.
The Good: Fallout 4 dwarfs the gameplay of Fallout 3 in gunplay and customization, to a point where I was supremely impressed. The amount of customizations for guns that are /literally made out of pipes/ is insane. This makes someone like me pretty happy. Power armor is at it's finest, and there's really not much more to say about the power armor than that. (Some raiders using the power armor is bunk for the canon though.)
I had tons of fun killing my first few Deathclaws. The first Alpha Deathclaw came out of nowhere, wasn't expecting to see anything but ghouls, and then suddenly my intestines were everywhere and I was loading a save.
I find it was somewhat too easy, and I had a hard time finding a suitable difficulty. It was a breeze until I put it on Very Hard. Legendary enemies are a delight to fight and loot.
Again, the combat is good, and the sudden difficulty spikes are actually pretty welcome in this title as long as they are not due to coding bugs.
The Bad:
Due to some issues with the dialogue system (Which everyone hates) it brings the immersion back a surprising amount in every story element. As we're mentioning the story, I find the characters and personalities really engaging, like most Bethesda titles. However, it's ruined for me by the lack of decent responses (they vary in the extremes for tone) and the fact that it all boils down to a "Pick one of four" faction system. New Vegas had this same problem for factions. It needs to have a linear goal, this much freedom of choice in the main story boils down to less interesting dialogue, and people hating eachother for the reason that "They have to" so you can't pick multiple factions at the same time. While it makes definite sense that the Brotherhood of Steel would hate the railroad, there's no real huge reason for them to outright try to kill all of them the second they can when the Institute is the immediate threat. Same thing with the Institute versus the Minutemen. While I understand what they're going for, it ultimately falls flat on it's face and makes me really not care about anyone at all.
The Ugly:
Along with that, you'll find that the leveling system is fluff for about half of it, locking out what (to me) are basic functions of the game you should have access to.
Why is it I need 6 charisma to get the local leader perk, to make stores in my settlements that already have a somewhat steep cap cost to make? Having a skill requirement on top of an item requirement for a lot of these upgrades and quality of life items makes little to no sense. It would be solved with removing those skills and refining balance. This is obviously padding. Some may enjoy it, I find it the games absolute worst feature.
The aforementioned starting SPECIAL wouldn't be a big deal in the long run if it wasn't absolutely ideal to start a character at max intelligence. There is no room for other builds really. Stealth is impossibly hard to maintain until you have everything else leveled already, and by then you already have a maxed out combat shotgun so who cares anymore? You're going to want to mod your weapons as soon as possible, getting the best receivers and long range mods possible to get max damage. Not to mention the medic perks and the nerd rage perk being insanely helpful compared to most other perks. Also the fusion core perk, that lets you use power armor for about an hour or so a core. Other than that you can assign as you want.
-
Somewhat off topic and more of a personal story. I had a .50 Cal hunting rifle that fired two shots at once. It was a legendary item. I modded this gun to be lightweight, short light barrel, glowing sights, small mag, but full stock. This weapon -firing on creatures my level- did maybe about 5-10% of their health worth of damage on a headshot. I removed the recoil mods, gave it the longest barrel, and bam. It kills everything in two (four) shots. I didn't /really/ have a choice to make a lightweight hunting rifle since it took a HUGE margin of the damage from me at anything more than shotgun range. This is one of the balance issues that pains me greatly.
-
Now we'll talk about how the game runs, and it's graphics.
Graphically the game is fine. Nothing special. I like some certain effects and textures. Water looks nice, lighting is good, some models and textures leave much to be desired.
However, this game will CHEW on your system no matter what range of power it's in.
My system is decent, getting kind of old. I can run games like Witcher 3 and Metro: Last Light on max just fine. This game drops down to about 10 frames a second in the city at max settings for me, sometimes even worse. I turned draw distance and shadows all the way down and it seems to have fixed to about 30-ish. It runs 60 everywhere else.
A large chunk of the game is in the city.
With some game breaking bugs, and other issues elsewhere that are too abundant to list...I just can’t say this game is really well put together at all. This is a running trend is Bethesda games generally, but not ever this bad for frame rate issues, that's new to me.
The Objective:
Some people like the changes to VATS. I don't like how it slows time instead of stops it, personally. I feel if your reflexes are fine already this serves no purpose. With max accuracy being 95%, the only reason for me to use VATS becomes crit chance and crit banking in the extreme late game. This is down to personal taste in the end.
Melee builds are extremely deadly, but come with the tradeoff that other melee enemies can sometimes stun lock you. Not to mention anything larger than your size will probably grab you and throw you, or just plain old hit you away from them. Melee builds are good, but have severe issues. This is somewhat expected given the setting.
-
NPCs will talk to you constantly while walking by which is lively (though sometimes depressing). I also put a radio right next to my workbench to add to this effect, but the radio announcer is just REALLY annoying. (As I'm writing this a friend informs me there's a quest to make him less of a punk.) There's a huge mess of radio stations, but you have to be in their area. This is another preference thing to me.
Final Opinion:
With how empty this game is, you have to look forward to the DLC here. Bethesda DLC is known to be excellent and worth every penny.
It’s just...The base game isn’t worth $60. If you’re currently really hurting to play this game, and just can’t afford it or don’t have the time to get invested, don’t worry. It’s worth probably about the upper $40s for me for a lack of content, unnecessary padding, and stability. Not $60.
So not recommended right now. It needs some work or a price drop.

For $60 dollars, this is definitely one of the most efficient uses of your money like any other Bethesda RPG game based on the hundreds of hours on vanilla content and the hundreds more on mods from steam and the nexus. Fallout has a very special place in my heart, but this game has its disappointments. So without further delay, let me give you the pros, trade offs, and cons...
Pros:
+ the focus on the gun gameplay :Multiple steps up from any fallout game. It almost gives a borderlands type feel for the game. That combined with the small cover mechanic and you honestly have a decent attempt at a FPS element in this game, which fallout has desperately needed since 3
+voice acting and moral questions: another big step up from fallout. Upon gaining the trust of your companions, the dialogue they provide makes you actually feel for the characters. Add the fluidity of the new dialogue system and you'll find yourself you care for Nick valentine or Piper while they weave their tales. As for the moral dilemmas, you'll find them in the campaign, especially in choosing where to side with. Bethesda really wants to see you make a decision on a group even when you know of its flaws, especially the final choice in the campaign.
+the crafting system: mods...mods everywhere...for everything...
+the world size and detail: the map itself may not be as huge as people hyped it up to be, but the amount of detail and sizes of areas within locations of the map truly make this the best space per action ratio ever in a Bethesda RPG. within Boston especially, buildings are enterable and have multiple levels, allowing CQB style combat within the building but across building combat allows snipers and scoped weapons to be utilized. I have never had to bring so many guns in my life in a fallout game to cover every type of combat compared to just bringing my standard rifle because the size of the map per action was pretty low.
+legendary enemies: need a bigger challenge? How about enemies that can activly cloak while fighting you, or raiders armed with the dreaded Fatman? And upon killing them you get something truly special. Sounds good, right?
+no level cap!
+MANY skill magazines and bobblehead that♥♥♥♥♥multiple benefits and perks
+8 days in, mods are already modding, there's already a lot of added material out there
+it's a new fallout story with a new feel, and honestly there's no reason not to play it as long as your computer can run it...
+VATS improvements. It slows time instead of stopping it. You'd be surprised how much of a difference it makes from a calm, calculated execution to rushing quick headshots as the enemy slowly fights you.
+you cam continue your game even after the main story is completed.
Trade offs
=quality vs quantity of items: alright, in terms of fallout, this game has the lowest diversity of items available, making the game really focus on its crafting system to diversify everything. Armors are also pretty static in terms of which one is better like skyrim, and even some of the mods follow the same pattern
=the power armor question: right in the beginning of the game so long as you follow the main quest line or do some exploring, you'll find a suit of power armor, which can make the game pretty easy so long as you know where to find fusion cores. Any person on their second of third play through can easilly keep their suit fueled because they know where every fusion core spawns. Within the " starting area" of the game (around sanctuary to Concord) there are at least 2 fusion cores I have found that can easilly keep your suit up and running to cover that entire area 3 fold. It's up to you whether you want to use power armor though.
=the skill and perk rebalance: personally I don't mind it, but there has been a lot of controversy here on how you can directly level up your special stats and perks in ranks, with no skills.
=very hard and survival difficulties: honestly it just turns enemies into bullet sponges... Whether you like that or not, its up to you.
=settlements: Bethesda wanted them to be an optional thing, but in doing so they have made them have no real use other than farming for specific items life purified water and crsftig material. Mods will surly make this feature much much better
Cons
- no karma or faction allegences: honestly I don't k ow why this is missing. It's clear companions rely on a karma based system depending on your actions and you can be enemies with certain factions based on your actions, so why are these two key fallout featursles missing?!?
-melee combat still sucks, and is nearly impossible on higher difficulties
-companions will still be infamous for getting in your way
-Vertibird AI needs some serious work. They die easilly, crash into the ground, and like to land on settlers.
-graphics: its Bethesda, what do you expect?
-specs: you can't run the game on your toaster or windows 95...
-stealth seems a little more of a challenge, enemies seem to have proximity sensors at times, even with the ninja perk and its multiple levels
-multiple unkillable characters: you can't be a psyco, there are too many immortal characters in the game.
Overall though, still worth your money.

Fallout 4 PC Review by Draul
Genre: Action , RPG
Publisher: Bethesda, Developer: Bethesda
Fallout 4 has been a game fans have been waiting to play for awhile. Sure there was New Vegas but that wasn’t developed by Bethesda and it wasn’t Fallout 4.  Personally I enjoyed New Vegas a lot. Almost more than Fallout 3.  I made a comment about how I felt the game was over-hyped on twitter and someone said I was out of my mind because the game was only announced earlier this year. Well that isn’t entirely true. People have been expecting it for awhile. A perfect example is Halflife 3. That game is extremely hyped and isn’t real yet. If and when it does get developed and announced all of that hype is still there.  So lets get real.
First and foremost I love Bethesda games. Every single Bethesda developed game is full of bug after bug. A lot of game breaking bugs at that. People say oh it’s okay because it’s Bethesda, we expect bugs. Well It’s Not Okay. Not even a little bit. A game in development as long as Fallout 4 (Claims being 5-7 years). It shouldn’t have the bugs it has. From followers glitching above levels or on top of buildings to npc pathing causing you to fail an escort mission because they get stuck on the map clutter and then teleport away. Or you being teleported 1500 feet into the air and falling to your death.  Heck there is an awful glitch of a follower getting into a suit of power armor.
Again, that is just not okay.  These are just a very small portion of the bugs in the game. Let us not forget about the graphics of Fallout 4. The game looks like an Xbox 360 game even on PC. Immediately I was upset after seeing the actual game itself. With games like Witcher 3, Dragon Age Inquisition out. I feel that Bethesda needed to compete and it just did not. There are two things I can think of when I see the graphics. Did Bethesda just not have time or want to put the budget to update the game to modern systems after it had been developed and decided to go for the inevitable cash grab ? Or Was it that they were like… Well someone is gonna mod it anyway so it’s okay. Welllll let me tell you… It’s NOT OKAY!
Moving onto the story of Fallout 4. Don’t worry this is a spoiler free review.  As I played the game I started realizing I cared very little about the lives of the wasteland survivors. As I did side quests it was all just rinse repeat content. Here is a settlement, clear it out. Here is a mission go to building and clear it out. There were times where I would go to these places and fight the copy paste raiders in those areas. Then one time I saw a group of them that all looked exactly like the generic character in the screenshots of the game that you play as. So the ” Cannon ” character.  Then aside from that I found the voice actors spoke with no emotion. Again I thought is this because in the future no one has emotion anymore?  I couldn’t tell really which….. says a lot.  Then you have the main character whom is trying to find his son.  He has no emotion when talking about his son. Look at movies or shows like Taken. Where the bad♥♥♥♥♥whom has a “particular” set of skills gets emotional and uses his aggression. Even when he was talking you could feel the urgency in his voice. But not in Fallout 4. Plus your character gets told about factions, events, or things in the game over and over. Every time he is told he is like huh ? what? It just gets so annoying after awhile.  I started skipping dialogue if it wasn’t in a main story cut scene and even then I just read the subtitles and moved on.
The gameplay of the game is the best parts. When it works. Though you will find a lot of illusion of content. IE a inventory weight system to make your game time pad to make it seem like you got more out of your game. The addition of the settlement mod from past Fallout games was cool. Next to useless which again is Illusion of content. Though It was interesting building my first settlement or two. After that I realized how pointless it actually was. The gun-play was said to be modeled after Destiny. I don’t see that, and it felt nothing like it at all. I loved Destiny and played almost 1000 hours in the game so I would know. That said the action was still fun. Just don’t try to be melee in third person. Your choices don’t seem to matter nearly as much as past Fallout titles though.
The most stand out point of the game for me was how they immediately have you using power armor and fighting deathclaws. These were things you normally did end game of past Fallout titles. So the further you went into the world, the further you got into the story you found new things to fight and areas to explore. There are a few random triggered events by doing certain quests or dungeons. Such as doing Vault 75 triggered a UFO event. So no spoilers are there I wont continue but that was one of the best parts of Fallout 4.   The addition of crafting was neat. It was similar to another mod from past Fallout titles as well. If you played the game How to Survive you will find the modding/crafting in Fallout 4 to be very similar. Especially when it comes to the pipe weapons.
The modding tools aren’t available yet for Fallout 4. There are still a few mods being made. Most of them just ways to cheat. Once more mods are available then I would definitely be going back to the game. At this point I have about 50 played hours in the game and have explored “Most” of the Commonwealth. I have finished the main story and I was mildly entertained. Still entertained though. I did enjoy playing the game. I do have the season pass pre-ordered for now. Lets see where Bethesda takes us for the remainder of the Fallout 4 journey.

The first thing I will say is that Fallout 4 is a good game, therefore I recommend it. While there are many pros and cons, it is not fair for me (everyone has their own opinion) to deem it as sub-par in today's game market.
The first thing I personally noticed is that the world is an interesting place and you come across people and places that catch your eye; this is important in a open-world game. I also noticed that the visuals are great, despite the overwhelming negativity over this subject I heard prior to playing the game. There are certain aspects of visuals and graphics settings that are a little dissapointing, but overall the game looks great visually. The atmospheric music, the music apart from the radio stations, is pretty good and meets the standards of other Fallout games. The radio stations, however, do not. I appreciated the throwback songs, but the lack of variety, annoying voices, and irritating conflicting sounds made me quickly turn my radio off.
The looting, armor, and weapon systems have been completely changed for the better. Customization works well and rewards playing smart and investing time into crafting and conserving. Not much more to say here, but a huge plus.
After the first hour or so of gameplay, some things started to wear on me. The four-button dialogue system, in all honesty, is not only disappointing but degrading in my eyes. Am I so impatient and simple-minded that I don't want to read more than 3 words as my response? This system frequently misleads the player into saying things that they either don't want to say or are forced into saying. As a sidenote, I personally shudder at the introduction of a voiced player in a Fallout game, but that won't affect my assessment of the game. I prefer choice over cinematics, depersonalization, or what Todd Howard calls "hitting emotional beats better". For me, it only withdrew me from the experiences and choices, and broke my immersion a lot of the time. Along with these ideas, the NPCs are very cringeworthy at times. Unsettling facial expressions, talking with no mouth movement, poor mouth movement with dialogue when it does happen, and honestly some poor voice acting all wore down on immersion and eventually made me resist talking to NPCs which is a huge hit to my experience. Also, the dialogue system in general is very flawed. I'm not talking about bugs, though they happen often in this system, but the simplicity in 3 and NV of being locked into conversation worked much better than the live-action conversation in 4. It seems to be an attempt to make dialogue dynamic and more realistic, but ends up a futile attempt that is very unnatural and clunky.
As far as performance goes, I haven't had many issues, but many other have. I personally found a few of the controls to be irritating, but manageable. Key-mapping is a thing even while limited. This game isn't a horrible console port like everyone says.
RPG elements have also been dumbed down. I found myself missing skills and being upset that I felt like a god too quickly. I was never limited to any type of weapon or armor and it felt unsettling. And again, the voiced character made me feel like an outsider rather than like I was immersed in an RPG.
Combat, however, is vastly improved in almost every facet. Dynamic VATS works great and shooting mechanics are amazingly improved. I enjoy using almost every type of weapon and no matter what fight I'm in, I find the experience satisfying. It was disheartening when I realized that I was still playing this game because I really enjoyed taking out Super Mutants and Raiders rather than making difficult decisions or meeting new characters, but it's still a plus.
The primary story isn't great, but it isn't the primary focus. Side-quests' stories are good, but not amazing for the most part. I generally found NPCs to be a bit disappointing both in functionality and depth.
The crafting system is great. It is tedious at times, but rewarding and satisfying. I personally am glad that Bethesda chose to use it as a non-essential activity because those hesitant to use it don't have to, and those that do are still rewarded in the activity itself and also with tangible rewards.
Overall I highly recommend Fallout 4. Don't expect the depth or experience of the previous 3 primary Fallout games, but expect a different yet worthwhile experience.
