Fallout 4 is a mixed bag, in it there’s an adventure around every turn and someone's story that you can uncover though the commonwealth, there are creatures a people that want nothing more then to see your dead body on the ground and to survive in the deadly wasteland, and there are is a city which remains are burnt to a crisp by the great war 200 years ago. Fallout 4 has a lot to offer but with that brings a lot of consequences.
Fallout 4 has a lot for you to do, whether you’re fighting off mutants, retrieving artifacts from the old world, uncovering secrets of the commonwealth, or building a shelter for a settlement. There’s a lot of content but the whole thing is held together by a single thread and is on the verge of falling apart. Fallout 4 is very buggy and can cause cheap death or sometimes unplayable missions. For example, I had to go with two people in a cave system under the city to loot a vault under Diamond City, to advance through the cave system I had to use this robot named Sonya to break through walls that look fragile. Unfortunately the robot would not break the final wall and I was unable to progress through the mission. Other bugs consist of getting stuck in a wall, enemies getting stuck in a wall, NPC’s heads in the camera when you're talking to them and graphical errors like pop in. Somehow though I was able to look past these bugs and found myself enjoying the game a lot. What I didn't enjoy was the overall look of the game. The graphics of Fallout 4 are very dated. This isn’t any more apparent than when you're in one of the skyscrapers in post apocalyptic Boston. Everything looks very low res and flat out ugly. It certainly does not help that game is using a engine that skyrim was made in 4 years ago and even then the graphical quality wasn’t that good. One thing I do like is that the art style is FAR better than previous Fallout games. Instead of using different shades of brown the environment has a lot more color while still maintaining the bleak no hope feel. Things the Nuclear Storms add a lot more to the environment and makes the atmosphere much better.
Bugs and Graphics aside, Fallout 4 does a great job in storytelling.  Everyone has a story to tell and usually has you go on a mission where you also uncover things about the commonwealth or other people you may have met throughout the main story. The voice acting is amazing, comparing it to Fallout 3 or new vegas is no competition. I liked almost all the characters except one or two. As for characters themselves, there also very good and most characters have a distinct personality that makes them stick out and makes the wasteland have more life.
The VATS system returns for Fallout 3 and New Vegas but this time it’s better. Time doesn’t stop but instead is just slowed down making the action faster and keeps the game moving at a solid pace. Now you can scope and shoot and actually hit your targets instead of it being blind luck. This is my favorite change as it is not like an arcade shooter but gunfights are faster  and  more hectic like it would be in a wasteland.  Finding ammo is fairly annoying as I found myself at the end of missions with no ammo and dying a bunch of times before I finally was able to make it out. The perk system is simplified but for the better as everything is laid out in a way where it's easy to understand and use. Some gunfights can be very monotonous at times if you don’t have the right weapon and you might have no choice but to die.
The new addition of building settlements is fun but doesn’t impact the story in any way. Most people will go through the entire main story and barely touch it.  The building system is a great break in the action and can add hours of gameplay itself. The only problem is that is is no proper tutorial and there is a lot of trial and error. Building shelter can add people to your settlements and make them happier. You can also modify weapons to make them stronger. You can turn a normal 10mm Pistol into a hand cannon and annihilate any enemies in your way.
One of my favorite things about Fallout 4 is the music. Whether it’s eerie sounds of wandering the wasteland of the victory tune that plays when you liberate an area from enemies it’s great. It really helps to set the mood of the game and I really feel that it is really overlooked by other people.
The AI is not good. There actions cook like there robots instead of people (even though some are actually robots). They can easily get stuck or sometimes face the wrong way when talking to you. You can walk up someone, crouch, and pick pocket someone in the middle of diamond city and nobody will notice. Don’t even try to be stealthy without a stealth boy because enemies will spot you even if your toe is visible they will shoot you and hunt you down.
Fallout 4 has a lot of flaws, but I was able to look over most of these and see what the commonwealth had to offer. Compelling stories, exciting battles, and fascinating locations kept on making me come back for more. There is a lot to do and if you're bored of one thing you can easily go and do something else. It’s nowhere near perfect but it’s a great change from the crazy arcade shooters or stealth action games that have flooded the market lately. Fallout 4 has a lot of room to improve but for now I happy with killing mutants and exploring the commonwealth.  After all war, war never changes, and Bethesda make that very clear in the latest edition of the fallout franchise. Fallout 4 gets a 8.6/10 -Infinite

A post-apocalyptic romp in the beautiful ruins of Boston filled with quests and things to do. While some things are a hit or miss (the main quest turning into mush at act 2, no dialogue skill checks) and some are just downright unacceptable (performance issues and the UI) the game manages to be engrossing, entertaining and a hell of a good time.
The combat is visceral and fast paced, a definite step up that feels like a proper first person shooter instead of the jerky 'Oblivion with guns' feel of FO3. The crafting system is very thorough and gives you a lot of leeway on how to play through the game. Power Armor has become actually badass to walk around and punch people in, which is a great thing as you can even mount a jetpack on it!
I really love the settlement system, while it is very shallow on the management side it manages to be a lovely little minigame where you can build whatever you want and make a homebase on the many plots around the Commonwealth. My huge five story tower on Spectacle Island was a blast to build and I can't wait to see what Bethesda and the modders add in the future to the settlement feature.
Some pointers on the main quest. I found that with (MQ Spoiler)
being a possibility, all the other factions coming to play naturally throughout the experience and some refusing to help you and turning into enemies past a certain point was very cleverly done. I wish they had fleshed out the factions even further, some motivations of the groups are left way too ambiguous, even though they really shouldn't be. The main motivation for your character is also shoddy and disconnected with the greater conflict going around, which is a shame, as the entire experience had so much more potential on that 'broken family' aspect. The twist was obvious and a bit cliche and the story itself a bit short, but it was a good time nonetheless.
I wish some aspects of the game were fleshed out, like having a proper settler management interface and more pieces to play with, but those are bound to come when the modders get their hands on the Creation Kit, so that's not a big deal.
Overall, I'd recommend this game wholeheartedly to anyone who wants to spend a good 50 to 100 hours roaming around Boston listening to "Worry Worry Worry" and blasting legendary deathclaws to shreds with gatling lasers. Fallout 4 has plenty of technical and other issues, but you won't find a boring experience here.

There are negative and positive things about Fallout 4, we will start with the negative parts first, since that's always the most interesting.
First off, the game is limited to 60 fps. It's sad to see modern games still having this restriction, especially when 144 hz monitors are becoming more and more common. It's possible to remove the cap by messing with the game files, but that results in the game soft locking when you leave terminals, so it becomes unplayable.
The game has no (in-game) settings for field of view, and no settings to remove mouse acceleration. These things can be fixed by editing the games .ini files, so if you're cool with that it's no real problem, but it's still sad to see this lack of proper configuration ability in a modern triple-A game.
The UI is pretty bad, especially manuvering around in the pip-boy.
That's pretty much it for the negatives as far as I'm concerned. The rest of the game is really well done and very fun. There is an incredible amount of content with sidequests wherever you go, in addition to the main quest. Some people complain about the graphics, or the AI, and while they are not perfect, I don't mind them. The great content and gameplay makes up for the minor lack in graphics or AI.
In short, if you're ok with 60 fps, buy the game, edit the .ini files so the game becomes playable (there are lots of guides out there), and enjoy it. Highly recommended.

If it wasn't a Bethesda game, I would have no complaints.  But it is a Bethesda game.
First, the pros:
* Combat feels better than in 3 or NV, though that's hardly a high bar
* Followers are a little smarter - but only a little.
* One of the better stories to come out of a Bethesda game.  Take that for what it's worth.
* Lots to do, although most of it is fairly shallow
* Beautiful environments
* Animations are significantly better than in previous Fallout games, but it's quite obvious that a lot of them were borrowed from Skyrim.
* Dogmeat
* Codsworth saying your name actually does wonders for immersion.  I robbed and murdered a group of people in the middle of nowhere at one point when he was with me and he said he disapproved whilst using my name.  Really made me feel like a jerk for killing them.
Now, the cons:
* The complete removal of RPG mechanics
* The conversation system has been simplified to four responses: Yes, No, Sarcasm, [insert question].  Aside from occasional things that will come up with followers or some things that happen in the main story, that's all you're going to get.
* Player voice.  This one's up for debate, but honestly, Bethesda games have always been about playing whoever you wanted however you wanted.  That is no longer possible - you are always going to be some variation of a concerned mother/father.  There is a mod which removes player voice, though the design issues still remain - namely the inability to really roleplay.  The mod is available here:
* Voice acting.  While not as bad as FO3 and Oblivion, some of the dialogue is genuinely awful.  Maybe it's the lines they were given, maybe it's the fact that they really aren't very good.  I've only played with a male character so far and nearly all of his dialogue sounds incredibly flat, like he really doesn't give a crap about anything that's happening.  That, or he's absolutely crazy.
* The settlement system, while great in theory, was implemented quite poorly in my honest opinion.  Design-wise, I, and I'm sure many others, will never bother to build up more than a couple of settlements.  It's just too much work to manage all of that, and I feel like it would've been better to have been able to designate a main settlement and let the others build themselves up.
* The build system honestly kind of sucks.  Aside from the fact that floating objects is inevitable - I'm looking at you, fences - the snapping is janky and you need to be able to do rotation snapping without having other objects already placed.
* The fact that you can only wait on furniture is annoying - often waiting could be used to fix bugs in older games.  So more obvious bugs.
* Piper likes to get stuck and her animations bug out.  A lot.  That may apply to other followers too, not sure as I've only really used her, dogmeat and Codsworth.
* Gamebryo really shows its age in many areas (the "Creation Engine" is still Gamebryo, people - it's less of a difference than there was between GoldSrc and the Quake engine; the change in name is mostly attributed to newer middleware and Papyrus over the old scripting language)
* Misc bugs, because Bethesda
Despite all of that, I still find myself recommending the game because it's fun, and mods will hopefully improve on some of the cons.  However, it definitely isn't something I'd say you need to stop whatever it is that you're doing and pick up right now.
But hey, I've always preferred Elder Scrolls.

I wanted to like this game. Here are a few reasons I dont.
eDIT: Easily the most annoying thing about this game is that enemy ai and companions know both were your targeting reticle is and when you have hit an attack key. In the case of enemy mobs they unsurprisingly but completely lamely avoid it(to the point of apparent precognition) and in the case of companion...well they are fantastic at saving an enemy mob per encounter by offering up their head to your bullet. There will be those who do not believe this to be the case just as there were in Skyrim. It is very easy to test. Observe unaware enemy ai without getting your targetting reticle near them..then put your targetting reticle near them. Their behavior clearly changes, to say nothing of the absurd speed they strafe at when you actually pull the trigger.
First is the quickweapons which are, at least for me, by no means quick. They frequently do not load your selected weapon or do it fantastically slowly.
Second is radscorpions. More specifically radscorpion burrow. They can burrow and be functionally immune? Annoying but fair enough. They can burrow through solid rock preventing you from tactical response? Not so fine and more than a little silly. They can use said burrow as a teleport reaching a sniper a considerable distance away almost instantly...Now that's just ridiculous. I've seen this very implementation in a number of games and in every single one it is immersion breaking and irritating.
More to come and as I've already stated I generally enjoy the game. Back to it.

Fallout 4 is far from a bad game. Would I recommend it to someone who has never played a Fallout game? Absolutely not, here's why:
The things that made Fallout unique are rarely found in this game:
Where are the RPG elements?
Why does this world not immerse me like Fallout New Vegas and Fallout 2 did?
Why does it feel like this game could've came out in 2010?
You see, if I would recommend someone a Fallout game, I would recommend Fallout 3 or Fallout New Vegas because these games actually feel like Fallout, the lore is interesting, the story is pretty good (except for the 2nd half of F3), it feels much more like an RPG and the Wasteland feels much more like it should in Fallout 3 and NV..
It's like Bethesda Game Studios wanted this game to be even more casual than it was before: it looks like they put a lot of attention into the shooting mechanics, which makes it feel like your daily doses of FPS where you can customize your weapons (I don't know why people were so excited about this, weapon customization has been in much more games before and Fallout 4's customization isn't even that deep). The exploration is still a good way to pass the time, the world might not be as interesting as Fallout New Vegas' world or the world from Fallout 2, where the game was mostly about the world and not about the player, but it's worth it to take a look around.
The story starts off incredibly familiar: you have to find a person (just like in Fallout 3 & New Vegas, good job Todd) and later on, it doesn't get much more interesting. "The Institute" is a pretty cool faction, but chances are that they will stick with you like the Enclave or the Brotherhood Of Steel is very low.
The design choice that bugged me the most is the player interaction:
Having a voiced protagonist makes you feel like you are playing a standard Fallout character, not like yourself like in the previous Fallout games, this does not make you feel like yourself as you were in previous Fallout games and that's why I'm probably not going to replay it. Also, the dialogue wheel is unclear at times, they should've stuck with the previous dialogue systems.
The presentation is just bad: the textures, it's like they're from 2009. The AI, feels worse than Skyrim. The optimization, just really bad, I get a lot of frame drops and load times are too long, while I should be able to run this game fine. The bugs, I've encountered a lot of them, varying from clipping through the wall to my blown off arm floating next to me (take a look at my screenshots).
If I were you, I would wait a few months till the mods arrive. I hope it fixes some of the flaws and improves the presentation. If you're new to Fallout, I recommend to start with Fallout 3 or Fallout New Vegas, they both feel much more complete and immersive (you can try Fallout 2 if you want to give it a shot, however the game is old and not suited for everyone).
If Todd Howard says "It just works", please don't trust him.

Beware our Lord and Saviour! The Post-Apocalyptic Looting Simulator 4.0 is here! Now with the ability to scan the contents  of containers before even opening them! Just point your eyes in the direction of the respective container! And of course, more supermutants, ghouls and the Universally beloved Brotherhood of Steel!
On a serious note though, the game is good at what it does: fulfilling your desire for exploration and looting. Now you can add crafting to this mix on small and big scale, including building your own private settlements. Is it fun? Of course. If you loved Fallout 3 and Fallout New Vegas most certainly you will love this one.
The game unfolds slowly, this time there is no Megaton right at your designated Vault Exit to overload your Pip-Boy with quests. You slowly make your way into the wasteland, acquiring new friends and bringing other settlements into your organized fold. You help protect them from all sort of scum. Then it's the usual Bethesda style exploration with massive amounts of side-quests which you will enjoy doing.
On a general note though, this is Fallout 3.5 not 4.0. Bethesda pretends that FNV never existed, so scrap any innovations from Obsidian. The lockpicking and computer hacking minigames are still the same. While I am ok with the lockpicking, but whoever at Bethesda thought that password letters mini-game is fun, must be a very dull person.
The skill point system is gone, completely replaced by perks which is great. No more imperative +10 INT builds. Thank God. It offers versatility and is FUN to pick a perk at every level up. While some of them could be better balanced, I am ok with the system.
Now let me get to the real painful part. The pip-boy inventory managent is a crime against humanity. How can you make such a stupid, annoying and unbearable interface for a game focused on looting is beyond my imagination. At least, thank you for Sort by weight function.
In conclusion, F4 is worth your time and money just because of it's ability to relive the pleasant memories of exploration in wasteland. Therefore people will generally dismiss the bad parts of the game and the lack of major innovations. However, if they continue this trend with Fallout 5, i am afraid many of us will be heavily disappointed.
To really sum this game up, you get overwhelmed by everything there is to do and you end up not knowing who you are anymore and just start collecting type writers and wonderglue. 10/10

Im gonna seperate this review into Positive, Negative, and Other.
Positive.
-The visuals are damned good, not groundbreaking but very nice for a first person game of this size (plus it has colour, not just brown/grey).
-The weapon and armour modding system is a great addition which gives you a much more personal touch to your arsenal.
-Power Armour, although you may get it a bit early, the mechanics of the suits make for a much more fun expereince, making you feel like a walking tank rather than the 'guy in big armour' that you felt like in previous installments.
-Throwbacks to Fallout 3, this may be a personal thing but mentions of things that my previous characters have done or been involved in is always really cool to me.
-Animations are a massive improvement all round, on humans, animals and everything else.
-Gunplay is far more satisfying than in previous games.
-Voice acting is pretty great all round in my opinion, not just on the player character.
Negative
-Bad optimisation in some areas leading to unwarranted frame drops.
-Pretty buggy, nothing game breaking for myself but i've heard of others having much worse experiences.
-Simplified dialogue and morality systems, with the former now having much more limited choices and the latter being based only on companions opinion of you, meaning you can't use your evil or good reputation to gain things like in previous games.
Other comments.
- The story is a good and bad point with it sacrificing that personal touch present in the previous games for a more engaging plot.
- The base building leaves a lot to be desired but is still an enjoyable experince, it can be clunky at times and frustrating at others but it is an addition that im glad of.
Conclusion? I would wholeheartedly recommend this game to anyone that enjoyed previous fallout games, it is an amazing expereince and well worth even the full asking price. It has some issues that will hopefully be patched out (not saying that excuses them), but I think this is an amazing game and an amazing addition to the franchise.

A lot has been said about this game in the past week. Here is the review of old-school Fallout fan, based on completing it and spending 80+ hours trying to find any sign of Fallout in this game.
BETRAYAL
I've been waiting for you for 7 years. I pre-ordered you. I upgraded my PC. I even took a vacation. And you betrayed me. You are not a Fallout game.
What is the essence of Fallout world? What makes us dive into it again and again? What makes gamers play 1998 game in 2015?
I think the answer is - Wasteland atmosphere and freedom of choice.
Atmosphere of destroyed by war and slowly degrading society, where word "moral" is long forgotten and gun is the law. Atmosphere of despair where only drugs can give you a brief relief from severe reality, if you are lucky enough to get them. Atmosphere of living, dynamic post-nuclear world. And the freedom of choice when every word, every action impacts the world. And of course countless variants of player customization via level progression. That makes these games special.
Fallout 1,2, NV meet these criteria, Fallout 3 partially. But not this abomination.
Wasteland feels like Wasteland no more. First of all because of new blurred cartoon-like graphics. Everything looks new, bright and polished, as if some invisible stealth cleaning guy has been wiping and waxing every damn brick in Boston for 200 years. And this polished Boston is filled up with targets. I can't call them "enemies" - they have no character, no history, no motivation, no ai; their only purpose is to die from your bullet.
I wonder how much does Todd Howard hate Fallout so he cut all RPG from it? This game is not an RPG. You cannot choose you role, it's been predefined for you. You cannot "do whatever you want ©", you can't even shoot whatever you want now. But you can choose whatever face, haircut or outfit you want, isn't that great?
Linear plot is death penalty to an RPG game (they call it so, not me) . And here Bethesda beats all records.
Each dialog has 4 options, but ALL lead to one (1) result. No matter what you say, it ends the same way - boring. This word can describe the whole thing. Boring. But there were pleasant surprises, couple of quests made impression of Alt-Tabbing to Fallout 3. Then idea came to my mind. I thought of ninja-designer, who sneaked into Bethesda office at night and wrote these quests, risking his life and freedom. Thank you, nameless hero.

A post-apocalyptic romp in the beautiful ruins of Boston filled with quests and things to do. While some things are a hit or miss (the main quest turning into mush at act 2, no dialogue skill checks) and some are just downright unacceptable (performance issues and the UI) the game manages to be engrossing, entertaining and a hell of a good time.
The combat is visceral and fast paced, a definite step up that feels like a proper first person shooter instead of the jerky 'Oblivion with guns' feel of FO3. The crafting system is very thorough and gives you a lot of leeway on how to play through the game. Power Armor has become actually badass to walk around and punch people in, which is a great thing as you can even mount a jetpack on it!
I really love the settlement system, while it is very shallow on the management side it manages to be a lovely little minigame where you can build whatever you want and make a homebase on the many plots around the Commonwealth. My huge five story tower on Spectacle Island was a blast to build and I can't wait to see what Bethesda and the modders add in the future to the settlement feature.
Some pointers on the main quest. I found that with (MQ Spoiler)
being a possibility, all the other factions coming to play naturally throughout the experience and some refusing to help you and turning into enemies past a certain point was very cleverly done. I wish they had fleshed out the factions even further, some motivations of the groups are left way too ambiguous, even though they really shouldn't be. The main motivation for your character is also shoddy and disconnected with the greater conflict going around, which is a shame, as the entire experience had so much more potential on that 'broken family' aspect. The twist was obvious and a bit cliche and the story itself a bit short, but it was a good time nonetheless.
I wish some aspects of the game were fleshed out, like having a proper settler management interface and more pieces to play with, but those are bound to come when the modders get their hands on the Creation Kit, so that's not a big deal.
Overall, I'd recommend this game wholeheartedly to anyone who wants to spend a good 50 to 100 hours roaming around Boston listening to "Worry Worry Worry" and blasting legendary deathclaws to shreds with gatling lasers. Fallout 4 has plenty of technical and other issues, but you won't find a boring experience here.

So basically I was having a blast. I love Fallout, I love Elder Scrolls, and for the most part I love Bethesda. I look past the bugs and the glitches just because I enjoy the gameplay and the world and all of the backstory that Bethesda cram into their games. But this game is proof of one point - quantity does not trump quality.
The graphics of this game are definitely an improvement, but they are by no means next gen. At best this game looks like a spruced up Fallout 3. They went on and on about writing a new engine for the game but it just doesn't seem that they have, at all. The game engine at its heart is still the "creation engine" (read: gamebryo) and it feels exactly like that. The physics and characters behave in exactly the way you expect them to in a Bethesda game, admittedly the art style for this game is miles beyond FO3 and Skyrim, but it just doesn't feel next gen. Not at all what should be coming out of a AAA developer in 2015.
I had a lot of fun with this game, as you can probably tell from the number of hours I've invested. I always found myself getting distracted and pottering off to do bits and pieces to break up the main questline, as I did with all of the other open world games I've ever played. However with FO4 there is one crucial difference - the repetition. A lot of the locations feel same-y, and a lot of the enemies you'll face are just clones of previous enemies with the word 'legendary' tacked on the front, and after encountering god knows how many legendary enemies they become somewhat underwhelming. The gunplay in this game is a vast improvement, but that doesn't make it any more interesting 40 hours or so into the world of Fallout - it still becomes just as monotonous as the rest of this game.
Plenty of ethical dilemmas in this one. Without spoiling too much, the story gives off a very SOMA-esque vibe - morality choices, "what makes a man a man", and that sort of thing. It's pretty interesting but the main quest, as with most other Bethesda games, trails off halfway through before being picked up again for the big finale. From what I could tell there's around 4/5 endings for this game depending on where your alliances lie and who you put your trust in, and I got close to finishing all of them were it not for a game-breaking bug that left me missing 8 hours of game progress, and thus ripped all of my desire to play away from me - repetition does not sit well with me.
As with a lot of Bethesda games though the side quests are far more manageable - shorter, more interesting, and often more heartbreaking. The world of Fallout is not a happy one, and if you're looking for a trip down Depression Lane, stopping off at Holy♥♥♥♥♥hatwasawful Avenue, then look no further than the side quests for your daily dose of emotional ballache.
Overall I can recommend this game to only hardcore FO/TES fans. If you enjoyed FO3 you'll probably enjoy this, if you haven't played a Fallout game before - don't start here. The repetition will break you before the bugs and glitches even get a chance to.

Im gonna seperate this review into Positive, Negative, and Other.
Positive.
-The visuals are damned good, not groundbreaking but very nice for a first person game of this size (plus it has colour, not just brown/grey).
-The weapon and armour modding system is a great addition which gives you a much more personal touch to your arsenal.
-Power Armour, although you may get it a bit early, the mechanics of the suits make for a much more fun expereince, making you feel like a walking tank rather than the 'guy in big armour' that you felt like in previous installments.
-Throwbacks to Fallout 3, this may be a personal thing but mentions of things that my previous characters have done or been involved in is always really cool to me.
-Animations are a massive improvement all round, on humans, animals and everything else.
-Gunplay is far more satisfying than in previous games.
-Voice acting is pretty great all round in my opinion, not just on the player character.
Negative
-Bad optimisation in some areas leading to unwarranted frame drops.
-Pretty buggy, nothing game breaking for myself but i've heard of others having much worse experiences.
-Simplified dialogue and morality systems, with the former now having much more limited choices and the latter being based only on companions opinion of you, meaning you can't use your evil or good reputation to gain things like in previous games.
Other comments.
- The story is a good and bad point with it sacrificing that personal touch present in the previous games for a more engaging plot.
- The base building leaves a lot to be desired but is still an enjoyable experince, it can be clunky at times and frustrating at others but it is an addition that im glad of.
Conclusion? I would wholeheartedly recommend this game to anyone that enjoyed previous fallout games, it is an amazing expereince and well worth even the full asking price. It has some issues that will hopefully be patched out (not saying that excuses them), but I think this is an amazing game and an amazing addition to the franchise.

The best explanation of how this game is different, is to look at Skyrim. When Bethesda made Fallout 3, they used the Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion engine. When they made Fallout 4, they used the ES V: Skyrim engine. When Skyrim came out, there was an inital (massive) backlash from PC gamers who had played Oblivion, because Skyrim simplified (in some cases "dumbed-down") many mechanics in an effort to make the game more accessible to more casual gamers, and to make a solid console version. Now, Skyrim is one of the most loved and well known games ever. The same thing is happening with Fallout 4, it is a simpler, more console oriented game, but it is still amazing, and I have no doubt that it will be as popular as Skyrim, if not moreso.

This isn't my full review, but an impression after almost 30 hours in the game.
Fallout 4 is easily the most impressive game this year, and one of the best Bethesda's best. Though, that doesn't mean it's even close to their best RPG. As you may know, they added a large base building/crafting system in order to make use of all the junk you find in the wasteland. Though this can be fun and add lots of content and hours to the play time, it doesn't add to the core gameplay.
That being said, the weapon and armor mods totally do and offer one of the most in depth weapon crafting system I have ever seen. Attachments can be removed and placed on different weapons, and perks from armor can be swapped around to similar sets, making every unique armor you find that much more useful. Though weapons and armor don't degenerate, the crafting system takes Skyrim's influences and makes it more fleshed out and satisfying.
Back to the role playing, since they spent the time animating faces for both protags and gave them voices, it meant that those resources (which don't serve to further immerse you in world, but rather make it more "cinematic") could have been used more efficiently.
On the other hand, the level up system has been greatly improved in place of numerical stats. I was very hesitant, as I love the tabletop math that has been a pivotal part of Bethesda's games since their origin, but after around 25 levels I understood the purpose of the new system. It's universal, it's fun, it's easy, and most of all it's aesthetic. The chart will make you double take the first time you see it, but when you realize how much you can do on your first level up (Nerd Rage and Mysterious Stranger by level 3!!!) you will discover how much freedom you have in the game as soon as you enter the world.
For people who claim it's not an RPG, but a FPSrpg, they clearly haven't made use of the system. There are lots of ways to approach any situation, allowing for melee, stealth, use of intelligence or similar perks to allow for many different ways to play the game. Though, the first person shooting mechanics are godly and VATS is better than ever so the fluid action is one of the game's strongest suits.
SPEAKING OF SUITS, power armor is the way to play the game if you want to have pure unadulterated fun. Bulldoze your enemies or drop down from the tallest buildings on to the raiders below. Less radiation, less vulnerable to bullets, and no fall damage really make something new and exciting for me. The 100 extra carry weight isn't too bad either, but watch your battery: fusion cores don't last that long.
I haven't played many main missions so I won't bother about the writing, but from what I've seen, it could be the best story in a Bethesda game yet.
So far, great game, good RPG, and you can kill people with teddy bears.

For those of you who read the reviews for this game (Which were mostly negative) when it first came out, and even now usually. Here's some advice for you.
Don't listen to a single thing they said.
After about 70 hours of this game, and gotten two of the endings (working on the third which so far i like more.) I can conclude that the issues that people have with this game are actually false. Here's some examples
People said that they removed everything that made this game an RPG. Which in reality all they did was remove the skills. I admit that's kind of a downer, but regardless they kept the Perks and even added more, which for some reason everyone was saying they removed the perks.
Another thing is people said the story was terrible. Well. Honestly it isn't a Stephen King novel. I'm sure by NOW people would expect Bethesda's storylines to be average. Or "meh" as I would say it. But I wouldn't say it was terrible. To be honest there was alot of plot twists that they could have I dunno. Put more to. But instead I didn't even realize most of the stuff that happens or is found out in plots because like I said. Meh. Even the big huge plot twist (you know the one) was lackluster. But it is still playable, I assure you. And even then you have a whole free open world to explore and do side quests anyways.
Also especially don't listen to the people that say the only dialogue is Yes, No, Sarcastic, and More Info. That is BARELY above the line of being used too much. I think one in every four lines of responses I saw that ensemble. I will admit though Sarcastic is very unclear. Because it ranges from pure poking fun to being a complete butt. Also this wasn't a real issue I heard of but the Voice Acting for the Male PC is awful imho. And I beat the game with him. But now, in my second playthrough with the female character. It's much better. Which kind of sucks considering the story pretty much makes alot more sense for your male character (considering he narrates the beginning and is a vet) while the female is just like.. a girl with a law degree. Glad they didn't make them too identical though.
Also for some reason Ron Perlman didn't narrate the beginning. Even though he was a voice actor in the game. I think he did the Anchorman voice in the pre-war beginning? I mean.. Come on man.. They broke the tradition.
Finally, and this one is different. A major issue I've had that everyone else is actually disagreeing with. Everyone is saying this is the least bug filled Bethesda game in a long time, which is surprising for them. Well as someone who played Oblivion, Fallout New Vegas, and Skyrim when they first came out... I can say that that is false. And that Fallout 4 has probably been the MOST bug filled Bethesda game for a while. At least for now, of course they will fix it. (Might take a while though. They're starting to hate Computer Gamers too)
It's definitely worth getting. Preferably during a sale but still. Let's just hope that Obsidian makes a spin-off sorta thing. Like with New Vegas, which I definitely would say is better than this, but this is still good. You have to remember most people that write negative reviews go into the game with a negative attitude that already prejudges their outcome. If you play a game, expecting it to suck. You're gonna say it sucks. I mean be honest how many people often have a complete 180 in opinion?
Overall I give this game a 7/10.

Worth the 60 dollars asking price because you will definitely be able to play for many hours to get your moneys worth at least as long as you dont mind appreciating the game for what it is. However i do want to bring up a few negative points, this game is not an RPG. They removed all skills, left the perk system and removed all branching paths for quests, as well as the abililty to be evil or really have any consequences for choices that you make.
If i was to classify it i would say this is an open world exploration FPS. The RPG elements are laughable the only differenes between a level 35 character and a level 1 is the loot the level 35 character has and his total HP. Fallout 4 uses a system very similar to Skyrims and its lame. Every level up you can choose between increasing one of your S.P.E.C.I.A.L skills or getting a perk in a different type of skill. For example there are perks like Gunslinger which allow you to do more damage with single fire pistols. There is also a tough guy perk which increases damage resistance and hacking and lockpicking perks which allow you to get better at both those activities. The game is fun but deep RPG it is not. The only real thing you can choose about your character is his/her looks. The new character creator is very well done and acutally allows you to create good looking characters for once. AI is very terrible, AI companions either get directly in your way or stuck in objeccts/ lost. It has always been much easier and more enjoyable to play a Bethesda game without companions and that hasnt changed here.
Most of the character animations are taken directly from Skyrim and even though the graphics do look good they are noticeably last generation. The graphics and animations reminded me a lot of Skyrim which is not good so many years later. The characters you do meet are very bland, very rarely do you actually run into interesting characters, especially not within the first 10-20 hours. I expereienced some frame rate drop when playing in some of the major settlements but otherwise the optimization was pretty good.
Next up that i would like to talk about is the conversation wheel. It is bland and uninspired, dialougue choices are so removed and unimportant to this game its hard to really get attached to your character when you can only choose between four similar responses to dialougue all game long(Sarcastic, yes, no, or more info). Another thing to be noted is that branching paths have been greatly removed from this game, most quests can only be completed in very shallow and straight forward ways.
This time around Bethesda has really removed a lot of the consequences for your actions. Most of the game i was able to keep three of the factions friendly with me even though they are supossed to be against eachother. It got so bad that a few missions i would go to the area where all three Factions were in combat and be friendlies to all of them, even after i started killing them! You really cant play evil, most of the NPCs are un-killable anyways.
This game is really all about the action and combat. RPG elements were left by the wayside in order to sell more copies and make this game easily playable for the COD fans. On that note though gunplay has been vastly improved. The writing suffers a lot from plotholes and using Bethesda's dynamic quest system. Besides a few quests that you can tell were created specifically for the game a lot of the factions even toss you these random dynamic quests which are always "kill this" or fetch quests.
Fallout 4 is a good shooter and worth the money but if your looking for a real RPG experience than Bethesda has not delivered, as this feels like another Skyrim in so many different ways. They did add a new building UI so that you can build all kinds of random structures for your settlements and things. However i didnt ask fallout to bring me a Minecraft gamemode(they didnt even bother adding a tutorial to this gamemode) i was hoping for it to actually be an RPG as it claims. For this reason i have to give it a negative review as Fallout 4 is definitely an over-hyped FPS.

If you thought Fallout 3 was better then New Vegas then you'll probably like this game, if your like me and you thought New Vegas was far better then 3 then this is definitely going to feel like a huge a step back.
Theres way less RPG; With the introduction of a voiced character it means there is far fewer options in conversations you can have then before (which we're less then the games before them already.), Skills are gone and replaced with a just a perk every level instead of every other level. There is almost no way to be Evil or anything close to Evil at all, your dialog choices basically Wasteland Jesus, Sarcastic Wasteland Jesus, Wasteland Merc or Inquisitive Person, if you decide to just go rogue and do what you like? Can't, I'd wager 80% of the named NPC's in the game are immortal via essential flags.
The story is exactly what you'd expect in a Bethesda game; overall less then NV but about the same as 3; aka utterly meaningless and just a excuse to for you to be in the world to roam around.
The companions are 'personality wise' fine, they're interesting enough and there's enough of them that you can continously swap them out when you get bored of them. However they suffer from the fact their nothing but that personality. There is literally no difference between any of them when given the exact same gear which is frankly rather Bizzare that say a Detective is just as handy in combat as a Brotherhood of Steel Paladin as long as both of them are in Power Armor with Gatling Lasers.
Gameplay itself it's now just a average FPS game in the Wasteland with all the dialog and RPG features removed. More akin to Borderlands then Fallout. Nearly every single quest/task in the game revolves around just slaughtering your way through a location, or waves of enemies or collecting a item from a chest.
They added in a build-your-own-settlement but I honestly have no idea why it even exists, the amount of resources and money a settlement generates per day wouldn't pay itself off in the time it took you to 100% the game if you built it day 1, and if that isn't the purpose you built it and for shopping instead there's already prebuilt cities with a ton of vendors, so yah pointless.
They also added a gun mod system that more or less is entirely what EA did from Dead Space 2 to 3. Instead of the guns existing already they're just in pieces and you can swappem around. The fact the random dropped guns and vendor sold guns level with you means that even if you ignore modding entirely you'll still likely have a near fully modded weapon anyway. In the end all it really exists to do is to drive you nuts looking through your inventory with the dozen adjectives and nouns every single item name has, alot with so many it stretches past the screen limits.
tl:dr --- Overall I'd say literally every possible thing is better in New Vegas with the exception of shooting. Here the reworked shooting is a bit better then 3/NV at the cost of pretty much everything else. It's good for just wasting time wandering around while you listen to podcasts. 6/10

The main complaints of this game that some people have are things like "it's super glitchy", "it doesn't feel like a Fallout game" and "the dialogue system is terrible", and I'm going to try to convince you that these are somewhat illegitimate arguments.
Glitches: I have hitherto put down about 53 hours into this game, and I am yet to find something that really bothers me (except for the terrible companion AI). My copy of the game, at least, has so far been glitch free and running at a smooth 60fps at the highest settings. It really concerns me that I've heard this "glitch argument" from people who haven't even played the game themselves, who have only seen compilations of glitch videos made by a variety of people, which also leads me to believe that each individual person rarely come across more than one or two glitches in their copy of the game. (Keep in mind that this is based upon personal experience. It is very possible that I might be wrong).
Not a Fallout Game: If you played Fallout 1, 2, tactics and BoS first, would you still consider 3 and New Vegas to "feel like Fallout games"? Probably not. And besides, isn't it a good thing that games develop? I, for one, wouldn't have supported the idea of making Fallout 3 and New vegas but with better graphics, and call it Fallout 4. It might've been the most accurate thing to do, but I would definitely have grown tired of it quickly and then went back to playing Fallout 3 and New Vegas again.
Dialogue System: I think that the new dialogue system was a great contribution for making the franchise go forward, instead of just making the same game over and over again. It might take away that sense of "being the character you create", but they've already made 6 games with the same dialogue system, and now we complain about them renewing it? Strange.
Now, from my own subjective perspective, I would definitely recommend it, but I cannot confirm how other people would react to it. It's definitely different from the previous games, but with reasonable changes, I would say.
So hell yeah, I'd recommend it, but don't get mad at me if you don't enjoy it yourself. It's not for everyone.

Worth the 60 dollars asking price because you will definitely be able to play for many hours to get your moneys worth at least as long as you dont mind appreciating the game for what it is. However i do want to bring up a few negative points, this game is not an RPG. They removed all skills, left the perk system and removed all branching paths for quests, as well as the abililty to be evil or really have any consequences for choices that you make.
If i was to classify it i would say this is an open world exploration FPS. The RPG elements are laughable the only differenes between a level 35 character and a level 1 is the loot the level 35 character has and his total HP. Fallout 4 uses a system very similar to Skyrims and its lame. Every level up you can choose between increasing one of your S.P.E.C.I.A.L skills or getting a perk in a different type of skill. For example there are perks like Gunslinger which allow you to do more damage with single fire pistols. There is also a tough guy perk which increases damage resistance and hacking and lockpicking perks which allow you to get better at both those activities. The game is fun but deep RPG it is not. The only real thing you can choose about your character is his/her looks. The new character creator is very well done and acutally allows you to create good looking characters for once. AI is very terrible, AI companions either get directly in your way or stuck in objeccts/ lost. It has always been much easier and more enjoyable to play a Bethesda game without companions and that hasnt changed here.
Most of the character animations are taken directly from Skyrim and even though the graphics do look good they are noticeably last generation. The graphics and animations reminded me a lot of Skyrim which is not good so many years later. The characters you do meet are very bland, very rarely do you actually run into interesting characters, especially not within the first 10-20 hours. I expereienced some frame rate drop when playing in some of the major settlements but otherwise the optimization was pretty good.
Next up that i would like to talk about is the conversation wheel. It is bland and uninspired, dialougue choices are so removed and unimportant to this game its hard to really get attached to your character when you can only choose between four similar responses to dialougue all game long(Sarcastic, yes, no, or more info). Another thing to be noted is that branching paths have been greatly removed from this game, most quests can only be completed in very shallow and straight forward ways.
This time around Bethesda has really removed a lot of the consequences for your actions. Most of the game i was able to keep three of the factions friendly with me even though they are supossed to be against eachother. It got so bad that a few missions i would go to the area where all three Factions were in combat and be friendlies to all of them, even after i started killing them! You really cant play evil, most of the NPCs are un-killable anyways.
This game is really all about the action and combat. RPG elements were left by the wayside in order to sell more copies and make this game easily playable for the COD fans. On that note though gunplay has been vastly improved. The writing suffers a lot from plotholes and using Bethesda's dynamic quest system. Besides a few quests that you can tell were created specifically for the game a lot of the factions even toss you these random dynamic quests which are always "kill this" or fetch quests.
Fallout 4 is a good shooter and worth the money but if your looking for a real RPG experience than Bethesda has not delivered, as this feels like another Skyrim in so many different ways. They did add a new building UI so that you can build all kinds of random structures for your settlements and things. However i didnt ask fallout to bring me a Minecraft gamemode(they didnt even bother adding a tutorial to this gamemode) i was hoping for it to actually be an RPG as it claims. For this reason i have to give it a negative review as Fallout 4 is definitely an over-hyped FPS.

I will do my best to give you a detailed pros and cons list, but all-in-all, this game is Fantastic and very in-depth. The main story is much better than Fallout NV and 3 (my personal opinion) and the world is teeming with life. It seems like it's own living breathing world, with random events and situations you will encounter in the wasteland. Here are the pros/cons.
PROS:
Better combat system than the previous games.  Weapons,explosions and gunfire seem and sound more deadly than before
Better Perk System (opinion): They have some interesting skills as in ramming people with power armor on, or using your dog to hold enemies on the ground for increased V.A.T.S Accuracy
Settlements: Building your own settlements and building up the community with resources and defensive capabilities give me a sense of ownership in the game. The crafting system is pretty in-depth (although a little rough around the edges). You come across people in the wasteland that you help and you can offer them safety at one of your settlements. Settlements come under attack as well so the need to intervene comes up as well.
Map: The world has an overly abundant amount of content as opposed to Skyrim and the Previous Fallout games. Yes, the maps were bigger, but there would be spans of open fields or wasteland with 1 or 2 caves and nothing else. FO4 has something around every block and over every hill it seems to me.
Power armor: Where do I start, The power armor in this game actually feels like power armor (if you know what I mean) It feels large and powerful. Jumping from a 4 story building onto the ground below, cracking the ground beneath you or popping sandbags and running into an enemy using the force of your power armor.The different "helmet" hud. Trying to cross a river and sinking to the riverbed floor. Also towering over other people makes you feel superior. Lets not forget the modding. You can upgrade your armor pieces, modify them and change the paint on your power armor as well. In fallout 3 it was no different than wearing a a jumpsuit, It just gave you better defense.
Story: I find the quests more mysterious and in depth than previous fallout games. Fallout 3: Find your dad, Fallout:NV find your killer. Fallout 4: Find the man who killed your wife and stole your son, which leads into something much much more. Some quests are pretty "MMO'ish" go here, kill this, go there kill that, but the overall story have me enticed. It was also nice to live a piece of the past in the pre-wasteland world for however brief the moment was.
Enemies: The enemies in this game are vast and numerous and the added "legendary" enemies are a nice touch as they are harder and give better loot. The monsters of the wasteland seem more vicious and brutal than previous games. For instance, Deathclaws are monstrous and tower over you even in power armor. They will hit you and stagger you and jump on top of you and slash you. Sentry bots are the most aggressive thing in this game. When you run across one you say to yourself &quot♥♥♥♥♥♥quot;. The unique "bosses" are nice as well.
Companions: A nice collection of companions to choose from, personally Dogmeat is the best. He will grab items for you or find hidden stashes. NEVER complains either.
Weather System: Same as the previous games except for Radiation Storms, which are fantastic.
Character Customization: You can truly make a detailed customized Toon in this game
Cons:
Graphics: Up close the Graphics are good, but the rendering further away seem very XBOX360-ish I guess you could say. For instance the skyscrapers in Boston do not look good from far away nor does the city when you are viewing it from high up or from across a river. Not sure if this was for performance reason or what, but I don't like that way it renders at a distance. I use a 6 gig msi 290x so all my settings are Ultra. Also some textures seem "meshed together" Graphics aren't that big of a deal to me, but to some it is.
Bugs: The corrupt saved games can get annoying and can ruin a good play through. The solution to this is NEVER quick save (f5) or use the auto saves. Open up your game and manually save the file. I lost 4 hours of game play early on when the games saved quick saves ( all 5 of them ) were corrupt.
Build/Scavenge System: Needs to be more polished for PC and it has absolutely no tutorial or help as to how it works. The first time using it took me a couple hours and some forum-diving to figure it out.
Dialogue: The only thing I don't like about the Dialogue is the color coded persuasion. It should be flat and not hint at what your % success rate is. Petty but still
Performance: I get a solid 60 fps Inside buildings and in the wilderness. When I'm in Boston I get 40-45 fps. At Random times or certain spots in the city I will hit a solid 20 fps for no reason what-so-ever. Not sure if some areas aren't optimized as others. The interesting thing is that if I come back to that area at a later date my fps is back up to 40 60 fps. I can't explain that one.
Ghouls: Ghoul movement is very weird and glitchy, some of their animations literally look like a frame by frame clip.
Map: I said earlier although the map is small, but there is plenty of content. I still stand by that, but I wish the map was larger regardless. If you walk from one side to the other is about a 41 minute walk where Skyrim was 2 hours.
Boston: I feel the city could be bigger. I believe its bigger than D.C but it still seems small to me. Although when you enter the city you get lost in it. When viewing it from above though seems small.
Adhesive: You will spend hours upon hours searching for Duct-Tape. Adhesive is used to make EVERY modification in the game. EVERY one.
Conclusion:
Thank you for taking the time to read this and I hope this helps you dictate your decision to buy this game. If you are a Fallout Fan than this game will give you just what you need. The immersion is there, the combat is there, and the stories are there. It's Fallout; Welcome to the wasteland!

So to get it out of the way:
I absolutely recommend this game.  For 60 dollars I feel like I have a better and more complete game on my hands than many studios deliver for 70+ with collector's editions and DLC.  Yes there will be DLC, and I will almost certainly happily buy it too if it's at all similar to Skyrim's - but you won't need it; because the game is already great, if not flawless.
----
Detailed breakdown -
The combat feels much more lively.  It's fast and brutal, but it's not so fast  you can't stop to think (especially if you use VATS mode strategically) - basically it's a proper shooter bolted on to a great RPG.
The story, at least so far, has been surprisingly interesting to me - it really hooked me in because it's so personal to start with; to the point where in the base construction side of things I've tried to keep some sentimental stuff just for that.  (I'm usually a bit more utilitarian with base building unless the game gives me an absolute ton of freedom, like Wildstar.)
The biggest thing though, is that I feel like I could play for ages and just not run out of stuff to do, find and explore - there's just so much STUFF there, and stuff I'd actually want to do.* - I've barely scratched the surface so far.
There are a few negatives though:
First of all, some areas are kind of poorly optimized - at least on my machine I'll go from 60FPS to a very sluggish sub-20 in a couple interior environments (not many, but it has happened).  This may be a deal breaker for some folks.
Another possible dealbreaker is the control scheme - it's very much usable with a mouse and keyboard (which is what I play with); BUT... it's not at all ideal, not even close; and there are keys you cannot rebind (or rebind entirely).  This... is frankly stupid and infuriating and I dont' know how Bethesda managed to skip it.  - Basically it's a console control scheme poorly ported to PC.  It's livable, but it's not ideal.  I like the rest of the game so much that putting up with the control hassles to play is well worth it; but you should be aware of this aspect before you buy.
The final negative, is that you will almost certainly be doing a LOT of inventory management, especially if you do any settlement stuff.  This is pretty par for the course in RPGs, but because of the console-style interface can be especially tedious.  It's worth putting up with;  but it is probably my single least favorite aspect of the game.
So to sum it up:
It's a fantastic game, a great RPG and solid shooter at the same time; it's vast and the crafting system is especially great.  It is however hobbled as it's console-oriented roots show through substantially, and optimization can be wonky.
Basically, if you love Fallout, post-apocalyptic settings, shooters or RPGs, you'll probably find something to like here if you're willing to put up with the foibles.
*It doesn't do much good if a game gives you a ton to do but it's all tedious crap right?

I have just finished the main story of this game and can finally say I have been overwhelmed by how little thought was put into this. There are no factions not relating to the main quest, and all but 2 settlements in the Commonwealth are built by yourself so there are no npc's to give out side quests or other interesting gems around the wastes. This also means that there is little to nothing to do in the game apart from continue the main story, which is in itself atrocious (disclaimer: I've never thought a Bethesda game has done a good story), and actually does everything to remove any consequences to any of your actions!
I went around for 90% of my playtime friendly to all 3 factions which were diametrically opposed to each other. This was despite the fact that I would often be given missions by each of these factions to kill the others, which would lead me to the very bizzare situation of walking up to a bunch of friendlies, killing one of them, then walking away. Of which there were NEVER any consequences for. Then suddenly on one mission I get a massive warning popup telling me if I used the teleporter I would permanently become opposed to the Brotherhood of Steel, for completing an action that they had no awareness of. This just felt arbritary, and frankly stupid to me.
The game likes to make you feel like some double agent performing for their own secret agenda, but it only comes off as if every other person is just a moron.
Bottom line, I'm sure most people who played fallout 3 or earlier might like this, but if you have had an aversion to the main story of other Bethesda games in the past and just like to explore and do side quests or rise ranks in organisations, then I would be surprised if you gained satisfaction from this game.

For those of you who read the reviews for this game (Which were mostly negative) when it first came out, and even now usually. Here's some advice for you.
Don't listen to a single thing they said.
After about 70 hours of this game, and gotten two of the endings (working on the third which so far i like more.) I can conclude that the issues that people have with this game are actually false. Here's some examples
People said that they removed everything that made this game an RPG. Which in reality all they did was remove the skills. I admit that's kind of a downer, but regardless they kept the Perks and even added more, which for some reason everyone was saying they removed the perks.
Another thing is people said the story was terrible. Well. Honestly it isn't a Stephen King novel. I'm sure by NOW people would expect Bethesda's storylines to be average. Or "meh" as I would say it. But I wouldn't say it was terrible. To be honest there was alot of plot twists that they could have I dunno. Put more to. But instead I didn't even realize most of the stuff that happens or is found out in plots because like I said. Meh. Even the big huge plot twist (you know the one) was lackluster. But it is still playable, I assure you. And even then you have a whole free open world to explore and do side quests anyways.
Also especially don't listen to the people that say the only dialogue is Yes, No, Sarcastic, and More Info. That is BARELY above the line of being used too much. I think one in every four lines of responses I saw that ensemble. I will admit though Sarcastic is very unclear. Because it ranges from pure poking fun to being a complete butt. Also this wasn't a real issue I heard of but the Voice Acting for the Male PC is awful imho. And I beat the game with him. But now, in my second playthrough with the female character. It's much better. Which kind of sucks considering the story pretty much makes alot more sense for your male character (considering he narrates the beginning and is a vet) while the female is just like.. a girl with a law degree. Glad they didn't make them too identical though.
Also for some reason Ron Perlman didn't narrate the beginning. Even though he was a voice actor in the game. I think he did the Anchorman voice in the pre-war beginning? I mean.. Come on man.. They broke the tradition.
Finally, and this one is different. A major issue I've had that everyone else is actually disagreeing with. Everyone is saying this is the least bug filled Bethesda game in a long time, which is surprising for them. Well as someone who played Oblivion, Fallout New Vegas, and Skyrim when they first came out... I can say that that is false. And that Fallout 4 has probably been the MOST bug filled Bethesda game for a while. At least for now, of course they will fix it. (Might take a while though. They're starting to hate Computer Gamers too)
It's definitely worth getting. Preferably during a sale but still. Let's just hope that Obsidian makes a spin-off sorta thing. Like with New Vegas, which I definitely would say is better than this, but this is still good. You have to remember most people that write negative reviews go into the game with a negative attitude that already prejudges their outcome. If you play a game, expecting it to suck. You're gonna say it sucks. I mean be honest how many people often have a complete 180 in opinion?
Overall I give this game a 7/10.

The companions are 'personality wise' fine, they're interesting enough and there's enough of them that you can continously swap them out when you get bored of them. However they suffer from the fact their nothing but that personality. There is literally no difference between any of them when given the exact same gear which is frankly rather Bizzare that say a Detective is just as handy in combat as a Brotherhood of Steel Paladin as long as both of them are in Power Armor with Gatling Lasers.
Gameplay itself it's now just a average FPS game in the Wasteland with all the dialog and RPG features removed. More akin to Borderlands then Fallout. Nearly every single quest/task in the game revolves around just slaughtering your way through a location, or waves of enemies or collecting a item from a chest.
They added in a build-your-own-settlement but I honestly have no idea why it even exists, the amount of resources and money a settlement generates per day wouldn't pay itself off in the time it took you to 100% the game if you built it day 1, and if that isn't the purpose you built it and for shopping instead there's already prebuilt cities with a ton of vendors, so yah pointless.
They also added a gun mod system that more or less is entirely what EA did from Dead Space 2 to 3. Instead of the guns existing already they're just in pieces and you can swappem around. The fact the random dropped guns and vendor sold guns level with you means that even if you ignore modding entirely you'll still likely have a near fully modded weapon anyway. In the end all it really exists to do is to drive you nuts looking through your inventory with the dozen adjectives and nouns every single item name has, alot with so many it stretches past the screen limits.
tl:dr --- Overall I'd say literally every possible thing is better in New Vegas with the exception of shooting. Here the reworked shooting is a bit better then 3/NV at the cost of pretty much everything else. It's good for just wasting time wandering around while you listen to podcasts. 6/10

[IGN. ca]
Exploration has its own rewards, as this is the most diverse Fallout world yet, with dilapidated urban areas, ominous dead forests, eerie swamps, a desolate area mired in a hellish radioactive haze, and even some areas that look borderline hospitable like beaches and budding farms. The Commonwealth’s much more color-saturated than Fallout 3’s Capital Wasteland, though it has its fair share of grays and browns, and it shares New Vegas’ bright blue sky (as opposed to oppressive clouds) when it’s not night time or raining or green with a terrifying radiation storm. It’s often beautiful. Attention to detail is evident everywhere – Fallout 4 might not be a leader in all areas of graphics technology (character animations are still a weakness) but from the intricate Pip-Boy wrist-computer interface (which completely changes when you’re in power armor), to careful arrangement of skeletal remains that tell the tragically dark or tragically funny stories of long-dead characters, to tattered poster art on the walls, to even raindrops on your visor (if you’re wearing one) it’s consistently impressive.
Perhaps because this adventure is such a long haul, Fallout 4 is  a bit overeager to hook us in the beginning. After a brief glimpse of pre-war life in Fallout’s familiar-but-strange near-future and a retelling of the events on the day the bombs fell in 2077, we barely have time to get our hands dirty in the post-apocalyptic era before Fallout 4 throws us into a big action moment: You’re given a suit of the big, stompy power armor and a heavy weapon, and put into an intense brawl against the series’ most iconic monster.
[The world, exploration, crafting, atmosphere, and story of Fallout 4 are all key parts of this hugely successful sandbox role-playing game. Great new reasons to obsessively gather and hoard relics of happier times, strong companions, and sympathetic villains driving tough decisions make it an adventure I’ll definitely replay and revisit. Even the technical shakiness that crops up here and there can’t even begin to slow down its momentum.]

A lot of the complaints seem to be people that are unhappy that it's not exactly the same game as Fallout 3 and New Vegas with a new engine, but oh well, everyone has their opinions. Nice break from the real world if you've got the time. If you're a fan of the series, you'll like the continuing saga that FO4 offers.
+ Nicely detailed post-apocalyptic environments
+ Gun mechanics feel greatly improved over the clunky execution seen in FO3
+ Appreciate the new settlement-building aspect but sometimes it feels tedious
+ Easy enough to stray off course and investigate something of particular interest in the landscape
+ Side quests keep things moving
+ Character models are very much improved from FO3/Skyrim
+ New creature and human enemy types are introduced which vary what you might run into
- Weak main storyline (but that's relative), there is very little new ground broken and no sense of urgency on the part of the player to make things right.
- Alot of the radio music is ported over from FO3
- The guns all start to feel the same after your first 20 hours of play
- Gun modding is a little convoluted initially and seems to add very little later on
- Graphics seem only slightly better than Fallout 3, but still improved and detailed
- Menu UI appears rather cumbersome initially but playtime fixes that
- Combat still remains unrealistic as targets can take several headshots from a super-modded weapon and still fight as if at full strength.
- Power Armor is too easy to come by and makes early combat far too easy in turn.
- The border map world limit ("You cant go that way") certainly removes realism
There are some bad qualities that remain from FO3 (and Skyrim for that matter) but none are a deal-breakers for those purchasers still on the fence. Despite its small improvements over FO3 I do not regret the purchase at full price.

So to get it out of the way:
I absolutely recommend this game.  For 60 dollars I feel like I have a better and more complete game on my hands than many studios deliver for 70+ with collector's editions and DLC.  Yes there will be DLC, and I will almost certainly happily buy it too if it's at all similar to Skyrim's - but you won't need it; because the game is already great, if not flawless.
----
Detailed breakdown -
The combat feels much more lively.  It's fast and brutal, but it's not so fast  you can't stop to think (especially if you use VATS mode strategically) - basically it's a proper shooter bolted on to a great RPG.
The story, at least so far, has been surprisingly interesting to me - it really hooked me in because it's so personal to start with; to the point where in the base construction side of things I've tried to keep some sentimental stuff just for that.  (I'm usually a bit more utilitarian with base building unless the game gives me an absolute ton of freedom, like Wildstar.)
The biggest thing though, is that I feel like I could play for ages and just not run out of stuff to do, find and explore - there's just so much STUFF there, and stuff I'd actually want to do.* - I've barely scratched the surface so far.
There are a few negatives though:
First of all, some areas are kind of poorly optimized - at least on my machine I'll go from 60FPS to a very sluggish sub-20 in a couple interior environments (not many, but it has happened).  This may be a deal breaker for some folks.
Another possible dealbreaker is the control scheme - it's very much usable with a mouse and keyboard (which is what I play with); BUT... it's not at all ideal, not even close; and there are keys you cannot rebind (or rebind entirely).  This... is frankly stupid and infuriating and I dont' know how Bethesda managed to skip it.  - Basically it's a console control scheme poorly ported to PC.  It's livable, but it's not ideal.  I like the rest of the game so much that putting up with the control hassles to play is well worth it; but you should be aware of this aspect before you buy.
The final negative, is that you will almost certainly be doing a LOT of inventory management, especially if you do any settlement stuff.  This is pretty par for the course in RPGs, but because of the console-style interface can be especially tedious.  It's worth putting up with;  but it is probably my single least favorite aspect of the game.
So to sum it up:
It's a fantastic game, a great RPG and solid shooter at the same time; it's vast and the crafting system is especially great.  It is however hobbled as it's console-oriented roots show through substantially, and optimization can be wonky.
Basically, if you love Fallout, post-apocalyptic settings, shooters or RPGs, you'll probably find something to like here if you're willing to put up with the foibles.
*It doesn't do much good if a game gives you a ton to do but it's all tedious crap right?

I have just finished the main story of this game and can finally say I have been overwhelmed by how little thought was put into this. There are no factions not relating to the main quest, and all but 2 settlements in the Commonwealth are built by yourself so there are no npc's to give out side quests or other interesting gems around the wastes. This also means that there is little to nothing to do in the game apart from continue the main story, which is in itself atrocious (disclaimer: I've never thought a Bethesda game has done a good story), and actually does everything to remove any consequences to any of your actions!
I went around for 90% of my playtime friendly to all 3 factions which were diametrically opposed to each other. This was despite the fact that I would often be given missions by each of these factions to kill the others, which would lead me to the very bizzare situation of walking up to a bunch of friendlies, killing one of them, then walking away. Of which there were NEVER any consequences for. Then suddenly on one mission I get a massive warning popup telling me if I used the teleporter I would permanently become opposed to the Brotherhood of Steel, for completing an action that they had no awareness of. This just felt arbritary, and frankly stupid to me.
The game likes to make you feel like some double agent performing for their own secret agenda, but it only comes off as if every other person is just a moron.
Bottom line, I'm sure most people who played fallout 3 or earlier might like this, but if you have had an aversion to the main story of other Bethesda games in the past and just like to explore and do side quests or rise ranks in organisations, then I would be surprised if you gained satisfaction from this game.

I really enjoyed this game. Gameplay was good; combat was fun. For story, it has a similar style to NV in which you have several different factions you can join up with to complete your end goal. Looting is much more streamlined, which is nice. While there only a few types of guns, moddifications to guns are plentiful, and I rather enjoyed the modding and crafting experience.  Like any fallout game, any content is optional. Do you even have to fight? No, not really. There are many occasions when you can talk your way out of fighting.
Side quests are phenomenal. They can be pretty tense and serious, and the can be fun and ridiculous. After 50 hours in the game, I am still finding new content, and new experiences I never had in game before. The colour scheme of the world really works for it.
What is wrong with this game? I've crashed twice without warning, experieneced a strange frame rate drop issue once, and I witnessed a broken car suddenly fly and flop over. None of that lessened my game expereince.
Settlement building is a nice feature. It is not like Skyrim's hearthfire add on, but a chance for you to design and build more freely. It's pretty optional, and reminds me of fallout shelter. I'm enjoying building up settlements.
The leveling system is a little different this time around. It no longer uses points to add to each indiviudal skill, but a SPECIAL and perk only system. Meaning, when you level up, you get one point, which can either go into a perk, or raise your special stat by one. When you start the game off, you'll have less SPECIAL stats then other fallout games because of this. For me, it doesn't make much difference to how I overall play. If anything, I'm coming to like this more than the old leveling system.
Followers are well written, I love some of the companions I can have, and I'm genuinely interested in their stories. Fallout 4 has been compelling, emotionally engaging, and a blast. No other game in recent memory has made me feel the need to make decisions, over the have to make decisions because the game tells me to. I had to make tough calls that sided with how I felt. As for getting in character, having a background made it easier to slip into that character's shoes for my first playthrough. My second playthrough, and ultimately my many others, will likely be stories based off of my own backgrounds that I make up. Because I can do that, being a mature adult with imagination.
I give this game a 10/10, Game of the Year, most fun since sliced bread.
