It is a well presented game with pleasing if simple graphical design and a nice atmosphere (even if the messages between levels can make you feel like you are being preached to by Xavier Renegade Angel at times), but there are some flaws:
-Some levels force you to wait several seconds before getting in to them which ramps up frustration a huge amount.
-Sometimes the timings and distances are incredibly tight on boring sections, its made worse because it seems like this wasnt made for keyboard/mouse given how easy it is with the slightest tap to hit a wall.
-Basic options like restart, volume sliders, and any obvious way to put it in windowed mode are missing, which is an incredibly annoying trend with a lot of indie games. This isnt minimal, its categorically bad design.
-Difficulty can be very variable, and the difficulty level can be the wrong way round due to the way timings line up better. (Also, the easy ending seems to me to be the best, but perhaps thats deliberate so most people see it.)
When it works, its a pleasure to play and the pacing of fairly rapid single screen levels, along with the changing geometry and sounds keeps you retrying and progressing. Just expect more than a couple of spots where the annoyance mounts up way too fast to be fun.

This is the standalone expansion to
.
Much like its core game, the Rise of the Owlverlord is fun, creative and difficult. The game forces the player to shift between "cute" and "punk" Giana constantly in order to make progress or survive traps even more than the original game. Traps are always there making the player balance out cleverness and reflexes, and enemies are strategically put most of times to aid reaching a secret area or merely to pose an extra challenge.
Swapping between cute and punk Giana is a must here and the game will never let you forget about this even once. Swapping can be done between a specific key assigned to it or by using the Fireball Roll (which automatically swaps to punk Giana) or twirling (which swaps to cute Giana). At first it may seem simple, but the game will have creative ways to spice up things as levels goes by.
Running and jumping is very precise as you'd expect (and want) in a platformer, the controls feels great and runs smoothly at all times.
Unlike the core game Rise of the Owlverlord holds no punches and throws everything it can as soon you decide to play. Mercifully there is a "Normal" mode which considerably ramps down the difficulty inserting safe places between death traps and removing certain gimmicks that would require split second reaction to bypass.
However as soon you decide to pick "Hard" mode you're in for a rough ride as the game will not hold your hand even for the first second of the first level, but playing at hard difficulty will allow you to earn rank stars and will unlock the finished level for Time Attack and Score Attack mode.
For those seeking for more challenge the game still have the Hardcore difficulty (which removes every checkpoint) and the Über Hardcore (which gives you one, single life for the entire game).
Rise of the Owlverlord follows just as well the core game and is more than a "more of the same" expansion, it is a fine platformer with beautiful graphics, amazing controls and brutally difficult if you are not used to platformers.

First thing I looked for after finishing this game was their OSTs because of the groove being presented in each of these levels. Although, the next thing I had to do (since I'm a semi-completionist when it comes to doable achievements) was to encounter an achievement bug for not discovering all secret areas (while I already finished with it along with beating the final boss).
PixelJunk Shooter Ultimate combines Shooter 1 and 2 in this nice pack of graphic update where you can choose between classic, vector-looking PixelJunk style, and ultimate style with remastered graphics that can run in 60 FPS (if your PC specs are decent enough). You play as a spacecraft and your main objective is to save scientists without killing them - doing so will increase damage casualties that would end your stage once it reached 5. As a bonus, you have some boss fights at the end of each episodes, plus treasures and hidden area discoveries to be done.
I really love the liquid physics this game has. There are some interesting logics about element combinations; each episodes has their own unique themes - except for Episode 5
. Suit and liftable object inclusions certainly make the run funner to spice things more in this action-puzzle game. Although, I feel Hunger Suit moments are really boring to be done just because how slow your spacecraft will be, as the movement's getting restrictive since you can only go to 4 directions instead of all. What is this, some kind of Pac-Man game?
Another off thing I need to address is the constant game freeze in random occasions. There was one time I was about to fight the final boss, then the game froze in the middle, forcing me to restart the game. Turns out I had to start from that particular stage aaall way around again to fight it.
I'm not going to talk about online system and co-op. I did hear some complains of them not working much - not much people play this for online system from what I know.
There are some interesting surprises in every episode
which keeps the game to be lively interesting. Controls are simple and responsive, too - I can finish only with mouse and keyboard, although controller seems to be the most recommended since the control tips are for controller user. Overall, PixelJunk Shooter Ultimate is pretty much mixed in my side. Regardless of the achievement bug and game freezes, this game is still worth checking if you're a fan of classic 2D shooter (and here I thank my friend to recommend this). Be wary if you encountered any bug or game freeze though, might be worth to get in PS3 instead.

PJSU is a great coop experience, but weirdly enough you'll notice a bunch of levels seem to be made with the mindset of a singleplayer game, as some levels felt too cramped and tight for the double action. Luckily, these levels appear a view times, mostly only in the second half of the game. This half happen to be my least favourite part, because the first half just had slightly better level design in overall.
I'd like to point out again how much fun the game is with a collabortive partner. Most levels are kind of boring by yourself, but are more intense and interesting with another player next to you as he or she can harm you too by accident. Nevertheless, while hunting down the last achievements by myself (because of a specific tracking bug), I still did enjoy the music (when it works 60% of the time) and the water mechanics. It's always satisfying to shoot open a hole where the water bursts out of and negates the magma below.
It's also these mechanics - though consistant and reliable - tend to be your biggest threat in the whole game. This is another reason why having a partner with you is great, because you don't constantly have to restart from checkpoint. As long as your partner is alive, you can just respawn with him or her. This certainly made the game less tedious to play.
There is also a versus mode playable, but you'll have to hook up with someone if you want to check it out. It's OK, but the thing that bugs me is: why the frick isn't this versus mode playable locally!? On the flip side, why can't the main game played online? It's seems so arbitrary. Btw, some achievements are tide to the versus mode. Completionists should be aware of that as well as the mentioned stat-tracking bug.
I think it's fair to notify you for the prevalent bugs. I didn't come across game-breaking glitches, but I did have a re-occuring music outage. Also, when hooking my laptop up to a TV screen at my friends house, the audio just refused to work through the TV. I did not have this problem at my place, but it was a bummer. The problem might have to do with the HDMI cable as I noticed (and heard) that cables tend to act differently from each other. Other players, as you'll see in other reviews, DID experience severe bugs, so be aware,

1. Do NOT purchase
2. Only if you have nothing else to do
